verses.heading: The Genealogy of Jesus Christ / The Genealogy of Jesus Christ / Lk. 3:23-38
verses.text: The record of the genealogy and ancestral line of Jesus Christ—the son of David (fulfilling the royal messianic promises) and the son of Abraham (fulfilling the covenant promises to the patriarch).
Abraham became the father of Isaac, and Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers—the twelve patriarchs of Israel.

And Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar—including this unusual union to show God’s grace even in irregular circumstances—and Perez became the father of Hezron, and Hezron became the father of Ram.
And Ram became the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon became the father of Salmon.

And Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab—the Gentile woman and former prostitute, demonstrating God’s inclusive grace—and Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth—another Gentile woman, showing God’s plan includes all nations—and Obed became the father of Jesse.

And Jesse became the father of David the king—the great king of Israel through whose line the Christ would come. And David became the father of Solomon by the wife of Uriah—deliberately referencing Bathsheba through her former husband to acknowledge David’s grievous sin, yet showing God’s redemptive grace.
And Solomon became the father of Rehoboam, and Rehoboam became the father of Abijah, and Abijah became the father of Asaph.
And Asaph became the father of Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat became the father of Joram, and Joram became the father of Uzziah.
And Uzziah became the father of Jotham, and Jotham became the father of Ahaz, and Ahaz became the father of Hezekiah.
And Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh, and Manasseh became the father of Amon, and Amon became the father of Josiah.
And Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the tragic deportation and exile to Babylon—marking a dark period in Israel’s history.
Then after the deportation to Babylon and during the exile, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel, and Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel—the governor who led the return from exile.
And Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud, and Abiud became the father of Eliakim, and Eliakim became the father of Azor.
And Azor became the father of Zadok, and Zadok became the father of Achim, and Achim became the father of Eliud.
And Eliud became the father of Eleazar, and Eleazar became the father of Matthan, and Matthan became the father of Jacob.

And Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary—noting that Joseph was the legal father though not the biological father—from whom Jesus was born, the One who is called Christ—the Messiah and Anointed One.

Therefore, all the generations from Abraham to David totalled fourteen generations, representing the period of promise; and from David to the deportation to Babylon were fourteen generations, representing the period of the kingdom; and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ were fourteen generations, representing the period of exile and anticipation—God’s sovereign plan unfolding through history in ordered progression.

verses.heading: The Birth of Jesus Christ / The Birth of Jesus Christ / Lk. 2:1-7
verses.text: Now the birth of Jesus Christ, the Messiah, happened in this miraculous way: When His mother Mary had been pledged in a legally binding betrothal to Joseph—a commitment as binding as marriage itself—before they came together in physical union as husband and wife, she was found to be with child, pregnant through the supernatural work of the Holy Spirit, not through any human father.

So Joseph, her husband and betrothed—being a righteous and just man who sought to obey God’s Law, and not willing to expose her publicly to shame and potential stoning for suspected adultery—intended to divorce her and send her away secretly and quietly, to protect her from public disgrace.

But while he was reflecting on and pondering these troubling matters, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream with divine revelation, saying, “Joseph, son of David—addressed as a descendant of the royal line—do not be afraid or hesitant to take Mary as your wife in full marriage, for the child that has been conceived in her womb is from the Holy Spirit, not from any human father.

And she will bear a Son, and you shall call His name ‘Jesus’—which means ‘Yahweh saves’—for He will save His people from their sins, accomplishing the work of redemption and delivering them from the guilt, penalty, and power of sin.”
Now, all this occurred and came to pass in order to fulfill what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet Isaiah, saying,

“Behold, the virgin—the young woman who has never known a man—will be with Child and will bear a Son, and they will call His name Emmanuel,” which is translated and means, “God with us”*—signifying that God Himself has come to dwell amongst His people in human flesh.
And when Joseph woke up from his sleep, he did exactly as the angel of the Lord commanded him; and he took Mary as his wife in full marriage,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And did not engage in sexual relations with her, preserving her virginity until after she had borne a Son—her firstborn. And he called His name Jesus, in obedience to the angel’s instruction. 23 Quoted from Is. 7:14

verses.heading: The Visit of the Magi / The Visit of the Magi
verses.text: Now, after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea—the prophesied birthplace of the Messiah—in the days of Herod the king—the Idumean king ruling under Roman authority—behold, magi from the East—learned men, possibly astrologers or wise men from Persia or Babylon—came to Jerusalem,
Saying, “Where is the One who has been born King of the Jews? For we saw His star at its emergence in the heavens, and we have come from afar to worship Him.”
Now, when King Herod heard this enquiry, he was troubled—fearing a rival to his throne—and all Jerusalem with him, sharing his fear and anxiety.

And having gathered together all the chief priests and scribes of the people—the religious authorities and experts in Scripture—he began enquiring and demanding from them where the Christ, the Messiah, was prophesied to be born.
And they answered him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for thus it is written and prophesied by the prophet Micah:

‘And you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least or insignificant amongst the rulers of Judah, for from you will come forth a ruler, a shepherd-king, who will shepherd, lead, and care for My people Israel.’ ”*
Then, Herod secretly and privately called the magi and ascertained and determined precisely from them the exact time when the star had first appeared—calculating the Child’s age.

And he sent them to Bethlehem with deceptive instructions and said, “Go, search carefully and diligently for the Child, and when you have found Him, bring a report back to me, so that I also may come and worship Him”—though his true intent was murderous.

And listening to the king’s instructions, they went out on their journey; and behold, the star which they had seen at its emergence guided them supernaturally until it came and stood directly over the place where the Child was—pinpointing the exact location.
Now, when they saw the star positioned over the location, they rejoiced profoundly with exceedingly great joy.

And coming into the house—no longer a stable but a dwelling where the family had taken residence—they saw the Child with Mary His mother, and they fell down prostrate and worshipped Him with reverence. And when they opened their valuable containers, they offered Him costly and significant gifts: gold—fit for a king, frankincense—fit for deity and priestly worship, and myrrh—foreshadowing His death and burial.

And having been divinely warned and instructed in a dream not to return to Herod—God protecting the Child from danger—they departed and returned to their own country by another route, avoiding Jerusalem.

verses.heading: The Flight to Egypt / The Flight to Egypt
verses.text: Now, after they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph with urgent instructions, saying, “Rise quickly, take the Child and His mother, and flee immediately to Egypt, and stay there in safety until I speak to you again. For Herod is about to search for the Child to destroy Him.”
So he got up immediately, and took the Child and His mother by night under cover of darkness, and departed and fled to Egypt for refuge.

And he remained there until the death of Herod, when the threat was removed. This was to fulfill what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet Hosea, saying, “Out of Egypt I have called My Son”*—the child Jesus recapitulating Israel’s history, as Israel was called God’s son who came out of Egypt.

verses.heading: Herod’s Murderous Action / Herod’s Murderous Action
verses.text: Then Herod, when he realized and saw that he had been mocked and outwitted by the magi, was intensely and violently enraged; and he sent soldiers and gave orders to put to death cruelly all the male boys in Bethlehem and in all its surrounding regions from two years old and under—massacring innocent children—according to the time which he had carefully ascertained from the magi regarding when the star appeared.
Then was fulfilled what was spoken prophetically by Jeremiah the prophet, saying,

“A voice was heard in Ramah—a town north of Jerusalem— weeping and loud lamentation and bitter mourning, Rachel—the matriarch representing the mothers of Israel— weeping inconsolably for her children; and she would not be consoled or comforted, because they are no more, they have been killed.”*

verses.heading: The Return to Israel and Nazareth / The Return to Israel and Nazareth
verses.text: Now, when Herod died and the threat was removed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt with new instructions,
Saying, “When you get up, take the Child and His mother, and go back to the land of Israel, for those who were seeking the life of the Child to kill Him are now dead.”
So, when he got up in obedience, he took the Child and His mother, and came back into the land of Israel to return home.

But having heard that Archelaus—Herod’s son, known for his cruelty—was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid and hesitant to go there to Bethlehem or Jerusalem; and having been divinely warned and instructed in a dream, he took refuge and withdrew to the district and region of Galilee in the north.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And he came and lived in a city called Nazareth—an insignificant city. This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophets collectively: “He will be called a Nazarene.” 6 Quoted from Mic. 5:2 15 Quoted from Hos. 11:1 18 Quoted from Jer. 31:15

verses.heading: The Preaching Ministry of John the Baptist / The Preaching Ministry of John the Baptist / Mk. 1:1-8; Lk. 3.1-9, 15-17; Jn. 1:19-28
verses.text: And in those days, during this period of expectation, John the Baptist—the forerunner and preparer of the way—came, preaching publicly in the Judean wilderness, the desert region near the Jordan River.
And saying with urgency, “Repent—turn from your sins and change your minds and hearts—for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near—God’s rule and reign is breaking into history.”
For this is the very one who was spoken of and prophesied by Isaiah the prophet, saying, “The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.’ ”*

Now John himself had his clothing and apparel made of camel’s hair—rough, humble clothing like the ancient prophets—and a leather belt around his waist; and his food was locusts and wild honey—simple, austere fare from the wilderness, demonstrating his separation from worldly comforts.
At that time, Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region around the Jordan were going out to him in large numbers, drawn by his prophetic message,
And they were being baptized in the Jordan River by him, publicly confessing their sins and acknowledging their need for repentance.

But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees—the religious elite and leaders—coming to his baptism, he said to them with sharp rebuke, “You offspring and brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath and judgment of God?
Therefore, bear fruit—produce evidence—appropriate to and consistent with true repentance, demonstrating genuine change in your lives.

And do not presume or think to say within yourselves with false confidence, ‘We have Abraham as our father and are his descendants.’ For I say to you that God is able, from these very stones lying here, to raise up children and true descendants for Abraham!

Even now, at this very moment, the axe is laid to the root of the trees, ready to cut them down; therefore, every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire of judgment.”

“I indeed baptize you with water as a sign of repentance, but the One who comes after me—the Messiah—is mightier and more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy or fit to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit, bringing spiritual transformation and empowerment, and with fire, bringing decisive judgment.

His winnowing fork is in His hand, ready to work, and He will thoroughly clean out His threshing floor, separating wheat from chaff, and He will gather His wheat—true believers—into the barn of safety, but the chaff—the unrepentant—He will burn up with unquenchable fire of eternal judgment.”

verses.heading: The Baptism of Jesus / The Baptism of Jesus / Mk. 1.9-11; Lk. 3:21-22
verses.text: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan River, to John, to be baptized by him—identifying with sinful humanity though Himself sinless.
But John attempted to prevent Him, saying with humility, “I have the need to be baptized by You, do You come to me?”
But in response, Jesus said to him, “Allow this to happen, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness”—to accomplish all that God requires and to identify fully with humanity.

Now, having been baptized and coming up immediately from the water, Jesus immediately went up out of the water, and behold, the heavens were opened supernaturally, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove in visible form and alighting upon Him—anointing Him for His messianic ministry.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And behold, a voice came from heaven, the Father’s voice, saying, “This is My Son, My beloved One, in whom I am well pleased”—the Father’s affirming declaration of Jesus’ identity and approval. 3 Quoted from Is. 40:3

verses.heading: The Temptation of Jesus / The Temptation of Jesus / Mk. 1:12-13; Lk. 4:1-13
verses.text: Subsequently, immediately after His baptism, Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit deliberately to be tempted by the devil—to prove His qualification as the sinless Messiah.
And after fasting forty days and forty nights, He was hungry afterward, physically weakened and vulnerable.

And the tempter, Satan, came and approached Him and said to Him, “If You are the Son of God—since You claim to be—speak and command that these stones become bread to satisfy Your hunger and prove Your power.”
But in response, He said, quoting Scripture, “It is written in Deuteronomy: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word which proceeds out of the mouth of God’ ”*
After this, the devil took Him to the holy city, Jerusalem, and placed Him on the pinnacle of the temple—the highest point overlooking the valley,

And he said to Him, “If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down from here, for it is written in the Psalms: ‘He will give orders to His angels concerning You,’ and ‘On their hands they will carry You, lest You strike Your foot against a stone’ ”*
Jesus said to him, “Once more, it is also written, ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test’ ”*
Once more, the devil took Him to a very high mountain, and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory and splendor in a moment,
And he said to Him, “All these things—all this power and authority—I will give to You, if You will fall down and worship me.”
Then Jesus said to him with authority, “Depart, Satan! Be gone! For it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God and Him only you shall serve’ ”*
Then the devil left Him, and behold, angels came and began attending to His needs.

verses.heading: The Beginning of Jesus’ Galilean Ministry / The Beginning of Jesus’ Galilean Ministry / Mk. 1:14-15; Lk. 4:14-15
verses.text: Now, having heard that John had been arrested and imprisoned by Herod Antipas, Jesus withdrew and returned to Galilee to begin His public ministry there.
And leaving Nazareth, His hometown, He went and settled in Capernaum—making it His base of operations—which is by the Sea of Galilee, in the region and territory of Zebulun and Naphtali.
This was to fulfill what was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, which says,
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles—a region despised and overlooked—

the people sitting and dwelling in darkness and ignorance have seen a great light of revelation, and for those sitting and dwelling in the territory and shadow of death, a light has dawned and risen upon them.”*
From that time on, Jesus began to preach publicly, saying, “Repent and turn from your sins, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near and God’s reign is at hand.”

verses.heading: Jesus Calls the Four Fishermen / Jesus Calls the Four Fishermen
verses.text: Now, as He was walking beside the Sea of Galilee one day, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen by trade.
And He spoke to them with a call, “Come, follow Me as My disciples, and I will make you fishers of men, catching people for the kingdom of God.”
And immediately, without hesitation, they left the nets and followed Him in full commitment.

And going on from there along the shore, He saw two other brothers: James, the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, in the boat with Zebedee, their father, repairing their nets; and He called them with the same invitation.
And without delay, they left the boat and their father, and followed Him.

verses.heading: Jesus’ Three-fold Ministry / Jesus’ Three-fold Ministry / Lk. 6:17-19
verses.text: And He went around traveling through all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues—instructing people in God’s truth, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom—proclaiming the good news of God’s saving reign, and healing every disease and every illness and infirmity amongst the people—demonstrating His divine authority and compassion.

And the report regarding Him and His miraculous works spread throughout all Syria, and they brought to Him all the sick and afflicted: those who had various diseases and pains, those who were tormented and demon-possessed by evil spirits, and those who were epileptic and paralyzed and unable to walk. And He healed them all, demonstrating His power over all forms of human suffering.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And large crowds followed Him from Galilee and Decapolis—the region of ten cities—and from Jerusalem and Judea, and from beyond the Jordan, drawn by His teaching and miracles. 4 Quoted from Deut. 8:3 6 Quoted from Ps. 91:11-12 7 Quoted from Deut. 6:16 10 Quoted from Deut. 6:13 15-16 Quoted from Is. 9:1-2

verses.heading: The Sermon on the Mount / The Sermon on the Mount / Matt. 5-7
verses.text: When Jesus saw the large crowds gathering, He climbed up the mountainside. After He settled into a teaching position, His disciples gathered around Him.

verses.heading: The Beatitudes / The Beatitudes / Lk. 6:20-23
verses.text: Opening His mouth to teach them, He declared:
“How blessed are those who recognize their spiritual poverty and need for God, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to them.
How blessed are those who grieve over sin, for God Himself will comfort them.
How blessed are the gentle and humble-hearted, for they will inherit the earth as God’s gift.
How blessed are those who have an intense spiritual hunger and thirst for right living, for they will be completely satisfied.
How blessed are those who show mercy to others, for they themselves will receive mercy.
How blessed are those whose hearts are undivided and pure in their devotion to God, for they will see Him face to face.
How blessed are those who actively work to bring peace and reconciliation, for God will acknowledge them as His true children.
How blessed are those who face persecution because they live righteously, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
How blessed you are when people insult your character, persecute you, and spread malicious lies about you because of your allegiance to Me.
Respond with joy and great celebration, for your reward in heaven is great. This is exactly how they persecuted the prophets who came before you.

verses.heading: Salt of the Earth and Light of the World / Salt of the Earth and Light of the World / Mk. 9:50; Lk. 14:34-35
verses.text: “You are the preserving salt of the earth. But if salt loses its distinctive quality and flavor, how can it be made salty again? It becomes worthless—fit only to be discarded and trampled underfoot.
You are the illuminating light of the world. A city built on a hilltop cannot be hidden from view.
No one lights a lamp only to cover it with a container; instead, they place it on a stand where it provides light for everyone in the house.
In the same way, let your light shine openly before people, so they can observe your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.

verses.heading: Concerning the Law / Concerning the Law
verses.text: “Do not assume for a moment that I came to abolish or set aside the Law or the prophetic writings. I did not come to destroy them but to fulfill and complete them.

I tell you with absolute certainty: Until the present heaven and earth pass away, not even the smallest letter or the tiniest stroke of a pen will disappear from the Law until God’s entire purpose is accomplished.

Therefore, anyone who disregards even the least significant of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be considered least important in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever practices and teaches them will be regarded as great in the kingdom.

For I assure you that unless your righteousness surpasses that of the religious scholars and Pharisees—going beyond their external rule-keeping to genuine heart transformation—you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

verses.heading: Concerning Anger / Concerning Anger
verses.text: “You have heard that it was taught to the ancients, ‘You must not commit murder,’* and ‘whoever commits murder will face judicial consequences.’*

But I tell you that everyone who harbors anger against his brother will face God’s judgment; whoever speaks contemptuously to his brother, calling him worthless, will be brought before the high court; and whoever calls him a fool worthy of damnation will be in danger of hell’s fire.
Therefore, if you are in the act of presenting your offering at the altar and suddenly remember that your brother has something against you—some unresolved conflict—
leave your gift right there at the altar. First go and be reconciled with your brother, restoring the relationship, and then return to present your gift.

Settle matters quickly with your legal opponent while you are still on the way to court, before your opponent hands you over to the judge, who hands you to the officer, and you are thrown into prison.
I assure you, you will not get out of there until you have paid the very last cent of what you owe.

verses.heading: Concerning Adultery / Concerning Adultery
verses.text: “You have heard the commandment: ‘You must not commit adultery.’*
But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman with the intent to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart—in his thoughts and desires.
If your right eye causes you to stumble into sin, tear it out and throw it away. It is far better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better to lose one part of your body than for your entire body to end up in hell.

verses.heading: Concerning Divorce / Concerning Divorce
verses.text: “It has also been taught: ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a formal certificate of divorce.’*
But I tell you that everyone who divorces his wife, except in cases of sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery when she remarries; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

verses.heading: Concerning Taking of Oaths / Concerning Taking of Oaths
verses.text: “Again, you have heard that the ancients were told, ‘You must not break your oaths, but must fulfill whatever vows you make to the Lord.’*
But I tell you, do not swear oaths at all—not by heaven, because it is God’s throne,
nor by the earth, because it serves as His footstool, nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.
Do not even swear by your own head, because you lack the power to make a single hair white or black.
Simply let your word be trustworthy: say ‘Yes’ when you mean yes, and ‘No’ when you mean no. Anything beyond this simple honesty comes from the evil one.

verses.heading: Concerning Retaliation / Concerning Retaliation
verses.text: “You have heard it said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’*

But I tell you, do not retaliate against the evildoer seeking revenge; instead, if someone strikes you on your right cheek, turn and offer him the other one as well, showing restraint rather than revenge.
If someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your outer cloak as well, demonstrating generosity instead of arguing.
If someone forces you into service to carry his load one mile, willingly go with him two, showing willingness to serve beyond what is demanded.
Give generously to the one who asks you for help, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you, embodying generosity and compassion in every encounter.

verses.heading: Love of Enemies / Love of Enemies
verses.text: “You have heard it taught, ‘You shall love your neighbor* and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
so that you may demonstrate that you are truly children of your Father in heaven. He makes His sun rise on both the evil and the good, and sends rain on both the righteous and the unrighteous.
For if you only love those who love you in return, what reward do you deserve? Do not even the tax collectors—society’s outcasts—do the same?
And if you only greet and show kindness to your brothers and friends, what are you doing that is extraordinary? Do not even the Gentiles do that much?

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Therefore, you must be perfect—complete and mature in love—just as your heavenly Father is perfect. 21 Quoted from Ex. 20:13; Deut. 5:17 21 See Deut. 16:18 27 Quoted from Ex. 20:14; Deut. 5:18 31 Quoted from Deut. 24:1 33 See Lev. 19:12 38 Quoted from Ex. 21:24; Lev. 24:20; Deut. 19:21 43 Quoted from Lev. 19:18

verses.heading: Concerning Philanthropic Acts / Concerning Philanthropic Acts
verses.text: “Be careful not to perform your acts of righteousness publicly before people just to gain their admiration and applause; otherwise, you will receive no reward from your Father in heaven.

Therefore, when you give to help the needy, do not announce it with fanfare—like the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets to gain public acclaim. I assure you, they have already received all the reward they are going to get.
But when you give to the poor, do it so secretly that even your left hand does not know what your right hand is doing,
so that your giving remains hidden. Then your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.

verses.heading: Concerning Prayer / Concerning Prayer / Lk. 11:2–4
verses.text: “When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites who love to pray standing prominently in the synagogues and on street corners where everyone can see them. I assure you, they have received their full reward already.
But when you pray, go into your private room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is in secret. Your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
“And when you pray, do not babble on with empty, repetitive phrases like the pagans do, who think they will be heard because they use so many words.
Do not be like them, for your Father already knows what you need before you even ask Him.
Therefore, this is how you should pray: “Our Father in heaven, may Your name be treated as holy and revered.
May Your kingdom come and Your rule be established, may Your will be accomplished on earth just as it is in heaven.
Give us today the bread we need for this day.
Forgive us our debts and sins, just as we have forgiven those who are indebted to us.
And do not lead us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.
For if you forgive others their sins and offenses against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
But if you refuse to forgive others, your Father will not forgive your offenses either.

verses.heading: Concerning Fasting / Concerning Fasting
verses.text: “When you fast, do not put on a gloomy, mournful appearance like the hypocrites do, who deliberately make their faces look miserable so everyone will know they are fasting. I assure you, they have received their full reward.
But when you fast, wash your face and anoint your head with oil as usual,
so that your fasting will not be obvious to others but only to your Father who is in secret. Your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.

verses.heading: Treasures in Heaven / Treasures in Heaven / Lk. 12:33–34
verses.text: “Do not accumulate treasures for yourselves here on earth, where moths and rust corrode and destroy them, and where thieves break in and steal.
Instead, store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moths nor rust can destroy, and where thieves cannot break in or steal.
For wherever your treasure is, that is where your heart will be focused as well.

verses.heading: The Light of the Body / The Light of the Body / Lk. 11:34–36
verses.text: “The eye functions as the lamp of the body. So if your eye is healthy and clear, your whole body will be filled with light.
But if your eye is diseased and darkened, your whole body will be full of darkness. So if the light within you has become darkness, how profound and terrible that darkness is!

verses.heading: God and Money / God and Money / Lk. 16:13
verses.text: “No one can serve two masters simultaneously. Either he will hate one and love the other, or he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money—you must choose.

verses.heading: Anxiety / Anxiety / Lk. 12:22–34
verses.text: “This is why I tell you: Do not be consumed with anxiety about your life—what you will eat or drink—or about your body and what you will wear. Is not life about more than just food? Is not the body worth more than clothing?

Look carefully at the birds flying through the sky: They do not plant seeds, harvest crops, or store food in barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them abundantly. Are you not far more valuable to Him than they are?
Besides, which of you can add even a single hour to your life or a single inch to your height by worrying?
And why do you worry about clothing? Study the wild lilies and how they grow: they do not labor or spin thread to make fabric,
yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his magnificent splendor was dressed as beautifully as one of these flowers.
Now if God clothes the grass in the field so beautifully—grass that is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven as fuel—will He not take far better care of you, you who have such little faith?
Therefore, do not be anxious, constantly asking, “What will we eat?” or “What will we drink?” or “What will we wear?”
These are the things unbelievers obsess over and pursue. Your heavenly Father already knows that you need all these things.
But seek first and foremost the kingdom of God and His righteousness—make these your top priority—and all these necessities will be provided for you.
Therefore, do not be anxious about tomorrow, because tomorrow will have its own concerns. Each day has enough trouble of its own to deal with.

verses.heading: Concerning Judging Others / Concerning Judging Others / Lk. 6:37–38, 41–42
verses.text: “Do not make yourselves judges over others with a critical and condemning spirit, lest you bring the same kind of severe judgment upon yourselves.
For God will apply to you the very same standard of judgment that you have used toward others, and the measure of mercy or harshness you extend will be measured back to you in equal proportion.
Why do you fixate on the insignificant speck of sawdust in your fellow believer’s eye while remaining completely blind to the massive wooden beam that obstructs your own vision?
How can you presume to say to your brother, ‘Allow me to remove that tiny speck from your eye,’ when your own eye is blocked by a plank so large you cannot even see clearly?

You hypocrite! You must first deal with the plank of sin in your own life, removing it through repentance and correction, and only then will your vision be clear enough to help your brother with his smaller fault.

“Do not take what is sacred and holy—the precious truths of the gospel—and cast them before those who are like dogs, who have no respect for spiritual things. Do not throw your pearls of divine wisdom before swine, who will only trample them in the mud and then turn on you with hostility and violence.

verses.heading: Concerning Asking, Seeking, and Knocking / Concerning Asking, Seeking, and Knocking / Lk. 11:9–13
verses.text: “Continue persistently in prayer: keep asking and God will give to you; keep seeking and you will discover what you need; keep knocking and the door of heaven’s provision will be opened to you.
For this is a divine principle: Everyone who asks with faith receives; the one who diligently seeks finds what he is looking for; and to the one who knocks persistently, the door will be opened.
What father among you would be so cruel that, if his son asks him for bread to satisfy his hunger, would hand him a stone instead?
Or if his son asks for a fish to eat, would give him a venomous snake that would harm him?

If you, then, though you are sinful and imperfect by nature, know how to give good and beneficial gifts to your children, how much more will your perfectly loving Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him in faith!

Therefore, this is the practical rule for all your relationships: In every situation, whatever you would desire people to do for you, do precisely that same thing for them. This single principle summarizes and fulfills all the requirements of the entire Law and the teaching of the Prophets.

verses.heading: Concerning the Narrow Gate / Concerning the Narrow Gate / Lk. 13:24
verses.text: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow gate of salvation, for the gate that leads to destruction is wide and the road is broad and easy, and tragically, many people are traveling on that path.
But the gate that leads to eternal life is narrow and restrictive, and the road is difficult and demanding, and only a few people find it and are willing to walk it.

verses.heading: A Tree and Its Fruit / A Tree and Its Fruit / Lk. 6:43–44
verses.text: “Be constantly on guard against false prophets who approach you disguised as harmless sheep in their outward appearance, but inwardly their true nature is that of vicious, predatory wolves who will devour the flock.
You will be able to recognize them by examining the fruit that their lives and teaching produce. People do not gather edible grapes from thornbushes, nor do they pick figs from thistles, do they?
In the same way, every healthy and sound tree produces fruit that is good and nourishing, but a diseased and corrupt tree produces fruit that is bad and worthless.
A healthy tree cannot produce bad fruit because it is sound at its core, just as a diseased tree is incapable of producing good fruit because it is rotten within.
Every tree that fails to produce good fruit is cut down by the owner and thrown into the fire for destruction.
So then, by this principle you will surely recognize false prophets—by carefully examining the fruit that their lives and ministries produce over time.

verses.heading: I Have Never Known You / I Have Never Known You / Lk. 13:25–27
verses.text: “Not everyone who addresses Me with the words ‘Lord, Lord’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the person who actually obeys and does the will of My Father who is in heaven.

On that final day of judgment, many will plead with Me, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy and preach in Your name? Did we not cast out demons by invoking Your name? Did we not perform many miracles and mighty works in Your name?’

And then I will declare to them with unmistakable clarity, ‘I never knew you in an intimate, saving relationship. Depart from My presence, you who practice lawlessness and rebellion against God despite your religious activities.’

verses.heading: The Two Foundations / The Two Foundations / Lk. 6:47–49
verses.text: “Therefore, everyone who hears these authoritative words of Mine and puts them into practice by obeying them will be like a wise and prudent man who built his house upon the solid rock.

The rain poured down in torrents, the floodwaters rose and surged, the winds blew with force and battered that house, yet it did not collapse because its foundation was firmly and securely established on the bedrock.
But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them or obey them will be like a foolish and shortsighted man who built his house upon the sand.

The rain poured down, the floodwaters rose and rushed against it, the winds blew and pounded violently against that house, and it collapsed completely in ruins—and its destruction was utter and catastrophic.”
When Jesus finished delivering these profound teachings, the crowds who had been listening were utterly astonished at His teaching,

because He taught them as one who possessed inherent divine authority in Himself, not like their scribes and religious teachers who merely quoted other rabbis and authorities to validate their interpretations.

verses.heading: The Cleansing of a Leper / The Cleansing of a Leper / Mk. 1:40–45; Lk. 5:12–16
verses.text: When He descended from the mountain where He had been teaching, large crowds of people followed Him, eager to hear more and witness His works.

Suddenly, a man severely afflicted with leprosy approached Him and knelt before Him in an act of worship and desperate supplication, saying, “Lord, if You are willing to heal me, I know You have the power to make me clean.”

Jesus stretched out His hand and touched him—an act no one else would dare to do because of the ceremonial defilement—saying with compassion, “I am willing; be cleansed and made whole.” Immediately, at that very moment, his leprosy was completely healed and he was restored.

Jesus gave him strict instructions, saying, “Make sure you do not tell anyone about this miracle; but go directly and show yourself to the priest for official examination, and offer the sacrifice that Moses commanded in the Law, as a public testimony to the religious authorities of your genuine healing.”

verses.heading: The Healing of a Centurion’s Servant / The Healing of a Centurion’s Servant / Lk. 7:1–10; Jn. 4:43–54
verses.text: When Jesus entered the town of Capernaum, a Roman centurion—a Gentile military officer—came to Him, urgently pleading with Him for help
and saying, “Lord, my servant is lying at home completely paralyzed, suffering in terrible and agonizing torment.”
Jesus responded to him, saying, “I will come to your home and heal him.”
But the centurion humbly responded, “Lord, I am not worthy or deserving to have You come under my roof and into my house. Just speak the word of command from here, and my servant will be healed.

For I myself am a man who operates under the authority of my superiors, and I have soldiers under my own command, and when I tell this one, ‘Go,’ he goes without question, and when I tell another, ‘Come,’ he comes immediately, and when I tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ he does it. I understand that You have even greater authority over sickness and disease.”

When Jesus heard this remarkable statement of faith, He was amazed, and He said to those who were following Him, “I tell you the solemn truth, I have not found anyone in all of Israel with such great and genuine faith as this Gentile soldier.

I tell you prophetically that many people will come from the east and from the west—Gentiles from all nations—and will recline at the banquet table with the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
but the sons of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping in sorrow and gnashing of teeth in anguish.”

Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go your way; it will be done for you exactly as you have believed and trusted.” And his servant was completely healed at that precise moment, though Jesus was not physically present.

verses.heading: Jesus Heals Many / Jesus Heals Many / Mk. 1:29–34; Lk. 4:38–41
verses.text: When Jesus arrived at Peter’s house in Capernaum, He found Peter’s mother-in-law lying in bed, sick and suffering with a high fever.
He touched her hand with healing power, and immediately the fever left her body. She got up, fully restored, and began attending to His needs.

When evening came and the Sabbath restrictions had ended, people brought to Him many individuals who were possessed by demons, and He cast out the evil spirits with a simple word of command. He also healed everyone who was sick with various diseases.

This widespread healing ministry happened in order to fulfill and bring to completion what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah, who wrote: “He Himself took upon Himself our infirmities and sicknesses and carried away our diseases.”*

verses.heading: The Cost of Following Jesus / The Cost of Following Jesus / Lk. 9:57–62
verses.text: When Jesus observed a large crowd gathering around Him and pressing in, He gave orders to His disciples to cross to the other side of the Sea of Galilee.
A scribe—a teacher of the Jewish Law—approached and said to Him with apparent enthusiasm, “Teacher, I will follow You wherever You go, no matter where Your journey takes You.”

Jesus replied to him, testing his commitment, “Foxes have dens where they live and birds of the air have nests for shelter, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head and call His own—I live without earthly security or comfort.”
Another of His disciples said to Him, “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father, fulfilling my family obligations.”
But Jesus told him with urgency, “Follow Me now without delay, and let the spiritually dead bury their own physical dead.”

verses.heading: The Calming of a Great Storm / The Calming of a Great Storm / Mk. 4:35–41; Lk. 8:22–25
verses.text: When He got into the boat to cross the sea, His disciples followed Him and embarked with Him.
Without warning, a violent storm erupted on the lake, with waves so high and powerful they were swamping the boat and threatening to sink it, yet Jesus remained peacefully sleeping.
The disciples came to Him in panic and woke Him up, crying out in fear, “Lord, save us! We are perishing and about to drown!”

He said to them, “Why are you so filled with terror, you men of little faith and weak trust?” Then He stood up and rebuked the winds and the sea with His authoritative word, and immediately there was a perfect calm.
The men were utterly amazed and filled with wonder, saying to one another, “What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey Him and submit to His command?”

verses.heading: The Healing of the Gadarene Demon-Possessed Men / The Healing of the Gadarene Demon-Possessed Men / Mk. 5:1–20; Lk. 8:26–39
verses.text: When He arrived on the other side of the sea in the region of the Gadarenes, two men who were demon-possessed came out from the tombs to meet Him. They were so extremely dangerous that no one could safely pass through that area.
They cried out with loud voices, saying, “What do You want with us, Son of God? Have You come here to torture us and inflict punishment before the appointed time of final judgment?”
Some distance away from them, there was a large herd of pigs feeding on the hillside.
The demons pleaded with Him, saying, “If You are going to cast us out of these men, send us into that herd of pigs instead.”

He said to them with authority, “Go.” So the demons came out of the men and went into the pigs, and suddenly the entire herd—about two thousand animals—rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned in the water.

The men who had been tending and watching the pigs fled in terror and went into the nearby town, reporting everything that had happened—including all the details about what had happened to the demon-possessed men.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Then the whole town came out to meet Jesus and see for themselves, and when they saw Him and understood what had occurred, they begged Him insistently to leave their region—valuing their economic interests over spiritual deliverance. 17 Quoted from Is. 53:4

verses.heading: The Healing of a Paralytic / The Healing of a Paralytic / Mk. 2:1–12; Lk. 5:17–26
verses.text: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over the Sea of Galilee, and came to His own town of Capernaum, which had become His base of ministry.

Some people brought to Him a paralyzed man lying helplessly on a stretcher. When Jesus saw their faith—the persistent faith of those who brought him through great difficulty—He said to the paralytic with authority, “Take courage and be of good cheer, son; your sins are forgiven.”
At this statement, some of the scribes said to themselves silently, “This man is blaspheming against God—claiming to do what only God alone can do!”
But Jesus, knowing their thoughts by divine insight, said, “Why are you harboring evil thoughts and hostile reasonings in your hearts?
Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ which cannot be verified by the eye, or 'Get up and walk,’ which can be immediately tested and observed?

But so that you may know with certainty that the Son of Man has divine authority on earth to forgive sins”—then He turned and said to the paralytic—“I say to you, get up, pick up your stretcher, and go home to your house.”
The man immediately stood up, completely healed, and went home, glorifying God.
When the crowds saw this astounding miracle, they were filled with reverential awe and glorified God for giving such authority to human beings, recognizing God’s power at work through Jesus.

verses.heading: The Calling of Matthew / The Calling of Matthew / Mk. 2:13–17; Lk. 5:27–32
verses.text: As Jesus was leaving that place, He saw a man named Matthew—also called Levi—sitting at the tax collector’s booth, and He said to him simply, “Follow Me and become My disciple.” Matthew immediately got up and followed Him.
Later, as Jesus was having dinner at Matthew’s house in celebration, many tax collectors and notorious sinners came and reclined at the table with Jesus and His disciples.

When the Pharisees observed this scandalous scene, they asked His disciples critically, “Why does your Teacher eat and associate with tax collectors and sinners—the outcasts and morally compromised people of society?”
When Jesus overheard this question, He responded, “Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are ailing do need medical care.

Go and learn the true meaning of what this Scripture says: ‘I desire mercy and compassion toward sinners, not merely sacrifice and ritual observance.’ For I did not come to call those who consider themselves righteous, but sinners.”

verses.heading: The Question About Fasting / The Question About Fasting / Mk. 2:18–22; Lk. 5:33–39
verses.text: Then the disciples of John the Baptist came to Him and asked, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast frequently as a spiritual discipline, but Your disciples do not practice fasting?”

Jesus answered them with an analogy, “How can the wedding guests mourn and fast while the bridegroom is present with them celebrating? But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then, in that period, they will fast.

No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment that has already been washed and shrunk, because when the patch is washed, it will shrink and pull away from the garment, making the tear even worse than before.

Neither do people pour new wine, which is still fermenting, into old wineskins that have become brittle. If they do, the skins will burst from the pressure, the wine will spill out and be lost, and the wineskins will be ruined and useless. Instead, people pour new wine into new wineskins that are flexible, and both the wine and the wineskins are preserved together.”

verses.heading: The Ruler’s Daughter and the Woman with Hemorrhage / The Ruler’s Daughter and the Woman with Hemorrhage / Mk. 5:21–43; Lk. 8:40–56
verses.text: While Jesus was speaking these things about fasting, a ruler of the synagogue came and bowed down before Him in desperate appeal, saying, “My daughter has just died, but if You will come and lay Your hand on her, she will live again.”
So Jesus got up and went with him, and His disciples accompanied them.
Just then, a woman who had suffered from chronic hemorrhaging for twelve long years came up behind Him in the crowd and touched the fringe of His outer garment.
For she kept saying to herself with faith, “If I can just touch His cloak, I will be healed and made whole.”
Jesus turned around, saw her, and said with compassion, “Take courage, daughter; your faith has healed you.” And the woman was instantly healed from that very moment.
When Jesus arrived at the ruler’s house and saw the flute players who were customarily hired for funerals and the noisy, disorderly crowd of mourners,
He said with authority, “Leave and make room, for the girl is not dead but sleeping.” But they laughed at Him scornfully, knowing she was dead.
But after the crowd had been forcibly put outside the house, He went in and took her hand in His, and the girl got up, alive and restored.
Reports of this astounding miracle spread rapidly throughout that entire region.

verses.heading: The Healing of Two Blind Men / The Healing of Two Blind Men
verses.text: As Jesus was leaving that place, two blind men followed Him persistently, crying out loudly, “Have mercy on us and heal us, Son of David!”—acknowledging Him as the Christ.

When He entered the house where He was staying, the blind men came directly to Him, and Jesus asked them, testing their faith, “Do you believe and are you convinced that I have the power to do this?” They answered Him with confidence, “Yes, Lord, we believe.”
Then He touched their eyes with compassion, saying, “According to your faith and in proportion to your trust, let it be done for you.”
And immediately their eyes were opened and they could see. Then Jesus gave them a stern warning, saying emphatically, “Make sure no one knows about this miracle.”
But they went out and spread the news about Him and what He had done throughout that entire region, unable to contain their joy.

verses.heading: The Healing of a Mute Man / The Healing of a Mute Man
verses.text: As they were leaving, some people brought to Him a man who was mute and unable to speak because he was demon-possessed.

When the demon had been cast out by Jesus’ authority, the man who had been mute spoke clearly. The crowds were utterly amazed, saying in astonishment, “Nothing like this has ever been seen or witnessed in Israel!”
But the Pharisees, hardening their hearts, said in willful rejection, “He casts out demons by the power of Beelzebul, the ruler of demons—He is in league with Satan himself.”

verses.heading: The Three-Fold Ministry of Jesus / The Three-Fold Ministry of Jesus
verses.text: Jesus traveled continuously through all the towns and villages throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every kind of disease and every kind of sickness among the people.

When He saw the crowds of people, He was moved with deep compassion for them, because they were harassed by their spiritual leaders and helpless in their spiritual condition—like sheep wandering without a shepherd to guide and protect them.
Then He said to His disciples, “The harvest of souls is plentiful and ready, but the workers who will gather the harvest are few and insufficient.

Therefore, pray earnestly and persistently to the Lord of the harvest—the sovereign God who oversees this work—that He will send out workers into His harvest field to gather the souls that are ready.”

verses.heading: Jesus Calls the Twelve Disciples / Jesus Calls the Twelve Disciples / Mk. 3:13-19; Lk. 6:12-16
verses.text: Jesus summoned His twelve disciples together and gave them delegated authority over unclean spirits—the supernatural power to cast them out—and to heal every kind of disease and every kind of sickness that afflicted the people.
Here are the names of the twelve apostles whom He commissioned: first in prominence, Simon, who is called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James, the son of Zebedee, and his brother John;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James, the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
Simon the Canaanite, who had been a zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who would later betray Him to death.

verses.heading: Jesus Commissioned the Twelve / Jesus Commissioned the Twelve / Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-6
verses.text: Jesus sent out these twelve apostles with specific and detailed instructions, saying, “Do not take the road that leads to Gentile territory, and do not enter into any city of the Samaritans,
but go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel—to God’s own chosen people who have wandered away from Him like sheep without a shepherd.
As you travel from place to place, preach and proclaim this message: ‘The kingdom of heaven has drawn near—God’s rule and reign is at hand and breaking into history.’

Heal the sick to demonstrate God’s power, raise the dead to show authority over death, cleanse those afflicted with leprosy, cast out demons to display victory over evil. You received this supernatural power freely as a gift from God, so give it freely to others without charging for your ministry.
Do not acquire or take with you gold, silver, or copper coins to put in your money belts for this journey,

or a traveler’s bag for provisions for the journey, or an extra tunic beyond what you are wearing, or sandals, or a walking staff—for the worker deserves to receive his support and provision from those he serves.
Whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy and receptive to your message, and stay in that hospitable home until you leave the area.
When you enter a house, extend your greeting of peace to it, blessing the household.

If the household proves worthy and receptive to your message, let your peace rest upon it and remain there; but if it is not worthy or receptive, let your peace return to you and withdraw your blessing.
If anyone refuses to welcome you or to listen to your message, as you leave that house or city, shake the dust off your feet as a solemn testimony against them and their rejection.

I assure you with absolute certainty and solemnity, it will be more tolerable and bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city that rejects the gospel message.

verses.heading: The Apostles Will Be Persecuted / The Apostles Will Be Persecuted / Mk. 13:9-13; Lk. 21:12-17
verses.text: “Listen carefully to what I am telling you: I am sending you out as vulnerable and defenseless sheep in the midst of vicious wolves. Therefore, you must be as shrewd and wise as serpents in avoiding danger, yet as harmless and innocent as doves in your conduct and motives.
But be on your guard and constantly vigilant against people, for they will hand you over to religious courts and councils, and they will flog you severely in their synagogues as punishment.

You will be brought and dragged before governors and kings because of your allegiance to Me and your testimony about Me, and this will serve as a testimony and witness to them and to the Gentile nations.

But when they arrest you and hand you over to the authorities, do not be anxious or worried about how you should speak or what you should say in your defense, for the words you need will be given to you at that very moment by the Holy Spirit.
For it will not really be you speaking in your own wisdom and strength, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you and giving you the words to say.
Brother will betray his own brother to death, and a father will betray his own child to the authorities; children will rise up in rebellion against their parents and have them put to death.

You will be hated by everyone in society because of your association with My name and your identification with Me. But the one who endures faithfully to the end without renouncing Me—this person will be saved and delivered.

When they persecute you in one city, flee quickly to another city for safety. I tell you the truth with certainty, you will not have finished going through all the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes in judgment or in glory.
“A disciple is not superior to or above his teacher, nor is a servant superior to or above his master.

It is sufficient for the disciple to become like his teacher in character and experience, and for the servant to become like his master. If they have called the head of the household Beelzebul—slandering him as the prince of demons—how much more will they malign and slander the members of his household with even worse names?

verses.heading: Fear Only God / Fear Only God / Lk. 12:2-7
verses.text: “Therefore, do not be intimidated by their threats, for nothing is concealed that will not be revealed, and nothing is secret that will not be brought to light.

What I tell you privately in the darkness, speak openly and boldly in the light of day; and what you hear whispered privately in your ear in secret, proclaim boldly and publicly from the housetops for all to hear.

Do not be afraid of those who can kill the body but are powerless to kill the soul. Instead, fear the One—God Himself—who has the power to destroy both soul and body in hell, the place of eternal judgment.

Are not two sparrows—insignificant birds—sold for just a penny, the smallest Roman coin? Yet not one of them falls to the ground and dies without your Father’s knowledge, permission, and sovereign care.
Even the very hairs on your head have all been counted individually—God knows you intimately and completely down to the smallest detail.
Therefore, do not be afraid or anxious; you are worth far more to God than many sparrows.

verses.heading: Acknowledging Christ Before Men / Acknowledging Christ Before Men / Lk. 12:8-9
verses.text: “Therefore, everyone who publicly acknowledges Me and confesses Me before others without shame, I will also acknowledge him and confess him before My Father who is in heaven.
But whoever denies and rejects Me before others out of fear or shame, I will also deny him and reject him before My Father who is in heaven.

verses.heading: Jesus Comes to the Earth to Bring a Sword / Jesus Comes to the Earth to Bring a Sword / Lk. 12:51-53; 14:26-27
verses.text: “Do not think or assume that I came to bring peace on the earth in this present age. I did not come to bring peace and unity, but a sword—causing division and conflict over allegiance to Me.

For I came to set a man in opposition against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law when they must choose between family loyalty and loyalty to Me.
A person’s enemies and opponents will often be the members of his own household who reject the gospel.
The one who loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me and cannot be My true disciple, and the one who loves son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me and cannot follow Me fully.
And whoever refuses to take up his cross—accepting suffering, rejection, and self-denial—and follow Me in obedient discipleship is not worthy of Me and cannot be My disciple.
The one who tries to preserve his life and save it by denying Me will lose it eternally, but the one who loses his life for My sake and the gospel will find true and eternal life.

verses.heading: Rewards / Rewards
verses.text: “The one who receives you as My representatives receives Me, and the one who receives Me receives the Father who sent Me into the world.

The one who receives a prophet because he recognizes him as a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward from God, and the one who receives a righteous person because he recognizes him as righteous will receive a righteous person’s reward.

And whoever gives even just a cup of cold water to one of these little ones—the least significant of My disciples—because he is My disciple and follower, I assure you with certainty, he will certainly not lose his reward but will be recompensed by God.”
After Jesus finished giving instructions and commissioning His twelve disciples for ministry, He left that place to continue teaching and preaching in the cities throughout Galilee.

verses.heading: Concerning John the Baptist / Concerning John the Baptist / Lk. 7:18-35
verses.text: When John the Baptist heard in prison—where Herod had confined him—about the works and miracles of Christ, he sent word through his disciples
to ask Jesus this question: “Are You the Coming One—the Christ we have been expecting—or should we continue to look for someone else to fulfill that role?”
Jesus answered them, “Go back and report to John what you are hearing with your ears and seeing with your eyes as evidence:

The blind receive their sight and can see, the lame walk and are mobile, lepers are cleansed from their disease, the deaf hear sounds and voices, the dead are raised to life, and the poor and destitute have the good news of the kingdom proclaimed to them with hope.
Blessed is the person who does not stumble over Me, take offense at Me.”

As John’s disciples were leaving to return to him, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John and his ministry: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see and observe? A reed swaying back and forth in the wind—representing someone weak, vacillating, and unstable in conviction?
What then did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft, expensive clothes like a courtier? No, certainly not—those who wear fine and luxurious clothes live in kings’ palaces, not in the wilderness.
So what did you go out to see? A prophet sent by God? Yes, I tell you emphatically, and he is far more than an ordinary prophet.
This is the one about whom Scripture prophesied when it says: ‘Look, I am sending My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You and make ready Your coming.’*

I tell you the truth with solemn emphasis: Among all people ever born of women throughout history, no one has been greater in his role and calling than John the Baptist. Yet the one who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he is—because they experience the fullness of the kingdom that John only announced.
From the days when John the Baptist began his ministry until now, the kingdom of heaven has been forcefully advancing and breaking into history, and violent men are seizing it by force.
For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied and pointed forward to the coming of the Christ and His kingdom until John appeared and began his ministry.
And if you are willing to accept and receive this truth, John himself is the fulfillment of Elijah—the one who was prophesied to come before the Messiah.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear and understand this profound truth.
“But to what should I compare this present generation and their response? They are like children sitting in the marketplaces, calling out to their playmates in complaint,
saying, ‘We played wedding music for you on the flute, but you did not dance and celebrate; we sang funeral songs and dirges, but you did not mourn and lament.’
For John came living an austere and ascetic lifestyle, neither eating normal food nor drinking wine, and they say critically, ‘He has a demon and is mentally unbalanced.’

The Son of Man came eating and drinking normally like others, and they say accusingly, ‘Look at Him—He is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners who keeps bad company!’ Yet wisdom and the truth of God’s plan is vindicated and proven right by the results it produces.”

verses.heading: Pronouncement of Woes on the Unrepentant Cities / Pronouncement of Woes on the Unrepentant Cities / Lk. 10:13-15
verses.text: Then Jesus began to pronounce judgment and woe on the cities where most of His miracles and mighty works had been performed, because they refused to repent and turn from their sins:

“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in your midst had been done in the pagan cities of Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, clothing themselves in sackcloth and ashes as visible signs of genuine repentance.
Nevertheless, I tell you with certainty, it will be more bearable and less severe for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than it will be for you who had greater light and greater opportunity.

And you, Capernaum—do you think you will be exalted to heaven because of your privilege in hosting My ministry? No, you will be brought down to Hades in judgment. For if the miracles performed in you had been done in Sodom, that city would have repented and would still be standing today.

Nevertheless, I tell you that it will be more tolerable and endurable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you, because you had the greater privilege and rejected the greater revelation.”

verses.heading: Jesus Praises the Father / Jesus Praises the Father / Lk. 10:21-22
verses.text: At that time, Jesus responded to this situation by saying in prayer, “I praise You and give You thanks, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these truths about the kingdom from those who consider themselves wise and intellectually learned, and have revealed them to those who are like little children—humble, dependent, and receptive to divine truth.
Yes, Father, for this was Your gracious will and sovereign good pleasure—Your deliberate plan for how the gospel would be received.
All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one fully knows the Son except the Father, and no one fully knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to make Him known.

verses.heading: Invitation to All Who Toil / Invitation to All Who Toil
verses.text: Come to Me, all of you who are weary and exhausted and burdened down with heavy loads—whether religious obligations, guilt, or the weight of life—and I will give you rest and relief.

Take My yoke upon you and submit to My teaching and authority, and learn from Me through close relationship, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest, refreshment, and peace for your souls.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: For My yoke is easy to bear and comfortable to wear, and My burden is light and not oppressive.” 10 Quoted from Mal. 3:1

verses.heading: Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath / Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath / Mk. 2:23-28; Lk. 6:1-5
verses.text: At that time, Jesus was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath day. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat the kernels.
When the Pharisees observed this, they said to Him accusingly, “Look! Your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath according to our traditions.”
But He replied to them, "Have you not read in the Scriptures what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need of food?

He entered the house of God, and they ate the consecrated bread—the bread of the Presence that was set before the Lord—which was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests who served in the tabernacle.

Or have you not read in the Law of Moses that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple violate the Sabbath rest by performing their duties and working, yet they remain innocent and guiltless before God?
But I tell you that something greater and more significant than the temple is here in your presence!

If you had truly understood what this Scripture means when it says: ‘I desire mercy and compassion, not mere sacrifice and ritual observance,’* you would not have condemned the innocent who have done no wrong.
For the Son of Man is Lord and Master even of the Sabbath, having authority to determine its proper observance.”

verses.heading: The Healing of a Man with a Shriveled Hand / The Healing of a Man with a Shriveled Hand / Mk. 3:1-6; Lk. 6:6-11
verses.text: Moving on from that place, Jesus entered their synagogue for worship and teaching.
A man was there who had a shriveled hand that was paralyzed and useless. Looking for grounds to accuse Jesus of breaking the Sabbath, they asked Him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?”
He said to them in response, “What man among you, if he owns a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out to save it?
How much more precious is a human being than a sheep! Therefore, it is lawful and right to do good deeds and acts of mercy on the Sabbath.”
Then He said to the man with the shriveled hand, “Stretch out your hand toward Me.” He stretched it out in faith, and it was completely restored, as healthy and functional as the other one.
But the Pharisees went out and immediately plotted together against Him, conspiring how they might destroy Him.

verses.heading: Jesus is God’s Chosen Servant / Jesus is God’s Chosen Servant
verses.text: Aware of their murderous plot through divine knowledge, Jesus withdrew from that place to avoid premature confrontation. Large crowds followed Him seeking healing, and He healed all their sick without exception.
He warned them sternly and commanded them not to make Him known publicly or proclaim His identity widely,
so that what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled and brought to completion:
“Behold My Servant whom I have chosen and appointed, My Beloved in whom My soul takes great pleasure. I will put My Spirit upon Him, and He will proclaim justice to the Gentile nations.
He will not quarrel contentiously or cry out loudly, nor will anyone hear His voice shouting in the streets in self-promotion.

A bruised reed—a broken and damaged person—He will not break, and a smoldering wick—a faintly burning flame of faith—He will not snuff out and extinguish, until He brings justice to ultimate victory and fulfillment.
And in His name the Gentiles will place their hope of salvation.”*

verses.heading: Jesus and Beelzebul / Jesus and Beelzebul / Mk. 3:20-30; Lk. 11:14-23; 12:10
verses.text: Then a demon-possessed man who was both blind and mute was brought to Jesus, and He healed him completely, so that the man who had been mute could both speak and see.
All the crowds were astonished, and kept asking one another, “Could this possibly be the Son of David—the promised Messiah who would perform such signs?”

But when the Pharisees heard the crowd’s speculation, they said with hardened hearts, “This man does not cast out demons except by the power of Beelzebul, the prince of demons—He is in league with Satan.”

Knowing their thoughts by divine insight, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself through internal conflict is brought to ruin and desolation, and every city or household divided against itself cannot stand but will collapse.
If Satan casts out Satan and wars against his own forces, he is divided against himself and fighting his own kingdom. How then can his kingdom stand and maintain its power?

And if I cast out demons by the power of Beelzebul as you claim, by whose power do your own followers and exorcists cast them out? Therefore, they themselves will be your judges and will testify against your inconsistent logic.
But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God working through Me, then the kingdom of God has come upon you and invaded Satan’s domain—this is proof of God’s presence and power.
How can anyone enter a strong man’s house and plunder his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man and overpowers him? Only then can he thoroughly ransack and rob his house.
The one who is not with Me in allegiance is against Me in opposition, and the one who does not gather souls with Me scatters them away from the kingdom.

Therefore, I tell you with solemn warning: Every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people when they repent, but blasphemy against the Holy Spirit—the persistent, willful rejection of His testimony—will not be forgiven.

Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man in His humiliation will be forgiven when he repents, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit in deliberate rejection of divine truth will not be forgiven, either in this present age or in the age to come—this is an eternal sin.

verses.heading: A Tree and Its Fruit / A Tree and Its Fruit / Lk. 6:43-45
verses.text: “Either make the tree good and recognize that its fruit will be good, or make the tree bad and recognize that its fruit will be bad, for a tree is recognized by the quality of fruit it produces.

You brood of vipers and offspring of serpents! How can you who are evil by nature say anything good? For the mouth speaks from the abundance of the heart—what fills the heart comes out through the lips.
The good person from his good treasure stored within brings out good things and wholesome words, and the evil person from his evil treasure stored within brings out evil things and corrupt speech.
But I tell you that people will give an account to God on the day of judgment for every careless, worthless word they have spoken thoughtlessly.
For by your words you will be justified—declared righteous—and by your words you will be condemned.”

verses.heading: The Sign of Jonah / The Sign of Jonah / Lk. 8:11-12; Lk. 11:29-32
verses.text: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees responded to Him, saying, “Teacher, we want to see a miraculous sign from heaven to authenticate Your claims and prove Your authority.”

But He answered them sternly, “An evil and spiritually adulterous generation craves and demands a sign for their unbelief, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet and his experience.

For just as Jonah was in the belly of the great fish for three days and three nights in apparent death, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights in the tomb.

The men of Nineveh will stand up at the final judgment with this generation and condemn it for its unbelief, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching when he was merely a prophet—and look, something infinitely greater than Jonah is here in your presence!

The Queen of the South—the Queen of Sheba—will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom—and look, something infinitely greater than Solomon is here teaching you!

verses.heading: Return of an Unclean Spirit / Return of an Unclean Spirit / Lk. 11:24-26
verses.text: “When an unclean spirit comes out of a person through exorcism, it wanders through waterless, desolate places searching for rest and a new dwelling but finds none.

Then it says to itself, ‘I will return to my house—the person I came out of—and reclaim my territory.’ When it arrives, it finds the house vacant, swept clean of demonic presence, and put in order but not filled with God’s Spirit.

Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil and powerful than itself, and they enter and live there together. The final condition of that person becomes far worse than the first condition before deliverance. That is how it will be for this evil generation that rejects Me after witnessing My works.”

verses.heading: Jesus’ Mother and Brothers / Jesus’ Mother and Brothers / Mk. 3:31-35; Lk. 8:19-21
verses.text: While Jesus was still speaking these words to the crowds, His mother Mary and His brothers were standing outside the building, seeking and desiring to speak with Him.
Someone said to Him, “Look, Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak with You about some matter.”
But He replied to the one who told Him, “Who is My mother, and who are My brothers in the truest spiritual sense?”
Stretching out His hand toward His disciples in a gesture of identification, He said, “Look—here are My mother and My brothers in the family of faith!

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven with obedient faith, this person is My brother and sister and mother—a true member of My spiritual family.” 7 Quoted from Hos. 6:6 18-21 Quoted from Is. 42:1-4

verses.heading: The Parable of the Sower / The Parable of the Sower / Mk. 4:1-9; Lk. 8:4-8
verses.text: That same day, Jesus left the house where He had been teaching and went to sit by the Sea of Galilee.
Such large crowds gathered around Him and pressed in so closely that He got into a boat and sat down to teach from it, while the entire crowd stood on the shore listening.
He taught them many profound truths using parables—earthly stories with heavenly meanings—saying: “Listen carefully! A farmer went out to sow his seed in his field.
As he was scattering the seed broadly, some seeds fell along the hard-packed path where people walked, and the birds came and devoured it before it could take root.
Other seed fell on rocky ground where there was not much soil covering the bedrock. It sprang up quickly and prematurely because the soil was shallow and not deep.
But when the sun rose high and beat down, the plants were scorched by the heat, and they withered and died because they had no deep root system to draw moisture.
Other seed fell among thorns and thistles, and as both grew together, the thorns grew up and choked the plants, preventing them from producing fruit.

Still other seed fell on good, fertile soil that was deep and receptive, and it produced a crop—some yielding a hundred times what was sown, some sixty times the amount, and some thirty times what was planted.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear and understand the spiritual meaning of this parable.”

verses.heading: The Purpose of the Parables / The Purpose of the Parables / Mk. 4:10-12; Lk. 8:9-10
verses.text: The disciples came to Him privately and asked, “Why do You speak to the crowds in parables rather than speaking plainly and directly?”

He replied, “Because you who are My followers have been granted the privilege and grace to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven—truths once hidden but now revealed—but they have not been granted that privilege because of their hardened hearts.
