For whoever has spiritual understanding and receptivity, more truth will be given to him and he will have abundance of knowledge; but whoever does not have such understanding and receptivity, even what little he has will be taken away from him as an act of judgment.

This is why I speak to them in parables: Though they are seeing with their physical eyes, they do not really see spiritual truth; though they are hearing with their physical ears, they do not really hear or understand the meaning because their hearts are hardened.
In them the prophecy of Isaiah is being fulfilled: ‘You will keep on hearing but never understand the meaning, and you will keep on seeing but never perceive the truth.

For this people’s heart has become calloused, dull, and hardened, their ears barely hear and are heavy, and they have deliberately closed their eyes to the truth, so that they might not see with their eyes spiritual realities, or hear with their ears the word of God, or understand with their heart and be converted, and turn back to Me in repentance, so I could heal them and restore them.’*
But blessed and privileged are your eyes because they see spiritual truth, and your ears because they hear and receive the word with faith.

For I tell you the solemn truth: Many prophets and righteous people throughout history longed to see what you are seeing but did not see it, and to hear what you are hearing but did not hear it—you are witnessing the fulfillment of prophecy.

verses.heading: The Interpretation of the Parable of the Sower / The Interpretation of the Parable of the Sower / Mk. 4:13-20; Lk. 8:11-15
verses.text: “Therefore, listen carefully to the meaning of the parable of the sower:

When anyone hears the message about the kingdom and does not understand it or receive it with faith, the evil one—Satan—comes immediately and snatches away what was sown in his heart like birds devouring seed. This is the seed sown along the hard path—representing a hardened heart.
The seed sown on rocky ground represents the person who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy and emotional enthusiasm.

But he has no deep root in himself—no genuine conversion or depth of character—and lasts only a short time in apparent faith. When trouble or persecution comes because of identifying with the word, he quickly falls away and abandons his profession.

The seed sown among thorns represents the person who hears the word and appears to receive it, but the worries and anxieties of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth and material pursuits choke the word, making it unfruitful and preventing spiritual growth and productivity.

But the seed sown on good, receptive soil represents the person who hears the word and understands it with genuine faith. He indeed produces a crop of spiritual fruit, yielding a hundred, sixty, or thirty times what was sown—according to individual faithfulness.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Wheat and Tares / The Parable of the Wheat and Tares
verses.text: Jesus presented another parable to them for instruction: “The kingdom of heaven in this age is like a man who sowed good seed—genuine believers—in his field—the world.
But while everyone was sleeping and not vigilant, his enemy—the devil—came under cover of darkness and sowed weeds among the wheat and slipped away undetected.
When the wheat sprouted and formed heads of grain and became visible, the weeds—false professors—also appeared growing among them.
The servants came to the owner of the field and said with concern, ‘Sir, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then did these weeds come from?’
He answered with understanding, ‘An enemy has done this malicious act.’ The servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go immediately and pull up the weeds and remove them?’
‘No,’ he replied with wisdom, ‘because while you are pulling up the weeds in your limited judgment, you might uproot the wheat along with them and harm genuine believers.

Let both grow together until the harvest at the end of the age. At harvest time I will tell the reapers—the angels: First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned in judgment, then gather the wheat into my barn for eternal safety.’ ”

verses.heading: The Parables of the Mustard Seed and the Leaven / The Parables of the Mustard Seed and the Leaven / Mk. 4:30-32; Lk. 13:18-21
verses.text: He told them another parable about kingdom growth: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.

Though it is the smallest of all seeds when planted, when it grows to maturity it becomes larger than all the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches—the kingdom starts small but grows to provide shelter for many.”

He told them another parable about kingdom influence: “The kingdom of heaven is like yeast—leaven—that a woman took and mixed into about sixty pounds of flour, working it through until it permeated all through the dough and caused the whole batch to rise.”

verses.heading: The Reason for Jesus’ Parables / The Reason for Jesus’ Parables / Mk. 4:33-34
verses.text: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables, and He did not say anything to them without using a parable to veil the truth from the hardened.

This teaching method fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet who wrote: “I will open My mouth in parables and speak in figurative language; I will declare what has been kept secret since the beginning of the world, now being made known.”

verses.heading: The Interpretation of the Parable of the Wheat and Tares / The Interpretation of the Parable of the Wheat and Tares
verses.text: After Jesus dismissed the crowds and sent them away, He went into the house for privacy. His disciples came to Him and said, “Explain to us clearly the parable of the weeds in the field—we want to understand its meaning.”
He answered, “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man—I Myself sowing the gospel.

The field is the world—the entire human sphere. The good seed represents the sons of the kingdom—true believers who belong to God, while the weeds represent the sons of the evil one—false professors and unbelievers who belong to Satan.
The enemy who sowed them is the devil working to corrupt the visible church. The harvest is the end of the age—the final judgment, and the harvesters are angels who serve as God’s agents of judgment.
Just as the weeds are pulled up and gathered and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of this age in final judgment.
The Son of Man will send out His angels, and they will gather from His kingdom everything that causes sin and stumbling and all who practice lawlessness and rebellion.
They will throw them into the fiery furnace of hell, where there will be weeping in sorrow and gnashing of teeth in anguish for all eternity.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in brilliant glory in the kingdom of their Father, freed from all mixture with evil. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear and take warning.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Hidden Treasure / The Parable of the Hidden Treasure
verses.text: “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field—of immeasurable value. When a man discovered it, he hid it again to secure it. Then in his joy at finding such wealth, he went and sold everything he owned and bought that field to possess the treasure—the kingdom is worth any sacrifice.

verses.heading: The Parable of a Very Precious Pearl / The Parable of a Very Precious Pearl
verses.text: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant traveling and searching for fine, valuable pearls.
When he found one pearl of extremely great value—surpassing all others, he went away and sold everything he had and bought it.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Dragnet / The Parable of the Dragnet
verses.text: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a large dragnet that was cast into the sea and caught all kinds of fish without discrimination.

When it was full and heavy with the catch, the fishermen pulled it ashore onto the beach. They sat down and sorted the catch, gathering the good, edible fish into containers but throwing the bad, inedible ones away.
This is how it will be at the end of the age in final judgment. The angels will come forth and separate the wicked from among the righteous who are mixed together,
and throw the wicked into the fiery furnace of eternal punishment, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth in endless agony.

verses.heading: New and Old Things / New and Old Things
verses.text: “Have you understood all these truths and parables that I have taught you?” They answered Him, “Yes, Lord, we have understood.”

He said to them, “Therefore every scribe—every teacher of Scripture—who has been trained and discipled for the kingdom of heaven is like the head of a household who brings out of his treasure both new things and old treasures.

verses.heading: Jesus Rejected in His Hometown / Jesus Rejected in His Hometown / Mk. 6:1-6; Lk. 4:16-30
verses.text: When Jesus had finished teaching these parables to the crowds, He departed from that place by the sea.

Coming to His hometown of Nazareth where He had been raised, He began teaching in their synagogue on the Sabbath, and they were astonished, saying with unbelief, “Where did this man get this wisdom and profound teaching and these miraculous powers?
Is not this merely the carpenter’s son—a common workman? Is not His mother called Mary, and His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas whom we all know?
Are not all His sisters here among us in this town? Where then did this man get all these things—His authority and power?”
And they took offense at Him and rejected Him, stumbling over His familiar origins. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown where familiarity breeds contempt.”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: He did not perform many miracles there because of their unbelief and hardness of heart. 14-15 Quoted from Is. 6:9-10

verses.heading: The Death of John the Baptist / The Death of John the Baptist / Mk. 6:14-29; Lk. 9:7-9
verses.text: At that time, Herod the tetrarch—the ruler of Galilee—heard the reports and growing reputation about Jesus and His mighty works,

and he said to his servants with superstitious fear, “This must be John the Baptist whom I beheaded! He has been raised from the dead and has come back to haunt me, and that is why these miraculous powers are at work in him.”
For Herod had arrested John, bound him with chains, and put him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife whom Herod had unlawfully taken,
because John had been telling him repeatedly with bold courage, “It is not lawful according to God’s Law for you to have her as your wife—you are living in adultery.”
Although Herod wanted to kill John to silence him, he was afraid of the crowd and public opinion because they regarded John as a genuine prophet of God.
But when Herod’s birthday celebration came, Herodias’ daughter danced before Herod and his guests with sensual movements and pleased Herod greatly.
So he promised rashly under oath to give her whatever she asked for, making an open commitment before his guests.
Prompted and coached by her mother Herodias, she said with evil intent, “Give me here immediately on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”
The king was deeply troubled by this request, but because of his oaths sworn publicly and his desire to save face before his dinner guests, he commanded that it be given to her.
He sent orders to the prison and had John beheaded there.
John’s head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she carried it to her mother as a trophy of revenge.
Then John’s disciples came sorrowfully, took the body, and buried it with respect. Then they went and told Jesus about what had happened.

verses.heading: The Feeding of the Five Thousand / The Feeding of the Five Thousand / Mk. 6:30-44; Lk. 9:10-17; Jn. 6:1-14
verses.text: When Jesus heard the news of John’s martyrdom, He withdrew from there by boat to a deserted place to be alone and grieve. But when the crowds heard about His location, they followed Him on foot from the surrounding towns.
When Jesus came ashore and saw the large crowd waiting for Him, He had compassion on them—He was moved with deep pity for their needs—and He healed their sick without reservation.

As evening approached and the day grew late, the disciples came to Him and said practically, “This is a remote place and it is already getting late. Send the crowds away so they can go to the surrounding villages and buy food for themselves.”
But Jesus told them, testing their faith, “They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat from your own resources.”
They answered with dismay, “We have nothing here except five loaves of bread and two fish—wholly inadequate for such a crowd.”
Jesus said with calm confidence, “Bring them here to Me.”

He directed the crowds to sit down on the grass in an orderly manner in a relaxed manner. Taking the five loaves and two fish in His hands and looking up to heaven in dependence on the Father, He gave thanks and blessed the food. After breaking the loaves into pieces, He gave them to the disciples, and the disciples distributed them to the crowds continuously.
They all ate and were completely satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve full baskets of leftover broken pieces—more than they started with, demonstrating abundance.
Those who ate numbered about five thousand men, not counting women and children.

verses.heading: Jesus Walks on the Water / Jesus Walks on the Water / Mk. 6:45-52; Jn. 6:15-21
verses.text: Immediately after this miracle, Jesus made the disciples get into the boat under compulsion and go ahead of Him to the other side of the sea, while He dismissed the crowds.
After sending the crowds away, He went up on the mountain by Himself to pray in solitude and communion with the Father. When evening came, He was there alone.

Meanwhile, the boat was already a considerable distance from the shore—several miles out, being battered and tossed by the waves because the wind was against them, blowing contrary to their direction.
During the fourth watch of the night—between three and six o’clock in the morning, in the darkest hours—Jesus came to them, walking on the surface of the sea in defiance of natural law.
When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea in the dim light, they were terrified and filled with fear, and cried out, “It is a ghost—an apparition!” And they screamed in panic.
But immediately Jesus spoke to them to calm their fear: “Take courage and be confident! It is I—do not be afraid of Me.”
Peter answered Him impulsively, “Lord, if it is really You and not a spirit, command me to come to You on the water.”
Jesus said, “Come.” So Peter got out of the boat in faith, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus successfully.
But when he saw the strength of the wind and the threatening waves, he became afraid and took his eyes off Jesus. As he began to sink into the water, he cried out desperately, “Lord, save me!”
Immediately Jesus reached out His hand, caught him and rescued him, and said to him, “O you of little faith, why did you doubt when you were doing well?”
When they climbed into the boat together, the wind died down immediately and there was calm.
Then those who were in the boat worshipped Him with reverence and awe, declaring with conviction, “Truly You are the Son of God—divine in nature and power!”

verses.heading: Healings at Gennesaret / Healings at Gennesaret / Mk. 6:53-56
verses.text: After crossing over the sea, they came to land at Gennesaret on the western shore.
When the men of that place recognized Jesus and knew who He was, they sent word throughout the surrounding region and brought to Him all who were sick with various diseases.
They begged Him earnestly to let them just touch the fringe of His garment, believing that even indirect contact would heal them, and all who touched it in faith were completely healed and restored.

verses.heading: The Tradition of the Elders / The Tradition of the Elders / Mk. 7:1-23
verses.text: Then Pharisees and scribes—religious leaders and experts in the Law—came to Jesus from Jerusalem with hostile intent, saying,
“Why do Your disciples violate and break the tradition of the elders that has been handed down? For they do not perform the ceremonial washing of their hands when they eat bread.”
But, in response, He said to them, turning their accusation back on them, “Why do you also violate and transgress the commandment of God because of your human tradition?
For God said clearly in the Law, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’* and ‘The one who speaks evil of father or mother must be put to death.’*

But you say in your tradition, ‘Whoever says to his father or his mother, “Whatever help or financial support you would have received from me is a gift consecrated to God—given to the temple instead,”
need not honor his father or provide for his parents.’ So you have invalidated the word of God for the sake of preserving your human tradition.
You hypocrites! Isaiah rightly prophesied concerning you and your spiritual ancestors, saying,
‘This people honors Me with their lips in outward profession, but their hearts are distant and kept far away from Me in true devotion;
and they worship Me to no purpose and in vain, teaching as authoritative doctrines the precepts and commandments of men rather than God's truth.’ ”
And calling the crowd to Himself to hear this important teaching, He said to them, “Hear this truth and understand its meaning:

It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles the man and makes him unclean before God, but what comes out of the mouth from the heart—this defiles the man and reveals his true spiritual condition.”
Then the disciples came and said to Him with concern, “Do You know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this saying that challenged their traditions?”
And in response, He said, “Every plant—every religious system and false teaching—that My heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted and destroyed in judgment.

Leave them alone and do not worry about their opposition. They are blind guides leading the blind in spiritual darkness. And if the blind lead the blind, both will fall into a ditch of judgment and destruction.”
And in response, Peter said to Him, “Explain this parable to us so we can understand its full meaning.”
But He said with some disappointment, “Are you also still without understanding at this point in time after all My teaching?
Do you not understand that whatever goes into the mouth proceeds to the stomach and is expelled into the latrine and has no spiritual significance?
But the things which proceed from the mouth come from the heart—the center of one’s being—and these defile the man and reveal his true character.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts that lead to action, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities of every kind, thefts, untrue testimonies and lies, slanders and malicious speech.
These are the things which defile the man and make him unclean before God. But to eat with ceremonially unwashed hands does not defile the man spiritually.”

verses.heading: The Faith of the Canaanite Woman / The Faith of the Canaanite Woman / Mk. 7:24-30
verses.text: And departing from that place, Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon—Gentile territory outside Israel.

And behold, a Canaanite woman from that region—a Gentile by birth—came out and began to cry out persistently, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is miserably demon-possessed and tormented.”

But He did not answer her a word, ignoring her initially to test her faith. And His disciples came to Him and were begging Him, saying, “Dismiss her, because she is crying out after us and making a disturbance.”
But in response, He said, explaining His mission, “I was not sent except to the sheep who have been lost from the house of Israel—My primary mission is to the Jewish people.”
But she came and knelt in reverence before Him with desperate faith, saying simply, “Lord, help me.”
And in response, He said, testing her further, “It is not right to take the children’s bread—the blessings intended for Israel—and throw it to the dogs—the Gentiles.”
And she said with humble persistence and faith, “Yes, Lord, that is true, for even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table—even Gentiles can receive the overflow of Your mercy.”

Then, in response, Jesus said to her with commendation, “O woman, great is your faith and perseverance. Let it be done for you as you desire and request.” And her daughter was healed and delivered from that very hour.

verses.heading: Jesus Heals Many People / Jesus Heals Many People
verses.text: And departing from that place, Jesus went along the Sea of Galilee, and He went up on the mountain and was sitting there to teach and minister.

And large crowds came to Him, bringing with them the lame, blind, crippled, mute, and many others with various afflictions. And they put them down at His feet in faith, and He healed them all without exception,

so that the crowd wondered and marveled, when they saw the mute speaking clearly, the crippled made well and whole, and the lame walking, and the blind seeing with restored sight. Therefore, they glorified the God of Israel for His mighty works.

verses.heading: The Feeding of the Four Thousand / The Feeding of the Four Thousand / Mk. 8:1-10
verses.text: And Jesus called His disciples to Himself, and said with compassion, “I have compassion on the crowd and feel deeply for them, because they have already remained with Me three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away hungry and weak, lest they faint on the way home.”
And the disciples said to Him, “Where in this deserted place far from any town can we get so much bread to satisfy such a great crowd?”
And Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have in your possession?” And they answered, “Seven loaves, and a few small fish.”
And when He had commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground in a relaxed posture in preparation for a meal,
He took the seven loaves and the fish, and after giving thanks to the Father, He broke them and began to give them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds continuously.
And they all ate and were satisfied and filled, and they picked up what was left over from the broken pieces, seven large baskets full—more than they started with.
Now those who ate were four thousand men, apart from women and children—the total was likely over twelve thousand people.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And having dismissed the crowds, He entered the boat and went to the region of Magadan on the western shore. 4 Quoted from Ex. 20:12 4 Quoted from Ex. 21:17

verses.heading: The Demand for a Sign / The Demand for a Sign / Mk. 8:11-13; Lk. 12:54-56
verses.text: Now the Pharisees and Sadducees—religious enemies who rarely agreed—came together, and testing Him with hostile intent, they asked Him to show them a sign from heaven to authenticate His claims.
And in response, He said to them, “When evening comes, you say with confidence, ‘It will be fair weather tomorrow, given that the sky is red at sunset.’

And in the morning, you say, ‘Today there will be a storm, given that the sky is red and overcast.’ You know how to discern and interpret the appearance of the sky and predict the weather, but you are not able to discern the signs of the times and recognize the Messiah in your midst.
An evil and spiritually adulterous generation demands a sign for their unbelief, but no sign will be granted to it except the sign of Jonah.” So He left them abruptly and went away.

verses.heading: The Leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees / The Leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees / Mk. 8:14-21
verses.text: And when the disciples came to the other side of the sea, they had forgotten to take bread with them.
And Jesus said to them, “Watch out, and beware of the leaven—the corrupting influence—of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
So they began to reason this among themselves, saying, “It is because we did not take bread—He is concerned about our lack of provisions.”
But Jesus, aware of this misunderstanding by divine insight, said, “Why are you reasoning among yourselves about the fact that you had no bread, O you of little faith?
Do you not yet understand spiritual truth or do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you collected afterward?
Or do you not remember the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you collected then?
How do you not understand that I was not speaking to you about physical bread? But beware of the leaven—the teaching and influence—of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Then they understood that He did not tell them to beware of the leaven of literal bread, but of the corrupting teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

verses.heading: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the Living God / Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the Living God / Mk. 8:27-30; Lk 9:18-21
verses.text: Now when Jesus came to the district of Caesarea Philippi—far from Jerusalem, He began to ask His disciples, saying, “Who do men—people in general—say that the Son of Man is?”
And they said, reporting various opinions, “Some say John the Baptist risen from the dead; and others Elijah returned; and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets come back.”
He said to them, pressing for their personal conviction, “But you, who do you say I am?”
And in response, Simon Peter said with conviction inspired by the Father, “You are the Christ—the Messiah—the Son of the living God.”
Jesus then responded and said to him with blessing, “Blessed and favored are you, Simon son of Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this truth to you, but My Father who is in heaven.

And I also say to you that you are Peter—which means rock—and on this rock of confession about who I am I will build My church—My called-out assembly, and the gates of Hades—the powers of death and hell—will not triumph over it.

I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven—the authority to open the gospel to all, and whatever you bind on earth in accordance with heaven’s will shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
Then He issued strict instructions to the disciples that they should tell no one at this time that He was the Christ—the Messiah—because the timing was not yet right.

verses.heading: Jesus Speaks of His Death and Resurrection / Jesus Speaks of His Death and Resurrection / Mk. 8:31-9:1; Lk. 9:22-27
verses.text: From that time forward, Jesus began to show His disciples plainly that it was necessary and divinely appointed for Him to go to Jerusalem and to suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and to be killed, and on the third day to be raised from the dead.
And Peter, taking Him aside privately, began to reprimand Him, saying, “Far be it from You, Lord! This will never happen to You.”

But He turned and said to Peter sternly, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are an obstruction to Me, because you are not setting your thoughts on the matters and purposes of God, but on the matters of men and human reasoning.”

Then Jesus said to His disciples, “If anyone desires to come after Me as a disciple, he must deny himself and his own interests and take up his cross—accepting suffering—and follow Me in obedient discipleship.
For whoever desires to save his life and preserve it by avoiding the cross will lose it eternally, but whoever loses his life for the sake of Me and the gospel will find it and gain eternal life.

For what will it benefit a man if he gains the whole world and all its wealth and pleasures, yet forfeits his soul and loses eternal life? Or what will a man offer as an exchange for his soul—what could possibly be worth more?
For the Son of Man is going to come in the glory of His Father with His angels in power, and then He will give to each one according to his deeds—rewarding or judging each person.
Truly, I say to you with solemn certainty, that there are some of those standing here who will never have a taste of death until they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom in power.”

verses.heading: The Transfiguration / The Transfiguration / Mk. 9:2-13; Lk. 9:28-36
verses.text: And after six days had passed, Jesus took along Peter and James and John his brother—His inner circle, and led them up a high mountain by themselves in isolation.
And He was transfigured before them, and His face shone like the sun in brilliant radiance, and His clothes became as white as the light itself.
And behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elijah, talking with Him about His coming death.

And in response, Peter said to Jesus impulsively, “Lord, it is fitting that we are here to witness this. If You desire, I will make here three tents—temporary shelters, one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

While he was still speaking these words, behold, a bright cloud of glory overshadowed them, and behold, a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, the Beloved One, with whom I am well pleased; listen to Him and obey His teaching!”
And when the disciples heard this divine voice, they fell down on their faces in terror and were greatly afraid.
And Jesus approached them and touched them, and said with comfort, “Rise, and do not be afraid.”
And when they raised their eyes and looked around, they saw no one but Jesus Himself alone—Moses and Elijah had departed.

And as they were descending from the mountain, Jesus commanded them strictly, saying, “Tell no one the vision of what you have seen until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead—then you may testify.”
And the disciples inquired of Him, saying, “Why then do the scribes assert and teach that Elijah must come first before the Messiah appears?”
And in response, He said, “Elijah indeed does come first, and he will restore all things and prepare the way.

But I say to you that Elijah has already come in the person of John the Baptist, and they did not recognize him or receive his message, but did to him whatever they wished and killed him. So also the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands in the same way.”
Then the disciples understood that He had spoken to them concerning John the Baptist as the fulfillment of the Elijah prophecy.

verses.heading: The Healing of a Demon-Possessed Boy / The Healing of a Demon-Possessed Boy / Mk. 9:14-29; Lk. 9:37-43a
verses.text: And when they came to the crowd at the base of the mountain, a man came to Him, kneeling before Him in desperation

and saying, “Lord, have mercy on my son, because he has seizures caused by demonic possession and suffers miserably, for often he falls into the fire and often into the water and is in danger of death.
And I brought him to Your disciples while You were on the mountain, but they could not heal him or cast out the demon.”

And in response, Jesus said with disappointment, “O unbelieving and perverse generation that lacks faith, how long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you and your unbelief? Bring him here to Me.”
And Jesus rebuked the demon with authority, and it came out of him immediately, and the boy was healed and restored from that very hour.
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, “Why were we not able to cast it out when we tried?”

And He said to them, “It is on account of your little faith and lack of trust. For truly, I say to you, if you have faith like a mustard seed—small but genuine—you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move in obedience, and nothing will be impossible for you when acting in God’s will.”*
Now when they gathered together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be betrayed and delivered into the hands of men,
and they will kill Him by crucifixion, and on the third day He will be raised from the dead.” And they were greatly sad and troubled by this news.

verses.heading: Miraculous Payment of the Temple Tax / Miraculous Payment of the Temple Tax
verses.text: Now when they arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma temple tax—the annual temple tribute—came to Peter and said, “Does your teacher not pay the two-drachma temple tax required of every Jewish male?”

He said, “Yes, He does pay it.” And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first before Peter could say anything, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect tolls or poll-tax, from their own sons who are royalty, or from foreigners and subjects?”
And when he said, “From foreigners and subjects,” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are exempt from such obligation—and as the Son of God, I am exempt from the temple tax.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: But so that we do not offend them or cause unnecessary stumbling, go to the sea, cast in a hook and fish, and take the first fish that comes up. And when you open its mouth, you will find a shekel—a four-drachma coin. Take that and give it to them for Me and you as payment for both of us.” 20 By interpolating the content of Mark 9:29, certain manuscripts create a verse 21 that states: “ This kind is able to come out by nothing except by prayer.”
verses.html:
But so that we do not offend them or cause unnecessary stumbling, go to the sea, cast in a hook and fish, and take the first fish that comes up. And when you open its mouth, you will find a shekel—a four-drachma coin. Take that and give it to them for Me and you as payment for both of us.”
20 By interpolating the content of Mark 9:29, certain manuscripts create a verse 21 that states: “ This kind is able to come out by nothing except by prayer.”

verses.heading: Who is the Greatest? / Who is the Greatest? / Mk. 9:33-37; Lk. 9:46-48
verses.text: At that time, the disciples approached Jesus, saying with competitive hearts, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
And summoning a child to Himself, He made him stand in the midst of them as an object lesson

and said, “Truly, I say to you with solemn emphasis: Unless you are converted and have a change of heart and become like children in humility and dependence, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven at all.
Therefore, whoever humbles himself and makes himself lowly like this child, he is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever accepts and welcomes one such child in My name and for My sake accepts Me.

But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to sin or stumble in their faith, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be plunged into the depths of the sea and drowned.

verses.heading: Causes of Sin / Causes of Sin / Mk. 9:42-48; Lk. 17:1-2
verses.text: Woe to the world on account of the causes of sin and stumbling, for it is unavoidable that causes of sin will come in a fallen world; nevertheless, woe to the man through whom the cause of sin comes.

And if your hand or your foot causes you to sin and stumble, cut it off and cast it away from you. It is better for you to enter eternal life crippled or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be cast into the eternal fire of hell.
And if your eye causes you to sin, tear it out and cast it away from you. It is better for you to enter life one-eyed than to have two eyes and be cast into the hell of fire.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Lost Sheep / The Parable of the Lost Sheep / Lk. 15:3-7
verses.text: “See to it that you do not despise one of these little ones who believe in Me, for I say to you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father who is in heaven and have access to Him.*
What do you think? If any man possesses a hundred sheep, and one of them wanders away, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills temporarily and go and seek the one which strayed?
And if he finds it after searching, truly, I say to you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which did not stray but remained safe.
So it is not the will or desire of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

verses.heading: A Brother Who Sins / A Brother Who Sins / Lk 17.3
verses.text: “Now if your brother sins against you and wrongs you, go and rebuke him between you and him alone. If he listens to you and repents, you have gained your brother and restored the relationship.
But if he does not listen to you, take with you in addition one or two others as witnesses, so that by the testimony of two or three witnesses every matter may be validated and established.

And if he fails to listen to them and remains unrepentant, tell it to the church for corporate discipline. But if he fails to listen even to the church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector.
“Truly, I say to you, whatever you bind on earth in accordance with God’s will shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
Truly, I tell you again: If two of you on earth come into agreement concerning any matter for which they ask, it will be done for them by My Father who is in heaven.
For where two or three are gathered together in My name, there I am present among them.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Unforgiving Slave / The Parable of the Unforgiving Slave
verses.text: Then Peter approached Him and said, “Lord, how many times will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?”
Jesus said to him, “I do not say to you, up to seven times, but rather up to seventy times seven—limitless forgiveness.
“For this reason, the kingdom of heaven is like a man—a king—who wanted to settle accounts with his servants and determine what was owed.
And when he began to settle the accounts, one was brought to him who had a debt of ten thousand talents—an impossible amount to repay.
And since he lacked the means to repay such an enormous debt, the master ordered him to be sold as a slave, as well as his wife and his children and all that he had, to effect partial repayment.
Then the servant fell prostrate and began to pay homage to him, saying with desperation, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’
And the master of that servant, moved by compassion for his plight, released him from the debt and forgave him the entire debt graciously.

But when that very servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii—a small amount, about three months' wages, and taking hold of him, he began to choke him violently, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe immediately.’
Therefore, his fellow servant fell to the ground and began to beg him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you.’
But he was not willing to show mercy. Instead, he went and threw him into prison until he would repay that which was owed.
So when his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were very sad and troubled, and went and explained fully to their master all that had taken place.
Then his master summoned him and said to him with anger, ‘Wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me and pleaded for mercy.
Ought you not to have shown compassion to your fellow servant, even as I showed compassion to you and forgave your enormous debt?’
And in anger, his master handed him over to the jailers to torture him until he should repay all that was owed—which was impossible.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: So also My heavenly Father will do to you and judge you, unless you each forgive your brother from your hearts with genuine forgiveness.” 10 Some ancient manuscripts interpolate Luke 19:10 at the end of this verse, thereby creating a new verse 11: “ For the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost.”
verses.html:
So also My heavenly Father will do to you and judge you, unless you each forgive your brother from your hearts with genuine forgiveness.”
10 Some ancient manuscripts interpolate Luke 19:10 at the end of this verse, thereby creating a new verse 11: “ For the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost.”

verses.heading: Concerning Divorce / Concerning Divorce / Mk. 10:1-12
verses.text: Now it occurred that, when Jesus had finished these sayings about forgiveness, He withdrew from Galilee and came to the region of Judea on the other side of the Jordan River.
And large crowds followed Him, and He healed them in that place.
And Pharisees came to Him, testing Him with a controversial question and asking whether it was lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause whatsoever—even trivial reasons.
And in response, He said, “Have you not read in the Scripture that the One who created them from the beginning made them male and female in His design,
and said, ‘For this reason, a man will leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife in covenant, and the two will become one flesh in marriage union’?*
So, they are no longer two separate individuals, but one flesh united by God. Therefore, what God has united together in marriage, let no man separate through divorce.”
They said to Him, pressing the issue, “Why then did Moses command to give a certificate of divorce and to send her away if divorce is wrong?”

He said to them, “Moses, in light of the hardness of your hearts and your sinful condition, allowed you to divorce your wives as a concession, but at the beginning in God’s original design it was not so.
But I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except on the grounds of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery because the covenant still stands.”
The disciples said to Him, troubled by this strict teaching, “If this is the case of a man with his wife—if divorce is nearly impossible, it is better not to marry at all.”
But He said to them, “Not everyone is able to accept this saying about celibacy, but only those to whom it has been given as a gift from God.

For there are eunuchs who have been so from their mother’s womb by birth, and there are eunuchs who have been made eunuchs by men through castration, and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs—who have chosen celibacy—for the sake of the kingdom of heaven and undistracted service. The one who is able to accept this calling to celibacy, let him accept it.”

verses.heading: Little Children Brought to Jesus / Little Children Brought to Jesus / Mk. 10:13-16; Lk. 18:15-17
verses.text: Then children were brought to Him by their parents, so that He might lay His hands on them and pray for them and bless them, but the disciples rebuked them thinking the children were a distraction.
But Jesus said, “Allow the children to come, and do not prevent them from coming to Me, for it is to such as these—the humble and dependent—the kingdom of heaven belongs.”
And He laid His hands on them in blessing and departed from that place.

verses.heading: The Rich Young Man / The Rich Young Man / Mk. 10:17-31; Lk. 18:18-30
verses.text: And behold, someone came to Him and said, “Teacher, what good thing shall I do in order that I may have eternal life and earn salvation?”
And He said to him, “For what reason do you ask Me about what is good? There is only One who is good—God Himself. But if you desire to enter life, keep the commandments of God perfectly.”
He said to Him, “Which ones must I keep?” And Jesus said, “You shall not murder; You shall not commit adultery; You shall not steal; You shall not bear false witness.*
Honor your father and your mother, and, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”*
The young man said to Him with confidence, “All these requirements I have kept from my youth. What do I still lack to have eternal life?”

Jesus said to him, exposing his heart, “If you desire to be perfect, go, sell what you possess and give the proceeds to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then, come, follow Me as a disciple.”
But when the young man heard the statement, he went away grieving, for he was one who had many possessions and great wealth that he loved more than God.
And Jesus said to His disciples, “Truly, I say to you that with great difficulty a rich person will enter the kingdom of heaven!
And I say to you once more, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person who trusts in wealth to enter the kingdom of God.”
So when the disciples heard this, they were exceedingly struck with amazement, saying, “Who then can be saved if even the wealthy cannot?”
But Jesus looked at them and said to them, “With men this is impossible through human effort, but with God all things are possible—including the salvation of the rich.”
Then, in response, Peter said to Him, “See, we have left everything and followed You in obedience. What then will there be for us as a reward?”

And Jesus said to them, “Truly, I say to you that in the regeneration—in the new age—when all things are made new, when the Son of Man sits on His throne of glory, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

And everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields, for the sake of My name will receive a hundredfold return and will inherit eternal life.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: On the contrary, many who are first in this age will be last in the kingdom, and the last will be first.” 5 Quoted from Gen. 2:24 18 Quoted from Ex. 20:12-16; Deut. 5:16-20 19 Quoted from Lev. 19:18

verses.heading: The Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard / The Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard
verses.text: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a man, the master of a house—a landowner, who went out early in the morning at dawn to engage workers for his vineyard.
And after reaching an agreement with the workers for a denarius per day—a normal day’s wage, he sent them into his vineyard to work.
And going out about the third hour—nine o’clock in the morning, he saw others standing aimlessly in the marketplace without employment.
And to them he said, ‘You too, go into the vineyard and work, and I will render to you whatever is equitable.’
So they departed to work. When he went out once more about the sixth hour—noon—and the ninth hour—three o’clock, he acted in the same way and hired more workers.

And about the eleventh hour—five o’clock, just one hour before quitting time, having gone out and found others standing around, he said to them, ‘Why have you been standing here the whole day aimlessly without work?’
They said to him, ‘Because no one has engaged us or hired us.’ He said to them, ‘You too, go into the vineyard and work.’
And when evening came at six o’clock, the master of the vineyard said to his domestic manager, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last hired unto the first hired.’
And when the ones who were engaged about the eleventh hour came forward, they each received a denarius—a full day’s wage.
And when the first workers hired came, they thought that they would receive more than the agreed amount, but they also each received a denarius—exactly what was promised.
And when they received it, they began to grumble against the master of the house in complaint.
saying, ‘These last people worked for only one hour and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the oppressive heat for twelve hours.’
But in response, he said to one of them, ‘Friend, I am not acting unjustly toward you. Did you not reach an agreement with me for a denarius?
Take what is yours according to our agreement and go. But I choose to give to this last person just as I give to you—this is my generous choice.
Is it not allowed for me to do what I choose with what is mine—my own money? Or is your eye evil with envy because I am good and generous?’
So the last will be first and the first last in the kingdom.”

verses.heading: Jesus Speaks of His Death a Third Time / Jesus Speaks of His Death a Third Time / Mk. 10:32-34; Lk. 18:31-34
verses.text: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem for the final time, He took the twelve disciples aside privately and said to them on the road,
“Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will sentence Him to death,
and will hand Him over to the Gentiles to mock Him, and to flog Him brutally, and to crucify Him; and on the third day, He will be raised from the dead.”

verses.heading: A Request for Preferment / A Request for Preferment / Mk. 10:35-45
verses.text: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached Him with her sons James and John and, kneeling in reverence, she requested something from Him.

And He said to her, “What do you desire and wish from Me?” She said to Him, “Say and grant that these two sons of mine may sit, one at Your right hand and one at Your left—the positions of highest honor—in Your kingdom.”
But in response, Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking for. Are you able to drink the cup of suffering that I am about to drink?” They said to Him naively, “We are able.”

He stated to them, “You will indeed drink My cup of suffering and martyrdom, but to sit at My right hand and at My left is not Mine to give as I choose, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by My Father according to His sovereign plan.”
And having heard this request, the ten other disciples were greatly indignant with the two brothers for their ambition and self-seeking.
But Jesus called them to Himself and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
It shall not be in this way among you in the kingdom. But whoever desires to become great among you must be your servant and minister to others,
and whoever desires to be first among you must be your slave—the lowest position, willing to serve all.
just as the Son of Man did not come to be served by others, but to serve sacrificially, and to offer His life a ransom for many—a payment to redeem sinners from bondage.”

verses.heading: Jesus Heals the Two Blind Men / Jesus Heals the Two Blind Men / Mk. 10:46-52; Lk. 18:35-43
verses.text: And as they were departing from Jericho on their way to Jerusalem, a large crowd followed Him.

And behold, there were two blind men sitting beside the road begging. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out loudly, saying, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!”—acknowledging Him as the Christ.
And the crowd rebuked them so that they would be quiet and not disturb Jesus. But they cried out all the more persistently, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
And when He stopped walking, Jesus called them to Him, and said, “What do you desire that I should do for you?”
They said to Him, “Lord, grant that our eyes may be opened so we can see.”

And, moved by compassion for their plight, Jesus touched their eyes with healing power, and immediately they regained their sight and were restored. And they followed Him as disciples, glorifying God.

verses.heading: The Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem / The Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem / Mk. 11:1-11; Lk. 19:28-38; Jn. 12:12-19
verses.text: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples ahead,
saying to them, “Go into the village before you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt—a young donkey—with her. Untie them and bring them to Me.
And if anyone says anything to you or questions you, you will say, ‘The Lord has need of them,’ and he will send them immediately without hesitation.”
Now this happened in order to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Zechariah, saying,
“Say to the daughter of Zion—the people of Jerusalem, ‘Behold, your King comes to you in humility, humble and mounted upon a donkey, and upon a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.’ ”*
So the disciples went and did just as Jesus had ordered them,
and brought the donkey and the colt, and laid their cloaks on them as a saddle; and He sat on them.
And a very large crowd spread their cloaks upon the road as a carpet of honor, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them upon the road in royal homage.

And the crowds who went before Him and those following were shouting, saying, “Hosanna—save us now—to the Son of David! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heaven!”
And when He entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up and in commotion, saying, “Who is this man causing such a stir?”
And the crowds were saying, “This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”

verses.heading: The Cleansing of the Temple / The Cleansing of the Temple / Mk. 11:15-19; Lk. 19:45-48; Jn. 2:13-22
verses.text: And Jesus entered the temple courts and expelled all those selling animals and buying in the temple, and He overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves for sacrifice.
And He said to them with righteous anger, “It is written in Scripture: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a hideout for robbers and a place of commercial exploitation!”
Then the blind and the lame came to Him in the temple courts and He healed them with compassion.

But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wondrous things which He performed, and the children shouting in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” they were greatly displeased and indignant.

And they said to Him, “Do You hear what these children are saying?” So Jesus said to them, “Yes; have you never read in the Scriptures, ‘From the mouth of infants and nursing babies You have prepared praise’?”*
And having left them without further explanation, He went out of the city to Bethany and spent the night there with friends.

verses.heading: The Cursing of the Fig Tree / The Cursing of the Fig Tree / Mk. 11:12-14, 20-24
verses.text: Now in the morning, as He was returning to the city, He became hungry.

And seeing a lone fig tree by the road, He went to it and found nothing on it except leaves alone—no fruit despite the appearance of fruitfulness. He then said to it, “May there be no more fruit from you for eternity.” And the fig tree withered immediately.
And when they saw it, the disciples marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly and completely?”

And in response, Jesus said to them, “Truly, I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be removed and thrown into the sea,’ it will take place.
And whatever you request in prayer, if you believe with genuine faith, you will receive.”

verses.heading: The Questioning of the Authority of Jesus / The Questioning of the Authority of Jesus / Mk. 11:27-33; Lk 20:1-8
verses.text: And when He had come into the temple to teach, the chief priests and the elders of the people approached Him while He was teaching, saying, “By what authority are You doing these things—cleansing the temple and teaching, and who gave You this authority?”
And in response, Jesus said to them, “I also will ask you one question, which, if you tell me the answer, then I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

From where did the baptism of John originate—from heaven as a divine commission or from men as merely human invention?” And they began to reason among themselves, saying, “If we say ‘From heaven,’ He will say to us, ‘Then why did you not believe him and his message?’
But if we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the crowd, for they all regard John as a prophet.”
And in response, they said to Jesus, “We do not know the answer.” Then He said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Two Sons / The Parable of the Two Sons
verses.text: “Now, what do you think? A man had two sons. And he came to the first and said, ‘Son, go and work in the vineyard today.’
And in response, he said, ‘I will not go,’ but afterward he repented and changed his mind and went.
And he came to the second and said the same. And in response, he said, ‘I will go, sir,’ but he did not go.

Which of the two did the will of his father?” They said, “The first who obeyed despite his initial refusal.” Jesus said to them, “Truly, I say to you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes go before you into the kingdom of God!

For John came to you in the way of righteousness preaching repentance, and you did not believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. And when you saw it, you did not even repent afterward and change your minds, and believe in him.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Vineyard and the Tenants / The Parable of the Vineyard and the Tenants / Mk. 12:1-12; Lk. 20:9-19
verses.text: “Hear another parable: There was a man, the master of a house—a landowner, who planted a vineyard, and placed a fence around it for protection, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower for security. Then he leased it to farmers and embarked on a journey.
And when the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the farmers to collect his fruits—his rightful share.
And the farmers took hold of his servants, one of whom they scourged and beat, and one of whom they killed, and one of whom they stoned.
Again, he sent other servants, more than the first ones, and they did likewise to them—rejecting and abusing them.
At last, he sent his son to them, saying, ‘They will have respect for my son and honor him.’
But seeing the son, the farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and appropriate his inheritance for ourselves.’
So they took hold of him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
Now, when the master of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
They said to Him, “He will consign those wretches to a wretched death, and lease the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruits in their proper seasons.”

Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone which the builders rejected as worthless, this has become the cornerstone—the most important stone. This was from the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes’?*
“For this purpose, I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you who reject Me and given to a people—the Gentiles—who produce its fruits.
And the one who falls upon this stone will be broken to pieces; and upon whomever it falls, it will crush him into powder.”*
And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard His parables, they knew that He was speaking about them and their rejection.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And although they wanted to seize Him and arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because they were regarding Him to be a prophet. 5 Quoted from Zech. 9:9 16 Quoted from the Septuagint of Ps. 8:2 42 Quoted from Ps. 118:22-23 44 Referring to Is. 8:14-15

verses.heading: The Parable of the Wedding Feast / The Parable of the Wedding Feast / Lk. 14:15-24
verses.text: And in response, Jesus spoke to them again in parables, saying,
“The kingdom of heaven is compared to a man, a king, who gave a wedding feast for his son.
And he sent his servants to summon those who had been invited to the wedding feast, but they refused the invitation.

Again he sent other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who have been invited, “Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and fattened calves have been slaughtered, and all things are set and ready. Come to the wedding feast.” ’
But they were indifferent and paid no attention and went away, this one to his own field and that one to his business.
And the rest, having taken hold of his servants, treated them violently and killed them.
And the king was enraged and, having sent his forces, he destroyed those murderers and set their city on fire in judgment.
Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding feast is set and ready, but those who had been invited were not fit or worthy.
Go, therefore, to the intersections of the highways, and invite as many people as you find to the wedding feast.’
And those servants went out into the roads and gathered together everyone whom they found, both evil and good. So the wedding hall was filled with guests reclining at the tables.
But when the king came in to see those guests reclining at the tables, he saw a man there who did not dress in wedding clothes provided by the host.
And he said to him, 'Friend, how did you come in here, not having a wedding garment?' But he was speechless and had no excuse.
Then the king said to the attendants, ‘Bind him hand and foot and cast him into the outer darkness. In that place, there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
Many are invited into the kingdom, but only a few are God’s chosen.”

verses.heading: Paying Taxes to Caesar / Paying Taxes to Caesar / Mk. 12:13-17; Lk. 20:20-26
verses.text: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel on how they might entrap Him in His speech and accuse Him.

And they sent their disciples to Him with the Herodians—political supporters of Herod, saying, “Teacher, we know that You are true and teach the way of God in truth, and You are not influenced by anyone, for You do not consider the external appearance of men and show no partiality.
Tell us, therefore, what You think. Is it lawful to pay tribute—taxes—to Caesar or not?”
But knowing their wicked intent by divine insight, Jesus said, “Hypocrites! Why are you testing Me with insincere flattery?
Show Me the coin for the tax.” And they brought to Him a denarius.
And He said to them, “Of whom is this likeness and inscription?”
They said to Him, “Caesar’s.” Then He said to them, “Therefore, give back to Caesar the things that belong to Caesar, and to God the things that belong to God.”
And when they heard this, they marveled at His wisdom. So they left Him and went away.

verses.heading: Concerning the Resurrection / Concerning the Resurrection / Mk. 12:18-27; Lk. 20:27-40
verses.text: On that day, Sadducees, who assert that there is no resurrection and deny the afterlife, approached Him and posed a question to Him,
saying, “Teacher, Moses said in the Law if someone dies without having children, his brother is to marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers among us. And the first after getting married died, and since he had no offspring, he left his wife to his brother according to the Law.
So also the second brother married her and died, and the third, continuing up to the seventh.
At last, the woman also died.
In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her as wife.”
But in response, Jesus said to them, “You are misled and in error, since you do not know the Scriptures nor the power of God.
For in the resurrection, they neither enter into marriage nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven who do not marry.
Furthermore, concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what has been spoken to you by God, saying,
‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living—they are alive to Him.”
And when the crowds heard this, they were struck with amazement at His teaching.

verses.heading: The Great Commandment / The Great Commandment / Mk. 12:28-34; Lk. 10:25-28
verses.text: Now when the Pharisees heard that He had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered themselves together.
And one of them, an authority in the Mosaic Law—an expert, posed a question, testing Him,
“Teacher, which is the great commandment in the Law?”
And He said to him, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind.
This is the great and first commandment in importance.
And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments—everything in Scripture is summarized by these.”

verses.heading: The Davidic Son / The Davidic Son / Mk. 12:35-37; Lk. 20: 41-44
verses.text: Now, while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus posed a question to them,
saying, “What do you think concerning the Christ—the Messiah? Whose Son is He?” They said to Him, “David’s son.”
He said to them, “Then how does David in the Spirit—by inspiration—call Him ‘Lord,’ saying,
‘The Lord God said to my Lord the Messiah, “Sit at My right hand in authority, until I put Your enemies under Your feet as a footstool?’ ”*
If, therefore, David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how is He merely his Son?”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And no one was able to answer Him a word, nor did anyone venture to ask Him any further questions from that day on. 44 Quoted from Ps. 110:1

verses.heading: Jesus Denounces the Scribes and Pharisees / Jesus Denounces the Scribes and Pharisees / Mk. 12:38-40; Lk.11:37-52; 20:45-47
verses.text: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples,
stating, “The scribes and the Pharisees sit on the chair of Moses as authoritative teachers of the Law.
Therefore, all that they tell you from the Law, do and keep, but do not do according to their works and example, for they say one thing and do not practice what they preach.
And they tie up heavy and oppressive burdens of legalistic requirements, and lay them on the shoulders of men, but they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger or help bear them.
And they do all their works in order to be seen by men and receive glory, for they broaden their phylacteries—the boxes containing Scripture—and lengthen their tassels to appear more pious.
And they love the place of honor at feasts, and the most honorable seats in the synagogues,
and the greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called ‘Rabbi’—teacher—by men.
But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for One is your Teacher—Christ, and you are all brothers on equal footing.
And do not call anyone your father on earth in a spiritual sense, for One is your Father, who is in heaven.
And do not be called instructors or masters, for One is your Instructor, the Christ.
And the greatest among you will be your servant who serves others.
And whoever exalts himself will be humbled by God, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

“But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of heaven before men and prevent them from entering. For you neither enter yourselves, nor permit those who would enter to go in.*

“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you journey across the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte—one convert, and when he becomes so, you make him twice as much a son of hell as yourselves—you corrupt him further.
“Woe to you, blind guides, who assert, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it is of no consequence and not binding; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’
Foolish and blind people! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that consecrates the gold and makes it holy?
And you assert, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it is of no consequence; but if anyone swears by the gift that is on it, he is bound by his oath.’
Blind people! For which is greater, the gift or the altar that consecrates the gift?
Therefore, the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by all things that are on it.
And the one who swears by the temple swears by it and by the one—God—who dwells in it.
And the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the One who sits upon it.

“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint and dill and cumin—even the smallest herbs, and have disregarded the weightier matters of the Law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. These you ought to have done without disregarding those things also.
Blind guides, who strain out the gnat—the smallest impurity, but swallow the camel—the largest defilement!
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you clean the outside of the cup and the dish to appear pure, but inside they are full of avarice and self-indulgence.
Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish through inner righteousness, so that its outside also may become clean.
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed tombs which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men's bones and of every kind of impurity.
So you also outwardly appear to men as righteous, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
and you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been collaborators with them in shedding the blood of the prophets!’
In this manner, you testify against yourselves that you are sons and spiritual descendants of those who murdered the prophets.
Complete, then, the measure of your fathers’ deeds—fill up the full measure of guilt by rejecting the Messiah.
Snakes! Offspring of vipers! By what means will you escape from the condemnation that leads to hell?

For this purpose, behold, I am sending to you prophets and wise men and scribes; some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will flog in your synagogues, and pursue from city to city,

so that upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on the earth from the blood of Abel the righteous up to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
Truly, I say to you, all these things will befall this generation in judgment!

verses.heading: Jesus Laments Over Jerusalem / Jesus Laments Over Jerusalem / Lk. 13:34-35
verses.text: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How many times have I desired to gather your children together in the way a hen gathers her young under her wings for protection, but you were not willing!
Behold, your house—the temple—is left to you in a condition of desolation!

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: For I say to you, you will never see Me from this moment on until you say, ‘Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!’ ” 13 A variant reading, attested in part of the manuscript tradition, expands the passage by introducing material from Luke 20:47, which forms an additional verse (14). This verse reads: “ But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows' houses and, as a pretext, pray at great length. For this purpose, you will receive greater condemnation.”
verses.html:
For I say to you, you will never see Me from this moment on until you say, ‘Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!’ ”
13 A variant reading, attested in part of the manuscript tradition, expands the passage by introducing material from Luke 20:47, which forms an additional verse (14). This verse reads: “ But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows' houses and, as a pretext, pray at great length. For this purpose, you will receive greater condemnation.”

verses.heading: Jesus Speaks About the Destruction of the Temple / Jesus Speaks About the Destruction of the Temple / Mk. 13:1-2; Lk. 21:5-6
verses.text: And after Jesus had departed from the temple courts and was going away, His disciples came to draw His attention to the edifices of the temple and its magnificent buildings.
But in response, He said to them, “You see all these things, do you not? Truly, I say to you, not a single stone will be left here upon another stone, which will not be thrown down.”

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Beginning of Woes / Eschatological Discourse: The Beginning of Woes / Mk. 13:3-13; Lk. 21:7-19
verses.text: And while He was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him in private, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the consummation—the end—of the age?”
And in response, Jesus said to them, “Watch out, lest anyone lead you astray.
For many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am the Christ—the Messiah,’ and they will mislead many people.
And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not frightened, for this must occur according to God’s plan, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in diverse locations throughout the world.
But all these events are merely the beginning of birth pains—the initial signs before the final culmination.
“Then they will deliver you over to persecution and tribulation and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations because of My name.
And then many will fall away from the faith, and betray one another, and hate one another.
And many false prophets will emerge and mislead many people;
and because lawlessness will be increased, the love of many will grow cold and their devotion will wane.
But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.
And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Abomination of Desolation / Eschatological Discourse: The Abomination of Desolation / Mk. 13:14-23; Lk. 21:20-24
verses.text: “Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation—the sacrilege—spoken of by Daniel the prophet standing in the holy place”—let the one who reads exercise discernment and understanding—
“then let those in Judea flee to the mountains immediately.
Let the one on the housetop not come down to take things out of his house,
and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
And alas for those women who are pregnant and for those who are nursing infants during those days of tribulation!
But pray that your escape may not take place in winter—when travel is difficult or on a Sabbath—when movement is restricted.
For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not occurred from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will occur again.
And unless those days were shortened by God’s mercy, no flesh would be saved or survive. But for the sake of the elect—the chosen ones, those days will be shortened.
“If anyone says to you at that time, ‘Behold, here is the Christ,’ or ‘Here He is,’ do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will emerge and give great signs and wonders so as to mislead, if possible, even the elect.
Behold, I have told you in advance—you have been warned.
So, if they say to you, ‘Behold, He is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or ‘Behold, He is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
For just as the lightning comes from the east and is visible as far as the west instantaneously, so will be the coming of the Son of Man—sudden and unmistakable.
Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will be gathered.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Coming of the Son of Man / Eschatological Discourse: The Coming of the Son of Man / Mk. 13:24-27; Lk. 21:25-28
verses.text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will cease to shine, the stars will fall from the heavens, and the cosmic powers will be violently disturbed.

Then the sign announcing the Son of Man will appear in the heavens. At that moment, all the peoples of the earth will mourn, and they will behold the Son of Man arriving upon the clouds of heaven, clothed with divine power and overwhelming glory.
He will then send His angels with a resounding trumpet blast, and they will assemble His elect from every direction—from the farthest reaches of the heavens to their furthest boundaries.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Lesson of the Fig Tree / Eschatological Discourse: The Lesson of the Fig Tree / Mk. 13:28-31; Lk. 21:29-33
verses.text: Take instruction from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and new leaves emerge, you recognize that the season of summer is approaching.
In the same way, when you observe all these events unfolding, understand that the time is near—right at the threshold.
I assure you with certainty that this generation will not disappear before all these matters are brought to fulfillment.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away—they are eternally true.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Unknown Day of the Son of Man’s Coming / Eschatological Discourse: The Unknown Day of the Son of Man’s Coming / Mk. 13:32-37; Lk. 17:26-30, 34-36
verses.text: “But concerning that day and hour of My return, no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son in His earthly ministry, but the Father alone.
For as the days of Noah were, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
For as in those days prior to the flood, they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
And they were unaware and unprepared until the flood came and carried them all away in judgment. So also will be the coming of the Son of Man.
In that moment, two men will be working side by side in the field—one will be taken, while the other will remain.
Likewise, two women will be grinding grain together—one will be taken, and the other will be left behind.
For this reason, remain spiritually awake, because you do not know the day on which your Lord will arrive.
Understand this: If the owner of a house had known the hour during the night when a thief would come, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his home to be broken into.
Therefore, you too must live in a state of readiness, for the Son of Man will come at a time when you are not anticipating Him.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: Lesson from the Faithful and Wicked Servants / Eschatological Discourse: Lesson from the Faithful and Wicked Servants / Lk. 12:41-48
verses.text: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant whom the master has set over his household to give to them their food at the right time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master will find so doing—faithfully serving—upon his return.
I assure you that the master will reward such a servant by placing him in charge of all his possessions.
But if that servant is corrupt and reasons within himself, ‘My master is taking a long time to return,’
and he begins to abuse his fellow servants while indulging himself with drunkards in reckless living,
the master of that servant will come on a day he does not anticipate and at an hour he has not perceived,
and will cut him in two in severe judgment and assign his share with the hypocrites. In that place, there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Ten Virgins / The Parable of the Ten Virgins
verses.text: “At that time, the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom as part of the wedding celebration.
Five of these young women were foolish and unprepared, while five were wise and prudent.
The foolish ones took their lamps but failed to bring along any extra olive oil to keep their lamps burning.
The wise ones, however, took containers of olive oil along with their lamps, prepared for any delay.
When the bridegroom was delayed in coming, all ten of the young women became drowsy and eventually fell asleep while waiting.
But in the middle of the night, a shout rang out: “Look, the bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!”
All ten young women woke up and began trimming their lamps, preparing them to burn brightly for the procession.
