The foolish ones said to the wise ones, “Give us some of your olive oil, because our lamps are going out and we have no fuel left.”
But the wise ones answered, saying, “No, there will not be enough oil for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell olive oil and purchase some for yourselves.”
While the foolish young women were away trying to buy oil, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready and prepared entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut and locked.
Later, the other young women arrived and called out, “Sir, sir, open the door for us!”
But the bridegroom answered them, “Truly, I say to you, I do not know you! You have no relationship with me.” He refused them entrance.
Therefore, keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour when the Son of Man will return.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Talents / The Parable of the Talents
verses.text: Jesus continued: “The kingdom of heaven is also like a man who was preparing to embark on a long journey. He called his own servants together and entrusted his wealth and property to them for management during his absence.

To one servant he gave five talents—a massive sum of money. To another he gave two talents, and to another he gave one talent. He distributed according to each servant’s individual ability. Then he departed on his journey without delay.
The servant who had received five talents immediately went out and put the money to work through investments and trade. He gained an additional five talents, doubling what had been entrusted to him.
Similarly, the servant who had received two talents also engaged in business and acquired an additional two talents, likewise doubling his master’s investment.
However, the servant who had received one talent went away, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money, doing nothing productive with it.
After a long time had passed, the master of those servants returned home and began settling accounts with them to see what they had accomplished.

The servant who had received five talents came forward and brought an additional five talents, saying, “Master, you entrusted five talents to me. Look, I have gained five more talents through my efforts.”

His master commended him warmly: “Well done, good and faithful servant! You have proven faithful in managing a few things, so I will now set you over many things with greater responsibility. Enter into the joy and celebration of your master.”
The servant who had received two talents also came and said, “Master, you entrusted two talents to me. Look, I have gained two more talents.”
His master gave him the same commendation: “Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful over a few things, so I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your master.”

Then the servant who had received one talent came and said, “Master, I knew you to be a hard and demanding man, reaping harvest where you have not sown seed and gathering crops from where you have not scattered seed.
Because I was afraid of failing and losing what you gave me, I went away and concealed your talent in the ground for safekeeping. Here, you have what belongs to you.”
But his master answered him, “You wicked and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather from where I have not scattered seed?
Then you should have at least deposited my money with the bankers, so that when I returned I would have received what was mine back with interest earned.”
The master commanded, “Therefore, take the talent away from him and give it to the servant who has ten talents.”

Jesus explained the principle: “For to everyone who has been faithful and productive, more will be granted, and he will have an abundance. But from the one who has nothing—who has been unfaithful and unproductive—even what he has will be taken away from him.

And cast this useless servant out into the outer darkness, away from the presence and blessing of the master. In that place of judgment, there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth in anguish and regret.”

verses.heading: The Separation of the Sheep from the Goats / The Separation of the Sheep from the Goats
verses.text: Jesus then spoke of the final judgment: When the Son of Man comes in His glory, accompanied by all the holy angels, at that time He will sit upon His glorious throne as King and Judge.
All the nations of the earth will be gathered before Him, and He will separate people from one another, just as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats in his flock.
He will place the sheep—the righteous—on His right side, the position of honor and favor, but He will place the goats—the unrighteous—on His left side.
Then the King will say to those on His right side, "Come, you who are blessed by My Father. Inherit the kingdom that has been prepared for you from the foundation of the world, before time began.

For when I was hungry, you provided Me with something to eat. When I was thirsty, you offered Me something to drink. When I was a stranger, you received Me with hospitality and welcomed Me into your homes.
When I was naked and without adequate clothing, you clothed Me. When I was sick, you looked after Me and cared for Me. When I was in prison, you came to visit Me and minister to Me."
Then the righteous will answer Him with genuine surprise, saying, “Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You something to drink?
When did we see You as a stranger and welcome You with hospitality, or naked and clothe You?
When did we see You sick or in prison and come to minister to You?”

The King will answer them, saying, “Truly, I say to you, to the extent that you did these acts of mercy and kindness to one of the least of these My brothers—even the most insignificant and overlooked—you did it to Me. I identify completely with My people, and service to them is service to Me.”

Then the King will also address those on His left side with words of judgment: "Depart from Me, you who are cursed and under condemnation. Go into the eternal fire that has been prepared for the devil and his fallen angels.
For when I was hungry, you provided Me with nothing to eat. When I was thirsty, you offered Me nothing to drink.
When I was a stranger, you did not welcome Me with hospitality. When I was naked, you did not clothe Me. When I was sick and in prison, you did not look after Me or care for Me.”
Then they will also answer in protest, saying, “Lord, when did we see You hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and fail to attend to Your needs?”

Then He will answer them with the same principle in reverse: “Truly, I say to you, to the extent that you did not do these things for one of the least of these, you did not do them for Me. Your neglect of the needy was neglect of Me.”

Jesus concluded: And these on the left will go away into eternal punishment—conscious, unending suffering separated from God. But the righteous on the right will go into eternal life—endless joy in the presence of God forever.”

verses.heading: The Conspiracy to Kill Jesus / The Conspiracy to Kill Jesus / Mk. 14: 1-2; Lk.22:1-2; Jn. 11:45-53
verses.text: When Jesus had completed delivering all these teachings and parables, He said to His disciples what was about to unfold.
“You know that after two days the Passover feast will arrive, and at that time the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
At that same time, the chief priests and the elders of the people assembled together in the palace courtyard of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas.
They conspired about how they might seize Jesus by stealth and cunning, without causing a public disturbance, so they could put Him to death.
However, they agreed among themselves, “We must not do this during the feast itself, or there may be uprising among the people,” since many people honored Jesus as a prophet.

verses.heading: Jesus Anointed in Bethany / Jesus Anointed in Bethany / Mk. 14: 3-9; Jn. 12:1-8
verses.text: While Jesus was staying in Bethany, He was a guest in the house of Simon the leper.

A woman came to Him carrying an alabaster flask filled with highly valuable perfumed oil. While Jesus was reclining at the table for the meal, she poured the expensive perfume on His head as an act of devotion and worship.
When the disciples observed what she had done, they were greatly indignant, saying to one another, “For what purpose is this extravagant waste?
This perfume could have been sold for a great price, and the money could have been given to the poor to meet their needs.”

But Jesus, knowing their thoughts and criticisms, said to them, “Why are you causing trouble for this woman and making her uncomfortable? She has performed a beautiful and noble act for Me that honors Me deeply.
You always have the poor with you, and you will have ongoing opportunities to help them. But you will not always have Me physically present with you—My time is short.
In pouring this perfumed oil on My body, this woman has acted with prophetic insight to prepare My body for burial. Whether she fully understood it or not, she has anointed Me for death.
Truly, I say to you with certainty, wherever this gospel is proclaimed throughout the entire world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of in her memory.”

verses.heading: Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus / Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus / Mk. 14: 10-11; Lk. 22:3-6
verses.text: Then one of the twelve disciples, the one called Judas Iscariot, went privately to the chief priests with a proposal.
He said to them, “What are you willing to pay me if I deliver Him over to you?” They were delighted and agreed to give him thirty pieces of silver—the price of a slave—as payment for his treachery.
From that moment forward, Judas began actively seeking a favorable opportunity to betray Jesus when He was away from the crowds.

verses.heading: The Passover with the Disciples / The Passover with the Disciples / Mk. 14:12-21; Lk. 22:7-14, 21-23; Jn. 13:21-30
verses.text: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, the disciples approached Jesus and asked, “Where do You want us to make preparations for You to eat the Passover meal?”

Jesus gave them specific instructions: “Go into the city to a certain man” whom Jesus knew, “and say to him, ‘The Teacher says, My appointed time draws near. I will celebrate the Passover at your house with My disciples.’ ”
The disciples did exactly as Jesus had directed them, and they made all the necessary preparations for the Passover celebration.
When evening arrived and the meal began, Jesus was reclining at the table with the twelve disciples.
While they were eating the meal together, Jesus made a shocking announcement: “Truly, I say to you that one of you sitting here will betray Me.”
The disciples were deeply distressed and filled with sorrow. Each one began asking Him individually, “Surely it is not I, Lord?”
Jesus answered, “The one who dips his hand into the bowl with Me at the same time will betray Me. The betrayer is sharing this meal with Me even now.”

Jesus continued, “The Son of Man will depart from this life just as it has been written about Him in the Scriptures—this is according to God’s sovereign plan. But woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had never been born.”
Then Judas, the very one who was in the process of betraying Him, asked with apparent innocence, “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” Jesus responded to him directly, “You have said it yourself.”

verses.heading: The Institution of the Lord’s Supper / The Institution of the Lord’s Supper / Mk. 14:22-26; Lk. 22:15-20; 1 Cor. 11:23-25
verses.text: While they were eating the Passover meal, Jesus took bread, blessed it and gave thanks to God, then broke it into pieces. Giving it to the disciples, He said, “Take this and eat it. This is My body, which will be broken for you.”
Then He took the cup of wine, gave thanks to God for it, and gave it to them, saying, “All of you drink from this cup.
For this is My blood of the new covenant, which is being poured out for many people for the forgiveness of sins.”

Jesus then made a promise to His disciples: “But I say to you, from this moment forward, I will never drink of this fruit of the vine again until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of My Father.”
After singing a hymn of praise together, they left the upper room and went out to the Mount of Olives.

verses.heading: Jesus Speaks About Peter’s Denial / Jesus Speaks About Peter’s Denial / Mk. 14:27-31: Lk. 22:31-34; Jn. 13:36-38
verses.text: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “All of you will fall away and abandon Me because of what happens to Me during this night. For it is written in Scripture: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered in all directions.’ ”
But Jesus gave them hope: “However, after I have been raised from the dead, I will go ahead of you into Galilee, and you will see Me there.”
Peter responded boldly and confidently, “Even if all the others fall away because of You, I will never fall away!”
Jesus looked at Peter and said with certainty, “Truly, I say to you that during this very night, before the rooster crows at dawn, you will deny knowing Me three times.”
Peter insisted even more vehemently, “Even if I must die with You, I will absolutely never deny You!” And all the other disciples made similar declarations of loyalty.

verses.heading: Jesus Prays in Gethsemane / Jesus Prays in Gethsemane / Mk. 10: 2-42; Lk. 22:39-46
verses.text: Then Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane, an olive grove on the Mount of Olives. He said to the larger group of disciples, “Sit here and wait while I go over there to pray.”
Jesus took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee—James and John—for closer support. As they went, He began to experience overwhelming sorrow and deep distress.
Then He said to these three disciples, “My soul is crushed with grief to the point of death. The anguish is unbearable. Remain here and stay awake, keeping watch with Me during this hour.”

Jesus went a little farther from them, fell on His face to the ground in agony, and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup of suffering and wrath pass from Me and not require Me to drink it. Nevertheless, not as I will, but as You will.”
Jesus returned to the three disciples and found them sleeping, unable to stay awake. He said specifically to Peter, “So, were you not able to stay awake and watch with Me for even one hour?
Stay awake and pray, so that you will not enter into temptation when it comes. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Jesus went away a second time and prayed, “My Father, if this cup of suffering cannot pass away from Me unless I drink it and experience it fully, then let Your will be done. I accept it.”
When He came back to the disciples, He found them sleeping again, for their eyes were heavy with exhaustion and they could not stay awake.
Leaving them once more, Jesus went away and prayed for a third time, saying the same words again, continuing to submit Himself to the Father’s will despite the agony.

Then Jesus returned to the disciples and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and taking your rest at a time like this? Look, the hour has arrived, and the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners even as we speak.
Get up, let us go from this place. Look, the one who is betraying Me has drawn near and is approaching right now.”

verses.heading: Jesus Betrayed and Arrested / Jesus Betrayed and Arrested / Mk. 14:43-50; Lk. 22:47-53; Jn. 18:3-12
verses.text: While Jesus was still speaking these words, Judas, one of the twelve disciples, suddenly arrived. With him came a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people.
Now Judas, the betrayer, had arranged a signal with them ahead of time, saying, “The man I kiss is the one you want. Seize Him immediately.”
Judas came directly to Jesus without hesitation and said, “Greetings, Rabbi,” and kissed Him warmly on the cheek, as was customary.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, proceed with the purpose for which you have come.” Then the men in the crowd came forward, laid hands on Jesus, and seized Him forcibly.
Suddenly, one of those who were with Jesus—Peter—reached out his hand, drew his sword, and struck the high priest’s servant, cutting off his ear in an attempt to defend Jesus.
But Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place where it belongs, for all who take up the sword in violence will perish by the sword.
Or do you not realize that I could call upon My Father right now, and He would immediately place at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels—over 72,000 angels—to deliver Me?
But if I did that, how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which declare that it must happen in this way?”

At that moment, Jesus addressed the crowds who had come to arrest Him: “Have you come out to arrest Me as if I were a dangerous robber, with swords and clubs? Every day I was sitting in the temple courts teaching publicly, and you did not seize Me then.
But all this has taken place so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples abandoned Him and fled into the night to save themselves.

verses.heading: Jesus Before Caiaphas and the Sanhedrin / Jesus Before Caiaphas and the Sanhedrin / Mk. 14:53-65; Lk. 22:54-55, 63-71; Jn. 18:13-14, 19-24
verses.text: Those who had arrested Jesus led Him away to the residence of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had already assembled for an emergency night trial.

Peter was following Jesus from a distance, far enough back to avoid detection. He followed as far as the courtyard of the high priest’s residence. After entering, he sat down with the guards and officers to observe what the outcome would be.
Meanwhile, the chief priests and the entire Sanhedrin—the Jewish ruling council—were actively seeking false testimony against Jesus so they could justify putting Him to death.

But they found no credible testimony, even though many false witnesses came forward with fabricated charges. Their testimonies contradicted each other and could not stand. Finally, two witnesses came forward with similar testimony.
These men said, “This man has been claiming, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and reconstruct it within three days.’ ”
The high priest stood up dramatically and said to Jesus, “Do You not respond to these charges? What is it that these men are testifying against You?”

But Jesus remained completely silent, refusing to answer the false charges. Then the high priest said to Him, “I place You under oath by the living God, that You tell us plainly if You are the Christ—the Messiah—the Son of God.”

Jesus answered him directly, “You have said it correctly—I am. But I say to you, from this moment forward, you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power—at God’s right hand—and coming on the clouds of heaven in judgment.”

At this declaration, the high priest tore his robes dramatically as a sign of horror at what he considered blasphemy, saying, “He has blasphemed by claiming equality with God! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, you have just now heard the blasphemy with your own ears.
What is your verdict?” In response, they answered, "He is deserving of death!”
Then they spat in His face in contempt and struck Him with their fists. Others slapped Him across the face.
They mocked Him, saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who is the one who hit You?” They blindfolded Him and beat Him, demanding He use supernatural knowledge to identify His attackers.

verses.heading: Peter’s Denial of Jesus / Peter’s Denial of Jesus / Mk. 14:66-72; Lk. 22:56-62; Jn. 18:15-18, 25-27
verses.text: Meanwhile, Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, trying to remain inconspicuous. A female servant of the high priest came up to him and said, “You also were with Jesus of Galilee. I recognize you.”
But Peter denied it before everyone present, saying, “I do not know what you are talking about.”

When he went out to the entryway, hoping to avoid further questioning, another female servant saw him and said to those standing nearby, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth. I have seen him with Jesus.”
Again Peter denied it, this time with an oath to make his denial more convincing: "I do not know the man!”
After a little while, some of the bystanders came up to Peter and said, “Certainly you are one of His disciples, for even your Galilean accent and manner of speech reveal you and give you away.”
Then Peter began to call down curses on himself and to swear with the strongest oaths possible, “I do not know the man!” Immediately after he said this, a rooster crowed, announcing the dawn.

Suddenly Peter remembered the statement Jesus had made to him earlier: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” He went outside away from the crowd, and wept bitterly in shame and repentance over his failure and betrayal.

verses.heading: Jesus Brought Before Pilate / Jesus Brought Before Pilate / Mk. 15:1; Lk. 23:1-2; Jn. 18:28-32
verses.text: When morning came and daylight arrived, all the chief priests and the elders of the people held a formal council meeting to take official action against Jesus with the goal of executing Him.
After binding Him with ropes, they led Him away and delivered Him over to Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor.

verses.heading: Judas Hangs Himself / Judas Hangs Himself / Acts 1:18-19
verses.text: Then Judas, the one who had betrayed Jesus, saw that Jesus had been condemned to death by the Sanhedrin. Overcome with remorse, he returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.
He said to them, “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood—a righteous man who did no wrong.” But they responded coldly, “What is that to us? That is your problem. See to it yourself.”
Judas threw the pieces of silver onto the floor of the temple and departed from them. Then he went away and hanged himself in despair, unable to live with what he had done.
The chief priests picked up the silver coins and said, “It is not lawful to put these into the temple treasury, because this is blood money—the price paid for a man's life.”
So after discussing the matter and taking counsel together, they used the money to purchase the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners and strangers who died in Jerusalem.
For this reason, that field has been called the Field of Blood from that day to this very day.

Then the prophecy spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, which said, “And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the One who had been valued and appraised, on whom a price had been set by the sons of Israel.
And they gave the silver coins for the potter’s field, just as the Lord commanded me.”

verses.heading: Jesus Questioned by Pilate / Jesus Questioned by Pilate / Mk. 15:2-5; Lk. 23:3-5; Jn. 18:33-38
verses.text: Jesus now stood before the governor Pontius Pilate for interrogation. The governor questioned Him directly, asking, “Are You the King of the Jews?” And Jesus said, “You say so.”
When Jesus was being accused by the chief priests and elders with many charges, He answered nothing in His own defense.
Then Pilate said to Him in amazement, “Do You not hear how many serious things they are testifying against You? Will You not defend Yourself?”
But Jesus did not respond to Pilate at all, not even to a single accusation, so that the governor was extremely amazed at His silence and composure.

verses.heading: Jesus Condemned to Death / Jesus Condemned to Death / Mk. 15:6-15; Lk. 23:13-25; Jn. 18:39–19:16
verses.text: Now it was the governor’s custom at the Passover Feast to release one prisoner to the crowd, whichever prisoner they preferred as an act of goodwill.
At that time, the Romans were holding a notorious and well-known prisoner named Barabbas, who was guilty of insurrection and murder.
So when the crowd had gathered together in front of Pilate’s residence, Pilate asked them, “Which prisoner do you prefer that I release to you—Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
Pilate asked this because he understood clearly that the religious leaders had delivered Jesus over to him because of envy, not because of any real crime.

While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat deliberating, his wife sent an urgent message to him, warning, “Have nothing to do with condemning that righteous Man, for I have suffered many disturbing things today in a dream because of Him.”
But the chief priests and elders worked through the crowd, persuading and convincing them to ask for Barabbas to be released and for Jesus to be destroyed.
The governor asked them again, “Which of the two do you prefer that I release to you?” The crowd shouted back, “Barabbas!”
Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do with Jesus, the One who is called Christ?” They all shouted together, “Let Him be crucified!”
Pilate asked, “Why? What evil has He done? What crime has He committed?” But they kept crying out with even greater intensity and volume, “Let Him be crucified!”

When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing and making no progress, but rather that a riot was beginning to develop, he took water and washed his hands ceremonially before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this Man. I bear no responsibility for His death. You must answer for it yourselves.”
In response, all the people shouted, “His blood be upon us and upon our children! We accept responsibility for His death.”

Then Pilate released Barabbas to them as they had requested. After having Jesus brutally scourged with a Roman whip embedded with metal and bone, Pilate delivered Him over to the soldiers to be crucified.

verses.heading: Jesus Derided by the Soldiers / Jesus Derided by the Soldiers / Mk. 15:16-20; Jn. 19:2-3
verses.text: Then the Roman soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the Praetorium—the governor’s headquarters—and gathered the entire cohort of soldiers around Him, numbering several hundred men.
They stripped off His clothes, humiliating Him, and put a scarlet military cloak around Him in mockery.

They twisted together a crown made of thorns and placed it on His head, causing Him pain and bleeding. They put a reed in His right hand as a mock scepter. Then they knelt down before Him in false homage and derided Him cruelly, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They spit on Him in contempt, took the reed from His hand, and repeatedly struck Him on the head, driving the thorns deeper into His skull.
After they had mocked and abused Him thoroughly, they stripped off the scarlet cloak and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him away to crucify Him.

verses.heading: Jesus is Crucified / Jesus is Crucified / Mk. 15:21-32; Lk. 23:26-43; Jn. 19:17-27
verses.text: As they were going out of the city toward the place of execution, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon. The soldiers compelled him to carry Jesus’ cross, as Jesus was too weakened from the scourging to carry it Himself.
When they arrived at a place called Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull” because of its appearance,
the soldiers offered Jesus wine mixed with gall—a bitter substance intended to dull pain. But after tasting it, Jesus refused to drink it, choosing to remain fully conscious during His suffering.
After they had crucified Him by driving nails through His hands and feet, they divided His garments among themselves by casting lots to determine who would receive which piece.
Then the soldiers sat down and kept watch over Him at that place, guarding Him to ensure He died and that His followers did not attempt a rescue.
Above His head they placed a written notice stating the charge against Him: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
Two robbers were also crucified alongside Jesus, one on His right side and one on His left, fulfilling the prophecy that He would be numbered with transgressors.
Those who passed by on the road hurled insults and spoke evil against Him, shaking their heads in contempt and mockery.
They said, “You who claimed You would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If You really are the Son of God, come down from the cross and prove it!”
In the same manner, the chief priests, along with the scribes and elders, were also mocking Him among themselves.
They said sarcastically, “He saved others by His miracles, yet He cannot save Himself! He claims to be the King of Israel. Let Him come down from the cross right now, and then we will believe in Him.
He has put His trust and confidence in God. Let God rescue Him now, if God truly delights in Him and desires to save Him. After all, He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’ ”
Even the two robbers who were crucified with Him were insulting and reviling Him in the same way.

verses.heading: The Death of Jesus / The Death of Jesus / Mk. 15:33-41; Lk. 23:44-49; Jn. 19:28-30
verses.text: From the sixth hour (noon) until the ninth hour (three o’clock in the afternoon), a supernatural darkness came over the whole land.
At approximately three o’clock in the afternoon, Jesus cried out with a loud voice in Aramaic, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?”—which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
Some of those standing nearby, when they heard Him cry out, misunderstood and said, “This man is calling for Elijah the prophet to come and save Him.”
Immediately, one of the bystanders ran and took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and lifted it up to Jesus' lips to give Him a drink.
But the rest of the crowd said, “Leave Him alone for now. Let us see whether Elijah will come to save Him from death.”
Then Jesus cried out once more with a loud voice and voluntarily yielded up His spirit.

At that very moment, the thick curtain of the temple that separated the Holy of Holies from the rest of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom by an unseen hand—signifying that the way into God’s presence was now open to all. The earth shook violently, and the rocks were split apart by the earthquake.
The tombs were also opened by the earthquake, and many bodies of the saints—believers who had died in faith—were raised from death.
These resurrected saints came out of their tombs after Jesus’ own resurrection, entered Jerusalem, the holy city, and appeared to many people as witnesses of the power of Christ’s resurrection.

Now the Roman centurion and those soldiers who were with him, keeping watch over Jesus, witnessed the earthquake and all the extraordinary things that happened. They were filled with great fear and awe, saying, “Truly, this was God’s Son! This man was righteous and divine.”
Many women were present at that place, watching from a distance. These were women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and had been ministering to Him and supporting His ministry with their resources.

Among these faithful women were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons, James and John. They remained nearby, witnessing His death when most of the male disciples had fled.

verses.heading: The Burial of Jesus / The Burial of Jesus / Mk. 15:42-47; Lk. 23:50-56; Jn. 19:38-42
verses.text: When evening had arrived, there came a rich man from the town of Arimathea named Joseph, who was himself also a disciple of Jesus, though he had kept this fact secret out of fear.
This man courageously came to Pilate and requested permission to take the body of Jesus for burial. Pilate ordered that the body be given to him.
Joseph took the body of Jesus down from the cross, wrapped it carefully in a clean linen cloth for burial.
He laid the body in his own new tomb, which he had recently cut out of the solid rock. Then he rolled a large stone against the entrance of the tomb to seal it, and departed from the place.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary remained there, sitting opposite the tomb, keeping watch and observing where Jesus had been laid.

verses.heading: The Guard of Soldiers at the Tomb / The Guard of Soldiers at the Tomb
verses.text: On the following day, which was the day after the Preparation Day—the Sabbath—the chief priests and the Pharisees went together before Pilate with a request.
They said, “Sir, we remember that while He was still alive, that deceiver Jesus said, ‘‘After three days I will rise from the dead.’’

Therefore, we request that you order the tomb to be made secure and guarded until the third day. Otherwise, His disciples might come during the night and steal His body, then tell the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead.’ If that happens, this last deception will be worse than the first deception of His messianic claims.”
Pilate said to them, “You have a guard of soldiers at your disposal. Go and make the tomb as secure as you know how to make it.”
So they went to the tomb and secured it by sealing the stone and posting a guard of soldiers to watch it continuously.

verses.heading: The Resurrection / The Resurrection / Mk. 16:1-8; Lk. 24:1-12; Jn. 20:1-10
verses.text: After the Sabbath had ended, at the first light of dawn on the first day of the week—Sunday morning—Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to visit and observe the tomb where Jesus had been laid.

Suddenly there was a violent earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven with power and glory. He came to the tomb, rolled away the large stone from the entrance, and sat down on it in triumph.
The angel’s appearance was like brilliant lightning, dazzling and glorious, and his clothing was white as snow, radiating purity and holiness.
The guards posted at the tomb were filled with dread at the sight of the angel. They became like dead men, falling to the ground from fear.
But the angel spoke to the women, saying, “Do not be afraid. I know that you are seeking Jesus, the One who was crucified.
He is not here in this tomb, for He has been raised from the dead, just as He told you He would be. Come here and see the place where He was lying. The tomb is empty.”

The angel commanded them, “Now go quickly and tell His disciples this message: ‘He has been raised from the dead, and behold, He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He promised.’ Listen carefully—I have given you this message to deliver.”
The women quickly departed from the tomb with mixed emotions—fear at what they had witnessed and great joy at the news of the resurrection. They ran to bring the report to His disciples.

As they were going to find the disciples, Jesus Himself suddenly met them on the path, saying, “Greetings!” The women immediately approached Him, took hold of His feet in worship and reverence, and worshipped Him as their risen Lord.
Then Jesus said to them reassuringly, “Do not be afraid. Go and take this message to My brothers—tell them to go to Galilee, and there they will see Me as I promised.”

verses.heading: The Report of the Guard / The Report of the Guard
verses.text: While the women were going to tell the disciples, some of the soldiers from the guard detail went into the city. They reported to the chief priests everything that had taken place at the tomb.
After the chief priests had assembled with the elders and consulted together about how to respond to this crisis, they gave a substantial sum of money to the soldiers as a bribe.
They instructed the soldiers, “You must say this: ‘His disciples came during the night while we were sleeping and stole His body away.’
And if this report reaches the governor’s ears and he questions you about sleeping on duty, we will satisfy him with our explanation and keep you out of trouble. You will not be punished.”
So the soldiers took the money and did exactly as they had been instructed. This fabricated story has been spread among the Jewish people and circulated to this very day.

verses.heading: The Great Commission / The Great Commission / Mk. 16:14-18; Lk 24.36-49; Jn. 20:19-23; Acts 1:6-8
verses.text: The eleven remaining disciples journeyed to Galilee as Jesus had directed them, going to the specific mountain that Jesus had designated for their meeting.
When they saw the risen Jesus, they worshiped Him in awe and wonder. However, some among them expressed doubt and skepticism, struggling to believe what they were seeing.

Jesus came near and spoke to them with words of ultimate authority, saying, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been granted to Me by the Father—I possess absolute sovereignty over all creation.

Therefore, based on My authority, go and make disciples of all the nations of the world, not just Israel. Baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit—bringing them into relationship with the Triune God.

Teach these new disciples to observe and obey everything I have commanded you throughout My ministry. And behold, I am with you always, every single day, until the end of the age when history is consummated.”

verses.heading: The Preaching of John the Baptist / The Preaching of John the Baptist / Matt. 3:1-12; Lk. 3:1-9, 15-17; Jn. 1:19-28
verses.text: This is the beginning of the good news about Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
The coming of Jesus was announced beforehand, just as it is written in the prophecy of Isaiah: “Behold, I am sending My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way.*
This messenger is the voice of one calling out in the wilderness, saying, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord. Make His paths straight.’ ”*
John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness of Judea, baptizing people and preaching a baptism of repentance that symbolized turning away from sin for the forgiveness of sins.
All the countryside of Judea and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem were going out to him in great numbers. They were being baptized by him in the Jordan River as they openly confessed their sins.
John was clothed with rough camel’s hair and wore a leather belt around his waist. His diet consisted of locusts and wild honey—the simple fare of a prophet living in the wilderness.

John was preaching this message: “One who is far mightier and more powerful than I is coming after me. I am not even worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of His sandals—a task reserved for the lowest slave.
I have baptized you with water as a sign of repentance, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit, bringing true spiritual transformation and power.”

verses.heading: The Baptism of Jesus / The Baptism of Jesus / Matt. 3:1-12; Lk. 3:1-9, 15-17; Jn. 1:19-28
verses.text: In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan River by John, identifying Himself with sinful humanity though He Himself was sinless.
Immediately as Jesus was coming up out of the water, He saw the heavens being torn open as God revealed Himself. He saw the Spirit descending like a dove and coming upon Him.

verses.heading: The Temptation of Jesus / The Temptation of Jesus
verses.text: A voice spoke from heaven, declaring, “You are My Son, the beloved One in whom I take infinite delight and with whom I am well pleased.” Μatt. 4:1-11; Lk. 4:1-13
verses.html:
A voice spoke from heaven, declaring, “You are My Son, the beloved One in whom I take infinite delight and with whom I am well pleased.”
Μatt. 4:1-11; Lk. 4:1-13

verses.text: Immediately after His baptism, the Spirit drove Jesus out into the wilderness for testing.
He remained in the wilderness for forty days, being tempted and tested by Satan. He was surrounded by wild animals, yet the angels of God were attending to His needs.

verses.heading: The Beginning of Jesus’ Galilean Ministry / The Beginning of Jesus’ Galilean Ministry / Matt. 4:12-17; Lk. 4:14-15
verses.text: After John the Baptist had been arrested and imprisoned by Herod, Jesus came into the region of Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God.
His message was: “The appointed time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent by turning from your sins and believe in this good news.”

verses.heading: Jesus Calls His First Disciples / Jesus Calls His First Disciples / Matt. 4:18-22; Lk. 5:1-11
verses.text: As Jesus was passing by alongside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting a fishing net into the sea, for they earned their living as fishermen.
Jesus said to them, “Come, follow Me as My disciples, and I will transform you and make you into fishers of men—catching people for the kingdom of God.”
At once, without hesitation, they left their nets and everything they knew and followed Him.
Going on a little farther along the shore, Jesus saw James the son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in their boat mending and repairing their fishing nets.
Immediately Jesus called them to follow Him. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants and went away to follow Jesus.

verses.heading: Jesus Casts Out an Unclean Spirit from a Man / Jesus Casts Out an Unclean Spirit from a Man / Lk. 4:31-37
verses.text: They entered the town of Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day, Jesus went into the synagogue and began to teach the people gathered there.
The people were utterly amazed at His teaching, for He was teaching them as one who possessed inherent authority, not like the scribes who merely quoted other rabbis and traditions.
Just then, there was a man in their synagogue who was possessed by an unclean spirit. The demon cried out through him,
saying, “What do You have to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us before the appointed time? I know who You are—You are the Holy One of God!”
But Jesus rebuked the demon sternly, commanding, “Be silent! Come out of him immediately!”
The unclean spirit threw the man into violent convulsions and cried out with a loud, terrible voice, then came out of him.

Everyone present was astonished, so that they began discussing among themselves, saying, “What is this? This is a new teaching backed by authority! He even commands the unclean spirits and they must obey Him!”
Immediately, the news and report about Jesus spread rapidly everywhere throughout the surrounding region of Galilee.

verses.heading: Jesus Heals Many People / Jesus Heals Many People / Matt. 8:14-17; Lk. 4:38-41
verses.text: As soon as they left the synagogue, they went to the house of Simon and Andrew, accompanied by James and John.
Simon’s mother-in-law was lying in bed suffering from a fever. Immediately they told Jesus about her condition.
Jesus came near to her, took hold of her hand, and raised her up. The fever left her instantly, and she began to serve them, demonstrating her complete healing.

When evening came and the sun had set—meaning the Sabbath was over and people could travel—they began bringing to Jesus all those who were sick with various diseases and those who were demon-possessed.
The whole city had gathered together at the door of the house, crowding around to see Jesus.

Jesus healed many people who were suffering from various diseases, and He cast out many demons from those who were possessed. He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew His true identity and He did not want testimony from evil spirits.

verses.heading: Jesus Preaches Throughout Galilee / Jesus Preaches Throughout Galilee / Lk. 4:42-44
verses.text: Very early in the morning, while it was still dark before dawn, Jesus got up, left the house, and went out to a deserted place where He could be alone. There He was praying to the Father.
Simon and those who were with him searched diligently for Jesus.
When they found Him, they said, “Everyone is looking for You! The whole town wants You to come back.”
But Jesus said to them, “Let us go elsewhere to the neighboring towns and villages, so that I may preach the gospel there as well. This is the purpose for which I have come out from the Father.”
So Jesus went throughout the region of Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and casting out demons, demonstrating the power of God’s kingdom.

verses.heading: The Cleansing of a Leper / The Cleansing of a Leper / Matt. 8:1-4; Lk. 5:12-16
verses.text: A man afflicted with leprosy came to Jesus, earnestly pleading with Him and falling on his knees before Him. He said, “If You are willing, You have the power to make me clean.”
Moved with deep compassion for the man, Jesus stretched out His hand and touched him—an act that would make most people ceremonially unclean. Jesus said to him, “I am willing. Be made clean.”
Immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was made completely clean and healed.
Jesus sternly warned him about what to do next, then sent him away immediately with urgent instructions.

Jesus said to him, “See that you say nothing about this to anyone along the way. But go and show yourself to the priest for examination, and offer for your cleansing the sacrifices that Moses commanded in the Law. This will serve as evidence to the priests of your healing.”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: However, the man went out and began to proclaim his healing freely and openly, spreading the account widely throughout the region. As a result, Jesus could no longer enter a city publicly without being mobbed, but He had to stay outside in deserted and uninhabited places. Yet even there, people kept coming to Him from every direction. 2 Quoted from Mal. 3:1 3 Quoted from Is. 40:3

verses.heading: Jesus Heals a Paralytic / Jesus Heals a Paralytic / Matt. 9:1-8; Lk. 5:17-26
verses.text: When Jesus entered Capernaum again after some days away, word spread that He was at home in the town.
Many people gathered together, so many that there was no longer any room left, not even at the door of the house. Jesus was speaking the word of God to them.
Four men came, carrying a paralyzed man on a mat, bringing him to Jesus for healing.

When they could not get near Jesus because of the dense crowd, they removed part of the roof above where Jesus was teaching. After digging through the clay and thatch, they lowered the mat on which the paralytic was lying down through the opening.
When Jesus saw their faith—demonstrated by their persistent effort to bring the man to Him—He said to the paralytic, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
But some of the scribes were sitting there, observing everything and reasoning in their hearts with criticism.
They thought, “Why does this man speak in such a way? He is blaspheming! Who has the authority to forgive sins except God alone?”
Immediately Jesus, knowing in His spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves, said to them, “Why are you reasoning about these things in your hearts?
Which is easier to say to the paralytic—‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say ‘Get up, take up your mat and walk’?
But so that you may know and be convinced that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—Jesus turned and said to the paralytic—
“I say to you, get up, take up your mat, and go to your house.”
Immediately the man got up, took up his mat, and walked out in full view of everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this before!”

verses.heading: The Calling of Levi / The Calling of Levi / Matt. 9:9-13; Lk. 5:27-32
verses.text: Jesus went out again beside the sea to teach. All the crowd kept coming to Him, and He was teaching them about the kingdom of God.

As He passed by the tax collection booth, He saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting there collecting taxes for Rome. Jesus said to him simply, “Follow Me!” Levi stood up and followed Him, leaving his lucrative position behind.

Later, as Jesus was reclining at the table for a meal in Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners were also reclining and eating with Jesus and His disciples. There were many such people, and they were following Jesus.

When the scribes who belonged to the party of the Pharisees saw that Jesus was eating with sinners and tax collectors—people considered unclean and unworthy—they said to His disciples, “Why does He eat and associate with tax collectors and sinners?”

When Jesus heard their criticism, He responded, “Those who are healthy and well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick do. I have not come to call the righteous who think they need nothing, but sinners who recognize their need for God.”

verses.heading: The Question About Fasting / The Question About Fasting / Matt. 9:14-17; Lk. 5:33-39
verses.text: The disciples of John the Baptist and the Pharisees were practicing regular fasting. Some people came to Jesus and asked, “Why do the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but Your disciples do not fast?”

Jesus answered them with an illustration: “Can the friends of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them at the wedding celebration? As long as they have the bridegroom present with them, they cannot fast—it would be inappropriate.
But days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast on that day when I am gone.”

Jesus continued with another illustration: “No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. If someone does, the new patch pulls away from the old cloth, and a worse tear results. The new and old are incompatible.

Similarly, no one puts new wine into old wineskins. If someone does, the new wine will burst the wineskins as it ferments and expands—and both the wine and the wineskins will be destroyed and ruined. Instead, new wine must be put into fresh, new wineskins.”

verses.heading: Plucking Grain on the Sabbath / Plucking Grain on the Sabbath / Matt. 12:1-8; Lk. 6:1-5
verses.text: It happened that Jesus was passing through grainfields on the Sabbath day. As they walked, His disciples began making their way through the fields while plucking heads of grain to eat.
The Pharisees confronted Jesus, saying, “Look! Why are Your disciples doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?” They accused the disciples of harvesting on the Sabbath.
Jesus responded, “Have you never read in the Scriptures what David did when he and his men were in need and hungry?

How David entered the house of God during the time when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the bread of the Presence—the consecrated bread that was placed before the Lord—which is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests? Yet David ate it and even gave it to those who were with him.”
Jesus then stated the principle: “The Sabbath was made for the benefit of people, and not people for the Sabbath.
Therefore, the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

verses.heading: The Man with a Shriveled Hand / The Man with a Shriveled Hand / Matt. 12:9-14; Lk. 6.6-11
verses.text: Jesus entered the synagogue again on another occasion. A man who had a shriveled hand was there.
The religious leaders were watching Jesus carefully to see if He would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they might have grounds to accuse Him of breaking the Sabbath law.
Jesus said to the man with the shriveled hand, “Stand up and come here into the middle where everyone can see.”

Then Jesus addressed the watching crowd and asked, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil? To save life or to kill?” But they remained silent, refusing to answer because any answer would expose their hypocrisy.

Jesus looked around at them with anger, being deeply grieved at the callousness of their hearts. Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” The man stretched it out, and his hand was completely restored to health.
The Pharisees went out immediately and began conspiring with the Herodians—their political enemies—taking counsel together about how they might destroy Jesus.

verses.heading: A Large Crowd Follows Jesus at the Seaside / A Large Crowd Follows Jesus at the Seaside
verses.text: Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the Sea of Galilee to avoid the plots against Him. A large crowd from Galilee followed Him, and also many from Judea,

and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea to the south, and from the region beyond the Jordan River to the east, and from the areas around Tyre and Sidon to the north. A vast multitude came to Him when they heard about all the mighty works He was doing.
Jesus told His disciples to have a small boat ready and waiting for Him because of the pressing throng, so that the crowd would not crush Him as they pressed forward.
He had healed so many people that all those who had diseases were pushing forward and pressing around Him, trying to touch Him in hope of healing.
Whenever the unclean spirits saw Jesus, they would fall down before Him in compelled submission, crying out and saying, “You are the Son of God!”
Jesus would strongly and repeatedly rebuke them, commanding them not to make His identity known publicly, as He did not want testimony from demons.

verses.heading: The Appointment of the Twelve / The Appointment of the Twelve / Matt. 10:1-4; Lk. 6:12-16
verses.text: Jesus went up on the mountain away from the crowds and called to Himself those whom He personally wanted. They came to Him in response to His call.

He appointed twelve men, whom He also named apostles—meaning “sent ones”—for two purposes: first, that they might be with Him in close relationship, and second, that He might send them out to preach the gospel.
He gave them authority to cast out demons, demonstrating the power of the kingdom over the forces of evil.
These are the twelve He appointed: To Simon He gave the name Peter, meaning “rock.”
There was James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James. To these two brothers Jesus gave the name Boanerges, which means “Sons of Thunder.”
The twelve also included Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon the Zealot—a former member of a revolutionary group.
And there was Judas Iscariot, who later betrayed Jesus to His enemies.

verses.heading: Jesus and Beelzebul / Jesus and Beelzebul / Matt. 12:22-32; Lk. 11:14-23; 12:10
verses.text: Jesus went to a house, and once again such a crowd gathered that He and His disciples were not even able to eat a meal.
When His own family members heard about His intense activity and the crowds, they went out to take charge of Him and bring Him home, for they were saying, “He is out of His mind.”

The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem to investigate Jesus were making serious accusations, saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul, the prince of demons,” and “He casts out demons by the power of the ruler of the demons.”
Jesus called them to Himself and began speaking to them in parables to expose the illogic of their accusation: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself and engaged in civil war, that kingdom cannot stand and will collapse.
If a household is divided against itself and fighting internally, that house cannot stand and will fall apart.
If Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, fighting against his own forces, he cannot stand but is coming to an end and approaching destruction!
No one can enter the house of a strong man and plunder his possessions and goods unless he first binds and overpowers the strong man. Only then can he plunder his house.”
Jesus then gave a solemn warning: “Truly, I say to you that all sins will be forgiven to human beings—even the most terrible sins and whatever blasphemies they may speak.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit—attributing the work of the Spirit to Satan—does not have forgiveness forever, but is guilty of an eternal sin that can never be pardoned.”
Jesus said this because they kept saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”

verses.heading: The Mother and Brothers of Jesus / The Mother and Brothers of Jesus / Matt. 12:46-50; Lk. 8:19-21
verses.text: Jesus’ mother and His brothers arrived at the house. While standing outside, unable to get through the crowd, they sent a message to Him, calling for Him to come out.
A crowd was sitting around Jesus, and someone said to Him, “Look, Your mother and Your brothers are outside looking for You.”
Jesus responded with a question: “Who are My mother and My brothers?”
Looking around at those who were sitting in a circle around Him, listening to His teaching, He said, “Behold, here are My mother and My brothers!
For whoever does the will of God, this person is My brother and sister and mother.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Sower / The Parable of the Sower / Matt. 13:1-9; Lk. 8:4-8
verses.text: Once again Jesus began to teach beside the Sea of Galilee. Such a very large crowd gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat down in it on the water, while the whole crowd remained on the shore.
Jesus was teaching them many things through parables—earthly stories with heavenly meanings. In His teaching He said to them:
“Listen carefully! A farmer went out to sow seed in his field.
As he was scattering the seed, some fell along the hardened path where people walked, and the birds came and devoured it before it could take root.
Other seed fell on rocky ground where there was only a thin layer of soil over limestone. It sprang up quickly because the soil had no depth.
But when the sun rose and beat down, the plant was scorched. Because it had no deep root system, it withered away and died.
Other seed fell among thorns and weeds. The thorns grew up around it and choked it out, so that it produced no crop.
Still other seed fell into good, fertile soil. It grew up, increased in size, and yielded a crop—some seed producing thirty times what was sown, some sixty times, and some a hundred times as much.”
Jesus concluded by saying, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear and understand the spiritual meaning.”

verses.heading: The Purpose of the Parables / The Purpose of the Parables / Matt. 13:10-17; Lk. 8:9-10
verses.text: When Jesus was alone away from the crowds, those who were around Him along with the twelve disciples began asking Him about the meaning of the parables.

Jesus explained, “To you who are My followers, the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given—you are granted understanding. But to those who are outside, who remain unbelievers, everything comes in parables that conceal as much as they reveal.

This happens so that the prophecy might be fulfilled: ‘While seeing with their eyes, they may see but not perceive the truth. While hearing with their ears, they may hear but not understand the meaning. Otherwise they might turn in repentance, and it would be forgiven them.’ ”

verses.heading: The Explanation of the Parable of the Sower / The Explanation of the Parable of the Sower / Matt. 13:18-23; Lk. 8:11-15
verses.text: Jesus said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? How then will you be able to understand all the other parables I teach?
The sower sows the word of God.

These are the ones along the hardened path where the word is sown: When they hear the message, Satan comes immediately and takes away the word that has been sown in their hearts before it can take root.
These are the ones sown on rocky ground: When they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy and enthusiasm.
But they have no root in themselves—no depth of commitment. They endure only for a moment. Then when affliction or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately stumble and fall away.
Others are the ones sown among the thorns: These are people who hear the word,

but the cares and worries of this world, the deceitfulness of riches that promise but do not deliver, and the desires for other things come in and choke out the word, so that it becomes unfruitful in their lives.

And these are the ones sown on the good soil: They hear the word, receive it with faith, and bear fruit for God—some producing thirty times what was sown, some sixty times, and some a hundred times as much.”

verses.heading: A Lamp Under a Basket / A Lamp Under a Basket / Lk. 8:16-18
verses.text: Jesus continued teaching them, saying, “A lamp is not brought into a room so that it may be hidden under a basket or placed under a bed, is it? Is it not brought in to be placed on a lampstand where it can give light?
For nothing is concealed except for the purpose that it might eventually be made manifest. Nothing is kept secret except that it should ultimately come to light.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear and pay attention.”

Jesus said to them, “Give careful consideration to what you hear. The measure of attention and care you give will determine the measure of understanding you receive, and even more will be added to you beyond that.

For whoever has spiritual understanding, more will be given to him so that he increases in knowledge. But whoever does not have understanding, even what little he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Growing Seed / The Parable of the Growing Seed
verses.text: Jesus continued, “The kingdom of God is like this: It is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
Night after night he sleeps, and day after day he rises and goes about his work. Meanwhile the seed sprouts and grows, though the man himself does not understand how it happens.
The soil produces crops by itself, automatically—first the green stalk appears, then the head of grain forms, then the full mature grain develops in the head.
When the crop is ripe and ready for harvest, the farmer immediately sends in the sickle to reap, because the harvest time has arrived.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Mustard Seed / The Parable of the Mustard Seed / Matt. 13:31-32; Lk. 13:18-19
verses.text: Jesus asked, “With what shall we compare the kingdom of God? What parable can we use to illustrate it?
The kingdom is like a grain of mustard seed. When it is sown in the soil, it is the smallest of all the seeds that are planted in the ground.
Yet when it is sown and begins to grow, it becomes larger than all the garden plants. It puts out such large branches that the birds of the sky are able to nest in its shade.”

verses.heading: The Use of Parables / The Use of Parables / Matt. 13:34-35
verses.text: With many parables like these, Jesus kept speaking the word to the crowds, teaching them as much as they were able to hear and understand.
Jesus would not speak to the crowds without using a parable to illustrate His teaching. But when He was in private with His own disciples, He would explain everything to them clearly.

verses.heading: The Calming of a Great Storm / The Calming of a Great Storm / Matt. 8:23-27; Lk. 8:22-25
verses.text: On that same day, when evening had come, Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross over to the other side of the lake.”
After dismissing the crowd, the disciples took Jesus along in the boat just as He was, without any preparation. Other small boats accompanied them across the lake.
A violent storm of wind suddenly arose. The waves were breaking over the sides of the boat, so that the boat was rapidly filling with water.

But Jesus was in the stern of the boat, sleeping peacefully on a cushion, apparently unconcerned. The disciples woke Him urgently and said, “Teacher, does it not matter to You that we are perishing and about to drown?”
Jesus got up and rebuked the wind sternly. He said to the sea, “Be silent! Be still!” Immediately the wind ceased its raging, and there was a great calm over the water.
Jesus said to His disciples, “Why are you so timid? Do you still have no faith in Me after all you have seen?”
The disciples were filled with extreme fear and awe. They said to one another, “Who then is this man, that even the wind and the sea obey Him and submit to His command?”

verses.heading: The Healing of the Gerasene Demon-Possessed Man / The Healing of the Gerasene Demon-Possessed Man / Matt. 8:28-34; Lk. 8:26-39
verses.text: They came to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, to the region of the Gerasenes in Gentile territory.
When Jesus had stepped out of the boat onto the shore, immediately a man with an unclean spirit came out from the tombs to meet Him.
This man had his dwelling among the burial tombs. No one could restrain or bind him anymore, not even with chains.

He had frequently been bound with shackles on his feet and chains on his hands, but he had torn the chains apart with supernatural strength, and he had shattered the shackles into pieces. No one was strong enough to subdue him.
Constantly, night and day, he would be among the tombs and on the mountains, crying out in torment and cutting himself with sharp stones in his misery.
When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran toward Him and fell on his knees before Him in compelled worship.
Crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What do You have to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I put You under oath by God, do not torture me before the appointed time!”
Jesus had been commanding him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” The demon answered, “My name is Legion, because we are many”—indicating thousands of demons possessed this man.
The demons begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of that region.
Now a large herd of pigs was feeding on the nearby mountainside.
The demons begged Jesus, saying, “Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter into them.”
Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out of the man and entered the pigs. The herd of about two thousand pigs rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water.
Those who had been tending the pigs fled and reported what had happened in the city and throughout the countryside. People came out to see for themselves what had taken place.

They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been demon-possessed sitting there, clothed and in his right mind—the very man who had been possessed by the legion of demons. They were afraid at the dramatic change.
Those who had witnessed the event described in detail to the others what had happened to the demon-possessed man, and also told them about what happened to the pigs.
The people began begging Jesus to depart from their region—valuing their pigs more than the deliverance of the man.
As Jesus was getting into the boat to leave, the man who had been demon-possessed begged Jesus that he might remain with Him and become His follower.

But Jesus did not permit him to come. Instead, He said to him, “Go to your home and to your own people, and report to them all that the Lord has done for you, and tell them how He has had mercy on you.”
The man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis—the region of ten Greek cities—all that Jesus had done for him. Everyone who heard continually marveled at his testimony.

verses.heading: Jairus’ Daughter and the Woman with the Discharge of Blood / Jairus’ Daughter and the Woman with the Discharge of Blood / Matt. 9:18-26; Lk. 8:40-56
verses.text: When Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side of the lake, a large crowd gathered around Him as He stood by the sea.
One of the rulers of the synagogue came to Him, a man named Jairus. When he saw Jesus, he fell down at His feet in desperation.
He begged Jesus earnestly many times, saying, “My little daughter is on the very verge of dying. Please come and lay Your hands on her, so that she may be healed and live.”
Jesus went with him. A large crowd followed Jesus and pressed against Him on all sides, thronging Him.
A woman was in the crowd who had suffered from a discharge of blood for twelve long years.

She had endured much suffering under the care of many physicians. She had spent all her financial resources on treatments, but had not been helped in any way. Instead, her condition had only grown worse.
When she heard the reports about Jesus and His healing power, she came up behind Him in the crowd and touched His outer garment.
She kept saying to herself, “If I can just touch even His clothes, I will be healed.”
Immediately the flow of blood stopped and dried up. She felt in her body that she had been healed from her affliction.
Immediately Jesus, knowing in Himself that power had gone out from Him, turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched My clothes?”
His disciples said to Him, “You see the crowd pressing against You from every side, and You ask ‘Who touched Me?’ ”
But Jesus kept looking around to see the woman who had done this.
The woman, fearful because she knew what had happened to her, came forward and fell down before Him. She told Him the whole truth about her condition and her healing.
Jesus said to her gently, “Daughter, your faith has healed you and made you whole. Go in peace and be permanently well from your disease.”
While Jesus was still speaking to the woman, messengers came from the house of Jairus the synagogue ruler, saying, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher any further? It is too late.”
But Jesus, overhearing what was being said and disregarding their message of despair, said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Do not be afraid. Only believe and trust Me.”
Jesus did not permit anyone to follow along with Him except Peter and James and John the brother of James.
They arrived at the house of the ruler of the synagogue. Jesus saw a commotion, with people weeping and wailing loudly in mourning.
When He entered the house, He said to them, “Why are you making such a commotion and weeping? The child has not died, but is sleeping.”

They began to ridicule and laugh at Him scornfully. But after putting all the mourners outside, Jesus took along only the child’s father and mother and His three disciples, and went into the room where the child was lying.
Taking the child by the hand, He said to her in Aramaic, “Talitha koum!”—which is translated, “Little girl, I say to you, arise and get up!”

Immediately the girl arose and began to walk around the room, fully restored to life and health. She was twelve years of age. Immediately all who witnessed this were completely and utterly amazed beyond measure.

Jesus strictly and sternly ordered them that no one should be told about this miracle. Then He said that something should be given to the girl to eat, demonstrating that she was truly alive and not a ghost.

verses.heading: Jesus Rejected in His Hometown / Jesus Rejected in His Hometown / Matt. 13:53-58; Lk. 4:16-30
verses.text: Then He went out from that place and came to His native town of Nazareth, and His disciples followed Him.

And when the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were struck with amazement, saying, “From what source did this man acquire these things—this wisdom and power, and what is this wisdom that has been granted to Him, and the mighty works such as these performed by His hands?

Is this not merely the carpenter—the common tradesman, the son of Mary, and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not His sisters here with us in this town?” And they took offense at Him because of His familiar background.
And Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor and respect, except in his hometown, and among his relatives, and within his own family.”
And He was not able to do any mighty work in that place, except to lay His hands on a few sick people and heal them.
And He was wondering because of their unbelief and hardness of heart. And He was going around the surrounding villages, teaching.

verses.heading: The Sending out of the Twelve Disciples / The Sending out of the Twelve Disciples / Matt. 10:1, 5-15; Lk. 9:1-6
verses.text: And He summoned to Himself the twelve disciples and began to send them out two by two for mutual support and witness, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
And He commanded them to take nothing for the journey except only a staff—no bread, no bag for provisions, no money in their belt—
but to put on sandals for the journey and not to put on two tunics—they were to travel simply and depend on God’s provision.
And He was saying to them, “Wherever you enter a house as guests, stay there until you depart from that place.
And whatever place does not receive you or listen to your message, as you go out from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet as a witness against them and their rejection.”
So when they had gone out, they preached that people should repent and turn from their sins to God.
And they were casting out many demons by the authority given to them, and were anointing many sick people with olive oil as a symbol of healing, and healing them.

verses.heading: The Death of John the Baptist / The Death of John the Baptist / Matt. 14:1-12; Lk. 9:7-9
verses.text: And King Herod heard about Jesus, for His name had become widely renowned. And they were saying, “John, the one who baptizes, has been raised from the dead, and for this reason, these miraculous powers are operating within him.”
But others were saying, “He is Elijah returned.” And others were saying, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”
But when Herod heard this speculation, he said with guilt, “John whom I beheaded—he has been raised from the dead to haunt me!”
For it was Herod himself who had sent and seized John and bound him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philip, his brother, because he had unlawfully married her.
For John had been saying to Herod boldly and repeatedly, “It is not permitted by God’s Law for you to have the wife of your brother.”
So Herodias held a grudge against him and continually desired to kill him in revenge. But she could not accomplish this,

for Herod was afraid of John, realizing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe from execution. And whenever he heard him preach, he was greatly perplexed by his message, and yet he listened to him with pleasure.
Now an opportune day arrived when Herod, on his birthday, held a banquet for his noble officials and military tribunes and the leading men of Galilee.

And when the daughter of Herodias herself came in, danced sensually, and pleased Herod and those reclining at the table with him, the king said to the girl rashly, “Ask me for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
And he swore to her with an oath, “Whatever you ask me, I will give to you, up to half of my kingdom.”
And when she had gone out, she said to her mother, “What shall I ask for?” And she said with vengeful intent, “The head of John, the one who baptizes.”
And immediately, entering with haste to the king, she asked, saying, “I desire that you give to me at once the head of John the Baptist on a platter.”
And the king became intensely distressed; but, on account of the oaths he had sworn publicly and those reclining at the table as witnesses, he was not willing to refuse her and lose face.
So immediately, the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring his head. And after he had gone out, he beheaded him in the prison,
and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl delivered it to her mother as a trophy.
And when his disciples heard about this tragedy, they came and took away his corpse, and laid it in a tomb with honor.

verses.heading: The Feeding of the Five Thousand Men / The Feeding of the Five Thousand Men / Matt. 14:13-21; Lk. 9:10-17; Jn. 6:1-14
verses.text: Then the apostles gathered to Jesus and reported to Him all that they had done and that they had taught during their mission.

And He said to them, “You yourselves come privately to a deserted place and rest for a short while.” For those who were coming and those who were going were many, and they did not even have an opportunity to eat.
So they went away in the boat to a deserted place, in private.
Now many saw them departing and recognized them, and they ran together on foot from all the cities and arrived there ahead of them.

And after disembarking, He saw a large crowd and was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep that had no shepherd to guide and protect them. So, He began to teach them many things.
And the hour had already become late when His disciples came up to Him, and they were saying, “This place is deserted, and the hour is already late.
Dismiss them, so that they may go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy for themselves something to eat.”
But in response, He said to them, “You give to them something to eat.’’ And they said to Him, “Shall we go and buy bread for two hundred denarii—eight months’ wages—and give it to them to eat?”
And He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go, see.” And when they found out, they said, “Five loaves, and two fish.”
Then He ordered them all to sit down in a relaxed posture in groups on the green grass.
So they sat down in a relaxed posture in groups, by hundreds and by fifties in orderly arrangement.

And taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, He blessed and gave thanks and broke the loaves and kept giving them to His disciples to set before them. And He distributed the two fish among them all.
So they all ate and were satisfied and filled.
Then they took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and of the fish—more than they started with.
Now those who had eaten of the loaves were five thousand men, not counting women and children.

verses.heading: Jesus Walks on the Water / Jesus Walks on the Water / Matt. 14:22-23; Jn. 6:15-21
verses.text: And immediately, He urged His disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of Him to the other side, to Bethsaida, while He Himself dismissed the crowd.
And when He had said goodbye to them, He departed to the mountain to pray in solitude with the Father.
And when evening arrived, the boat was in the middle of the sea, while He was alone on the land.

And He saw them being distressed while rowing, for the wind was against them and blowing contrary. Around the fourth watch of the night—between three and six in the morning, He came to them, walking on the sea in defiance of natural law, intending to pass by them;
but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they supposed that it was a ghost, and they cried out in terror.
For they all saw Him and were troubled. But immediately, He spoke to them and said to them, “Have courage; it is I. Do not be afraid.”
Then He went up into the boat to them, and the wind ceased raging. And they were utterly amazed within themselves beyond measure.
For they had not understood concerning the loaves and what it revealed about His divine power, but their hearts were hardened and slow to comprehend.

verses.heading: The Healings at Gennesaret / The Healings at Gennesaret / Matt. 14:34-36
verses.text: Now when they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and anchored there.
And as they were coming out of the boat, He was immediately recognized by the people.
They ran about that whole region and began to carry around those who were sick on their beds to wherever they heard that He was.

And wherever He would go—into villages, or into cities, or into rural areas, they were laying those who were sick in the marketplaces and begging Him that they might touch even the fringe of His garment. And as many as touched it were healed.

verses.heading: The Traditions of the Elders / The Traditions of the Elders / Matt. 15:1-20
verses.text: The Pharisees and some of the scribes who were experts in the Law gathered together around Jesus in opposition to Him, having come all the way from Jerusalem specifically to confront Him.
They observed that some of His disciples were eating their bread with hands that were ceremonially defiled—that is, unwashed according to the ritual traditions handed down through generations.

Mark explains for his Gentile readers: The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they thoroughly wash their hands with a specific ritual washing, carefully adhering to the traditions of the elders that have been passed down through oral teaching.
