When they come home from the marketplace where they might have touched Gentiles or unclean things, they do not eat unless they perform ceremonial washings. There are many other traditions that they have received and strictly observed, including elaborate rituals for washing cups, pitchers, copper vessels, and even dining couches.

The Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus, saying, “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders that we all follow, but instead eat their bread with ceremonially defiled hands?”

Jesus responded to them, “Isaiah prophesied accurately and rightly about you hypocrites, as it is written in Scripture: ‘This people honors Me with their lips in outward profession and religious talk, but their heart is distant and far away from Me in true devotion and love.
They worship Me to no purpose, accomplishing nothing, because they teach as divine doctrines the mere precepts and commandments of men.’ ”*
Jesus continued, “You are leaving aside the commandment of God that truly matters, while you cling tightly to the tradition of men that has no divine authority.”
He was also saying to them, “You expertly and cleverly nullify the commandment of God in order to preserve your own tradition.
For Moses, speaking for God, said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’* and also said, ‘The one who speaks evil of father or mother must be put to death.’*

But you say and teach, ‘If a man says to his father or to his mother, “Whatever financial help you might have received from me to support you in your old age is Corban’ ”—that is, a gift that has been consecrated to God—
then you no longer permit him to do anything to help his father or his mother financially.

Thus you are invalidating the word of God by your tradition which you have handed down through the generations. And you do many other things like this, systematically placing your traditions above God’s clear commands.”
Jesus called the crowd to Himself again and began to say to them, “Listen to Me carefully, everyone, and understand this truth:

There is nothing outside the man—no food or drink—that is able to defile him spiritually by going into him. Rather, it is the things that come out of the man from his heart that defile the man and make him unclean before God.”*
When Jesus had left the crowd and went into the house away from the public, His disciples began to ask Him privately about the meaning of the parable He had just spoken.

Jesus said to them with some exasperation, “So are you also without understanding like the crowds? Do you not comprehend that whatever goes into the man from outside is not able to defile him spiritually,

because it does not enter into his heart where moral character resides, but into his stomach, and then passes out into the latrine?” By this statement, Mark explains, Jesus was declaring all foods ceremonially clean—abolishing the Old Testament dietary restrictions.
Jesus continued His teaching, saying, “What comes out of the man from within—that is what defiles the man and makes him unclean.
For from within, from the heart of men, come the evil thoughts that lead to sinful actions: sexual immoralities of all kinds, thefts, murders,

adulteries, acts of greed and covetousness, acts of wickedness and malice, deceit and deception, licentiousness and sensuality, envy toward others, slander against others, arrogance and pride, foolishness and moral stupidity.
All these evil things come from within the heart, and they are what defile the man and make him unclean before God.”

verses.heading: The Faith of the Syrophoenician Woman / The Faith of the Syrophoenician Woman / Matt. 15:21-28
verses.text: From there Jesus got up and traveled away to the region of Tyre in Gentile territory. When He entered a house, He desired that no one should know of His presence there, seeking rest and privacy. Yet He was not able to escape notice.
But immediately, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit possessing her heard about Jesus being there. She came and fell down at His feet in desperate pleading.
Now this woman was a Greek by culture, a Syrophoenician by birth and ethnicity—a Gentile with no claim on the Jewish Messiah. She kept asking Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
Jesus was testing her faith, saying to her, “Let the children be satisfied first with the bread. It is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she responded to Him with remarkable faith and humility, saying, “Yes, Lord, that is true. Yet even the household dogs under the table eat from the children’s crumbs that fall.”
Jesus said to her with commendation, “Because of this utterance and the faith it demonstrates, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”
When she went away to her home, she found her child lying peacefully on the bed, with the demon having departed completely.

verses.heading: The Healing of a Deaf and Mute Man / The Healing of a Deaf and Mute Man
verses.text: Jesus then departed from the region of Tyre and traveled through Sidon, then came to the Sea of Galilee, passing through the midst of the region of the Decapolis—the ten Greek cities.
People brought to Him a man who was deaf and had great difficulty speaking clearly. They were begging Jesus earnestly that He would lay His hand on the man for healing.
Jesus took him away from the crowd in private, and put His fingers into his ears, and after spitting, He touched the man’s tongue with the moisture.
Looking up to heaven in prayer to the Father, Jesus sighed deeply with compassion and said to him in Aramaic, “Ephphatha!”—which is translated, “Be opened!”
Immediately the man’s ears were opened and the impediment that had bound his tongue was removed completely. He began to speak accurately and clearly, with perfect speech.

Jesus strictly charged the people who witnessed this that they should tell no one about the miracle. But the more He strictly charged them to silence, the more extensively and abundantly they persisted in proclaiming it everywhere.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: The people were struck with amazement beyond all measure, saying, “He has done everything well and perfectly! He even makes the deaf to hear and the mute to speak!” 7 Quoted from Is. 29:13 10 Quoted from Ez. 20:12 10 Quoted from Ez. 21:17 15 Some ancient manuscripts include a verse 16 containing the exhortation: “ If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
verses.html:
The people were struck with amazement beyond all measure, saying, “He has done everything well and perfectly! He even makes the deaf to hear and the mute to speak!” 7 Quoted from Is. 29:13 10 Quoted from Ez. 20:12 10 Quoted from Ez. 21:17
15 Some ancient manuscripts include a verse 16 containing the exhortation: “ If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”

verses.heading: The Feeding of the Four Thousand / The Feeding of the Four Thousand / Matt. 15:32-39
verses.text: In those days, there was again a large crowd gathering around Jesus to hear Him teach, and they had nothing to eat. Jesus called His disciples to Himself and said to them,
“I have compassion for the crowd, because they have remained with Me for three days now and have nothing left to eat.
If I send them away hungry to their homes, they will faint and collapse on the way from weakness, and some of them have come from a long distance.”
His disciples answered Him practically, “From where can anyone provide sufficient bread to satisfy all these people here in this deserted and remote place?”
Jesus was asking them, “How many loaves do you have?” They answered, “Seven loaves.”

Jesus commanded the crowd to sit down in a relaxed posture on the ground in preparation for a meal. Taking the seven loaves and giving thanks to God, He broke them into pieces and kept giving them to His disciples to distribute before the people. So they set the bread before the crowd.
They also had a few small fish. After blessing them and giving thanks, Jesus told the disciples to set these also before the people.
The people ate and were completely satisfied and filled. Afterward, they picked up the leftover broken pieces, filling seven large baskets full.
There were approximately four thousand people who had eaten. Then Jesus dismissed them to return home.
Immediately after this, Jesus got into the boat with His disciples and traveled across the water to the district of Dalmanutha on the western shore.

verses.heading: The Unbelief of the Pharisees / The Unbelief of the Pharisees / Matt. 16:1-4
verses.text: The Pharisees came out and started to argue with Jesus, seeking from Him a sign from heaven to authenticate His claims. They were testing Him and trying to trap Him.
Sighing deeply in His spirit with grief over their unbelief, He said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly, I say to you with certainty, no sign will be given to this generation!”
Leaving them without further discussion, Jesus got into the boat again with His disciples and went across to the other side of the lake.

verses.heading: The Leaven of the Pharisees and Herod / The Leaven of the Pharisees and Herod / Matt. 16:5-12
verses.text: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread with them, and except for one single loaf, they had none with them in the boat.
Jesus was issuing instructions and warnings to them, saying, “Watch out! Beware of the leaven—the corrupting influence—of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod!”
The disciples were reasoning and discussing with one another about the literal fact that they had no bread, completely missing Jesus’ spiritual point.

Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Why are you reasoning about the fact that you have no bread? Do you not yet consider or understand spiritual truth? Have your hearts been hardened and become dull?
You have eyes—do you not see spiritual realities? You have ears—do you not hear and comprehend? Do you not remember what I have done and demonstrated?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand people, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up afterward?” They answered Him, “Twelve baskets full.”
“When I also broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many large baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up?” They said, “Seven.”
So Jesus was saying to them, “Do you not yet understand that I was not speaking about literal bread, but about the dangerous teaching of the Pharisees?”

verses.heading: Jesus Heals a Blind Man at Bethsaida / Jesus Heals a Blind Man at Bethsaida
verses.text: They came to the village of Bethsaida. People brought to Jesus a blind man and begged Him earnestly that He would touch the man and heal him.
Taking hold of the blind man’s hand, Jesus led him gently out of the village for privacy. After spitting on his eyes and laying His hands on him, Jesus was asking him, “Do you see anything?”
The man looked up and kept saying, “I see the men, for I see them as trees, walking around.”

Then Jesus laid His hands on the man’s eyes again with a second touch. The man looked intently and saw clearly. His sight was completely restored, and he continued to see everything distinctly and sharply.
Jesus sent him away to his home with instructions, saying, “Do not even go into the village to tell what happened.”

verses.heading: The Confession of Peter / The Confession of Peter / Matt. 16:13-20; Lk. 9:18-21
verses.text: Jesus and His disciples went out to the villages surrounding Caesarea Philippi in the far north of Israel. On the way, He began to ask His disciples a question, saying to them, “Who do people say that I am?”
They reported to Him, saying, “Some say John the Baptist risen from the dead. Others say Elijah returned as promised. Still others say one of the prophets of old.’’

Jesus continued to press the question more personally: “But who do you yourselves say that I am?” In response, Peter spoke up and said to Him, “You are the Christ!”—the Messiah, the Anointed One of God.
Then Jesus warned them sternly that they should tell no one about Him yet, as the time was not right for this public declaration.

verses.heading: Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection / Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection / Matt. 16:21-28; Lk. 9:22-27
verses.text: Jesus began to teach them clearly that it was necessary and ordained by God for the Son of Man to suffer many things, to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, to be killed, and after three days to rise again from the dead.
He was speaking openly and plainly about this matter, holding nothing back. Peter, after taking Jesus aside privately, began to reprimand Him for speaking of such things.

But Jesus turned around and, seeing His other disciples watching, He reprimanded Peter sharply and said, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are an obstacle to Me because you are not setting your thoughts on the matters of God and His purposes, but on the matters of men and human thinking.”

When Jesus had called the crowd to Himself along with His disciples, He said to them all, “If anyone desires to come after Me and be My disciple, he must deny himself, refusing to make himself the center. He must take up his cross daily like a condemned man walking to execution, and follow Me.
For whoever desires to save his life and preserve it will lose it eternally. But whoever loses his life for the sake of Me and for the sake of the gospel will save it and find true life.
For what does it benefit or profit a man to gain possession of the whole world with all its wealth and power, yet forfeit his own soul in the process?
For what can a man give as an exchange or ransom to buy back his soul once it is lost?

For whoever is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, refusing to identify with Me publicly, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in the glory of His Father, accompanied by the holy angels, for final judgment.”
Jesus was saying to them, “Truly, I say to you with certainty that there are some of those standing here who will never taste death until they see the kingdom of God when it has come with power.”

verses.heading: The Transfiguration of Jesus / The Transfiguration of Jesus / Matt. 17:1-13; Lk. 9:28-36
verses.text: Six days after this conversation, Jesus took along Peter and James and John, and led them up a high mountain by themselves alone, away from everyone else. There He was transfigured before them—His appearance was dramatically transformed.
His garments became dazzling, glistening, and extremely white—so brilliant and radiant that no launderer on earth would be able to whiten them in this way. His glory shone through.
Suddenly Elijah appeared to them alongside Moses, and these two great figures from Israel’s past were conversing with Jesus.
Peter responded impulsively to Jesus, saying, “Rabbi, it is good and wonderful for us to be here. Let us make three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
Mark explains that Peter did not know what he should say or how to respond appropriately, for all three disciples were greatly terrified by what they were witnessing.
Then a cloud appeared, overshadowing them with God’s presence. A voice came from the cloud, declaring, “This is My Son, the beloved One. Listen to Him!”
Suddenly, looking around them, the disciples saw no one with them anymore—Moses and Elijah had vanished. Only Jesus remained alone with them.
As they were descending from the mountain, Jesus issued strict instructions to them that they should tell no one what they had seen, except after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
So they kept the saying to themselves as Jesus had commanded, but they were puzzling over it and reasoning among themselves about what “rising from the dead” could mean.
They began asking Jesus for clarification, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first before the Messiah appears?”

Jesus was explaining to them, “Elijah indeed does come first and restores all things in preparation. But how is it written in Scripture concerning the Son of Man that He should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?

But I say to you that Elijah has indeed already come in the person of John the Baptist, and they did to him whatever they wanted, treating him cruelly and finally killing him, just as it is written prophetically of him.”

verses.heading: The Healing of a Boy with a Mute and Deaf Spirit / The Healing of a Boy with a Mute and Deaf Spirit / Matt. 17:14-20; Lk. 9:37-43a
verses.text: When Jesus and the three disciples came back down to where the other disciples were, they saw a large crowd gathered around them and scribes arguing with them.
Immediately when all the crowd saw Jesus approaching, they were greatly astonished. Running to Him eagerly, they greeted Him.
Jesus asked the disciples and scribes, “What matter are you disputing with them?”
One man from the crowd answered Him, “Teacher, I brought my son to You because he has a mute spirit that prevents him from speaking.

Whenever it seizes him violently, it throws him down to the ground. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth together, and becomes rigid. I asked Your disciples to cast it out, but they were not able to do so.”
Jesus responded by saying to them all, “O unbelieving generation! How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with your lack of faith? Bring the boy to Me!”
So they brought the boy to Jesus. When the demon saw Jesus, it immediately seized the boy with violent convulsions. Falling on the ground, he began to roll around, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus inquired of the boy’s father, “How long has this been happening to him?” The father said, “From early childhood.
The demon has often thrown him both into fire and into water, attempting to destroy and kill him. But if You are able to do anything at all, have compassion on us and help us!”
Jesus responded to his conditional statement, saying, ‘ “If You are able'? Why do you say ‘if’? All things are possible to the one who believes and has faith.”
Immediately, the father of the child cried out in desperation and was saying with tears, “I believe! Help my unbelief and strengthen my weak faith!”

When Jesus saw that a crowd was rapidly running together to see the spectacle, He rebuked the unclean spirit authoritatively, saying to it, “Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!”

After crying out loudly and seizing the boy with violent convulsions one last time, the spirit came out. The boy became as if he were dead and lifeless, lying motionless, so that many bystanders said, “He is dead.”
But Jesus took hold of him by the hand and lifted him up, and the boy stood up alive and well.
When Jesus had come into the house away from the crowd, His disciples began to ask Him privately, “Why were we not able to cast out this demon?”
Jesus said to them, “This particular kind of demon can come out by nothing but by prayer and dependence on God.”

verses.heading: Jesus Again Predicts His Death and Resurrection / Jesus Again Predicts His Death and Resurrection / Matt. 17:22-23; Lk. 9:43b-45
verses.text: From there, they went out and began to pass through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know their whereabouts,

for He was teaching His disciples privately and saying to them, “The Son of Man is being delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill Him. But when He has been killed, after three days He will rise from the dead.”
But the disciples did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask Him to explain what He meant.

verses.heading: Who is the Greatest? / Who is the Greatest? / Matt. 18:1-5; Lk. 9:46-48
verses.text: They came to Capernaum. When Jesus was in the house with them, He began to ask them, “What were you arguing and discussing on the way here?”
But they kept silent and would not answer, for on the way they had been discussing and debating with one another about who among them was the greatest.
Jesus sat down deliberately, called the twelve to Himself, and said to them, “If anyone desires to be first in rank, he must become last of all and servant of all.”
Jesus took a little child and had him stand among them in their midst. Embracing the child tenderly, He said to them,
“Whoever accepts one of these children such as this in My name accepts Me. And whoever accepts Me does not accept Me only, but also accepts the One who sent Me—the Father.”

verses.heading: Whoever Is Not Against Us Is for Us / Whoever Is Not Against Us Is for Us / Lk. 9:49-50
verses.text: John spoke up and began to say to Jesus, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name, and we kept trying to prevent him from doing so because he was not following us as part of our group.”
But Jesus said, “Do not stop him from ministering. No one who performs a mighty work and miracle in My name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of Me.
For whoever is not against us is for us. Those who honor My name are on our side.
For whoever gives you even a cup of water to drink in My name because you belong to Christ, truly I say to you that he will never lose his reward, no matter how small the act of kindness.”

verses.heading: Temptations to Sin / Temptations to Sin / Matt. 18:6-9; Lk. 17:1-2
verses.text: “But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble into sin, it would be better for him if a large millstone used by a donkey were placed around his neck and he were thrown into the sea to drown.

If your hand causes you to sin and leads you into temptation, cut it off from your life. It is better for you to enter eternal life crippled and maimed, than to have both hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire of judgment.*
If your foot causes you to sin and leads you astray, cut it off from your life. It is better for you to enter eternal life limping, than to have both feet and be cast into hell.
If your eye causes you to sin by what you look at, gouge it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye, than to have both eyes and be cast into hell,
where ‘their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.’ ”
“For everyone will be salted with fire—tested and purified through trials, or judged by the fire of hell.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Salt is good and valuable, preserving and flavoring. But if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it and restore it? Have salt in yourselves and be at peace with one another.” 43 A variant reading in part of the manuscript tradition expands the passage to include verse 44, which states: “ where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.”
verses.html:
Salt is good and valuable, preserving and flavoring. But if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it and restore it? Have salt in yourselves and be at peace with one another.”
43 A variant reading in part of the manuscript tradition expands the passage to include verse 44, which states: “ where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.”

verses.heading: Concerning Divorce / Concerning Divorce / Matt. 19:1-12
verses.text: Jesus set out from there and came to the region of Judea and to the area on the other side of the Jordan River. Crowds came together to Him again, and as was His custom, He began to teach them again about the kingdom.
Some Pharisees came to Him and began to question Him, asking, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?” They were testing Him, trying to trap Him in a controversial issue.
Jesus responded with a question, saying to them, “What did Moses command you in the Law?”
They answered, “Moses allowed a man to write a certificate of divorce and to send his wife away.”
But Jesus said to them, “Moses wrote this commandment for you only as a concession because of the hardness of your hearts and your stubborn refusal to live according to God’s will.
But at the beginning of creation, God’s original design was different. ‘He made them male and female.’*
‘On account of this design, a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined permanently to his wife,
and the two shall become one flesh,’* united inseparably. So they are no longer two separate individuals, but one flesh joined by God.
Therefore, what God has united together in marriage, let no human being separate by divorce.”
Later, in the privacy of the house, the disciples began to ask Jesus again about this difficult teaching.
Jesus said to them clearly, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.
And if she herself divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”

verses.heading: Jesus Embraces and Blesses Children / Jesus Embraces and Blesses Children / Matt. 19:13-15; Lk. 18:15-17
verses.text: People were bringing little children to Jesus so that He might touch them in blessing, but the disciples rebuked those who brought them, thinking children were unimportant.
But when Jesus saw this, He was greatly indignant. He said to the disciples, “Permit the children to come to Me. Do not prevent them, for it is to such as these that the kingdom of God belongs.
Truly, I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child in humility, dependence, and trust will never enter it.”
Jesus took the children in His arms and embraced them lovingly. He began to bless them earnestly, laying His hands on them in benediction.

verses.heading: The Rich Man / The Rich Man / Matt. 19:16-30; Lk. 18:18-30
verses.text: As Jesus was setting out on the road to continue His journey, one man ran up eagerly, fell on his knees before Him, and asked, “Good Teacher, what must I do so that I may inherit eternal life?”
But Jesus challenged his casual use of the word “good,” saying to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good in an absolute sense except God alone.

You know the commandments from Scripture: ‘You shall not murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false evidence against your neighbor. You shall not defraud anyone. Honor your father and mother.’ ”
The man said to Him confidently, “Teacher, all these requirements I have carefully observed and kept from my youth onward.”

Jesus looked at him intently and loved him, seeing his sincerity. He said to him, “You lack one thing to complete your righteousness: Go, sell everything that you have, and give the proceeds to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven instead of on earth. After that, come and follow Me as My disciple.”
But at this statement, the man looked gloomy. He went away grieving and sorrowful, for he was one who possessed many material possessions that he could not give up.
Jesus looked around at His disciples and said to them, “How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God!”
The disciples were astounded at His words, since wealth was seen as God’s blessing. But Jesus responded and said to them again, “Children, how difficult it is to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel—the largest animal in Palestine—to go through the eye of a sewing needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
The disciples were exceedingly struck with amazement, saying to one another, “Who then can possibly be saved, if even the rich cannot?”
Jesus looked directly at them and said, “With men, salvation is impossible. No one can save themselves. But not with God—for all things are possible with God, including the salvation of the rich.”
Peter began to say to Jesus, “Look, we have left everything behind and have followed You. What will we receive?”

Jesus was answering, “Truly, I say to you, there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or mother, or father, or children, or farms and lands, for the sake of Me and for the sake of the gospel,

who will not receive a hundred times as much now in this present age—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and farms, along with persecutions that will come—and in the age to come, eternal life.
On the contrary, many who are first in this age will be last, and those who are last now will be first then.”

verses.heading: Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection a Third Time / Jesus Predicts His Death and Resurrection a Third Time / Matt. 20:17-19; Lk. 18:31-34
verses.text: Now they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them, leading the way. The disciples were astonished at His determination, and those who were following behind Him were afraid of what lay ahead. Jesus took aside the twelve once more and began to tell them in detail the events that were soon to happen to Him:

“Listen carefully. We are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over and betrayed to the chief priests and the scribes. They will sentence Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles for execution.
The Gentiles will mock and deride Him, spit on Him in contempt, flog Him brutally, and kill Him. But after three days, He will rise from the dead in victory.”

verses.heading: The Request of James and John / The Request of James and John / Matt. 20:20-28
verses.text: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to Jesus privately and said to Him, “Teacher, we desire that You do for us whatever we ask of You.”
Jesus said to them, “What do you desire that I should do for you?”
They said to Him boldly, “Grant us that we may sit in positions of honor, one at Your right hand and one at Your left, when You come in Your glory and establish Your kingdom.”

But Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking for. Are you able to drink the cup of suffering which I must drink, or to be baptized with the baptism of suffering with which I am baptized?”

They answered Him naively and confidently, “We are able.” Jesus said to them, “You will indeed drink the cup which I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized—you will share in My sufferings.
But to sit at My right hand or at My left is not Mine to give. Those positions are for those for whom they have been prepared by My Father according to His sovereign plan.”
When the other ten disciples heard about this request, they began to be greatly angry with James and John for their presumption and ambition.
Jesus called all twelve to Himself and said to them, “You know that those who are considered to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
But it shall not be in this way among you and your community. Instead, whoever desires to become great among you must become your servant, ministering to others.
And whoever desires to be first and foremost among you must become the slave of all, taking the lowest position.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served and waited upon, but to serve others, and to give His life as a ransom payment for many, purchasing their freedom from sin.”

verses.heading: The Healing of Bartimaeus / The Healing of Bartimaeus / Matt. 20:29-34; Lk. 18:35-43
verses.text: Then they came to the city of Jericho. As Jesus was departing from Jericho with His disciples and a large crowd following, Bartimaeus the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene passing by, he began to call out loudly and persistently, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Many people in the crowd were rebuking him and telling him to be quiet and stop bothering Jesus. But he continued to call out all the more urgently, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped walking when He heard the cry. He said, “Call him here to Me.” The crowd called the blind man and said to him, “Take heart! Rise up! He is calling you.”
Bartimaeus, in his excitement, threw aside his beggar’s cloak and leaped up with joy. He came to Jesus.
In response, Jesus said to him, “What do you desire that I should do for you?” The blind man said to Him, “Rabboni”—my Master and Teacher—“I desire that I may recover my sight.”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Jesus said to him, “Go your way. Your faith has healed you and made you whole.” Immediately Bartimaeus recovered his sight completely. He began to follow Jesus on the way to Jerusalem as a grateful disciple. 6 Quoted from Gen. 1:27 7-8 Quoted from Gen. 2:24

verses.heading: The Triumphal Entry / The Triumphal Entry / Matt. 21:1-11; Lk. 19:28-40; Jn. 12:12-19
verses.text: When they drew near to Jerusalem, approaching the villages of Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two of His disciples ahead
and said to them, “Go into the village ahead of you. Immediately as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it to Me.
If anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say to them, ‘The Lord has need of it, and He will send it back here as soon as possible.’ ”
So the two disciples departed and found a colt tied at a door outside in the street, exactly as Jesus had said. They untied it.
But some of those who were standing there began to say to them, “What are you doing, untying that colt?”
The disciples spoke to them just as Jesus had instructed, and the people granted them permission to take it.
Then they brought the colt to Jesus and threw their outer cloaks over it as a saddle. Jesus sat on it to ride into Jerusalem.
Many people in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road as a carpet of honor, while others spread leafy branches which they had cut from the fields, creating a royal pathway.
Those who went ahead of Jesus and those following behind were crying out loudly, “Hosanna!”—meaning “Save us now!” “Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest heaven!”

Jesus entered Jerusalem and proceeded into the temple courts. After looking around carefully at everything, observing the corruption in God’s house, He went out to Bethany with the twelve since the hour was already late in the evening.

verses.heading: The Cursing of the Fig Tree / The Cursing of the Fig Tree / Matt. 21:18-19
verses.text: On the next day, having departed from Bethany in the morning, Jesus was hungry.

Seeing from a distance a fig tree that had leaves—suggesting it should have fruit—He went to see if perhaps He might find anything on it. But when He came to it, He found nothing except leaves, for it was not yet the season for figs to be ripe.
Jesus responded to the tree as a symbolic act, saying to it, “May no one eat fruit from you anymore forever!” His disciples heard this unusual statement.

verses.heading: The Cleansing of the Temple / The Cleansing of the Temple / Matt. 21:12-17; Lk. 19:45-48; Jn. 2:13-22
verses.text: Then they came to Jerusalem. Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out forcefully those who were selling animals for sacrifice and those who were buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves for offerings.
He would not permit anyone to carry merchandise and goods through the temple courts, treating God’s house like a marketplace or shortcut.

Jesus was teaching the people and saying to them, “Is it not written in Scripture, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers and a hideout for thieves!”

When the chief priests and the scribes heard what Jesus had done, they began to seek how they might destroy Him and put Him to death. They were afraid of Him because all the crowd was struck with amazement at His teaching and authority.
When evening came, Jesus and His disciples would go out of the city to spend the night in Bethany.

verses.heading: The Significance of the Withered Fig Tree / The Significance of the Withered Fig Tree / Matt. 21:20-22
verses.text: Now as they went along the road in the morning, returning to Jerusalem, they saw the fig tree completely withered and dried up from the roots.
When Peter remembered what had happened the day before, he said to Jesus, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which You cursed has withered!”
In response, Jesus said to them, “Have faith in God—constant, unwavering trust in His power.

Truly, I say to you that whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be removed and thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart with uncertainty, but believes with confidence that what he says will happen, it will be done for him.
Therefore, I say to you, everything that you pray and ask for, believe that you have received it from God, and it will be done for you.
And whenever you stand praying, forgive others if you have anything against anyone. Do this in order that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses.”*

verses.heading: Jesus’ Authority Questioned / Jesus’ Authority Questioned / Matt. 21:23-27; Lk. 20:1-8
verses.text: They came again to Jerusalem. While Jesus was walking in the temple courts teaching, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders approached Him in a delegation.
They began to say to Him in challenge, “By what authority are You doing these things—cleansing the temple and teaching the people? Who gave You this authority to do these things?”
But Jesus responded with His own question, saying to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer Me, and then I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
The baptism that John performed—did it originate from heaven as divine authority, or did it come from men as merely human activity? Answer Me.”
They began to reason and debate this among themselves privately, saying, “If we say ‘From heaven,’ He will say to us, ‘Then why did you not believe him and accept his message?’
But if we say, ‘From men’ ” —they hesitated, for they were continually afraid of the crowd and public opinion, because all the people held firmly that John really was a prophet sent from God.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: So they answered Jesus, saying, “We do not know the answer.” They refused to commit themselves. Then Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.” 25 A variant reading attested in part of the manuscript tradition adds verse 26, which states: “ But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father, who is in heaven, forgive your trespasses.”
verses.html:
So they answered Jesus, saying, “We do not know the answer.” They refused to commit themselves. Then Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
25 A variant reading attested in part of the manuscript tradition adds verse 26, which states: “ But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father, who is in heaven, forgive your trespasses.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Vineyard and the Farmers / The Parable of the Vineyard and the Farmers / Matt. 21:33-46; Lk. 20:9-19
verses.text: Jesus then began teaching them through parables, saying: “There was a landowner who established a vineyard, surrounding it with a protective wall, constructing a winepress pit, and building a watchtower. After completing these preparations, he entrusted the vineyard to tenant farmers and traveled to another country.
When harvest season arrived, the owner dispatched a slave to the tenants to retrieve his portion of the vineyard’s yield.
The tenants, however, seized this slave, assaulted him violently, and dismissed him with nothing.
The owner sent another slave to them, whom they struck on the head and dishonored severely.
He dispatched yet another slave, whom they murdered. He continued sending numerous other slaves—some were beaten, others were killed.
The owner had one remaining emissary: his cherished son. As a final attempt, he sent his son to them, reasoning, ‘Surely they will show respect to my son.’
The tenant farmers, however, conspired among themselves: ‘This is the heir to the estate. If we kill him, we can seize his inheritance for ourselves!’
They seized the son, murdered him, and discarded his body outside the vineyard boundaries.
What action will the vineyard’s owner take? He will arrive personally, execute those wicked tenants, and transfer the vineyard’s stewardship to others who will prove faithful.
Have you not encountered this prophetic Scripture: ‘The builders dismissed a particular stone as defective and useless, yet this rejected stone has now become the principal cornerstone.
The Lord Himself has accomplished this reversal, and we marvel at its wonder’?”*

The religious authorities recognized that Jesus had directed this parable against them and sought to arrest Him immediately, yet they feared the crowd’s reaction. Consequently, they departed, leaving Him temporarily.

verses.heading: Paying Taxes to Caesar / Paying Taxes to Caesar / Matt. 22:15-22; Lk. 20:20-26
verses.text: The religious leaders then dispatched representatives from both the Pharisees and Herodians to Jesus, hoping to ensnare Him through His own words.

These representatives approached Jesus with feigned respect: “Teacher, we recognize Your integrity and impartiality. You show no favoritism based on social standing but teach God’s way truthfully. Given this, tell us: Does Jewish Law permit paying taxes to the Roman Caesar, or should we refuse?”
Jesus, perceiving their duplicity, responded: “Why do you test Me with this trap? Bring Me a Roman denarius for examination.”
When they produced the coin, Jesus inquired, “Whose portrait and title appear on this coin?” They acknowledged, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus declared to them, “Then render to Caesar what rightfully belongs to Caesar’s realm, and render to God what rightfully belongs to God’s realm.”

verses.heading: Concerning Resurrection / Concerning Resurrection / Matt. 22:23-33; Lk. 20:27-40
verses.text: Next came Sadducees—a sect that rejects the doctrine of resurrection—who presented Jesus with a question:
“Teacher, Moses instructed us that when a man dies childless, his brother must marry the widow to produce offspring for the deceased brother’s lineage.
Consider this scenario: Seven brothers existed. The eldest married but died without children.
The second brother then married the widow but likewise died childless. The same occurred with the third brother.
All seven brothers successively married this woman, yet none produced offspring. Finally, the woman herself died.
At the resurrection, whose wife will this woman be, given that all seven brothers married her?”
Jesus replied, “Your error stems from ignorance—both of Scripture and of God’s power.
When people rise from death, earthly marriage institutions cease. Instead, resurrected believers exist like angels in heaven’s realm.
Regarding resurrection itself, have you not carefully read Moses’ account of the burning bush, where God declared to Moses, ‘I am Abraham’s God, Isaac’s God, and Jacob’s God’?
God is not the God of the dead but of the living. Your theological understanding is profoundly mistaken.”

verses.heading: The Great Commandments / The Great Commandments / Matt. 22:34-40; Lk. 10:25-28
verses.text: A scribe who had been observing these exchanges approached Jesus, impressed by His responses. He inquired, “Among all the commandments, which holds primary importance?”
Jesus answered, “The foremost commandment is: ‘Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the one and only Lord.
Love the Lord your God with your complete heart, your entire soul, your full mind, and your total strength.’
The second commandment is: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ No other commandments surpass these in importance.”
The scribe responded approvingly, “Teacher, You speak truthfully. God is absolutely one, with no other deity existing beside Him.
To love God completely—with one’s whole heart, understanding, and strength—and to love one’s neighbor as oneself far exceeds the value of all burnt offerings and ritual sacrifices.”
Observing the scribe’s wise response, Jesus told him, “You are not distant from God’s kingdom.” After this, no one ventured further questions.

verses.heading: Concerning David’s Son / Concerning David’s Son / Matt. 22:41-46; Lk. 20:41-44
verses.text: While teaching in the temple courts, Jesus posed this question: “How can the scribes claim that the Messiah is merely David’s descendant?
David himself, inspired by the Holy Spirit, declared: ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand until I subjugate Your enemies beneath Your feet.’*
David himself addresses Him as ‘Lord’—so how can the Messiah be merely David’s son?” The large crowd listened with delight.

verses.heading: The Denouncing of the Scribes / The Denouncing of the Scribes / Matt. 23:1-36; Lk. 20:45-47
verses.text: In His teaching, Jesus warned: “Beware of the scribes who desire to parade in elaborate robes and receive respectful greetings in public squares,
who seek prominent synagogue seats and honored positions at banquets,
who financially exploit widows while performing lengthy prayers for appearance’s sake. These men will receive the most severe condemnation.”

verses.heading: The Poor Widow’s Contribution / The Poor Widow’s Contribution / Lk. 21:1-4
verses.text: Jesus seated Himself opposite the temple treasury, observing how people deposited their offerings. Numerous wealthy individuals contributed substantial amounts.
Then a destitute widow approached and deposited two tiny copper coins—collectively worth less than a penny.
Jesus summoned His disciples and declared, “I tell you truthfully: this impoverished widow has contributed more than all the other donors combined.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: They gave from their surplus wealth, but she gave from her poverty—she donated everything she possessed, her entire livelihood.” 10-11 Quoted from Ps. 118:22-23 36 Quoted from Ps. 110:1

verses.heading: The Destruction of the Temple Predicted / The Destruction of the Temple Predicted / Matt. 24:1-2; Lk. 21:5-6
verses.text: As Jesus departed the temple courts, one disciple exclaimed to Him, “Teacher, observe these magnificent stones and impressive structures!”
Jesus responded, “You see these grand buildings? Every single stone will be toppled—not one will remain stacked upon another.”

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Beginning of Woes / Eschatological Discourse: The Beginning of Woes / Matt. 24:3-14; Lk. 21:7-19
verses.text: Later, as Jesus sat on the Mount of Olives overlooking the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned Him privately,
“Tell us when these events will occur, and what sign will indicate their imminent fulfillment?”
Jesus began answering: “Guard yourselves against deception.
Numerous imposters will arrive claiming My identity, declaring themselves the Messiah, and will deceive many people.
When you hear about wars and war rumors, do not panic. Such events must transpire, but they do not signal the immediate end.
Nations will wage war against one another, kingdoms will attack kingdoms. Earthquakes will strike various regions. Famines will occur. These represent merely the initial birth pangs.

“Be vigilant concerning your own safety. Authorities will arrest you and hand you over to councils. You will suffer beatings in synagogues and stand trial before governors and monarchs because of your association with Me, providing testimony before them.
The gospel must first be proclaimed throughout all nations before the end arrives.

When they arrest and prosecute you, do not worry beforehand about your defense. Simply speak whatever the Holy Spirit provides at that moment—you will not be speaking independently but through the Spirit.
Brothers will betray brothers to execution, fathers will betray their children, and children will rebel against parents, causing their deaths.
Everyone will hate you because of your allegiance to Me. Yet whoever endures faithfully until the end will experience salvation.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Great Tribulation / Eschatological Discourse: The Great Tribulation / Matt. 24:15-28; Lk. 21:20-24
verses.text: “When you observe the abomination of desolation positioned where it should never be”—let the reader exercise discernment—“then Judean residents must flee immediately to the mountains.
Anyone on a rooftop must not descend or enter the house to retrieve possessions.
Anyone working in the fields must not return home to fetch a cloak.
How terrible it will be for pregnant women and nursing mothers during those days!
Pray that this does not occur during winter.
Those days will bring tribulation unprecedented since God’s creation began, and unmatched thereafter.
Unless the Lord had shortened those days, no one would survive. But for His chosen people’s sake, He has reduced the duration.
“If anyone tells you during that time, ‘Look, here is the Messiah!’ or ‘Look, there He is!’—do not believe it.
False messiahs and false prophets will emerge, performing signs and wonders attempting to deceive even God’s chosen people, if possible.
Remain alert! I have forewarned you about everything.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Coming of the Son of Man / Eschatological Discourse: The Coming of the Son of Man / Matt. 24:29-31; Lk. 21:25-28
verses.text: “Following that tribulation period, the sun will lose its brightness, the moon will cease reflecting light,
stars will plummet from the sky, and celestial powers will be destabilized.
Then people will witness the Son of Man arriving in clouds with tremendous power and glory.
He will dispatch His angels to gather His chosen people from every direction—from earth’s farthest boundaries to heaven’s extremities.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Lesson of the Fig Trees / Eschatological Discourse: The Lesson of the Fig Trees / Matt. 24:32-35; Lk. 21:29-33
verses.text: “Learn this lesson from the fig tree: when its branches become supple and sprout leaves, you recognise summer’s approach.
Similarly, when you observe these events unfolding, recognize that He stands at the threshold.
I tell you truthfully: This generation will not pass away before all these things transpire.
Heaven and earth will eventually cease existing, but My words will never cease being valid.

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Unknown Day and Hour / Eschatological Discourse: The Unknown Day and Hour / Matt. 24:36-44
verses.text: “Concerning that specific day or hour, no one possesses knowledge—not heaven’s angels, not even the Son—only the Father knows.
Stay alert! Remain vigilant! You do not know when the appointed moment arrives.
It resembles a man departing on a journey who leaves his household, delegates authority to his servants, assigns each one specific responsibilities, and commands the doorkeeper to stay watchful.
Therefore remain watchful, since you do not know when the household master returns—whether at evening, midnight, rooster-crow, or dawn,
lest he arrive unexpectedly and discover you sleeping.
What I tell you, I tell everyone: Stay watchful.”

verses.heading: The Conspiracy to Kill Jesus / The Conspiracy to Kill Jesus / Matt. 26:1-5; Lk. 22:1-2; Jn. 11:45-53
verses.text: Two days remained until Passover and the Unleavened Bread festival. Chief priests and scribes were scheming about how to arrest Jesus secretly and execute Him.
They agreed, “We must not act during the festival, or the people might riot.”

verses.heading: Jesus Anointed in Bethany / Jesus Anointed in Bethany / Matt. 26:6-13; Jn. 12:1-8
verses.text: While Jesus dined at Simon the leper’s house in Bethany, a woman arrived carrying an alabaster jar filled with expensive pure nard perfume. She broke the jar’s seal and poured the perfume over Jesus’ head.
Some guests reacted indignantly, muttering, “What waste!
This perfume could have sold for over three hundred denarii—nearly a year’s wages—and the proceeds distributed to the poor.” They rebuked her harshly.
Jesus intervened: “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has performed a beautiful deed for Me.
The poor remain with you constantly, and you can help them whenever you choose. But I will not remain with you much longer.
She has done what she could—she has anointed My body in preparation for burial.
I tell you truthfully: Wherever the gospel is proclaimed worldwide, people will remember and recount her deed.”

verses.heading: Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus / Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus / Matt. 26:14-16; Lk. 22:3-6
verses.text: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve disciples, went to the chief priests offering to betray Jesus to them.
They were delighted and promised him payment. Judas began seeking an opportune moment for betrayal.

verses.heading: Jesus Eats the Passover with His Disciples / Jesus Eats the Passover with His Disciples / Matt. 26:17-25; Lk. 22:7-14, 21-23; Jn. 13:21-30
verses.text: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when Passover lambs were sacrificed, the disciples asked Jesus, “Where should we prepare the Passover meal for You?”
Jesus sent two disciples with instructions: “Enter the city. You will encounter a man carrying a water jar. Follow him.
Tell the house owner: ‘The Teacher asks: Where is My guest room for eating Passover with My disciples?’
He will show you a large upstairs room already prepared. Make our preparations there.”
The disciples departed, found everything exactly as Jesus described, and prepared the Passover meal.
That evening, Jesus arrived with the twelve disciples.
While they reclined eating, Jesus announced, “I tell you truthfully: One of you dining with Me will betray Me.”
They grew distressed, asking Him individually, “Surely not I?”
Jesus answered, “It is one of the twelve—someone sharing this meal with Me.
The Son of Man proceeds along His appointed course as Scripture foretells, but woe to the man who betrays the Son of Man! That man would have been better off never being born.”

verses.heading: The Lord’s Supper Instituted / The Lord’s Supper Instituted / Matt. 6:26-30; Lk. 22:15-20; 1 Cor. 11:23-25
verses.text: During the meal, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it into pieces, distributed it to them, saying, “Take this—it represents My body.”
Then He took a cup, gave thanks, offered it to them, and they all drank from it.
He explained, “This represents My covenant blood, which is being poured out for many people.
I tell you truthfully: I will not drink wine again until that day when I drink it anew in God’s kingdom.”
After singing a hymn, they departed for the Mount of Olives.

verses.heading: Peter’s Denial Foretold / Peter’s Denial Foretold / Matt. 26:31-35; Lk. 22:31-34; Jn. 13 36-38
verses.text: Jesus told them, “You will all abandon Me, for Scripture says: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter.’
However, after My resurrection, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter protested, “Even if everyone else abandons You, I will not!”
Jesus replied, “I tell you truthfully: Today—this very night—before the rooster crows twice, you will deny knowing Me three times.”
Peter insisted more emphatically, “Even if I must die with You, I will never deny You!” All the others made similar declarations.

verses.heading: Jesus Prays in Gethsemane / Jesus Prays in Gethsemane / Matt. 26:36-46; Lk. 22:39-46
verses.text: They arrived at an olive grove called Gethsemane. Jesus instructed His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
He took Peter, James, and John with Him. He began experiencing profound anguish and distress.
He told them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
Going a short distance away, He fell to the ground, praying that if possible, this hour might pass from Him.
He prayed, “Abba, Father, everything is possible for You. Take this cup of suffering away from Me. Yet not what I want, but what You want.”
Returning, He found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Could you not stay awake one hour?
Stay alert and pray so you will not succumb to temptation. Your spirit is willing, but your flesh is weak.”
He went away again and prayed, repeating the same words.
When He returned, He found them sleeping again—their eyes were heavy with exhaustion. They did not know how to respond to Him.
He came a third time and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being betrayed into sinners’ hands.
Get up! Let us go! My betrayer approaches!”

verses.heading: The Betrayal and Arrest of Jesus / The Betrayal and Arrest of Jesus / Matt. 26:47-56; Lk. 22:47-53; Jn. 18:3-12
verses.text: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, appeared with a mob carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
The betrayer had arranged a signal: “The man I kiss is Jesus. Arrest Him and guard Him securely.”
Judas immediately approached Jesus, said “Rabbi,” and kissed Him.
The mob seized Jesus and arrested Him.
One of those standing nearby drew a sword, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
Jesus responded, “Have you come with swords and clubs to arrest Me as if I were a dangerous criminal?
Daily I was teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me there. But Scripture must be fulfilled.”
Then all the disciples abandoned Jesus and fled.

verses.heading: A Young Man Who Fled / A Young Man Who Fled
verses.text: A certain young man followed Jesus, wearing only a linen cloth around his body. When the mob seized him,
he abandoned the cloth and escaped naked.

verses.heading: Jesus Before the Sanhedrin / Jesus Before the Sanhedrin / Matt. 26:57-68; Lk. 22:54-55, 63-71; Jn.18:13-14, 19-24
verses.text: They took Jesus to the high priest’s residence, where all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled.
Peter followed at a distance into the high priest’s courtyard. He sat with the guards, warming himself by the fire.
The chief priests and entire Sanhedrin sought testimony against Jesus sufficient for execution, but found none.
Many witnesses gave false testimony against Him, but their accounts contradicted each other.
Some stood and testified falsely:
“We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this human-made temple and in three days build another not made by human hands.’ ”
Even then their testimony did not agree.
The high priest stood in the center and questioned Jesus: “Have You no response to these accusations?”
Jesus remained silent and offered no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him: “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
Jesus declared, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man seated at the Mighty One’s right hand and coming with heaven’s clouds.”
The high priest tore his robes, exclaiming, “Why do we need additional witnesses?
You have heard His blasphemy! What is your verdict?” They all condemned Him as deserving death.
Some began spitting on Him, blindfolding Him, and striking Him, taunting, “Prophesy!” The guards beat Him with their fists.

verses.heading: Peter Denies Jesus / Peter Denies Jesus / Matt. 26:69-75; Lk. 22:56-62; Jn. 18:15-18, 25-27
verses.text: While Peter remained below in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s servant girls approached.
Seeing Peter warming himself, she looked directly at him and said, “You were also with Jesus the Nazarene.”
But Peter denied it: “I neither know nor understand what you are talking about!” He went out to the entrance area, and a rooster crowed.
The servant girl saw him again and began telling the bystanders, “This man is one of them!”
Peter denied it again. Shortly afterward, the bystanders said to Peter, “You certainly are one of them—you are a Galilean.”
Peter began cursing and swearing, “I do not know this man you are talking about!”
Immediately a rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered Jesus’ words: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” He broke down and wept.

verses.heading: Jesus Before Pilate / Jesus Before Pilate / Matt. 27:1-2, 11-14; Lk. 23:1-5; Jn. 18:28-38
verses.text: At daybreak, the chief priests convened with the elders, scribes, and the entire Sanhedrin. After reaching a decision, they bound Jesus, led Him away, and delivered Him to Pilate.
Pilate interrogated Him: “Are You the King of the Jews?” Jesus replied, “You have said so.”
The chief priests leveled numerous accusations against Him.
Pilate questioned Him again: “Are You not going to respond? Consider how many charges they are bringing against You!”
Jesus offered no further response, which amazed Pilate.

verses.heading: Jesus Sentenced to Die / Jesus Sentenced to Die / Matt. 27:15-26; Lk. 23:13-25; Jn. 18:39-19:16
verses.text: During the festival, Pilate customarily released one prisoner chosen by the crowd.
A prisoner named Barabbas was incarcerated with rebels who had committed murder during an insurrection.
The crowd arrived and began requesting that Pilate follow his usual custom.
Pilate asked them, “Do you want me to release the King of the Jews for you?”
He recognized that the chief priests had delivered Jesus over because of envy.
However, the chief priests incited the crowd to request Barabbas’ release instead.
Pilate asked them again, “Then what should I do with the one you call the King of the Jews?”
They shouted back, “Crucify Him!”
Pilate asked, ‘Why? What crime has He committed?” But they shouted even louder, “Crucify Him!”
Wanting to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas. After having Jesus flogged, he handed Him over for crucifixion.

verses.heading: Jesus Mocked by the Soldiers / Jesus Mocked by the Soldiers / Matt. 27:27-31; Jn. 19:2-3
verses.text: The soldiers led Jesus inside the palace (the Praetorium) and assembled the entire regiment.
They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a thorn crown, and placed it on His head.
They began saluting Him mockingly: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They repeatedly struck His head with a reed, spit on Him, and knelt before Him in mock worship.
After mocking Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.

verses.heading: The Crucifixion of Jesus / The Crucifixion of Jesus / Matt. 27:32-44; Lk. 23:26-43; Jn. 19:17-27
verses.text: They forced a passerby named Simon from Cyrene—father of Alexander and Rufus—who was coming from the countryside, to carry Jesus’ cross.
They brought Jesus to Golgotha (meaning “Skull Place”).
They offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He refused it.
They crucified Him and divided His clothing among themselves, casting lots to determine each person’s share.
It was nine o’clock in the morning when they crucified Him.
The written charge against Him read: “The King of the Jews.”
They crucified two criminals with Him—one on His right, one on His left.*
Passersby hurled insults, shaking their heads and saying, “Ha! You who would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
save Yourself by coming down from the cross!”
Similarly, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves: “He saved others; He cannot save Himself!
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, descend from the cross now so we can see and believe!” Even those crucified with Him hurled insults at Him.

verses.heading: The Death of Jesus / The Death of Jesus / Matt. 27:45-56; Lk. 23:44-49; Jn. 19:28-30
verses.text: At the sixth hour (noon), darkness covered the entire land until the ninth hour (three o’clock in the afternoon).
At three o’clock, Jesus cried out loudly, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?”—which translates, “My God, My God, why have You abandoned Me?”
Some bystanders heard this and said, “Listen, He is calling Elijah!”
Someone ran, soaked a sponge in sour wine, put it on a reed, and offered Him a drink, saying, “Wait! Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
Jesus uttered a loud cry and breathed His last.
The temple curtain tore in two from top to bottom.
When the centurion standing opposite Jesus saw how He died, he declared, “This man truly was God’s Son!”
Women were watching from a distance, including Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, and Salome.
These women had followed Jesus and served Him while He was in Galilee. Many other women who had come to Jerusalem with Him were also there.

verses.heading: The Burial of Jesus / The Burial of Jesus / Matt. 27:57-61; Lk. 23:50-56; Jn. 19:38-42
verses.text: Evening arrived. Since it was Preparation Day (the day before the Sabbath),
Joseph from Arimathea, a respected council member who was himself anticipating God’s kingdom, courageously approached Pilate and requested Jesus’ body.
Pilate was surprised that Jesus had already died. Summoning the centurion, he asked if Jesus was already dead.
After learning from the centurion, Pilate granted the body to Joseph.
Joseph purchased a linen cloth, took Jesus down from the cross, wrapped Him in the cloth, and placed Him in a tomb carved from rock. He rolled a stone against the tomb entrance.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses observed where Jesus was laid. 27 A textual variant present in part of the manuscript tradition expands the passage by inserting a fulfillment formula—“ And the Scripture was fulfilled which says, ‘And He was counted with the transgressors’’ —thereby creating a new verse (v. 28 in some versions). This insertion achieves a degree of harmonization with the parallel account in John 19:23-24.
verses.html:
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses observed where Jesus was laid.
27 A textual variant present in part of the manuscript tradition expands the passage by inserting a fulfillment formula—“ And the Scripture was fulfilled which says, ‘And He was counted with the transgressors’’ —thereby creating a new verse (v. 28 in some versions). This insertion achieves a degree of harmonization with the parallel account in John 19:23-24.

verses.heading: The Resurrection of Jesus / The Resurrection of Jesus / Matt. 28:1-8; Lk. 24:1-12; Jn. 20:1-10
verses.text: When the Sabbath ended, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome purchased aromatic spices to anoint Jesus’ body.
Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.
They were discussing among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone from the tomb entrance for us?”
Looking up, they saw that the stone—which was extremely large—had already been rolled away.
Entering the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side. They were alarmed.
He told them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here. See the place where they laid Him.
Now go tell His disciples and Peter: ‘He is going ahead of you to Galilee. You will see Him there, just as He told you.’ ”
Trembling and bewildered, they fled from the tomb. They said nothing to anyone because they were afraid.

verses.heading: The Appearance of Jesus to Mary Magdalene / The Appearance of Jesus to Mary Magdalene / Matt. 28:9-10; Jn. 20:11-18
verses.text: [[After rising early on the first day of the week, Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had expelled seven demons.
She went and reported this to those who had been with Him, who were mourning and weeping.
When they heard that Jesus was alive and that she had seen Him, they did not believe her.
Afterward, Jesus appeared in a different form to the two of them while they were walking in the countryside.
They returned and reported this to the others, but they did not believe them either.

verses.heading: The Great Commission / The Great Commission / Matt. 28:16-20; Lk. 24:36-49; Jn. 20:19-23; Acts 1:6-8
verses.text: Later, Jesus appeared to the eleven disciples as they were eating. He rebuked them for their lack of faith and stubborn refusal to believe those who had seen Him after His resurrection.
He told them, “Go throughout the world and proclaim the gospel to all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever refuses to believe will be condemned.
These signs will accompany believers: In My name they will drive out demons, they will speak in new tongues,
they will handle serpents, and if they drink anything poisonous, it will not harm them. They will place their hands on sick people, and they will recover.”
After speaking to them, the Lord Jesus was taken up into heaven and sat at God’s right hand.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: The disciples went out and preached everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed His message through accompanying signs.]]* 9-20 Mark 9:20 is not found in key early manuscripts, indicating that the Gospel likely ended at 8:39 in its original form, with the longer ending possibly being a later addition

verses.heading: Introduction / Introduction
verses.text: Since many others have already undertaken the task of compiling an orderly narrative account concerning the events that have been accomplished among us by God’s sovereign plan,
just as those who were eyewitnesses from the very beginning and who became servants of the word have handed down these accounts to us through careful testimony,

it seemed good and appropriate to me also, having carefully investigated and traced all these things accurately from the very beginning, to write them down for you in an orderly and sequential manner, most excellent Theophilus.
I write so that you may know with certainty and have full assurance concerning the matters about which you have been instructed.

verses.heading: Prophecy Regarding the Birth of John / Prophecy Regarding the Birth of John
verses.text: During the reign of Herod, who was king of Judea, there lived a certain priest named Zechariah who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah. His wife was a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, and her name was Elizabeth.
Both of them were righteous in God’s sight, walking blamelessly and faithfully in all the commandments and ordinances that the Lord had given.
However, they had no child because Elizabeth was barren and unable to conceive. Moreover, both of them were now advanced in years, well past the normal age for childbearing.
One day, while Zechariah was serving as priest before God during his division’s appointed turn of service in the temple,
he was chosen by lot according to the established custom of the priesthood to enter the temple sanctuary of the Lord and burn the incense offering.
At that sacred hour when the incense was being burned, the whole assembled crowd of people was praying outside in the courtyard.
Then an angel of the Lord suddenly appeared to Zechariah, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.
When Zechariah saw the angel, he was troubled, and fear overwhelmed him.
But the angel spoke reassuringly to him, saying, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah. Your prayer has been heard and answered by God. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to name him John.
He will bring you great joy and gladness, and many people will rejoice at his birth.

For he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He must never drink wine or any strong drink, maintaining a Nazirite-like consecration. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit even while still in his mother’s womb.
He will turn many of the children of Israel back to the Lord their God in repentance.

He will go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah the prophet, turning the hearts of fathers back to their children and turning the disobedient to embrace the wisdom of the righteous. In this way, he will make ready for the Lord a people who are fully prepared for His coming.”
Zechariah responded to the angel with doubt, saying, “How can I be certain that this will happen? By what means will I know this is true? I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years.”
The angel answered him, saying, “I am Gabriel, who stands continually in the very presence of God. I have been sent specifically to speak to you and to announce to you this good news.

Listen carefully: You will become silent and unable to speak until the day these things actually take place, because you did not believe my words, which will certainly be fulfilled at their appointed time.”
Meanwhile, the people outside were waiting for Zechariah, and they began to wonder at his unusual delay in the temple.

When he finally came out, he was unable to speak to them. They quickly realized that he must have seen a vision while in the temple. He kept making signs and gestures to them, but remained unable to speak.
When the days of his appointed priestly service came to an end, he departed from the temple and returned to his home.
After these days, his wife Elizabeth conceived a child. She secluded herself in private for five months, saying with thanksgiving,
“This is what the Lord has done for me in these days when He looked upon me with favor, removing my disgrace and reproach among people.”

verses.heading: Prophecy Regarding the Birth of Jesus / Prophecy Regarding the Birth of Jesus
verses.text: In the sixth month of Elizabeth’s pregnancy, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a town in the region of Galilee named Nazareth,
to a virgin who was legally pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, a descendant of the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.
The angel came to her and said, “Greetings, you who have been highly favored by God! The Lord is with you in a special way.”
But Mary was deeply troubled at this greeting, and she kept pondering in her mind what kind of greeting this might be.
The angel said to her reassuringly, “Do not be afraid, Mary. You have found favor with God.
Listen: You will conceive in your womb and give birth to a Son, and you are to name Him Jesus.
This Child will be great and magnificent. He will be called the Son of the Most High God. The Lord God will give to Him the throne of His ancestor David,
and He will reign over the house of Jacob forever and ever. His kingdom will have no end—it will be eternal.”
Mary said to the angel, “How can this be? How will this happen, since I am a virgin?”

The angel answered her, saying, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you in power, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you like a cloud of glory. Therefore, the Holy One who will be born will be called the Son of God.
Moreover, Elizabeth your relative has also conceived a son in her old age. This is now the sixth month of pregnancy for her who was called barren.
For nothing will be impossible with God. No word from God will ever fail to be fulfilled.”

Mary responded in faith and submission, “Behold, I am the maidservant of the Lord, fully surrendered to His will. May it happen to me exactly according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her presence.

verses.heading: Mary Visits Elizabeth / Mary Visits Elizabeth
verses.text: In those days, Mary arose and traveled with eagerness into the hill country, to a town belonging to the tribe of Judah.
She entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby in her womb leaped for joy. Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and given supernatural insight.
She cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Blessed are you among all women, and blessed is the Child you carry in your womb!
Why has this gracious thing happened to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to visit me?
For the moment the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy and excitement.
Blessed is she who believed that there would be a complete fulfillment of what was spoken to her from the Lord.”

verses.heading: The Magnificat / The Magnificat
verses.text: Mary responded with a song of praise, saying, “My soul magnifies and exalts the Lord,
and my spirit has rejoiced greatly in God my Savior,
for He has looked with favor upon the humble and lowly state of His maidservant. For look, from this moment forward, all generations throughout history will count me blessed and favored,
because the Mighty One has done great and magnificent things for me, and holy is His name.
His mercy extends to those who fear Him with reverence, from generation to generation throughout all time.
He has demonstrated mighty power with His arm. He has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts and intentions of their hearts.
He has brought down rulers and the powerful from their thrones, and He has exalted and lifted up those who are lowly and humble.
He has filled those who are hungry with good things, and those who are rich He has sent away empty-handed.
He has helped Israel His servant, remembering and fulfilling His mercy,
just as He spoke and promised to our fathers, to Abraham and to his descendants forever.”
Mary remained with Elizabeth for approximately three months, then returned to her own home.

verses.heading: The Birth of John / The Birth of John
verses.text: The time was fulfilled for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.
Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had greatly demonstrated His mercy to her, and they began to rejoice together with her.
On the eighth day, according to Jewish custom, they came to circumcise the child. They wanted to name him after his father, calling him Zechariah.
But his mother spoke up and said, “No, he will not be named after his father. He will be called John.”
They protested to her, “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.”
So they made signs to his father Zechariah, inquiring what he would like the child to be called.
Zechariah asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “John is his name.” Everyone present marveled at this.
Immediately Zechariah’s mouth and tongue were opened and freed. He began to speak, blessing and praising God.
Fear and awe came upon all those who lived in the surrounding area, and all these remarkable events were being talked about throughout the entire hill country of Judea.

All those who heard about these things kept them in their hearts, pondering them and saying, “What then will this child become? What is his destiny?” For it was evident that the hand of the Lord was powerfully with him.

verses.heading: Zechariah’s Prophecy / Zechariah’s Prophecy
verses.text: Zechariah, the child’s father, was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
“Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited His people and accomplished redemption for them.
He has raised up a horn of salvation—a mighty Savior—for us in the house of David, His servant,
just as He spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from ancient times,
promising salvation and deliverance from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us.
He has acted to show mercy to our fathers and to remember His holy covenant,
the oath which He swore to Abraham our father. He promised to grant us
that we, having been delivered from the hand of our enemies, might serve Him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before Him all the days of our lives.
And you, my child, will be called the prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare His ways,
giving to His people the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins.
This will happen because of the tender mercy and compassion of our God, by which the Sunrise from on high—the Messiah—will visit us.
He will shine as light on those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, and He will guide our feet into the way of peace.”
The child John continued to grow physically and to become strong in spirit. He lived in the desert places until the day of his public appearance and ministry to Israel.

verses.heading: The Birth of Jesus / The Birth of Jesus / Matt. 1:18-25
verses.text: In those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus, the Roman emperor, that a census should be taken to register all the inhabited world under Roman rule.
This registration was the first of its kind, taking place when Quirinius was serving as governor of Syria.
Everyone went to be registered for the census, each person traveling to his own ancestral town.
