Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David which is called Bethlehem. He made this journey because he was a descendant of the house and family line of David.
He went to be registered along with Mary, who was legally pledged to be married to him and who was expecting a Child.
While they were in Bethlehem, the time came for Mary to give birth.
She gave birth to her firstborn Son, wrapped Him in swaddling cloths to keep Him warm, and laid Him in a manger—a feeding trough for animals—because there was no room available for them in the inn.

verses.heading: The Shepherds and the Angels / The Shepherds and the Angels
verses.text: In that same region, there were shepherds living out in the fields, keeping watch over their flock during the night.
An angel of the Lord suddenly stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone brilliantly around them. They were terrified and filled with great fear.
The angel said to them, “Do not be afraid! I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all people.
Today in the city of David, a Savior has been born to you. He is Christ the Lord—the Messiah!
This will be the sign for you to identify Him: You will find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.”
Suddenly there appeared with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host—a vast army of angels—praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those with whom He is pleased!”

When the angels had departed from them and returned to heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let us go immediately to Bethlehem and see this thing that has taken place, which the Lord has made known to us.”
They came quickly and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger, just as they had been told.
When they saw the Child, they made known to everyone the message that had been told to them by the angels concerning this Child.
All who heard the shepherds’ report marveled at what had been told to them.
But Mary treasured all these words and events, pondering them carefully in her heart.
Then the shepherds returned to their flocks, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen. It was exactly as it had been told to them.

When eight days were fulfilled and the time came for Him to be circumcised according to Jewish law, He was given the name Jesus—the name He had been called by the angel before He was conceived in the womb.

verses.heading: Jesus Presented in the Temple / Jesus Presented in the Temple
verses.text: When the days of their purification were completed according to the Law of Moses, Joseph and Mary brought Jesus up to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord.
This was done as it is written in the Law of the Lord: “Every firstborn male who opens the womb shall be consecrated and called holy to the Lord.”
They also came to offer a sacrifice according to what is stated in the Law of the Lord: “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

verses.heading: The Prophecy of Simeon / The Prophecy of Simeon
verses.text: There was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, eagerly waiting for the consolation of Israel—the coming of the Messiah. The Holy Spirit rested upon him.
It had been divinely revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not experience death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ—the Messiah.
Moved by the Spirit, he came into the temple courts. When the parents brought in the child Jesus to perform for Him the customary requirements prescribed by the Law,
Simeon took Jesus in his arms, blessed God with thanksgiving, and said:
“Now, Lord, You are releasing Your servant to depart in peace, according to Your word and promise,
for my eyes have seen Your salvation,
which You have made ready in the sight of all peoples everywhere—
a light that will bring revelation to the Gentiles, and glory to Your people Israel.”
Joseph and Mary, His earthly parents, were filled with wonder at what was being said concerning Him.

Simeon blessed them and said to Mary His mother, “Listen carefully: This Child is appointed to cause the fall and rising of many in Israel. He will be a sign that will be spoken against and rejected by many.
A sword will pierce through your own soul as well, bringing you deep anguish. All this will happen so that the hidden thoughts and intentions of many hearts may be revealed and exposed.”

verses.heading: Prophetess Anna / Prophetess Anna
verses.text: There was also a prophetess named Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She was very advanced in years, having lived with her husband seven years after her marriage.
Then she lived as a widow until she reached the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple courts, but worshiped God continually night and day with fasting and prayers.

At that very moment when Simeon was speaking, she approached them. She began to give thanks to God and to speak about the Child to all those who were waiting expectantly for the redemption of Jerusalem.

verses.heading: The Boy Jesus / The Boy Jesus
verses.text: When Joseph and Mary had completed everything required according to the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The Child continued to grow physically and to become strong in body. He was filled with wisdom beyond His years, and the gracious favor of God rested upon Him.

verses.heading: Jesus at the Temple / Jesus at the Temple
verses.text: Every year His parents would travel to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover, as faithful Jews.
When Jesus was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast.
After they had completed the days of celebration and were returning home, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem. His parents did not realize this.
Assuming He was somewhere in their traveling company, they went a full day’s journey before they began searching for Him among their relatives and acquaintances.
When they did not find Him, they returned anxiously to Jerusalem, searching for Him.
After three days of searching, they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers of the Law, both listening to them and asking them insightful questions.
All who heard Him were astonished at His understanding and His answers.

When His parents saw Him, they were struck with amazement. His mother said to Him, “Child, why have You treated us this way? Your father and I have been distressed and anxious, searching everywhere for You.”
Jesus said to them, “Why were you searching for Me? Did you not know that it was necessary for Me to be in My Father’s house, occupied with My Father's business?”
But they did not understand the profound meaning of what He was saying to them.
Then Jesus went down with them and returned to Nazareth. He continued to be submissive to them in all things. His mother continued to treasure all these events in her heart.
Jesus continued to grow in wisdom and in physical stature, and He increased in favor with both God and people.

verses.heading: John the Baptist Prepares the Way / John the Baptist Prepares the Way / Matt. 3:1-12; Mk. 1:1-8; Jn. 1:19-28
verses.text: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar as Roman emperor, when Pontius Pilate was serving as governor of Judea, and Herod was tetrarch ruling over Galilee, and his brother Philip was tetrarch of the region of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene—
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came powerfully upon John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
John went throughout all the surrounding region of the Jordan River, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
This fulfilled what is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “The voice of one calling out in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make His paths straight and ready.
Every valley shall be filled in, and every mountain and hill shall be leveled. The crooked places shall become straight, and the rough places shall become smooth paths.
Then all humanity will see the salvation of God.’ ”*
Therefore John was saying to the crowds that came out to be baptized by him, “You offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath of God?

Produce fruit that is appropriate to and consistent with repentance. Do not even begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ I tell you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones!
Even now the axe is laid at the root of the trees, ready to cut. Therefore, every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire of judgment.”
The crowds were asking him, “What then should we do? How should we demonstrate true repentance?”
John would answer them, saying, “The one who has two tunics should share with the one who has none. The one who has food should do the same and share with those in need.”
Even tax collectors—despised for their collaboration with Rome—came to be baptized. They said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He said to them, “Collect no more tax money than what has been prescribed for you. Do not use your position to extort people.”

Soldiers who were serving in the military were also asking him, “What should we also do?” He said to them, “Do not extort money from anyone by threats or false accusations. Be satisfied with your wages.”
As the people were filled with expectation, and all were questioning in their hearts concerning John, wondering whether he might possibly be the Christ,

John answered them all, saying, “I baptize you with water as a symbol of repentance, but One who is mightier and more powerful than I is coming. I am not worthy even to untie the strap of His sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His winnowing fork is in His hand, ready to thoroughly clean out His threshing floor. He will gather the wheat into His barn, but the chaff He will burn up with unquenchable fire.”
With many other exhortations and warnings, John kept preaching the good news to the people.

But Herod the tetrarch, who had been reproved and rebuked by John concerning Herodias—the wife of his brother Philip whom Herod had unlawfully taken—and concerning all the evil acts that Herod had committed,
added this sin to all the others: He also confined John in prison, silencing the prophet.

verses.heading: The Baptism of Jesus / The Baptism of Jesus / Matt. 3:13-17; Mk. 1:9-11
verses.text: When all the people were being baptized, Jesus also was baptized. While He was praying after His baptism, heaven was opened,
and the Holy Spirit descended upon Him in bodily form like a dove. A voice came from heaven, declaring, “You are My Son, the Beloved One. In You I am well pleased.”

verses.heading: The Genealogy of Jesus / The Genealogy of Jesus / Matt. 1:1-17
verses.text: Jesus Himself was about thirty years old when He began His public ministry. He was the son, as people supposed, of Joseph, who was the son of Heli,
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
the son of Joshua, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Sala, the son of Nahshon,
the son of Amminadab, the son of Admin, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God. 6 Quoted from Is. 40:3-5

verses.heading: The Temptation of Jesus / The Temptation of Jesus / Matt. 4:1-11; Mk. 1:12-13
verses.text: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan River. He was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
for forty days, where He was being tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they came to an end, He was hungry and physically weak.
The devil said to Him, “If You are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.”
But Jesus answered him, “It is written in Scripture: ‘Man shall not live by bread alone.’ ”*
Then the devil led Him up to a high place and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a single instant of time.
The devil said to Him, “I will give You all this authority and glory, for it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
Therefore, if You will worship before me, all this will be Yours.”
But Jesus answered him, “It is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him alone you shall serve.’ ”*
Then the devil brought Jesus to Jerusalem and set Him on the highest point of the temple. He said to Him, “If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down from here,
for it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You, to guard You,’
and ‘On their hands they will bear You up, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’ ”
Jesus answered him, “It has been said: ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’ ”*
When the devil had finished every form and type of temptation, he withdrew from Jesus to wait for a more opportune time.

verses.heading: The Beginning of Jesus’ Galilean Ministry / The Beginning of Jesus’ Galilean Ministry / Matt. 4:12-17; Mk. 1:14-15
verses.text: Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit. News and reports about Him spread throughout all the surrounding region.
He was teaching in their synagogues, and He was being praised and glorified by everyone.

verses.heading: The Rejection of Jesus in Nazareth / The Rejection of Jesus in Nazareth / Matt. 13:53-58; Mk. 6:1-6
verses.text: Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up as a child. According to His custom on the Sabbath day, He went into the synagogue and stood up to read from Scripture.
The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him. He unrolled the scroll and found the place where it was written:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim freedom to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind, to set free those who are oppressed,
to proclaim the favorable year of the Lord’s grace.”*
He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down to teach. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed intently on Him, waiting to hear what He would say.
Jesus began to say to them, “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing—I am the One this prophecy speaks of.”

All were bearing witness to Him and were marveling at the gracious words that were coming from His mouth. Yet they were also saying with skepticism, “Is this not Joseph’s son? How can He claim such things?”
Jesus said to them, “Surely you will quote to Me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself.’ You are thinking, ‘Whatever we heard happened in Capernaum, do here in Your hometown as well.’ ”
He continued, “Truly, I tell you that no prophet is accepted and honored in his own hometown.
But I tell you the truth: There were many widows in Israel during the time of Elijah, when the sky was shut up for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land.*
Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but only to a widow in Zarephath, in the region of Sidon—a Gentile woman.*
There were also many lepers in Israel during the time of Elisha the prophet, yet none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian—another Gentile.”*
When they heard these things, all in the synagogue were filled with rage.
They rose up, drove Him out of the city, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, intending to throw Him down the cliff to His death.
But passing through the midst of them supernaturally, He went on His way.

verses.heading: The Healing of a Man with a Spirit of an Unclean Demon / The Healing of a Man with a Spirit of an Unclean Demon / Mk. 1:21-28
verses.text: Jesus went down to Capernaum, a city in Galilee. He was teaching the people on the Sabbath day,
and they were utterly astonished at His teaching, because His word carried divine authority.
In the synagogue there was a man who had the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice,
“Ha! What do You have to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us before our time? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked the demon, commanding, “Be silent and come out of him!” After the demon had thrown the man down violently in their midst, it came out of him without doing him any lasting injury.
Amazement came over all the people, and they were saying to one another, “What kind of word is this? He commands the unclean spirits with authority and power, and they come out!”
Reports about Jesus were spreading rapidly into every place in the surrounding region.

verses.heading: The Healing of Many / The Healing of Many / Matt. 8:14-17; Mk. 1:29-34
verses.text: Jesus left the synagogue and went into Simon Peter’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they appealed to Jesus on her behalf.
Standing over her, Jesus rebuked the fever with authority, and it left her immediately. She got up at once and began to serve them.
As the sun was setting and the Sabbath was ending, all those who had people sick with various diseases brought them to Jesus. He laid His hands on each one of them individually and healed them.

Demons also were coming out from many people, crying out and saying, “You are the Son of God!” But Jesus rebuked them sternly and would not allow them to speak, because they knew Him to be the Christ.

verses.heading: Extension of Jesus’ Preaching Ministry / Extension of Jesus’ Preaching Ministry / Mk. 1:35-39
verses.text: When daylight came, Jesus left the house and went to a deserted place to pray. The crowds were looking for Him eagerly, and when they found Him, they tried to prevent Him from leaving them.
But He said to them, “It is necessary for Me to preach the gospel of the kingdom of God to the other cities as well, because this is the purpose for which I was sent by the Father.”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: He continued preaching in the synagogues throughout Judea, proclaiming the good news of God’s kingdom. 4 Quote from Deut. 8:3 8 Quoted from Deut. 6:13 12 Quoted from Deut. 6:16 18-19 Quoted from Is. 61:1-2 25 This is a reference to 1 Kgs. 17:1; 18:1 26 This is a reference to 1 Kgs. 17:9 27 This is a reference to 2 Kgs. 5:1-14

verses.heading: The First Disciples of Jesus / The First Disciples of Jesus / Matt. 4:18-22; Mk. 1:16-20
verses.text: On one occasion, as the crowd was pressing in on Jesus to hear the word of God, He was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret—also known as the Sea of Galilee.
He saw two boats lying at the water’s edge. The fishermen had gotten out of them and were washing their nets after a night of fishing.
Jesus got into one of the boats, which belonged to Simon Peter. He asked Simon to put out a little distance from the shore. Then Jesus sat down and began to teach the crowds from the boat.
When He had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into the deep water, and let down your nets for a catch.”
Simon answered and said, “Master, we worked hard throughout the entire night and caught nothing at all. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”
When they did this, they enclosed such a very large number of fish that their nets began to tear from the weight.
They signaled frantically to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats so full that the boats began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw this miraculous catch, he fell down at Jesus’ knees in awe, saying, “Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man!”
Amazement had seized him and all those with him at the overwhelming catch of fish they had taken.
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners, were similarly amazed. But Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid. From now on you will be catching men for the kingdom of God.”
When they had brought their boats to shore, they left everything behind—their livelihood, their security—and followed Jesus.

verses.heading: The Cleansing of a Leper / The Cleansing of a Leper / Matt. 8:1-4; Mk. 1:40-45
verses.text: While Jesus was in one of the cities, a man appeared who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged Him, saying, “Lord, if You are willing, You have the power to make me clean.”
Jesus stretched out His hand and touched him—an act that would normally make someone ceremonially unclean. He said, “I am willing. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.

Jesus commanded him, “Tell no one about this. But go and show yourself to the priest for examination, and make an offering for your cleansing just as Moses commanded in the Law. This will serve as evidence to them of your healing.”

verses.heading: Jesus’ Habitual Ministry and Prayer Life / Jesus’ Habitual Ministry and Prayer Life
verses.text: But the news about Jesus kept spreading even more widely, and large crowds would gather to hear Him teach and to be healed from their sicknesses.
Yet Jesus Himself would often withdraw quietly to deserted places to pray.

verses.heading: The Healing of a Paralytic / The Healing of a Paralytic / Matt. 9:1-8; Mk. 2:1-12
verses.text: On one of those days, while Jesus was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the Law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem, to investigate Him. The power of the Lord was present for Jesus to perform healings.
Some men came carrying on a stretcher a man who was paralyzed. They were trying to bring him inside and set him before Jesus.

When they could not find a way to bring him in because of the dense crowd, they went up on the roof. They removed the tiles and lowered him on his mat down through the opening into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw their faith—demonstrated by their persistent effort—He said, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”
The scribes and Pharisees began to question and reason, saying, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemies? Who has the authority to forgive sins except God alone?”
But Jesus, knowing their thoughts and reasoning, answered them, “Why are you questioning these things in your hearts?
Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—He said to the paralyzed man—“I say to you, get up, take up your mat, and go to your house.”
Immediately the man stood up before them, picked up what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
Astonishment seized everyone present, and they began to glorify God. They were filled with awe, saying, "We have seen extraordinary and remarkable things today.”

verses.heading: The Calling of Levi / The Calling of Levi / Matt. 9:9-13; Mk. 2:13-17
verses.text: After these events, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax collection booth. Jesus said to him, “Follow Me.”
Levi left everything behind, got up immediately, and began to follow Jesus, abandoning his lucrative but despised occupation.
Levi held a great banquet for Jesus in his house. A large crowd of tax collectors and others were reclining at the table with them.
The Pharisees and their scribes began to complain to Jesus’ disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “Those who are in good health have no need of a physician, but those who are sick do.
I have not come to call the righteous who think they have no need, but sinners to repentance.”

verses.heading: Question Regarding Fasting / Question Regarding Fasting / Matt. 9:14-17; Mk. 2:18-22
verses.text: They said to Jesus, “The disciples of John the Baptist fast frequently and offer prayers regularly. Likewise, the disciples of the Pharisees do the same. But Your disciples are eating and drinking freely.”
Jesus responded, “Can you make the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them?
But days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days when I am gone.”
Jesus also told them a parable: “No one tears a patch from a new garment and sews it on an old garment. If he does, he will ruin the new garment, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
No one puts new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the wineskins as it ferments. The wine will be spilled, and the wineskins will be ruined.
Instead, new wine must be put into fresh wineskins so both are preserved.
No one who has been drinking old wine immediately desires the new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’ ”

verses.heading: Plucking and Eating Heads of Grain on the Sabbath / Plucking and Eating Heads of Grain on the Sabbath / Matt. 12:1-8; Mk. 2:23-28
verses.text: On a Sabbath day, Jesus was passing through grainfields. His disciples were plucking and eating the heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands to remove the husks.
Some of the Pharisees challenged them, saying, “Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
Jesus answered them, “Have you not read in Scripture what David did when he and those with him were hungry?*
He entered the house of God and took the consecrated bread of the Presence, ate it, and gave some to those with him. This bread was not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests alone.”
Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.” He has authority over the Sabbath and its proper observance.

verses.heading: Jesus Heals a Man with a Withered Hand / Jesus Heals a Man with a Withered Hand / Matt. 12:9-14; Mk. 3:1-6
verses.text: On another Sabbath, Jesus entered the synagogue and began to teach. A man was there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and Pharisees were watching Jesus carefully to see if He would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find grounds to accuse Him.
But Jesus knew their thoughts and intentions. He said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand here in the middle where everyone can see.” The man rose and stood there.
Jesus said to them, “I ask you: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to destroy it?”
He looked around at all of them, then said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and his hand was completely restored.
But the Pharisees were filled with fury. They began discussing among themselves what they might do to Jesus.

verses.heading: The Choosing of the Twelve / The Choosing of the Twelve / Matt. 10:1-4; Mk. 3:13-19
verses.text: In those days, Jesus went out to the mountain to pray. He spent the entire night in prayer to God—seeking the Father’s will.
When day came, He summoned His disciples to Himself and chose twelve from among them, whom He also named apostles—meaning “sent ones”:
Simon, whom He also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon who was called the Zealot,
Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became the traitor.

verses.heading: Jesus Before a Great Multitude / Jesus Before a Great Multitude / Matt. 4:23-25
verses.text: Jesus descended from the mountain with the twelve and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great multitude of people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon.
They had come to hear Him teach and to be healed of their diseases. Those who were troubled and tormented by unclean spirits were also being healed.
The whole crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was flowing out from Him and healing everyone.

verses.heading: The Sermon on the Plain: Blessings and Woes / The Sermon on the Plain: Blessings and Woes / Matt. 5:1-12
verses.text: Jesus lifted up His eyes toward His disciples and began to teach, saying: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you who are hungry now for righteousness, for you will be satisfied. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh with joy.
Blessed are you when people hate you, when they exclude you from their fellowship, when they insult and defame you, and when they reject your name as evil on account of the Son of Man.
Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for your reward is great in heaven. Their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
But woe to you who are rich and comfortable, for you have already received your consolation and comfort.
Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when all people speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.”

verses.heading: The Sermon on the Plain: Love for Enemies / The Sermon on the Plain: Love for Enemies / Matt. 5:38-48; 7:12a
verses.text: “But to you who are listening, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat and insult you.

When someone strikes you, refuse retaliation and be willing to endure further injustice without seeking revenge. And if someone forcefully takes your outer cloak, be ready to surrender even your inner garment rather than respond with resistance rooted in personal vengeance.
Be generous toward those who ask for help, and when someone takes what is yours, do not insist on reclaiming it in a vindictive or grasping spirit.
Treat others just as you desire that people would treat you.
If you love only those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them in return.
If you do good only to those who do good to you, what credit is that? Even sinners do the same.
If you lend only to those from whom you expect to be repaid, what credit is that? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to receive back the same amount.
But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for He is kind to the ungrateful and evil.
Be merciful and compassionate, just as your Father is merciful.”

verses.heading: The Sermon on the Plain: Judging and Condemning Others and Forgiveness / The Sermon on the Plain: Judging and Condemning Others and Forgiveness / Matt. 7:1-5
verses.text: “Do not judge others, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

Give generously, and it will be given to you. A good measure—pressed down, shaken together, and running over—will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use to measure others, it will be measured back to you.”
Jesus also spoke a parable to them: “Can a blind person guide another blind person? Will they not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the log in your own eye?

How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck from your eye,’ when you yourself do not see the log in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the log from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.”

verses.heading: The Sermon on the Plain: The Good Man and the Evil Person / The Sermon on the Plain: The Good Man and the Evil Person / Matt. 7:17-20; 12:34b-35
verses.text: “No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.
Each tree is known and recognized by its own fruit. People do not gather figs from thornbushes, nor do they pick grapes from brambles.
The good person out of the good treasure stored in his heart brings forth good. The evil person out of his evil treasure brings forth evil. For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.”

verses.heading: The Sermon on the Plain: The Two Foundations / The Sermon on the Plain: The Two Foundations / Matt. 7:24-27
verses.text: “Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and yet do not do what I say?
Everyone who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them—I will show you what he is like:

He is like a man building a house who dug down deep and laid the foundation on solid rock. When a flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it had been well built on a firm foundation.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: But the one who hears My words and does not put them into practice is like a man who built a house on the ground without digging a foundation. When the torrent burst against it, the house immediately collapsed, and the destruction of that house was complete and catastrophic.” 3 This is a reference to I Sam. 21:1-6

verses.heading: The Healing of a Centurion’s Servant / The Healing of a Centurion’s Servant / Matt. 8:5-13; Jn. 4:43-54
verses.text: When Jesus had completed delivering all His teachings within hearing of the people, He entered the city of Capernaum.
A certain Roman centurion had a servant who was highly valued and precious to him. This servant was gravely ill and at the point of death.
When the centurion heard about Jesus and His healing power, he sent Jewish elders to Him, earnestly requesting that Jesus would come and heal his servant.
When they came to Jesus, they began to plead with Him urgently, saying, “This centurion is worthy that You should grant him this favor.
He loves our nation, and he himself built the synagogue for us at his own expense.” The centurion was a Gentile who honored the God of Israel.

So Jesus went with them. When He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to meet Him with a message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself further, for I am not worthy that You should enter under my roof.
For this reason, I did not even consider myself worthy to come to You in person. But simply speak a word, and let my servant be healed.

For I myself am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under my command. I say to one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it. If I have such authority, how much more do You?”

When Jesus heard these words, He marveled at the centurion’s faith. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such remarkable faith as this Gentile has shown.”
When those who had been sent returned to the house, they found the servant in perfect health, completely restored.

verses.heading: The Raising of a Widow’s Son / The Raising of a Widow’s Son
verses.text: On the following day, Jesus traveled to a town called Nain. His disciples and a large crowd accompanied Him on the journey.

As He approached the gate of the city, a funeral procession was coming out. A dead man was being carried out—the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. A substantial crowd from the city was with her in mourning.
When the Lord saw her, He was moved with deep compassion for her situation. He said to her gently, “Do not weep.”
Jesus came up and touched the burial bier, and those carrying it stopped. He said with authority, “Young man, I say to you, arise!”
The dead man sat up and began to speak. Jesus gave him back to his mother, alive and well.
Fear and awe seized everyone present, and they began to glorify God, saying, “A great prophet has risen among us!” and “God has visited and looked upon His people with favor!”
This report concerning Jesus spread throughout all of Judea and into all the surrounding region.

verses.heading: Delegates from John the Baptist / Delegates from John the Baptist / Matt. 11:2-19
verses.text: John’s disciples brought him a full report about all these remarkable things Jesus was doing.
John summoned two of his disciples and sent them to the Lord with a question: “Are You the Coming One we have been expecting, or should we look for someone else?”
When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to You to ask, ‘Are You the Coming One, or should we look for another?’ ”
At that very hour, Jesus was healing many people of diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits. He was also freely granting sight to many who were blind.

Jesus answered the messengers, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, those with leprosy are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised to life, and the good news is being proclaimed to the poor.
Blessed is the one who does not stumble in faith or take offense at Me because I do not meet his expectations.”

verses.heading: Concerning John the Baptist / Concerning John the Baptist
verses.text: After John’s messengers had departed, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken and swayed by the wind—someone weak and changeable?
What then did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft, luxurious garments? No! Those who wear splendid clothing and live in luxury are found in royal palaces, not in the wilderness.
What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and far more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written in Scripture: ‘Behold, I am sending My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’*
I tell you, among those born of women, there is no one greater than John. Yet the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
Luke adds parenthetically: When all the people heard this—even the despised tax collectors—they acknowledged God's way as just and right, having been baptized with John’s baptism.
But the Pharisees and experts in the Law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, refusing to be baptized by John.
Jesus continued, “To what then shall I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?

They are like children sitting in the marketplace, calling out to one another and saying, ‘We played wedding music on the flute for you, but you did not dance. We sang funeral songs, but you did not mourn and wail.’
For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon and is possessed.’
The Son of Man has come eating and drinking normally, and you say, ‘Look at Him! A glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ You cannot be pleased no matter what we do.
Yet wisdom is vindicated and proven right by all her children—by those who respond rightly to God’s message.”

verses.heading: The Forgiveness of a Sinful Woman / The Forgiveness of a Sinful Woman
verses.text: One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to dine with him. Jesus entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table for the meal.
A woman in the city who was known as a sinner learned that Jesus was reclining at the table in the Pharisee’s house. She brought an alabaster jar filled with expensive fragrant oil.

Standing behind Jesus at His feet, weeping with repentance, she began to wet His feet with her tears. She wiped them with her hair, kissed His feet repeatedly, and anointed them with the fragrant oil.

When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were truly a prophet, He would know who and what kind of woman this is who is touching Him—that she is a notorious sinner.”
Jesus responded to his unspoken thoughts, saying, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” Simon replied, “Speak, Teacher.”
Jesus said, “There were two debtors who owed money to a certain creditor. One owed five hundred denarii—nearly two years’ wages—and the other owed fifty.
When neither of them had the means to repay their debts, the creditor graciously pardoned and forgave the debts of both. Now which of them will love him more?”
Simon answered, “I assume it would be the one to whom he forgave the larger debt.” Jesus said to him, “You have judged correctly.”

Then turning toward the woman, Jesus said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not provide Me with water for My feet—a basic courtesy. But she has wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You did not give Me a customary kiss of greeting. But from the time I entered, she has not stopped kissing My feet.
You did not anoint My head with ordinary olive oil. But she has anointed My feet with expensive fragrant oil.
Therefore, I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven, as demonstrated by the fact that she loved much. But the one to whom little is forgiven loves only a little.”
Jesus said to the woman, “Your sins have been forgiven.”
Those reclining at the table with Jesus began to say among themselves, “Who is this man who even forgives sins?”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Jesus said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.” 27 Quoted from Mal. 3:1

verses.heading: Women Who Assisted Jesus and His Disciples / Women Who Assisted Jesus and His Disciples
verses.text: Soon afterward, Jesus was traveling from one city and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The twelve apostles were with Him.
Certain women who had been healed from evil spirits and diseases were also traveling with them: Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had been cast out;
Joanna, the wife of Chuza who was Herod’s household manager; Susanna; and many other women who were providing for their material needs from their own financial resources.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Sower / The Parable of the Sower / Matt. 13:1-9; Mk. 4:1-9
verses.text: As a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from one city after another, He spoke to them by way of a parable:
“A farmer went out to sow his seed. As he was scattering the seed, some fell along the pathway and was trampled underfoot. The birds of the sky came and devoured it.
Other seed fell on rocky ground. When it sprouted and grew, it quickly withered away because it had no moisture.
Other seed fell in the midst of thorns. The thorns grew up with the plants and choked them out.

Still other seed fell into good, fertile soil. It grew and produced a crop yielding a hundred times what was sown.” After saying these things, Jesus called out, “The one who has ears to hear, let him hear and understand!”

verses.heading: The Purpose of the Parables / The Purpose of the Parables / Matt. 13:10-17; Mk. 4:10-12
verses.text: His disciples began to ask Him what this parable meant and signified.

Jesus said, “To you it has been granted to know the mysteries and secrets of the kingdom of God. But to the rest, these truths come in parables, so that ‘seeing they may not perceive, and hearing they may not understand.’

verses.heading: The Interpretation of the Parable of the Sower / The Interpretation of the Parable of the Sower / Matt. 13:18-23; Mk. 4:13-20
verses.text: Jesus explained: “Now this is what the parable means: The seed represents the word of God.
Those along the pathway are the ones who hear the word, but then the devil comes and snatches away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.

Those on the rocky ground are the ones who, when they hear the word, receive it with joy and enthusiasm. But these people have no root. They believe for a while, but in a time of testing and trial, they fall away.

As for what fell among the thorns—these are the ones who hear the word, but as they go along through life, they are choked by the cares, riches, and pleasures of this life. They do not bring fruit to maturity.
As for the seed that fell on good soil—these are the ones who, upon hearing the word with a noble and good heart, hold fast to it firmly. They bear fruit through perseverance and patient endurance.”

verses.heading: A Lamp on a Stand / A Lamp on a Stand / Mk. 4:21-25
verses.text: Jesus continued His teaching: “No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a clay jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he sets it on a lampstand so that those who enter the room may see the light.
For nothing is concealed that will not eventually become manifest. Nothing is kept secret that will not be brought to light.

Therefore, pay careful attention to how you listen and hear. For whoever has spiritual understanding, more will be given to him. But whoever does not have understanding, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”

verses.heading: Jesus’ Mother and Brothers / Jesus’ Mother and Brothers / Matt. 12:46-50; Mk. 3:31-35
verses.text: Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see Him, but they were not able to reach Him because of the dense crowd.
Someone reported to Him, “Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.”
But Jesus responded, “My mother and My brothers are these—the ones who hear the word of God and put it into practice.”

verses.heading: Jesus Calms a Storm / Jesus Calms a Storm / Matt. 8:23-27; Mk. 4:35-41
verses.text: One day Jesus got into a boat with His disciples and said to them, “Let us cross over to the other side of the lake.” So they set sail.
As they were sailing across, Jesus fell asleep. A violent storm of wind descended upon the lake. The boat was being swamped with water, and they were in serious danger of sinking.
The disciples came to Jesus and woke Him urgently, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” Jesus awoke, rebuked the wind and the raging water, and they ceased. There was a great calm.

Jesus said to His disciples, “Where is your faith?” But they were afraid and filled with awe, saying to one another, “Who then is this man, that He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him?”

verses.heading: The Healing of the Gerasene Demon-Possessed Man / The Healing of the Gerasene Demon-Possessed Man / Matt. 8:28-34; Mk. 5:1-20
verses.text: They sailed across to the region of the Gerasenes, which is on the opposite side of the lake from Galilee.
When Jesus stepped out onto the land, a certain man from the city met Him. This man had demons and had not worn clothes for a considerable time. He was not living in a house but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down before Him, and said in a loud voice, “What do I have to do with You, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You, do not torment me!”

Jesus had been commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him. Though he was bound with chains and shackles and kept under guard, he would break the bonds. The demon would drive him into solitary places.
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He answered, “Legion”—because many demons had entered into him.
The demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to depart into the abyss—the place of eternal confinement.
A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside. The demons implored Jesus to permit them to enter the pigs. Jesus gave them permission.
The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the city and throughout the countryside.

People went out to see what had taken place. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out. He was sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind. They were frightened at the transformation.
Those who had witnessed the event reported to the others how the demon-possessed man had been healed and delivered.
All the people from the surrounding region of the Gerasenes requested Jesus to depart from them, for they were seized with great fear. So Jesus got into the boat and returned across the lake.
The man from whom the demons had gone out kept begging Jesus to let him accompany Him as a disciple.

But Jesus sent him away with different instructions, saying, “Return to your home and tell what great things God has done for you.” The man went away, proclaiming throughout the whole city all that Jesus had done for him.

verses.heading: The Healing of a Woman with the Flow of Blood and the Raising of Jairus’ Daughter / The Healing of a Woman with the Flow of Blood and the Raising of Jairus’ Daughter / Matt. 9:18-26; Mk. 5:21-43
verses.text: When Jesus returned to the other side, the crowd welcomed Him, for they had all been waiting for Him.
A man named Jairus came to Jesus. He was a ruler of the synagogue. Falling down at Jesus’ feet, he began to beg Him earnestly to come to his house,
because his only daughter, about twelve years old, was dying. As Jesus was going, the crowds were pressing against Him from all sides.
A woman was there who had suffered from a discharge of blood for twelve years. She had spent all her living on physicians but had not been healed by anyone.
She came up behind Jesus in the crowd and touched the fringe of His garment. Immediately her flow of blood stopped.
Jesus said, “Who is the one who touched Me?” When everyone denied it, Peter said, “Master, the crowds are pressing and thronging against You from every direction.”
But Jesus insisted, “Someone deliberately touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.”
When the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling. She fell down before Him and declared before all the people why she had touched Him and how she had been immediately healed.
Jesus said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
While Jesus was still speaking, someone came from the house of the synagogue ruler with devastating news: “Your daughter is dead. Do not trouble the Teacher any longer.”
But when Jesus heard this, He responded, “Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will be made well.”
When Jesus arrived at the house, He did not permit anyone to enter with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and mourning for the girl. But Jesus said, “Do not weep. She is not dead but sleeping.”
They began ridiculing Jesus, knowing with certainty that she was dead.
But Jesus took her by the hand and called out, “Child, arise!”
Her spirit returned to her body, and she stood up immediately. Jesus ordered that something should be given to her to eat, demonstrating that she was truly alive.
Her parents were utterly astonished. But Jesus commanded them not to tell anyone what had taken place.

verses.heading: Jesus Commissioned the Twelve / Jesus Commissioned the Twelve / Matt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13
verses.text: Jesus called the twelve apostles together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.
He sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
Jesus said to them, “Take nothing for your journey—no staff, no bag, no bread, no money. Do not even take two tunics apiece.
Whatever house you enter, stay there until you depart from that town.
Wherever people do not receive you, when you leave that city, shake the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.”
So the apostles departed and traveled throughout the villages, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere.

verses.heading: The Thorough Perplexity of Herod / The Thorough Perplexity of Herod / Matt. 14:1-12; Mk. 6:14-29
verses.text: Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening through Jesus’ ministry. He was thoroughly confused, because some people were saying that John the Baptist had been raised from the dead,
while others claimed that Elijah had appeared, and still others that one of the ancient prophets had risen.
Herod said, “I beheaded John myself. But who is this about whom I hear such things?” He kept seeking an opportunity to see Jesus.

verses.heading: The Miraculous Feeding of the Five Thousand / The Miraculous Feeding of the Five Thousand / Matt. 14:13-21; Mk. 6:30-44; Jn. 6:1-14
verses.text: When the apostles returned from their mission, they gave Jesus a full report of all they had done. Jesus took them and withdrew privately to a town called Bethsaida.
But when the crowds learned where He had gone, they followed Him. Jesus welcomed them and began speaking to them about the kingdom of God. He continued healing those who needed healing.

As the day began to draw to a close, the twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go into the surrounding villages and countryside to find lodging and get food, because we are in a deserted place here.”
But Jesus said to them, “You give them something to eat.” They protested, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish—unless we go and buy food for all these people.”
There were approximately five thousand men present, not counting women and children. Jesus said to His disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
The disciples did as Jesus instructed and made everyone sit down.
Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed and gave thanks, then broke them. He kept giving them to the disciples to distribute before the crowd.
They all ate and were satisfied. What was left over was picked up—twelve baskets full of broken pieces.

verses.heading: Jesus is the Christ of God / Jesus is the Christ of God / Matt. 16:13-19; Mk. 8:27-29
verses.text: On one occasion while Jesus was praying in solitude, the disciples were with Him nearby. He questioned them, saying, “Who do the crowds say that I am?”
They answered, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others say that one of the ancient prophets has risen.”
Jesus asked them, “But you—who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God—the Messiah.”

verses.heading: Jesus Speaks of His Death and Resurrection the First Time / Jesus Speaks of His Death and Resurrection the First Time / Matt. 16:20-23; Mk. 8:33
verses.text: Jesus warned them sternly and commanded them to tell this to no one.
He said, “It is necessary for the Son of Man to suffer many things, to be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, to be killed, and on the third day to be raised.”

verses.heading: Following Jesus / Following Jesus / Matt. 16:24-28; Mk. 8:34-9:1
verses.text: Jesus began to say to everyone, “If anyone desires to come after Me, he must deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow Me.
For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake—this person will save it.
For what does it profit a person if he gains the whole world yet loses or forfeits his own soul?
For whoever is ashamed of Me and of My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of this one when He comes in His glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
But I tell you with certainty: There are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.”

verses.heading: The Transfiguration / The Transfiguration / Matt. 17:1-8; Mk. 9:2-8
verses.text: About eight days after saying these things, Jesus took Peter, John, and James and went up on the mountain to pray.
As He was praying, the appearance of His face was dramatically altered, and His clothing became white and flashing like lightning.
Suddenly two men were talking with Him—Moses and Elijah.
They appeared in glorious splendor and were speaking about His departure, which He was about to accomplish in Jerusalem—referring to His death, resurrection, and ascension.
Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep. But when they became fully awake, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with Him.

As Moses and Elijah were parting from Jesus, Peter said, “Master, it is wonderful for us to be here. Let us make three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” He did not know what he was saying.
While Peter was speaking, a cloud appeared and began to overshadow them. They became afraid as they entered the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud, declaring, “This is My Son, the One whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”
When the voice had spoken, Jesus was found alone. The disciples kept silent about this and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.

verses.heading: The Healing of a Boy with an Unclean Spirit / The Healing of a Boy with an Unclean Spirit / Matt. 17:14-18; Mk. 9:14-27
verses.text: On the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a large crowd met Jesus.
A man from the crowd cried out desperately, “Teacher, I beg You to look with compassion on my son, because he is my only child.
A spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out. It convulses him with foaming at the mouth. It departs from him only with great difficulty, crushing and bruising him severely as it leaves.
I begged Your disciples to cast it out, but they were not able to do so.”
Jesus responded, “O unbelieving and perverse generation! How long must I remain with you and endure you? Bring your son here.”
Even as the boy was approaching, the demon threw him to the ground and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy completely, and gave him back to his father.

verses.heading: Jesus Speaks of His Death the Second Time / Jesus Speaks of His Death the Second Time / Matt. 17:22-23; Mk. 9:30-32
verses.text: Everyone was struck with amazement at the majesty and greatness of God. While everyone was marveling at all that Jesus was doing, He said to His disciples,
“Let these words sink deeply into your ears: The Son of Man is about to be betrayed into the hands of men.”
But the disciples did not understand this saying. It was hidden from them so that they could not grasp it. They were afraid to ask Him about this statement.

verses.heading: The Argument on Who is Greatest Among the Disciples / The Argument on Who is Greatest Among the Disciples / Matt. 18:1-5; Mk. 9:33-37
verses.text: An argument arose among the disciples regarding which of them might be the greatest.
Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their hearts, took a child and had him stand beside Him.

He said to them, “Whoever receives this child in My name receives Me. And whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me. For the one who is least among all of you—this is the one who is truly great.”

verses.heading: Whoever Is Not Against You Is for You / Whoever Is Not Against You Is for You / Mk. 9:38-40
verses.text: John responded, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name, and we kept trying to prevent him because he does not follow with us in our group.”
But Jesus said to him, “Do not prevent him, for whoever is not against you is for you.”

verses.heading: The Rejection of Jesus in a Samaritan Village / The Rejection of Jesus in a Samaritan Village
verses.text: As the time approached for Jesus to be taken up to heaven, He resolutely set His face to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of Him. They went and entered a Samaritan village to make preparations for Him.
But the people did not receive Him because His destination was Jerusalem. The Samaritans were hostile to Jews going to worship there.
When the disciples James and John saw this rejection, they said, “Lord, do You want us to command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?”
But Jesus turned and rebuked them for their vindictive spirit.
They went to another village instead.

verses.heading: The Demands of Following Jesus / The Demands of Following Jesus / Matt. 8:19-22
verses.text: As they were traveling along the road, someone said to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.”
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens, and birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”
Jesus said to another person, “Follow Me.” But that person said, “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”
Jesus said to him, “Let the dead bury their own dead. But you go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
Yet another person said, “I will follow You, Lord, but first let me say farewell to those at my home.”
But Jesus said, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for service in the kingdom of God.”

verses.heading: The Appointment of the Seventy-two Others / The Appointment of the Seventy-two Others
verses.text: Following these events, the Lord commissioned seventy additional disciples, dispatching them in pairs ahead of Him to every town and location He intended to visit personally.
He instructed them: “The spiritual harvest is abundant, yet laborers are scarce. Therefore, entreat the Lord who oversees this harvest to dispatch additional workers into His harvest fields.
Proceed with this mission; understand that I am sending you forth as vulnerable lambs among predatory wolves.
Travel without carrying a money pouch, supply bag, or extra sandals, and refrain from stopping to exchange greetings along your journey.
Upon entering any household, immediately pronounce: ‘May peace rest upon this dwelling.’
If a person receptive to peace resides there, your blessing will settle upon them. Otherwise, your blessing will return to you unfulfilled.
Remain in that same household, accepting whatever food and drink they offer, for laborers deserve compensation. Do not relocate between different houses.
When you enter a town that welcomes you, consume whatever meals are provided for you,
heal those who are sick within it, and proclaim to them, ‘God’s kingdom has drawn near to your community.’
However, when you enter a town that rejects you, proceed into its public streets and declare,
‘We are removing even the dust from your town that adheres to our feet as a testimony against you. Nevertheless, understand this: God’s kingdom has approached your community.’
I assure you that on the day of judgment, Sodom will receive more tolerable treatment than that town which rejects the gospel message.

verses.heading: Pronouncement of Woes on the Unrepentant Cities / Pronouncement of Woes on the Unrepentant Cities / Matt. 11:20-24
verses.text: Woe upon you, Chorazin! Woe upon you, Bethsaida! Had the miraculous demonstrations performed among you occurred in the pagan cities of Tyre and Sidon, those cities would have turned from their sins long ago, adopting mourning attire and ashes as outward expressions of genuine repentance.
Nevertheless, Tyre and Sidon will experience more bearable judgment than you will endure.
And you, Capernaum—do you presume you will be elevated to heaven’s glory? No; you will descend to Hades in judgment.
Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever dismisses you dismisses Me; and whoever dismisses Me dismisses the Father who commissioned Me.”

verses.heading: The Return of the Seventy-two / The Return of the Seventy-two
verses.text: The seventy disciples returned filled with joy, reporting, “Lord, even demonic spirits submit to us when we invoke Your name.”
He responded to them, “I observed Satan plummeting from heaven like a lightning bolt.
Listen carefully: I have granted you authority to trample upon serpents and scorpions, and authority over all the enemy’s power, ensuring nothing will harm you.
Nevertheless, do not rejoice primarily because spirits submit to your authority, but rejoice because your names have been written in heaven’s register.”

verses.heading: Jesus Rejoices in the Holy Spirit / Jesus Rejoices in the Holy Spirit / Matt. 11:25-27; 13:16-17
verses.text: At that precise moment, Jesus rejoiced greatly through the Holy Spirit and declared, “I offer You praise, Father, sovereign Lord over heaven and earth, because You have concealed these truths from those who consider themselves wise and intellectually sophisticated, yet revealed them to those who approach with childlike humility. Yes, Father, this approach pleased You.

My Father has entrusted all authority to Me, and no one truly comprehends the Son’s identity except the Father, nor does anyone truly comprehend the Father’s identity except the Son, along with anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.”
Turning privately toward His disciples, He said, “How privileged are the eyes that witness what you are witnessing.
For I tell you that numerous prophets and monarchs longed to observe what you are observing but never saw it; they desired to hear what you are hearing but never heard it.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Good / The Parable of the Good / Samaritan / Samaritan
verses.text: Then a legal expert in Mosaic Law stood to test Jesus, inquiring, “Teacher, what actions must I perform to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus replied, “What does the Law state? How do you interpret it?”
The man answered, “You shall love the Lord your God from your entire heart, with your complete soul, with your full strength, and with your whole mind; and love your neighbor as yourself.”
Jesus affirmed, “Your response is correct. Live according to this principle, and you will obtain life.”
But the man, attempting to justify himself, pressed Jesus, “And who qualifies as my neighbor?”

Jesus continued with a parable: “A certain individual was traveling down from Jerusalem to Jericho when bandits attacked him. They stripped his clothing, assaulted him severely, and abandoned him barely alive.
By coincidence, a priest was traveling down that same road. Upon seeing the injured man, he deliberately passed by on the opposite side.
Similarly, a Levite arrived at that location, observed the victim, and likewise passed by on the opposite side.
However, a certain Samaritan who was journeying came upon him, and upon seeing him, felt deep compassion.
He approached the victim, bandaged his wounds while pouring on olive oil and wine as medicinal treatment. Then he placed him upon his own animal, transported him to an inn, and provided care for him.
The following day, he produced two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, instructing, ‘Care for him, and whatever additional expenses you incur, I will reimburse you upon my return.’
Which of these three individuals, in your judgment, proved to be a neighbor to the man assaulted by bandits?”
The legal expert replied, “The one who demonstrated compassion toward him.” Jesus instructed him, “Proceed and conduct yourself likewise.”

verses.heading: Martha and Mary / Martha and Mary
verses.text: As they continued their journey, Jesus entered a particular village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
She had a sister named Mary, who seated herself at Jesus’ feet and listened intently to His teaching.

Martha, however, was distracted by extensive hospitality preparations. She approached Jesus and protested, “Lord, does it not concern You that my sister has abandoned me to serve alone? Instruct her to assist me.”
The Lord responded to her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and agitated about numerous matters.
Yet only one thing is truly necessary. Mary has chosen the superior portion, which will not be removed from her.”

verses.heading: The Lord’s Prayer / The Lord’s Prayer / Matt. 6:9-15; 7:7-11
verses.text: On one occasion, Jesus was praying at a certain location. When He concluded, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John instructed his disciples.”
He instructed them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, may Your name be revered as holy. May Your kingdom come.
Provide us each day with our daily sustenance.
And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves forgive everyone indebted to us. And do not lead us into temptation.’ ”
Then He said to them, “Suppose one of you has a friend, and you go to him at midnight, saying to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
because a friend of mine has arrived from a journey, and I have nothing to offer him.’
And that friend answering from inside responds, ‘Do not trouble me. The door is already locked and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up to give you anything.’
I tell you, even though he will not arise and provide anything because of friendship, yet because of your shameless persistence, he will get up and give you whatever you need.
Therefore, I tell you: Ask persistently and it will be given to you; seek diligently and you will discover; knock continually and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives; the one who seeks discovers; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
What father among you, if his son requests a fish, will give him a serpent instead of a fish?
Or if he requests an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
If you then, despite being sinful by nature, understand how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”

verses.heading: Jesus and Beelzebul / Jesus and Beelzebul / Matt. 12:12-30; Mk. 3:20-27
verses.text: Jesus was expelling a demon that rendered someone mute. When the demon departed, the previously mute person spoke, and the crowds marveled.
But certain individuals declared, “He expels demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons.”
Others, testing Him, persisted in demanding a miraculous sign from heaven.
But Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom experiencing internal division becomes devastated, and a household divided against itself collapses.
If Satan also experiences internal division, how will his kingdom endure? For you claim I expel demons by Beelzebul.
But if I expel demons by Beelzebul, by whose power do your followers expel them? Therefore, they will serve as your judges.
However, if I expel demons by God’s finger, then God’s kingdom has arrived among you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own estate, his possessions remain secure.
But when someone stronger than he attacks and overpowers him, he confiscates all the armor in which he trusted and distributes his plundered goods.
“Whoever does not align with Me opposes Me; and whoever does not gather with Me scatters.

verses.heading: The Return of the Unclean Spirit / The Return of the Unclean Spirit / Matt. 12:43-45
verses.text: “When an unclean spirit departs from a person, it travels through waterless regions seeking rest but discovers none. Then it declares, ‘I will return to my dwelling from which I departed.’
Upon arriving, it discovers the house swept clean and orderly.

Then it departs and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and after entering, they inhabit that person. Consequently, that person’s final condition becomes worse than the initial state.”

verses.heading: True Blessedness / True Blessedness
verses.text: As He was speaking these words, a certain woman from the crowd raised her voice and declared to Him, “Blessed is the womb that carried You, and the breasts that nursed You!”
But He replied, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear God’s word and obey it!”

verses.heading: Seeking After a Sign / Seeking After a Sign / Matt. 12:38-42; Mk. 8:12
verses.text: As the crowds increased, He began saying, “This generation is a wicked generation. It seeks a miraculous sign, but no sign will be provided to it except the sign of Jonah.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so too the Son of Man will be to this generation.

The queen of the South will arise at the judgment alongside the people of this generation and will condemn them, because she traveled from earth’s distant regions to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and consider this, someone infinitely greater than Solomon is here.
The people of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching; and consider this, someone infinitely greater than Jonah is here.

verses.heading: The Light of the Body / The Light of the Body / Matt. 5:15; 6:22-23
verses.text: “No one, after lighting a lamp, conceals it in a cellar or under a basket, but places it on a lampstand, so that those who enter can perceive the light.
Your eye serves as the body’s lamp. When your eye is healthy, your entire body is illuminated. But when it is diseased, your body is also darkened.
Therefore, be careful lest the light within you is actually darkness.
If then your whole body is illuminated, having no darkened part, it will be completely bright, as when a lamp illuminates you with its radiance.”

verses.heading: Pronouncement of Woes on the Pharisees and Legal Experts / Pronouncement of Woes on the Pharisees and Legal Experts / Matt. 23:1-36; Mk. 12:38-40; Lk. 20:45-47
verses.text: When He finished speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him, and He entered and reclined at the table.
The Pharisee, observing this, was astonished that He did not perform the ceremonial washing before the meal.
But the Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the cup’s and dish’s exterior, but your interior is filled with greed and wickedness.
Foolish people! Did not the One who created the exterior also create the interior?
Rather, give as charity what is within; and observe, everything becomes clean for you.
“But woe to you, Pharisees, because you tithe mint and rue and every garden herb, yet neglect justice and God’s love. These you ought to have practiced without neglecting those other matters.
Woe to you, Pharisees, because you desire the most prominent seats in the synagogues and respectful greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you, because you resemble unmarked graves, and people who walk over them remain unaware.
Then one of the legal experts responded to Him, “Teacher, by saying these things, you insult us also.”
He replied, “Woe to you also, legal experts, because you burden people with oppressive loads, yet you yourselves refuse to touch the burdens with even one finger.
Woe to you, because you construct monuments for the prophets, yet your ancestors murdered them.
Consequently, you serve as witnesses and approve of your ancestors’ deeds, because they murdered them and you build their monuments.
Indeed, for this reason, God’s Wisdom declared, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles, and some they will kill and persecute,’
so that the blood of all prophets, shed from the world’s foundation, may be charged against this generation,
from Abel’s blood to Zechariah’s blood, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, it will be charged against this generation.
Woe to you, legal experts, you have removed the key of knowledge. You did not enter yourselves, and you prevented those who were attempting to enter.”
When He departed from there, the scribes and Pharisees became extremely hostile and interrogated Him about numerous matters,
plotting to trap Him in something He might say.

verses.heading: Warning Against the Leaven of / Warning Against the Leaven of / the Pharisees / the Pharisees
verses.text: During this time, an enormous crowd of many thousands assembled, so packed together that people were trampling one another. Jesus began speaking first to His disciples: “Be vigilant and guard yourselves against the corrupting influence of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
There is nothing covered up that will not eventually be uncovered, nothing hidden that will not ultimately be brought into the open.
Therefore, whatever you have whispered in the darkness will be proclaimed in broad daylight, and what you have spoken privately behind closed doors will be announced publicly from the housetops.

verses.heading: Fear Only God / Fear Only God / Matt. 10:28-31
verses.text: “I say to you who are My friends: Do not be afraid of those who can kill the physical body but afterward possess no further power to harm you.
Let Me show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after taking your life, has the authority to cast your soul into hell. Yes, I tell you emphatically, fear Him alone!
Are not five small sparrows sold for merely two pennies in the marketplace? Yet not a single one of them is forgotten or overlooked in God’s sight.
In fact, even the individual hairs on your head are all numbered and known by God. Stop being afraid—you are worth far more than many sparrows.

verses.heading: Acknowledging Christ Before Men / Acknowledging Christ Before Men / Matt. 10:32-33; 12:32; 10:19-20
verses.text: “I tell you this truth: Everyone who openly acknowledges and confesses Me before other people, the Son of Man will likewise acknowledge him before the angels of God.
But whoever denies Me before people will be denied and disowned before the angels of God.
Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man may receive forgiveness. But the person who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit—attributing God’s work to Satan—will not receive forgiveness.
When they bring you before synagogues, rulers, and authorities for trial, do not become anxious about how you should defend yourself or what you should say in your defense.
The Holy Spirit will teach and instruct you in that very hour what you must say.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Rich Fool / The Parable of the Rich Fool
verses.text: Someone in the crowd spoke up and said to Jesus, “Teacher, command my brother to divide the family inheritance with me.”
But Jesus replied to him, “Man, who appointed or authorized Me to be a judge or arbitrator to settle disputes between you?”
Then Jesus warned the people, “Keep watch against every form of greed and covetousness, because a person’s life does not consist in or depend on the abundance of material possessions he owns.”
Jesus told them this parable: “The land belonging to a certain wealthy man produced an exceptionally abundant harvest.
He began reasoning to himself, saying, ‘What should I do? I do not have sufficient space to store all my crops.’
Then he said, ‘Here is what I will do: I will tear down my existing barns and build much larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have plenty of goods laid up for many years to come. Take your ease, relax, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.’ ”
But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your soul is being demanded of you. And the things you have prepared and accumulated—whose will they be after you die?’
This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God—who accumulates earthly wealth but has no spiritual riches.”

verses.heading: Do Not Be Anxious / Do Not Be Anxious / Matt. 6:25-34; 19:21
verses.text: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “For this reason I tell you: Stop worrying about your life—what you will eat, or about your body—what you will wear.
Life is far more important than food, and the body is far more important than clothing.
Consider and observe the ravens: they do not sow seed or reap harvest; they have no storeroom or barn, yet God feeds them. How much more valuable and precious you are than birds!
Which of you by worrying and being anxious can add a single hour to your lifespan or a single inch to your height?
If you cannot accomplish even this smallest thing, why do you worry about all the other matters?
Consider how the lilies grow: they do not toil or spin thread to make clothing, yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his royal splendor was dressed as beautifully as one of these flowers.
Now if God so clothes the grass of the field—which is alive today but tomorrow is thrown into the oven as fuel—how much more will He clothe you, O you people of little faith!
As for you, do not keep seeking what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not have a worried, anxious mind.
