For all the pagan nations of the world eagerly seek after all these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.
Instead, seek His kingdom first and foremost, and these material necessities will be provided to you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has chosen in His good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Make for yourselves money bags that do not wear out or become old, an unfailing treasure in heaven where no thief can come near and no moth can destroy.
For wherever your treasure is located, there your heart will be focused also.”

verses.heading: Be Prepared for Action / Be Prepared for Action / Matt. 24:45-51
verses.text: “Keep your waists girded and ready for action, and keep your lamps burning brightly.
Be like servants who are waiting expectantly for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can immediately open the door for him.

Blessed are those servants whom the master will find alert and watching when he arrives. Truly, I tell you that he will dress himself for service, have them recline at the table, and will personally come and serve them.
Even if he comes back in the second watch of the night (about 9.00 p.m. to midnight) or the third watch (about midnight to 3.00 a.m.) and finds them watching faithfully, blessed are those servants.
But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and not allowed his house to be broken into.
You also must be ready and prepared, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour when you do not expect Him.”
Peter asked, “Lord, are You telling this parable for us apostles specifically, or for everyone in general?”
The Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager whom the master will put in charge over his household servants to give them their food allowance at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing so when he returns.
Truly, I tell you that the master will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time in coming,’ and he begins to beat the male and female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
The master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know. He will cut him in pieces and assign him a place with the unfaithful.
That servant who knew his master’s will but did not get ready or act according to his will shall be beaten with many blows.

But the one who did not know his master’s will and did things worthy of punishment will be beaten with a few blows. From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required. To whom much was entrusted, they will ask even more from him.”

verses.heading: Jesus’ Mission to Cast Fire on the Earth / Jesus’ Mission to Cast Fire on the Earth / Matt. 10:34-36
verses.text: Jesus declared, “I came to cast fire upon the earth—to bring judgment and division—and how I wish it were already kindled and burning!
But I have a baptism of suffering to undergo, and how greatly distressed I am until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I came to bring peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but rather division and separation!
For from now on, five people in one household will be divided against each other: three against two and two against three.

They will be divided: Father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”

verses.heading: Interpreting the Time / Interpreting the Time / Matt. 16:2-3
verses.text: Jesus also said to the crowds: “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you immediately say, ‘A rainstorm is coming,’ and so it happens.
And when the south wind is blowing, you say, ‘There will be scorching heat,’ and it comes to pass.

You hypocrites! You know how to interpret and analyze the appearance of the earth and sky, but how is it that you do not know how to interpret this present time and recognize the signs of the Messiah’s presence?

verses.heading: Settling with Your Opponent / Settling with Your Opponent / Matt. 5:25-26
verses.text: Why do you not judge for yourselves what is right and just?

As you are going with your adversary to appear before the magistrate, make every effort to settle the matter with him along the way, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid back every last penny.”

verses.heading: Repent or Perish / Repent or Perish
verses.text: At that very time some people arrived who brought Jesus news about certain Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices—killing them while they were worshipping.
Jesus responded to them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered this fate?
No, I tell you emphatically. But unless you repent and turn from your sins, you will all likewise perish.
Or those eighteen people on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think they were more guilty sinners than all the other people living in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Fig Tree / The Parable of the Fig Tree
verses.text: Then Jesus told this parable: “A certain man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it but found none.

So he said to the vineyard worker, ‘Look, for three years now I have been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree and have found none. Cut it down! Why should it continue using up the soil and depleting its nutrients?’
But the worker replied to him, ‘Sir, leave it alone for one more year. Let me dig around it and put fertilizer on it.
If it bears fruit next year, excellent. But if not, then you can cut it down.’ ”

verses.heading: A Woman with a Spirit of Disability / A Woman with a Spirit of Disability
verses.text: Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.
A woman was there who had been afflicted by a spirit of disability for eighteen years. She was bent over and completely unable to straighten herself up.
When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said to her, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”
He laid His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began glorifying and praising God.

But the synagogue ruler was indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. He said to the crowd, “There are six days in which work should be done. Come on those days and be healed, not on the Sabbath day.”
But the Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Does not each one of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it away to give it water?
This woman is a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years. Should she not be released from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”
When Jesus said these things, all those who opposed Him were put to shame and humiliated. But the entire crowd was rejoicing over all the glorious things being done by Him.

verses.heading: The Parables of the Mustard Seed and the Leaven / The Parables of the Mustard Seed and the Leaven / Matt. 13:31-33; Mk. 4:30-32
verses.text: Therefore Jesus said, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?
It is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.”
Again Jesus asked, “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like yeast that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour until the entire batch of dough was leavened.”

verses.heading: The Narrow Door / The Narrow Door / Matt. 7:13-14, 21-23
verses.text: Jesus was traveling through towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.
Someone asked Him, “Lord, are only a few people going to be saved?” He said to them,
“Strive and exert yourselves to the utmost to enter through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will try to enter but will not be able.

Once the master of the house has gotten up and shut the door, you will stand outside knocking on the door, saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’ But He will answer you, ‘I do not know where you come from.’
Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets.’
But He will reply, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you come from. Depart from Me, all you workers of unrighteousness and evildoing!’
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves thrown outside.
People will come from east and west, from north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
And take note: Some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”

verses.heading: Jesus Laments Over Jerusalem / Jesus Laments Over Jerusalem / Matt. 23:37-39
verses.text: At that very hour some Pharisees came and said to Jesus, “Leave this place and go away, because Herod wants to kill You.”
Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Listen: I am casting out demons and performing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will complete My work.’
Nevertheless, I must keep going on My way today and tomorrow and the day following, because it is unthinkable that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were not willing!
Look, your house is left to you desolate and abandoned. I tell you, you will not see Me again until the time comes when you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!’ ”

verses.heading: The Healing of a Man Suffering from Dropsy / The Healing of a Man Suffering from Dropsy
verses.text: One Sabbath day, when Jesus went to eat a meal at the house of a prominent Pharisee, they were watching Him closely with hostile intent.
Right there in front of Him was a man suffering from dropsy.
Jesus asked the lawyers and Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?”
But they remained silent, refusing to answer. Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.
Then Jesus asked them, “Which of you, if your son or ox falls into a well on the Sabbath day, will not immediately pull him out?”
They could give no answer to refute these arguments.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Guests and a Host at a Wedding Feast / The Parable of the Guests and a Host at a Wedding Feast
verses.text: When Jesus noticed how the invited guests were choosing the places of honor for themselves, He told them this parable:
“When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not take the place of honor, lest someone more honored than you has been invited by the host.
Then the one who invited both of you will come and say to you, ‘Give this person your place.’ And you will begin with shame to take the lowest and least honorable place.

Instead, when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when your host comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all the other guests.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

Then Jesus addressed His host, saying, “When you host a luncheon or dinner, do not call your friends, your siblings, your relatives, or your prosperous neighbors. If you do this, they may reciprocate by inviting you, and in this way you will receive your recompense.
Rather, when you host a feast, extend invitations to the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind.
Then you will experience blessing, because they lack the means to repay you. You will receive your reward at the resurrection of the righteous.’’

verses.heading: The Parable of the Great Dinner / The Parable of the Great Dinner / Matt. 22:1-10
verses.text: When one of those sharing the meal with Jesus heard these words, he declared to Him, “How blessed is the person who will share a meal in God’s kingdom!”
Jesus replied to him with a parable: “A certain man was hosting a magnificent banquet and sent out invitations to many people.
At the appointed hour for the dinner, he dispatched his servant to inform those who had received invitations, ‘Come now, because everything stands prepared.’
But one after another they all started offering excuses. The first declared to him, ‘I have purchased a piece of land, and it is necessary for me to go examine it. I ask you to excuse me.’
And another stated, ‘I have purchased five pairs of oxen, and I am going to test them. I ask you to excuse me.’
Yet another responded, ‘I have just married a wife, and for this reason I am unable to come.’

The servant returned and conveyed all these responses to his master. Then the master of the house grew angry and commanded his servant, ‘Go out at once into the city’s streets and narrow lanes and bring here the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’
The servant reported, ‘Master, what you commanded has been accomplished, and still there is available space.’
Then the master instructed the servant, ‘Go out to the highways and along the hedgerows and urge people to enter, so that my house may be filled.
I declare to you, not one of those individuals who received invitations will have a taste of my banquet.’ ”

verses.heading: The Cost of Discipleship / The Cost of Discipleship / Matt. 10:37-38
verses.text: Great crowds were journeying alongside Jesus. Turning toward them, He declared,
“If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother, and wife and children, and brothers and sisters, and indeed even his own life, he is unable to be My disciple.
Whoever does not bear his own cross and come after Me is unable to be My disciple.
For which among you, intending to construct a tower, does not first sit down and compute the expense to determine whether he has sufficient resources to finish it?
Otherwise, having laid the foundation and proving unable to complete the project, all who observe will start ridiculing him,
declaring, ‘This person initiated construction but lacked the ability to bring it to completion.’

Or what king, marching out to engage another king in battle, does not first sit down and deliberate whether he has the capability with ten thousand soldiers to confront the one advancing against him with twenty thousand?
And if he cannot, while the other king is still at a distance, he dispatches an embassy and requests conditions for peace.
So in the same manner, any among you who does not renounce all his possessions is unable to be My disciple.”

verses.heading: The Uselessness of Salt Without Taste / The Uselessness of Salt Without Taste / Matt. 5:13; Mk. 9:50
verses.text: Salt is excellent and beneficial, but if the salt becomes tasteless, by what means can its flavor be restored?
It proves suitable neither for the ground nor for the compost heap. People discard it. Let the one who has ears for hearing, hear.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Lost Sheep / The Parable of the Lost Sheep / Matt. 18:12-14
verses.text: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were approaching to hear Jesus.
But the Pharisees and the scribes were complaining, saying, “This person receives sinners and shares meals with them.”
So He communicated this parable to them:
“What person among you, possessing a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not abandon the ninety-nine in the wilderness and pursue the lost one until he locates it?
And having found it, he lays it on his shoulders with joy.
And arriving at his home, he summons his friends and neighbors, declaring to them, 'Share in my joy, because I have located my sheep that was lost!’
I declare to you that in this same manner, there will be greater joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous individuals who have no need of repentance.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Lost Coin / The Parable of the Lost Coin
verses.text: “Or what woman, possessing ten silver coins and losing one coin, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and conduct a thorough search until she discovers it?
And having discovered it, she gathers her friends and neighbors, declaring, ‘Share in my joy, because I have discovered the coin I had lost!’
In this same manner, I declare to you, joy occurs in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Prodigal Son / The Parable of the Prodigal Son
verses.text: Jesus went on to say: “There was a man who had two sons.
The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the portion of the inheritance that belongs to me.’ So the father apportioned his estate between them.
A short time later, the younger son gathered everything he owned and left for a far-off land. There he wasted his wealth through irresponsible and self-indulgent living.
When he had exhausted all his resources, a severe famine swept through that region, and he found himself in desperate need.
He went and attached himself to a citizen of that country, who sent him out to his fields to tend pigs.
He was so hungry that he wished he could eat the food given to the pigs, but no one offered him anything.
When he finally came to his right mind, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired workers have food to spare, while I am perishing here from hunger!
I will rise, return to my father, and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.
I am no longer deserving to be called your son. Treat me as one of your hired servants.” ’
He got up and went back to his father. While he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with deep compassion. He ran to him, embraced him, and kissed him warmly.
The son said, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
But the father said to his servants, ‘Hurry! Bring the finest robe and put it on him. Place a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf and slaughter it. Let us celebrate with a feast,
because this son of mine was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found.’ And they began to celebrate.
Meanwhile, the older son was working in the field. As he came near the house, he heard music and dancing.
He called one of the servants and asked what all this meant.
The servant said to him, ‘Your brother has returned, and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has received him back safe and well.’
The older son became angry and refused to enter the house. His father came out and urged him to come in.
But he answered his father, ‘Look, I have served you all these years and never ignored your commands. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours returned—after wasting your property with immoral living—you slaughtered the fattened calf for him!’
The father said to him, ‘My son, you are always with me, and everything I have belongs to you.
But it was right for us to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has now been found.’ ”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Unrighteous Manager / The Parable of the Unrighteous Manager
verses.text: Jesus also spoke to His disciples and said: “There was a wealthy man who employed a steward to manage his estate. Charges were brought to him that this steward was mismanaging and squandering his property.
So the master summoned him and said, ‘What is this report I hear about you? Turn in a full account of your administration, because you can no longer remain in charge.’

The steward began reasoning within himself, ‘What am I going to do now that my master is removing me from my position? I do not have the strength to do manual labor, and I am too ashamed to survive by begging.
I know what course of action I will take, so that after I am dismissed from my stewardship, people will receive me into their homes.’
So he called each one of his master’s debtors to him individually. He asked the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
He replied, ‘Eight hundred gallons of olive oil.’ The steward said to him, ‘Take your bill, sit down immediately, and revise it to four hundred.’
Then he said to another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ He answered, ‘A thousand measures of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill and change it to eight hundred.’

The master praised the dishonest steward, not for his corruption, but because he had acted with shrewd foresight. For the sons of this present age show greater practical wisdom in dealing with their own affairs than the sons of light do.
And I tell you, make use of earthly wealth to cultivate relationships for eternal purposes, so that when such wealth comes to an end, you will be welcomed into everlasting dwellings.
The one who proves faithful in very small matters will also be faithful in great matters, and the one who is dishonest in small things will also be dishonest in much.
Therefore, if you have not shown yourselves trustworthy in handling unrighteous wealth, who will entrust to you the true and lasting riches?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is truly your own?
No servant can remain loyal to two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will cling to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.”

verses.heading: Pharisaic Love of Money and Hypocrisy / Pharisaic Love of Money and Hypocrisy
verses.text: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, were listening to all these things and were mocking Him with contempt.

Jesus said to them, “You are the ones who present yourselves as righteous in the sight of men, but God has full knowledge of your hearts. What is highly esteemed among men is repulsive in the sight of God.”

verses.heading: The Law and the Kingdom of God / The Law and the Kingdom of God / Matt. 11:12–13
verses.text: “The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed up until the time of John. From that point on, the good news of the kingdom of God is being announced, and people are pressing into it with urgent determination.
But it would be easier for the entire created order to collapse than for the smallest mark of the Law to lose its authority or fail to be fulfilled.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman divorced from her husband also commits adultery.”

verses.heading: The Rich Man and Lazarus / The Rich Man and Lazarus
verses.text: “There was a rich man who clothed himself in purple garments and fine linen and lived in continual luxury and self-indulgence.
And laid at his gate was a poor man named Lazarus, whose body was covered with open sores.
He longed to be fed with what fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his wounds.
The day came when the poor man died, and he was carried by angels to Abraham’s side. The rich man also died and was buried.
While he was in Hades, suffering torment, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham from a great distance, with Lazarus resting at his side.
He cried out and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am suffering terribly in this flame.’

But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that during your lifetime you received what you considered good, while Lazarus received what was painful and harmful. Now he is being comforted here, and you are in anguish.
And beyond all this, a vast chasm has been permanently fixed between us and you, so that those who desire to pass from here to you are unable to do so, and no one can cross from there to us.’
Then he said, ‘I beg you, father, send Lazarus to my father’s household,
for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also come to this place of torment.’
But Abraham said, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; they must listen to them.’
He replied, ‘No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’ ”

verses.heading: Some Sayings of Jesus: Causes of Sin / Some Sayings of Jesus: Causes of Sin / Matt. 18:6-7; 21-22; Mk. 9:42
verses.text: Jesus told His disciples, “It is inevitable that temptations and occasions to sin will come into the world. But woe and judgment await the person who becomes the instrument through which they come!
It would be far better for that person to have a heavy millstone fastened around his neck and be hurled into the sea than to cause even one of these little believers to stumble and fall into sin.
Pay careful attention to your own conduct! If your brother commits a sin, confront him directly about it. If he repents and turns from it, forgive him.
Even if he sins against you seven times in a single day and returns to you seven times saying, ‘I repent,’ you must grant him forgiveness.”

verses.heading: Augmenting Faith / Augmenting Faith
verses.text: The apostles said to the Lord, “Grant us greater faith! Increase our capacity to believe and trust!”

The Lord replied, “If you possessed faith even as tiny as a mustard seed—the smallest of all seeds—you could command this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and transplanted into the sea,’ and it would obey you.”

verses.heading: Unmeritorious Servants / Unmeritorious Servants
verses.text: Jesus continued His teaching: “Suppose one of you has a servant who has been plowing the field or shepherding the sheep. When he returns from the field, would you immediately say to him, ‘Come at once and recline at the table to eat’?
Would you not rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, dress yourself properly, and serve me while I eat and drink. Afterward you may eat and drink your own meal’?
Does the master thank the servant simply for doing what was commanded of him? Certainly not.

In the same way, when you have done everything you were commanded to do, you should say, ‘We are unworthy servants who deserve no special recognition. We have merely done our duty and what was expected of us.’ ”

verses.heading: The Healing of the Ten Lepers / The Healing of the Ten Lepers
verses.text: While Jesus was traveling toward Jerusalem, He passed through the border region between Samaria and Galilee.
As He was entering a certain village, ten men afflicted with leprosy approached Him. Because of their ceremonial uncleanness, they stood at a distance as required by Law.
They raised their voices and called out, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us and heal us!”
When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go and show yourselves to the priests for examination and certification of your healing.” As they were going on their way in obedience, they were miraculously cleansed.
One of them, when he realized that he had been healed, turned back to Jesus, glorifying God with a loud voice.
He threw himself down at Jesus’ feet in gratitude and worship, thanking Him profusely. And this man was a Samaritan—a despised foreigner.
Jesus responded by asking, “Were not all ten cleansed from their leprosy? Where are the other nine?
Has no one returned to give glory and praise to God except this foreigner?”
Then Jesus said to him, “Stand up and go on your way. Your faith has made you completely well.”

verses.heading: The Coming of God’s Kingdom / The Coming of God’s Kingdom / Matt. 24:23-28; 37-41
verses.text: When the Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come, He answered them, “The kingdom of God does not come with careful observation of signs or with visible display.
People will not be able to say, ‘Look, here it is!’ or 'There it is!’ For the kingdom of God is already in your midst through My presence.”
Then Jesus said to His disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man—to experience My presence again—but you will not see it.
People will say to you, ‘Look, there He is!’ or ‘Here He is!’ Do not go running after them or follow them.
For when the Son of Man comes in His day, He will be like lightning that flashes and illuminates the sky from one end to the other—unmistakable and visible to all.
But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
Just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.
People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, right up until the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all without warning.
It was exactly the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building—carrying on with normal life.
But on the day Lot departed from Sodom, fire and burning sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
It will be precisely like this on the day when the Son of Man is revealed to the world.
On that day, no one who is on the housetop should go down into the house to retrieve their belongings. Likewise, no one in the field should turn back toward home.
Remember what happened to Lot’s wife when she looked back longingly.”
Whoever attempts to preserve and save his life will lose it, but whoever is willing to lose his life will preserve it for eternity.
I tell you, on that night two people will be lying in one bed together. One will be taken and the other will be left.
Two women will be grinding grain together at the mill. One will be taken and the other left.”*

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: The disciples asked Him, “Where will this happen, Lord?” Jesus replied, “Where the dead body is, there the vultures will naturally gather.” 35 A textual variant appears in some ancient manuscripts, inserting a verse 36. Its content— “Two [men] will be in the field. The one will be taken and the other will be left” —serves to harmonize the narrative with its parallel in the Gospel of Matthew 24:40
verses.html:
The disciples asked Him, “Where will this happen, Lord?” Jesus replied, “Where the dead body is, there the vultures will naturally gather.”
35 A textual variant appears in some ancient manuscripts, inserting a verse 36. Its content— “Two [men] will be in the field. The one will be taken and the other will be left” —serves to harmonize the narrative with its parallel in the Gospel of Matthew 24:40

verses.heading: The Parable of the Persistent Widow and the Judge / The Parable of the Persistent Widow and the Judge
verses.text: Jesus told His disciples a parable to teach them that they should always pray and never lose heart or give up.
He said: “In a certain town there was a judge who had no fear of God and no respect or regard for people.
There was a widow in that same town who kept coming to him repeatedly, pleading, ‘Grant me justice against my adversary.’
For a long time the judge refused to help her. But eventually he said to himself, ‘Even though I have no fear of God and no concern for people,
yet because this widow keeps bothering me persistently, I will grant her justice, so that she will not eventually wear me down completely with her continual coming.’ ”
The Lord said, “Pay attention to what this unjust judge says.
Will not God bring about justice for His chosen ones who cry out to Him day and night? Will He delay long in helping them?
I tell you, He will see that they receive justice, and He will do it quickly. However, when the Son of Man comes, will He find such faith and persistent, faithful prayer on the earth?”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector / The Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector
verses.text: Jesus also told this parable to some people who were confident in their own righteousness and looked down with contempt on everyone else:
“Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other was a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood apart by himself and prayed about himself: ‘God, I thank You that I am not like other people—robbers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector over there.
I fast twice a week and give a tenth of everything I earn and acquire.’
But the tax collector stood at a distance, far from the holy place. He would not even lift his eyes toward heaven, but beat his breast in contrition and said, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
I tell you, this man went home justified before God rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted by God.”

verses.heading: Receiving the Kingdom of God Like a Child / Receiving the Kingdom of God Like a Child / Matt. 19:13-15; Mk. 10:13-16
verses.text: People were bringing even their babies and infants to Jesus so that He might place His hands on them and bless them. When the disciples saw this, they rebuked the people for bothering Jesus.
But Jesus called the children to Himself and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not prevent them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child—with simple trust and humility—will never enter it.”

verses.heading: The Rich Ruler / The Rich Ruler / Matt. 19:16-30; Mk. 10:17-31
verses.text: A certain ruler, a man of authority and wealth, asked Jesus, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus answered him, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good in an absolute sense except God alone.
You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not give false testimony, honor your father and mother.’ ”*
The man replied confidently, “I have faithfully kept all these commandments since I was young.”
When Jesus heard this, He said to him, “You still lack one thing. Sell everything you possess and distribute the proceeds to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow Me.”
When the ruler heard this, he became extremely sad, for he was extraordinarily wealthy and could not bring himself to part with his possessions.
Jesus looked at him and said, “How hard it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God!
Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a sewing needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God!”
Those who heard this asked in amazement, “Who then can be saved?”
Jesus replied, “What is impossible with human beings is possible with God.”
Peter said, “Look, we have left everything we had—our homes, our occupations, our security—to follow You!”
Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left home or wife or brothers or sisters or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive many times as much in this present age, and in the age to come, eternal life.”

verses.heading: Jesus Speaks of His Death and Resurrection the Third Time / Jesus Speaks of His Death and Resurrection the Third Time / Matt. 20:17-19; Mk. 10:32-34
verses.text: Jesus took the Twelve aside privately and told them, “Listen carefully: We are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that has been written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled and accomplished.
He will be handed over to the Gentiles. They will mock Him, insult Him, and spit on Him in contempt.
They will flog Him mercilessly and kill Him. But on the third day He will rise again from the dead.”
The disciples did not understand any of this teaching. Its meaning was completely hidden from them, and they could not grasp what Jesus was talking about.

verses.heading: The Healing of a Blind Beggar Near Jericho / The Healing of a Blind Beggar Near Jericho / Matt. 20:29-34; Mk. 10:46-52
verses.text: As Jesus was approaching the city of Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road begging for alms.
When he heard the crowd passing by, he inquired what was happening.
They informed him, “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by this way.”
He called out loudly, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Those who were leading the procession rebuked him and told him to be quiet. But he shouted all the more insistently, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and ordered that the man be brought to Him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
“What do you want Me to do for you?” The blind man replied, “Lord, I want to receive my sight.”
Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you.”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Immediately he received his sight and began following Jesus, praising God. When all the people witnessed this miracle, they also gave praise to God. 20 Quoted from Ex. 20:12-16; Deut. 5:16-20

verses.heading: Zacchaeus Seeks Jesus / Zacchaeus Seeks Jesus
verses.text: Jesus entered the city of Jericho and was passing through it.
A man named Zacchaeus was there. He was a chief tax collector—a supervisor over other tax collectors—and he was very wealthy.
Zacchaeus wanted to see who Jesus was, but he could not see over the crowd because he was short in stature.
So he ran ahead of the crowd and climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree to see Jesus, since Jesus was going to pass that way.
When Jesus reached that spot, He looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, come down immediately. I must stay at your house today.”
So Zacchaeus came down quickly and welcomed Jesus gladly into his home.
All the people who saw this began muttering, "He has gone to be the guest of a notorious sinner."

But Zacchaeus stood before the Lord and said, “Look, Lord! Here and now I am giving half of my possessions to the poor. And if I have cheated anyone out of anything through false accusations, I will pay back four times the amount.”
Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this household, because this man, too, is a true son of Abraham by faith.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save those who are lost.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Ten Minas / The Parable of the Ten Minas / Matt. 25:14-30
verses.text: While the people were listening to this encounter, Jesus went on to tell them a parable. He did this because He was near Jerusalem and the people thought that the kingdom of God was going to appear immediately.
Jesus said: “A man of noble birth traveled to a distant country to be appointed as king and then to return home.
Before leaving, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas—a substantial sum. He instructed them, ‘Put this money to work in business until I return.’
But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to declare, ‘We do not want this man to reign as king over us.’
Nevertheless, he was appointed king and returned home. Then he summoned the servants to whom he had given the money, in order to find out what profit they had gained through trading.
The first servant came and reported, ‘Sir, your mina has earned ten more minas.’
His master commended him: ‘Well done, my good servant! Because you have been trustworthy and faithful in a very small matter, I am putting you in charge of ten cities.’
The second servant came and said, ‘Sir, your mina has earned five more minas.’
His master told him, ‘You are to be in charge of five cities.’
Then another servant came and said, ‘Sir, here is your mina. I have kept it safely laid away in a piece of cloth.
I was afraid of you, because you are a hard and demanding man. You take out what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.’
His master replied, ‘I will judge you by your own words, you wicked servant! You knew that I am a hard man, taking out what I did not put in and reaping what I did not sow?
Then why did you not put my money on deposit with the bankers, so that when I returned, I could have collected it with interest?’
Then he said to those standing nearby, ‘Take his mina away from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’
They protested, ‘Sir, he already has ten!’
The master replied, ‘I tell you that to everyone who has been faithful, more will be given. But from the one who has nothing—who has been unfaithful—even what he has will be taken away.
But those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign as king over them, bring them here and execute them in my presence.’ ”

verses.heading: The Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem / The Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem / Matt. 21:1-11; Mk. 11:1-11; Jn. 12:12-19
verses.text: After Jesus had said these things, He went on ahead of the group, going up toward Jerusalem.
As He approached Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples ahead,
saying to them, “Go to the village ahead of you. As you enter it, you will find a colt tied there that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here to Me.
If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?' simply say, 'The Lord needs it.’ ”
Those who were sent went ahead and found everything just as Jesus had told them.
As they were untying the colt, its owners asked them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
They answered, “The Lord needs it.”
They brought the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks on it, and set Jesus on it.
As Jesus rode along, people spread their cloaks on the road as a carpet of honor.
When He came near the place where the road descends from the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples began joyfully praising God in loud voices for all the miracles they had witnessed:
“Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
Some Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples and make them stop!”
Jesus replied, “I tell you, if they kept silent, the very stones would cry out in proclamation.”

verses.heading: Jesus Weeps Over Jerusalem / Jesus Weeps Over Jerusalem
verses.text: As Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city spread before Him, He wept over it
and said, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes and you cannot see it.
The days will come upon you when your enemies will build siege walls against you. They will encircle you and hem you in on every side.
They will dash you to the ground—you and your children within your walls. They will not leave one stone standing on another, because you did not recognize the time when God visited you.”

verses.heading: The Cleansing of the Temple / The Cleansing of the Temple / Matt. 21:12-17; Mk. 11:15-19; Jn. 2:13-22
verses.text: When Jesus entered the temple courts, He began driving out those who were selling sacrificial animals and exchanging money.
He declared to them, “It is written in Scripture, ‘My house shall be a house of prayer,’ but you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”
Every day Jesus was teaching in the temple courts. But the chief priests, the teachers of the Law, and the leaders among the people were actively seeking to kill Him.
Yet they could not find any way to accomplish this, because all the people hung on His words and listened to Him intently.

verses.heading: Jesus’ Authority Questioned / Jesus’ Authority Questioned / Matt. 21:23-27; Mk. 11:27-33
verses.text: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the good news, the chief priests and teachers of the Law, together with the elders, confronted Him.
They challenged Him, “Tell us by what authority You are doing these things. Who gave You this authority to teach and act as You do?”
Jesus replied, “I will also ask you a question. Tell Me:
Was John’s baptism from heaven—from divine authority—or from human origin?”
They discussed this among themselves and reasoned, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask us, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From human origin,’ all the people will stone us, because they are firmly convinced that John was a prophet.”
So they responded that they could not tell where John’s authority originated.
And Jesus declared to them, “Neither will I inform you by what authority I perform these actions.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Wicked Farmers / The Parable of the Wicked Farmers / Matt. 21:33-46; Mk. 12:1-12
verses.text: Then He began communicating this parable to the people: “A certain man established a vineyard, rented it out to farmers, and departed to a distant region for an extended period.
When the season dispatched a servant to the farmers so they might give him his portion of the vineyard’s produce. But the farmers struck the servant and sent him back without anything.
He proceeded to send another servant, but they beat him as well, subjected him to shameful treatment, and sent him back empty-handed.
He went on to send a third, and they wounded this one and cast him out.
Then the vineyard’s owner said, ‘What course of action should I take? I will send my son whom I love. Surely they will show reverence to him.’
But upon seeing the son, the farmers reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him so that the inheritance will transfer to us.’
So they expelled him from the vineyard and killed him. What action, then, will the vineyard’s owner take against them?
He will come and eliminate those farmers and entrust the vineyard to different people.” Upon hearing this, they responded, “May such a thing never occur!”
But He looked intently at them and asked, “What then is the significance of this written passage: ‘The stone that the builders discarded has become the chief cornerstone’?*
Everyone falling upon that stone will be shattered to pieces, and the person upon whom it falls will be pulverized.”*
The scribes and the chief priests sought to seize Him at that very moment, for they understood that He had directed this parable against them. Yet they feared the people’s response.

verses.heading: Paying Taxes to Caesar / Paying Taxes to Caesar / Matt. 22:15-22; Mk. 12:13-17
verses.text: So they watched Him closely and sent agents who posed as righteous men, hoping to trap Him in His speech so they might deliver Him to the governor's jurisdiction and authority.
They questioned Him, saying, “Teacher, we recognize that You communicate and instruct rightly and without error. You demonstrate no favoritism but teach God’s way according to truth.
Is it lawful for us to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?”
But perceiving their craftiness, He said to them,
“Display a denarius for Me. Whose likeness and inscription does it bear?” They replied, “Caesar's.”
He declared to them, “Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
They proved unable to entrap Him in His statement in the people’s presence. Marveling at His response, they became silent.

verses.heading: Concerning Marriage and the Resurrection / Concerning Marriage and the Resurrection / Matt. 22:23-33; Mk. 12:18-27
verses.text: Some of the Sadducees—who deny that there is a resurrection—came to Jesus with a hypothetical question.
They said, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us in the Law that if a man’s brother dies leaving a wife but no children, the man must marry the widow and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there existed seven brothers. The first took a wife and died without children.
The second married her,
and the third took her. In this same manner, all seven married her and died without leaving children.
Afterward, the woman died as well.
In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife does she become, since all seven had her as wife?”
Jesus responded to them, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
But those judged worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
For they are no longer able to die, being equal to angels. And they are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised—even Moses indicated this at the passage about the bush, when he designates the Lord as ‘the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
Now He is not God of the dead but of the living, for to Him all are alive.”
Some of the scribes replied, “Teacher, You have spoken well!”
And they no longer had courage to question Him about anything.

verses.heading: Question about David’s Son / Question about David’s Son / Matt. 22:41-46; Mk. 12:35-37
verses.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Why do people say that the Christ is the son of David?
David himself declares in the Book of Psalms: ‘The Lord said to my Lord: “Sit at My right hand
until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.” ’
David calls Him ‘Lord.’ How then can the Christ be his son?”

verses.heading: Beware of the Scribes / Beware of the Scribes / Matt. 23:1-36; Mk. 12:38-40; Lk. 11:37-54
verses.text: While all the people were listening, Jesus said to His disciples,

“Beware of the teachers of the Law. They love to walk around in flowing robes and love to receive respectful greetings in the marketplaces. They desire the most important seats in the synagogues and the places of honour at banquets.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: They devour widows’ houses, and for show they make lengthy prayers. These men will receive the most severe condemnation and punishment.” 17 Quoted from Ps. 118:22 18 Referring to Is. 8:14-15

verses.heading: The Poor Widow’s Offering / The Poor Widow’s Offering / Matt. 12:41-44
verses.text: Jesus looked up and observed the wealthy people depositing their generous gifts into the temple treasury.
He also noticed a certain poor widow placing two small copper coins into the offering—the smallest denomination of currency.
Jesus said to His disciples, “Truly, I tell you that this poor widow has given more than all the others combined.
For all these wealthy people gave their gifts out of their abundance and surplus. But she, out of her poverty and need, has given all the means of livelihood she possessed.”

verses.heading: Prediction of the Destruction of the Temple / Prediction of the Destruction of the Temple / Matt. 24:1-2; Mk. 13:1-2
verses.text: As some of the disciples were commenting on the temple—how it was adorned with beautiful stones and dedicated offerings—Jesus made a startling prediction.
He said, “Regarding these things you are admiring—the days will come when not one stone will be left upon another. Everything will be completely demolished.”

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Beginning of Woes / Eschatological Discourse: The Beginning of Woes / Matt. 24:3-14; Mk. 13:3-13
verses.text: The disciples asked Him, “Teacher, when will these things happen? What will be the sign indicating when these events are about to occur?”
Jesus answered, “Be careful that you are not led astray. Many will come claiming My authority, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and ‘The time of the end has drawn near!’ Do not follow after them.
When you hear reports of wars and political upheavals, do not be terrified or panic-stricken. These things must take place first, but the end of the age will not come immediately.”
Jesus continued His instruction: “Nation will rise up in conflict against nation, and kingdom will war against kingdom.
There will be massive earthquakes, and in various places famines and devastating plagues. There will be terrifying events and great miraculous signs appearing from heaven.

But before all these things happen, they will arrest you and persecute you severely. They will hand you over to the synagogues for punishment and throw you into prisons. You will be brought before kings and governors because of your association with My name.
This persecution will result in opportunities for you to bear witness and testify about Me.
Therefore, settle it firmly in your hearts not to worry in advance about how you will defend yourselves or what you will say.
For I will give you a mouth to speak and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.
You will be betrayed even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. Some of you will be put to death for your faith.
You will be hated by everyone because of your identification with My name.
Yet not a single hair of your head will perish.
By your patient endurance and steadfast faithfulness, you will preserve your souls and gain eternal life.”

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: Prediction of the Destruction of Jerusalem / Eschatological Discourse: Prediction of the Destruction of Jerusalem / Matt. 24:15-21; Mk. 13:14-19
verses.text: Jesus continued, “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then understand that its desolation has come near.
At that time, let those in Judea flee immediately to the mountains. Let those inside the city depart quickly. Let those in the countryside not enter the city.
For these will be days of divine vengeance, when all the things written in Scripture will be fulfilled.
How terrible it will be for women who are pregnant and for those nursing infants in those days! There will be great distress upon the land and divine wrath against this people.

They will fall by the edge of the sword and be taken captive into all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down and controlled by Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are completed and fulfilled.”

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Coming of the Son of Man / Eschatological Discourse: The Coming of the Son of Man / Matt. 24:29-31; Mk. 13:24-27
verses.text: Jesus also spoke about more distant events: “There will be observable signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars. On the earth, the nations will be overwhelmed with anxiety and confusion as they face the violent roaring and upheaval of the sea and its waves.
People will faint from terror and apprehension about what is coming upon the world. The powers of the heavens will be shaken and destabilized.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory to establish His kingdom.
When these things begin to take place, stand up straight and lift up your heads in confidence, because your redemption and deliverance is drawing near!”

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Lesson of the Fig Tree / Eschatological Discourse: The Lesson of the Fig Tree / Matt. 24:32-35; Mk. 13:28-31
verses.text: Jesus spoke a parable to them: “Observe the fig tree and all the other trees.
As soon as they sprout leaves, you see for yourselves and know that summer is already near.
In the same way, when you see these prophesied events occurring, know with certainty that the kingdom of God is near.
Truly, I tell you that this generation will not pass away until all these things have taken place. Some of these events will occur within the lifetime of those listening.
Heaven and earth will pass away and cease to exist, but My words will never pass away.”

verses.heading: Eschatological Discourse: The Imperatives to Pay Attention to Oneself and to Keep Watching Always / Eschatological Discourse: The Imperatives to Pay Attention to Oneself and to Keep Watching Always
verses.text: Jesus warned, “Pay careful attention to yourselves. Be on guard lest your hearts become weighed down and dulled by dissipation, drunkenness, and the anxious worries of this life. If you are not vigilant, that day will come upon you suddenly and unexpectedly like a trap.
For it will come upon all those who live on the face of the whole earth.
Stay awake at all times. Pray constantly that you may have strength to escape all these things that will happen, and to stand with confidence before the Son of Man when He returns.”

verses.heading: Jesus Teaches in the Temple / Jesus Teaches in the Temple
verses.text: During the day, Jesus was teaching in the temple courts. But at night He would leave the city and spend the night on the hill called the Mount of Olives.
All the people would come to Him at daybreak in the temple to listen to His teaching.

verses.heading: The Conspiracy to Kill Jesus / The Conspiracy to Kill Jesus / Matt. 26:1-5, 14-16; Mk. 14:1-2, 10-11; Jn. 11:45-53
verses.text: The Feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called the Passover, was drawing near.
The chief priests and the scribes were actively seeking how they might put Jesus to death, but they feared the reaction of the people who honored Jesus.

verses.heading: Judas Will Betray Jesus at the Instigation of Satan / Judas Will Betray Jesus at the Instigation of Satan
verses.text: Then Satan himself entered into Judas, the one called Iscariot, who was numbered among the twelve apostles.
Judas went away and held discussions with the chief priests and the officers of the temple guard about how he might betray Jesus to them.
They were delighted and agreed to pay him money for his treachery.
Judas consented to their proposal and began looking for a favorable opportunity to betray Jesus to them when no crowd was present.

verses.heading: Jesus Celebrates the Passover with the Disciples / Jesus Celebrates the Passover with the Disciples / Matt. 26:17-25; Mk. 14:12-21; Jn. 13:21-30
verses.text: Then came the day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed according to the Law.
Jesus sent Peter and John with instructions, saying, “Go and make preparations for us to eat the Passover meal together.”
They asked Him, “Where do You want us to make preparations?”
Jesus said to them, “Listen carefully: When you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into whatever house he enters.
Say to the owner of that house, ‘The Teacher asks you: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”
Peter and John departed and found everything exactly as Jesus had told them. They prepared the Passover meal.

verses.heading: The Lord’s Supper Instituted / The Lord’s Supper Instituted / Matt. 26:26-30; Mk. 14:22-26; 1 Cor. 11:23-25
verses.text: When the hour arrived, Jesus reclined at the table with the twelve apostles.
He said to them, “I have earnestly and intensely desired to eat this Passover meal with you before I suffer.
For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it finds its fulfillment in the kingdom of God.”
Jesus took the cup, gave thanks to God, and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
For I tell you, from this moment forward, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes in its fullness.”
Then Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, which is given for you as a sacrifice. Do this in remembrance of Me.”
In the same way, He took the cup after they had eaten, saying, “This cup represents the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
But understand this: The hand of the one who is betraying Me is with Me right now on this table.
The Son of Man will go to His death according to what has been predetermined and decreed by God. But woe to that man by whom He is betrayed!”
The disciples began discussing among themselves which one of them it might possibly be who would do such a thing.

verses.heading: Dispute About Who Seems to be the Greatest / Dispute About Who Seems to be the Greatest
verses.text: A serious argument arose among the disciples concerning which one of them should be regarded as the most prominent.
Jesus addressed them, saying, “The rulers of the nations dominate their peoples, and those who exercise authority expect recognition as benefactors.
This must not define life among you. Rather, the one who is regarded as greatest must take the place of the least, and the one who governs must live as a servant.
Consider this: who is regarded as greater, the one reclining at the table or the one attending to him? Is it not the one reclining? Yet here I am among you, living as one who serves.
You are the ones who have remained with Me during My trials and hardships.
Just as My Father entrusted royal authority to Me, I now entrust a kingdom to you,
so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and you will sit on thrones exercising judgment over the twelve tribes of Israel.”

verses.heading: Peter’s Denial Foretold / Peter’s Denial Foretold / Matt. 26:31–35; Mk. 14:27–31; Jn. 13:36–38
verses.text: Jesus then said, “Simon, Simon, listen carefully. Satan has demanded permission to test all of you, shaking you as grain is shaken in a sieve.
But I have interceded for you in particular, that your faith may not collapse. When you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
Peter responded, “Lord, I am prepared to go with You both to imprisonment and to death.”
Jesus replied, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.”

verses.heading: Scripture Must Be Fulfilled / Scripture Must Be Fulfilled
verses.text: Jesus asked them, “When I sent you out without money, supplies, or sandals, did you lack anything?” They answered, “Nothing.”
He said, “But now, whoever has money should take it, and likewise supplies. And whoever does not have a sword should sell his outer garment and acquire one.
For I tell you that what is written must be fulfilled in Me: ‘He was numbered among the lawless.’ Everything written about Me is now approaching its completion.”
They said, “Lord, here are two swords.” He answered, “That is sufficient.”

verses.heading: Jesus Prays on the Mount of Olives / Jesus Prays on the Mount of Olives / Matt. 26:36–46; Mk. 14:32–42
verses.text: Jesus departed and went, according to His established practice, to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed Him.
When He arrived at the place, He said to them, “Pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
He withdrew from them about a stone’s throw away, knelt down, and began to pray.
He said, “Father, if You are willing, remove this cup from Me. Yet not My will, but Yours, must be done.”
Then an angel from heaven appeared to Him, strengthening Him.
Being in deep anguish, He prayed with greater intensity, and His sweat became like heavy drops of blood falling to the ground.
When He rose from prayer, He came to the disciples and found them asleep, exhausted by sorrow.
He said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation.”

verses.heading: The Arrest of Jesus / The Arrest of Jesus / Matt. 26:47–56; Mk. 14:43–50; Jn. 18:3–11
verses.text: While He was still speaking, a crowd appeared, led by Judas, one of the twelve. He approached Jesus to greet Him with a kiss.
Jesus said to him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
When those around Jesus saw what was unfolding, they asked, “Lord, should we strike with the sword?”
One of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
Jesus said, “Enough. Stop this.” And He touched the man’s ear and healed him.
Then Jesus said to the chief priests, officers of the temple guard, and elders who had come for Him, “Have you come with swords and clubs as though I were a violent criminal?
I was with you daily in the temple teaching, and you did not seize Me. But this is your hour, when the authority of darkness is permitted to act.”

verses.heading: Peter Denies Jesus / Peter Denies Jesus / Matt. 26:57–58, 69–75; Mk. 14:53–54, 66–72; Jn. 18:12–18, 25–27
verses.text: They arrested Jesus and led Him away to the residence of the high priest. Peter followed at a distance.
When a fire had been lit in the center of the courtyard and people sat down together, Peter sat among them.
A servant girl saw him seated by the fire, looked closely at him, and said, “This man was also with Him.”
But Peter denied it, saying, “Woman, I do not know Him.”
Shortly afterward, another said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter replied, “Man, I am not.”
About an hour later another insisted strongly, “Certainly this man was also with Him, for he is a Galilean.”
Peter answered, “Man, I do not know what you are saying.” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked directly at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word the Lord had spoken to him, that before the rooster crowed he would deny Him three times.
And Peter went outside and wept bitterly.

verses.heading: Jesus Mocked and Beaten / Jesus Mocked and Beaten / Matt. 26:67–68; Mk. 14:65
verses.text: The men guarding Jesus mocked Him and struck Him.
They blindfolded Him and demanded, “Prophesy. Who struck You?”
And they hurled many other blasphemous insults against Him.

verses.heading: Jesus Before the Council / Jesus Before the Council / Matt. 26:59–66; Mk. 14:55–64; Jn. 18:19–24
verses.text: When daylight came, the elders of the people assembled, including the chief priests and scribes, and they brought Him before their council.
They said, “If You are the Christ, tell us.” He replied, “If I tell you, you will not believe,
and if I question you, you will not answer.
But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
They all said, “Are You then the Son of God?” He answered, “You yourselves declare that I am.”
Then they said, “What further testimony do we need? We have heard it ourselves from His own mouth.”

verses.heading: Jesus Before Pilate / Jesus Before Pilate / Matt. 27:1-2, 11-14; Mk. 15:1-5; Jn. 18:28-38
verses.text: The whole assembly of the Sanhedrin rose up and brought Jesus before Pilate, the Roman governor.
They began to accuse Him, saying, “We have found this man subverting and perverting our nation. He forbids paying taxes to Caesar, and He claims to be Christ—a King.”
Pilate questioned Jesus directly: “Are You the King of the Jews?’’ Jesus answered him, “You have said so. The words are yours.”
Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no basis for guilt in this man. He has committed no crime deserving punishment.”
But they kept insisting forcefully, “He stirs up the people with His teaching throughout all Judea, starting from Galilee and coming all the way here to Jerusalem.”

verses.heading: Jesus Before Herod / Jesus Before Herod
verses.text: When Pilate heard this mention of Galilee, he inquired whether the man was a Galilean.
When he learned that Jesus fell under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who happened to be in Jerusalem during those days.
When Herod saw Jesus, he was extremely glad. He had been wanting to see Him for a long time because he had heard reports about Him. Herod was hoping to see Jesus perform some miraculous sign.
Herod questioned Jesus at length with many words, but Jesus gave him no answer whatsoever.
The chief priests and scribes stood by, fiercely accusing Jesus.
Herod, along with his soldiers, treated Jesus with contempt and mocked Him. They dressed Him in an elegant, shining robe to ridicule His claim to kingship, then sent Him back to Pilate.
Herod and Pilate, who had previously been enemies, became friends with each other on that very day.

verses.heading: Jesus Receives a Verdict of Condemnation / Jesus Receives a Verdict of Condemnation / Matt. 27:15-26; Mk. 15:6-15; Jn. 18:39–19:16
verses.text: Pilate assembled the chief priests, the ruling authorities, and the people together.

He declared to them, “You delivered this man to me with accusations that He was stirring up rebellion among the people. I have conducted a thorough examination in your presence and have discovered no basis for the charges you are leveling against Him.
Herod also found nothing worthy of condemnation, which is why he returned Him to us. It is evident that He has committed no offense deserving execution.
I will therefore have Him scourged and then set Him free.”*
But the entire crowd erupted, shouting in one voice, “Remove this man from our sight! Give us Barabbas instead!”
Now Barabbas was someone who had been incarcerated for leading an uprising within the city and for committing murder.
Pilate spoke to them once more, desiring to set Jesus free.
But they continued shouting back, “Crucify! Crucify Him!”

A third time Pilate questioned them, “What crime has this man actually committed? I have discovered nothing in Him that warrants the death penalty. I will therefore discipline Him with a beating and let Him go.’’
But they persisted with loud, insistent voices, demanding that He be crucified. Their shouting gained momentum and overpowered all opposition.
Then Pilate rendered his verdict, deciding to grant what they were demanding.
He freed the man who had been jailed for insurrection and murder—the very one they had requested. But Jesus, he handed over to their will to be crucified.

verses.heading: The Crucifixion of Jesus / The Crucifixion of Jesus / Matt. 27:32-44; Mk. 15:21-32; Jn. 19:17-27
verses.text: As they led Jesus away for execution, they grabbed hold of a man named Simon, a native of Cyrene, who was entering the city from the rural areas. They forced him to carry the cross, making him walk behind Jesus.
A substantial multitude of people followed Him, including women who were beating their breasts and wailing in grief over Him.
But Jesus turned toward them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, stop weeping over Me. Weep instead for yourselves and for your children.
For the time is certainly approaching when people will say, ‘How blessed are the women who never had children, the wombs that never conceived, and the breasts that never nursed an infant!’
At that time people will cry out to the mountains, ‘Collapse on top of us!’ and to the hills, ‘Bury us and conceal us!’
For if such things happen to the green tree that is full of vitality, what will become of the dry tree?”
Two others, both criminals, were also being taken away to be put to death alongside Jesus.
Upon arriving at the location known as The Skull, they crucified Him there along with the criminals—positioning one to His right and one to His left.
Jesus spoke these words: “Father, pardon them, for they have no comprehension of what they are doing.” The soldiers then proceeded to distribute His garments among themselves by throwing dice.

The crowd stood observing the scene. Meanwhile, the religious leaders ridiculed Him with scorn, declaring, “He rescued others from their afflictions. If He truly is God’s Messiah, the Chosen One, let Him rescue Himself!”
The soldiers likewise mocked Him. They approached and extended sour wine toward Him.
They taunted Him, saying, “If You are truly the King of the Jews, deliver Yourself from this cross!”
Above Him was posted a placard with this inscription: “This is the King of the Jews.”
One of the criminals who was hanging there began hurling abuse at Jesus: “Are You not the Christ? Prove it by saving Yourself and us!”
But the other criminal responded with a rebuke: “Have you no fear of God whatsoever, considering you are experiencing the identical punishment?
Our punishment is entirely just, for we are receiving exactly what our actions have earned. But this man has committed absolutely nothing improper.”
Then he said, “Jesus, keep me in Your memory when You enter Your royal domain.”
Jesus replied to him, “I assure you with absolute certainty: this very day you will be with Me in Paradise.”

verses.heading: The Death of Jesus / The Death of Jesus / Matt. 27:45-56; Mk. 15:33-41; Jn. 19:28-30
verses.text: By this time it was approximately the sixth hour, and darkness enveloped the entire region until the ninth hour.
The sun ceased giving its light. The massive veil of the temple sanctuary split down the center into two pieces.
Jesus cried out in a powerful voice, “Father, into Your care I entrust My spirit!” Having spoken these words, He breathed his last.
When the centurion witnessed what had transpired, he began praising God, proclaiming, “This man was certainly righteous and without guilt!”
All the crowds that had assembled to observe this spectacle, upon seeing what had occurred, returned to their homes striking their chests in sorrow and regret.
All who were acquainted with Jesus, including the women who had accompanied Him from Galilee, stood far off observing these events.

verses.heading: The Burial of Jesus / The Burial of Jesus / Matt. 27:57-61; Mk. 15:42-47; Jn. 19:38-42
verses.text: Now there was a man named Joseph, a member of the Sanhedrin Council—a man of good character and righteousness.
He had not given his approval to the Council’s plan and their actions against Jesus. He came from the Judean town of Arimathea and was eagerly anticipating the arrival of God’s kingdom.
This man approached Pilate courageously and requested permission to take possession of Jesus’ body.
After taking the body down, he wrapped it in fine linen fabric and laid it in a rock-hewn tomb where no one had previously been buried.
This took place on the Preparation Day, with the Sabbath about to commence at sunset.
The women who had journeyed with Jesus from Galilee followed closely behind Joseph. They carefully noted the tomb’s location and observed exactly how His body was positioned.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Then they went back and made preparations of aromatic spices and fragrant ointments. However, they observed the Sabbath rest in accordance with the commandment. 16 A textual variant present in part of the manuscript tradition incorporates verse 17. Its phrasing, “ Now he was duty-bound to release to them one person at the Feast ,” serves to bring the narrative into conformity with the Synoptic and Johannine parallels (Matt. 27:15; Mk. 15:6; Jn. 18:39)
verses.html:
Then they went back and made preparations of aromatic spices and fragrant ointments. However, they observed the Sabbath rest in accordance with the commandment.
16 A textual variant present in part of the manuscript tradition incorporates verse 17. Its phrasing, “ Now he was duty-bound to release to them one person at the Feast ,” serves to bring the narrative into conformity with the Synoptic and Johannine parallels (Matt. 27:15; Mk. 15:6; Jn. 18:39)

verses.heading: The Resurrection / The Resurrection / Matt. 28:1-10; Mk. 16:1-8; Jn. 20:1-10
verses.text: At daybreak on the first day of the week, the women arrived at the tomb carrying the aromatic spices they had made ready.
They found that the stone blocking the tomb’s entrance had been rolled aside.
Upon entering, they were unable to locate the body of the Lord Jesus.
As they stood there completely bewildered by this situation, two men dressed in garments that gleamed brilliantly suddenly appeared standing next to them.
Filled with terror, the women dropped to the ground with their faces downward. The men asked them, “Why are you searching for the Living One in a place of death?
He is not in this place—He has risen! Recall what He told you when He was still with you in Galilee.
He declared that the Son of Man had to be handed over to sinful people, undergo crucifixion, and be raised to life on the third day.”
At that moment the women recalled His words.
They hurried back from the tomb and recounted everything to the eleven and to everyone else who was with them.
The ones reporting these events to the apostles were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women in their company.
But the apostles regarded their account as utter foolishness and refused to believe them.

Peter, however, jumped up and raced to the tomb. When he bent down to peer inside, he observed nothing except the linen burial cloths lying by themselves. He departed, deeply puzzled about what had taken place.

verses.heading: On the Road to Emmaus / On the Road to Emmaus / Mk. 16:12-13
verses.text: That same day, two of His followers were making their way to a village named Emmaus, located approximately seven miles distant from Jerusalem.
They were engaged in conversation about everything that had occurred.
As they talked and reasoned together, Jesus Himself drew near and joined them on their journey.
Yet their eyes were restrained so they could not recognize His identity.
He asked them, “What matters are you debating with each other as you travel? They came to a halt, their expressions filled with sadness.
The one called Cleopas responded, “Are You the only person visiting Jerusalem who remains unaware of the events that have unfolded there during these past few days?”
He asked them, “What events?” They replied, "The events involving Jesus of Nazareth, who demonstrated Himself to be a prophet powerful in both action and teaching before God and all the people.
The chief priests and our leaders handed Him over to receive a death sentence, and they had Him crucified.
Yet we were holding onto the hope that He was the one expected to liberate Israel. What is more, this is now the third day since all this took place.
Furthermore, certain women from our group have left us astounded. They visited the tomb at first light this morning
but failed to find His body there. They returned claiming they had witnessed a vision of angels who announced that He is alive!
Some of our companions then went to the tomb and discovered conditions exactly as the women had described, but Him they did not see.”
He said to them, “How foolish you are, and how sluggish your hearts are to trust everything the prophets declared!
Was it not ordained that the Messiah should endure these sufferings and then enter into His glory?”
Then, starting with Moses and continuing through all the Prophets, He interpreted for them what was written about Himself throughout all the Scriptures.
As they drew near to the village that was their destination, He gave the impression He intended to continue farther.
But they pressed Him earnestly, saying, “Remain here with us, because evening is approaching and the day has nearly ended.” So He entered to lodge with them.
As He reclined at the table with them, He took bread, offered a blessing, broke it into pieces, and distributed it to them.
At that instant their eyes were fully opened, and they recognised Him. But immediately He disappeared from their view.
They said to each other, “Did not our hearts feel as though they were aflame within us as He conversed with us along the road and unfolded the meaning of the Scriptures for us?”
They rose up that very hour and made their way back to Jerusalem, where they located the eleven and their companions assembled together.
These were declaring, “The Lord has genuinely risen! He has made an appearance to Simon!”
Then the two recounted what had transpired on the road and how they had come to recognize Jesus when He broke the bread.

verses.heading: Jesus’ Appearance to the Disciples and the Great Commission / Jesus’ Appearance to the Disciples and the Great Commission / Matt. 28:16-20; Mk. 16:14-18; Jn. 20:19-23; Acts 1:6-8
verses.text: As they were discussing these matters, Jesus Himself took His place among them and said, “Peace to you.”
They were shocked and overcome with fear, convinced they were witnessing a ghostly apparition.
He asked them, “Why are you so disturbed? Why do questions of doubt surface in your minds?
Examine My hands and My feet—confirm that it is truly I! Put your hands on Me and verify this for yourselves. A spirit does not possess flesh and bones, which you can plainly see I have.”
Having said this, He displayed His hands and feet to them.
While they remained unable to believe because of their overwhelming joy and continued to marvel, He asked, “Have you any food available here?”
They handed Him a portion of cooked fish.
He accepted it and consumed it before their eyes.
Then He told them, “This is what I explained to you while I was still among you: everything recorded about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to reach fulfillment.”
Then He opened their understanding so they could comprehend the Scriptures.
He explained to them, “It stands written that the Messiah would suffer and rise from death on the third day,
and that repentance leading to forgiveness of sins would be proclaimed in His name to all the nations, commencing in Jerusalem.
