You are witnesses to all these events.
Take notice: I am sending upon you what My Father has promised. Remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from heaven.”

verses.heading: The Ascension / The Ascension / Mk. 16:19-20; Acts 1:9-11
verses.text: Then He led them out to the vicinity of Bethany, and lifting His hands, He pronounced a blessing upon them.
While He was in the act of blessing them, He parted from them and was taken up into heaven.
After worshipping Him, they returned to Jerusalem filled with immense joy.
They spent their time constantly in the temple, offering praise and glory to God.

verses.heading: The Enfleshment of the Word / The Enfleshment of the Word
verses.text: Before time began, before creation came into existence, the Word already was. The Word existed in intimate fellowship with God, sharing in the divine presence. And this Word was Himself fully divine—the Word was God in His essential nature.
This same One, the Word, existed from eternity past in intimate communion with God the Father.
Every created thing owes its existence to Him. He was the active agent in bringing all things into being. Apart from His creative work, not even one thing that exists would have come into existence.
Within Him resided life itself— the very source and essence of life. And this life that He possessed served as the illuminating light for humanity, revealing truth and dispelling darkness.
This light continues to shine forth into the darkness of human sin and ignorance, and the darkness has proven powerless to extinguish it, overcome it, or even comprehend it.
God commissioned a man to appear on the scene of human history, and his name was John.
This individual came with a specific mission: to bear witness concerning the Light, in order that all people might come to faith through his testimony about the Light.
John himself was not the Light he proclaimed; rather, he came for the purpose of bearing witness to and pointing others toward the Light.
The genuine Light, who provides spiritual illumination to every person who comes into the world, was at that very moment making His entrance into human history.
He was present in the world that He Himself had created through His power, yet the world and its people failed to recognize Him or acknowledge His identity.
He came to His own people—Israel, who stood in covenant relationship with God under the Law—but His own people did not receive Him.

Yet to all those who did receive Him and welcome His presence, to those who placed their trust in His name and person, He granted the authority and privilege to become children of God, adopted into His family.

These individuals were born into God’s family not through natural descent or bloodline, not through human desire or the physical act of procreation, not through the decision or effort of any human being, but through the supernatural work of God Himself.

The eternal Word took on human flesh and made His dwelling among us as a man, taking up residence in our midst. We have gazed upon His glory with our own eyes—a glory that befits the unique Son who came from the Father. He was abundantly filled with grace that provides what we do not deserve, and truth that reveals reality as it truly is.

John bore testimony concerning Him and made a public declaration, proclaiming these words: “This is the One about whom I spoke previously when I said, ‘The One who is coming after me in time has surpassed me in rank and dignity, because He existed before me in eternity.’ ”
For out of the abundant fullness of His inexhaustible resources, all of us have received blessing upon blessing, one gracious gift replacing another in continuous succession.
For the Law with its demands and requirements was given through Moses as an intermediary, but grace that pardons and truth that liberates came into the world through Jesus Christ.

No human being has ever gazed directly upon God at any time in history. The unique, one-and-only God, the One who eternally exists in the closest relationship with the Father, that very One has made Him known and revealed Him fully to humanity.

verses.heading: The Testimony of John the Baptist / The Testimony of John the Baptist / Mt. 3:1-12; Mk. 1:2-8; Lk. 3:15-17
verses.text: This is the testimony that John gave when the Jewish religious authorities sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem with instructions to interrogate him, demanding to know, “Who do you claim to be?”
John made a clear and unambiguous confession without any denial or evasion. He openly confessed, “I am not the Christ, the Messiah you are expecting.”

Therefore they pressed him further with their questions: “Then who are you claiming to be? Are you Elijah, the prophet who was to return?” And his response was direct: “I am not.” They continued their interrogation: “Are you the Prophet that Moses promised would come?” And he answered definitively, “No, I am not.”

So they said to him with some urgency, “Tell us who you are, so that we may carry back an answer to those who commissioned us to come here. What do you declare concerning your own identity and mission?”

He responded by saying, “I am the voice of one person crying out in the wilderness with this message: ‘Prepare a straight highway for the Lord to travel upon,’* exactly as Isaiah the prophet declared in his prophecy.”
(Now it should be noted that those who had been commissioned and sent to question him were representatives from the party of the Pharisees.)
They continued their questioning of him, asking, “Why then are you performing baptisms, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah who was to prepare His way, nor the Prophet whom Moses foretold?”
John gave them this response: “I am baptizing with water as a symbol of repentance. But standing among you at this very moment is One whom you do not recognize or know,
the One who is coming after me in His public ministry, whose sandal strap I am not worthy or qualified to untie as His lowest servant!”
These interrogations and interactions took place in Bethany, which was located on the far side of the Jordan River, at the place where John was conducting his baptizing ministry.

verses.heading: Jesus, the Lamb of God / Jesus, the Lamb of God
verses.text: On the day following this questioning, John caught sight of Jesus making His way toward him, and he made this proclamation: “Look! Behold the Lamb of God, the One who takes away the sin of the entire world!
This is the very person concerning whom I spoke when I said, ‘A man is coming after me who ranks far above me in importance and dignity, because He existed before I was ever born.’
I myself did not know His true identity initially, but the very reason I came baptizing with water was in order that He might be publicly revealed and made known to the nation of Israel.”

Then John proceeded to give this testimony, declaring, “I have witnessed with my own eyes the Spirit descending from heaven in a manner resembling a dove, and He settled upon Him and remained there continuously.

I myself did not recognize Him at first, but the One who sent me with the mission to baptize with water, that very One gave me these instructions: ‘The One upon whom you observe the Spirit descending and remaining in permanent residence, He is the One who will baptize people with the Holy Spirit.’
I have seen this with my own eyes and have given my testimony that this One is the Son of God.”

verses.heading: The First Disciples of Christ / The First Disciples of Christ
verses.text: On the following day, John was again standing in the company of two of his disciples,
and as he observed Jesus walking past them, he declared, “Look! There is the Lamb of God!”
The two disciples heard him making this statement, and they began to follow Jesus.

Jesus turned around and saw them following behind Him, and He addressed them with this question: “What are you seeking?” They responded to Him with their own question: “Rabbi” (which, when translated into Greek, means Teacher), “where are You residing?”

He extended an invitation to them: “Come with Me and you will discover the answer.” So they accompanied Him and saw the place where He was staying, and they remained with Him as guests that entire day. It was approximately the tenth hour of the day, around four o’clock in the afternoon.
Andrew, who was the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two disciples who had heard John’s declaration and had followed Jesus as a result.
This man immediately sought out his own brother Simon and announced to him with great excitement, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is translated into Greek as Christ, the Anointed One).
He brought his brother to meet Jesus. When Jesus looked intently at him, He declared, “You are Simon, the son of John. Your name will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter, meaning “rock”).

verses.heading: The Calling of Philip and Nathanael / The Calling of Philip and Nathanael
verses.text: On the day that followed, Jesus decided to depart for the region of Galilee, and He encountered Philip. Jesus issued this direct command to him: “Follow Me as My disciple.”
Now Philip’s hometown was Bethsaida, which was known as the city where Andrew and Peter also originated.

Philip sought out Nathanael and announced to him, “We have found the very One about whom Moses wrote in the Law, and about whom the prophets also wrote—Jesus, the son of Joseph, who comes from the town of Nazareth.”
Nathanael responded to him with skepticism: “Can anything good or worthwhile come out of Nazareth?” Philip replied to him simply, “Come and see for yourself.”

Jesus observed Nathanael approaching Him and made this assessment about him: “Look at this man! Here is a true Israelite, an authentic member of God’s people, in whom there is no deceit, no hypocrisy, no guile!”

Nathanael asked Him with astonishment, “How do You know anything about me? From what source do You have knowledge of my character?” Jesus answered and said to him, “Before Philip ever called you to come, while you were sitting beneath the fig tree, I saw you there.”
Nathanael responded to Him with a confession of faith: “Rabbi, You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
Jesus spoke in response and said to him, “Do you believe simply because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree? You will witness and experience far greater things than these!”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Then He continued speaking to him: “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth. You will see heaven opened wide, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.” 23 Quoted from Is. 40:3

verses.heading: The Wedding in Cana of Galilee / The Wedding in Cana of Galilee
verses.text: Now on the third day following these events, a wedding celebration was taking place in Cana, a town in the region of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was present there as a guest.
Jesus and His disciples were also invited to participate in the wedding festivities.
When the wine supply was depleted, the mother of Jesus approached Him and informed Him of the situation: “They have no more wine to serve.”
Jesus responded to her, “What concern is that situation to Me and to you, woman? Why do you involve Me in this? My hour, the appointed time for My public manifestation, has not yet arrived.”
His mother turned to the servants and gave them this instruction: “Do whatever He tells you to do, following His directions exactly.”
Now there were six stone water jars standing there, set aside according to the ceremonial purification practices of the Jews, each one having the capacity to hold twenty or thirty gallons of liquid.
Jesus directed them with these instructions: “Fill the water jars completely with water.” And they filled them up to the very brim, leaving no empty space.
Then He said to them, “Now draw out some of this water and carry it to the master of the feast, the one overseeing the celebration.” So they carried it to him as instructed.

When the master of the feast tasted the water that had been transformed into wine, not knowing where it had come from (though the servants who had drawn the water knew the source), the master of the feast called the bridegroom aside

and said to him, “Every host customarily serves the good wine first at the beginning of the celebration, and when the guests have drunk freely and their taste is less discerning, then he brings out the inferior wine. But you have kept the good wine until this present moment!”

This miraculous sign, the beginning and first of His signs, Jesus performed in Cana of Galilee, and through it He manifested His glory and revealed His divine nature. As a result, His disciples placed their faith in Him.
After this event, He went down to the town of Capernaum, accompanied by His mother and His brothers and His disciples, and they remained in that place for a brief period, not many days.

verses.heading: The Cleansing of the Temple / The Cleansing of the Temple / Matt. 21:12-13; Mk. 11:15-17; Lk. 19:45-46
verses.text: The Passover festival of the Jews was drawing near, and Jesus traveled up to the city of Jerusalem to observe it.
Upon arriving, He found in the outer courts of the temple those who were selling oxen and sheep and doves for sacrifices, as well as the money changers who were seated at their tables.

After fashioning a whip out of cords, He drove them all out of the temple area—both the sheep and the oxen—and He poured out and scattered the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables with force.
To those who were selling doves, He issued this command: “Remove these things from this place! Do not turn My Father’s house into a place of commercial business and merchandise!”
His disciples recalled that it stands written in Scripture: “The zeal and passionate concern for Your house will consume Me completely.”
In response to these actions, the Jewish authorities challenged Him and demanded, “What miraculous sign can you show us to prove Your authority and validate these actions You are performing?”
Jesus responded to them and said, “Destroy this temple, and in the space of three days, I will raise it up again!”
The Jewish leaders then said with incredulity, “This temple took forty-six years to construct, and You claim You will raise it up in three days?”
However, He was speaking symbolically concerning the temple of His physical body, not the physical building.
Therefore, when He was raised from the dead following His crucifixion, His disciples remembered that He had made this statement, and they believed the Scripture and the words that Jesus had spoken.

verses.heading: Jesus Does Not Entrust Himself to Men / Jesus Does Not Entrust Himself to Men
verses.text: While He was in Jerusalem during the Passover feast, at the time of the feast, many people believed in His name, having observed His miraculous signs which He was performing publicly.
But Jesus, for His part, was not entrusting Himself to them or committing Himself to their care, because He possessed complete knowledge of all people and their hearts.
He had no need for anyone to give Him testimony or information concerning human nature, for He Himself knew intimately and completely what was in the heart of every person.

verses.heading: Jesus and Nicodemus / Jesus and Nicodemus
verses.text: There was a man belonging to the party of the Pharisees, Nicodemus by name, who held the position of a ruler among the Jews, a member of the Sanhedrin.

This man came to Jesus by night, under cover of darkness, and said to Him, “Rabbi, we recognize and know that You are a teacher who has come with a commission from God, for no one has the ability to perform these miraculous signs that You are performing unless God is present with him and empowering him.”
Jesus answered and said to him, “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: Unless a person is born again from above, he cannot see or perceive or enter the kingdom of God.”

Nicodemus said to Him in confusion, “How is it possible for a man to be born when he is already old and advanced in years? Surely he is not able to enter into his mother’s womb for a second time and experience birth again, is he?”

Jesus responded with this explanation: “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: Unless a person is born of water and Spirit, experiencing spiritual rebirth, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

That which is born of the flesh, through natural human generation, is flesh and remains flesh in its nature. That which is born of the Spirit, through supernatural regeneration, is spirit in its nature.
Do not be amazed that I declared to you, ‘‘You must be born again from above.’’

The wind blows wherever it chooses to blow, and you hear the sound it makes, but you do not know where it is originating from and where it is traveling to. This is the way it is with everyone who has been born of the Spirit—the Spirit’s work is sovereign and mysterious.”
Nicodemus answered and said to Him, “How can these things possibly come to pass?”
Jesus answered and said to him, “Are you the distinguished teacher of Israel, one who instructs others, and yet you do not understand or know these fundamental truths?

I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: We speak authoritatively concerning what We know with certainty, and We testify to what We have personally seen and witnessed, but you people do not accept or receive Our testimony as true.
If I have told you about earthly things, matters that occur on earth, and you do not believe what I say, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things, spiritual realities?
No one has ascended into heaven to bring back divine truth, except the One who descended from heaven to reveal it—the Son of Man.
Just as Moses lifted up the bronze serpent on a pole in the wilderness for the healing of the people, so it is necessary for the Son of Man to be lifted up on the cross,
so that everyone who believes in Him and trusts in Him may possess eternal life that lasts forever.

For God loved the world and its people with such tremendous love that He gave His unique Son, so that everyone who believes in Him and places his trust in Him shall not perish in eternal destruction, but instead possess eternal life.
For God did not send the Son into the world with the purpose of condemning the world to judgment, but rather so that the world might be saved and rescued through Him.

The one who believes in Him and trusts in Him is not condemned to judgment. But the one who does not believe in Him has already been condemned, because he has refused to believe in the name and person of the unique Son of God.

Now this is the basis for judgment: The light has come into the world to illuminate truth, and people loved the darkness and preferred it rather than the light, because their deeds were evil and wicked.
For everyone who practices evil and engages in wickedness hates the light and refuses to come to the light, so that his deeds may not be exposed and shown to be evil.
But the one who practices the truth comes to the light willingly, so that his deeds may be clearly made visible, demonstrating that they have been accomplished in God and through His power.”

verses.heading: Jesus and John the Baptist / Jesus and John the Baptist
verses.text: After these interactions, Jesus and His disciples traveled into the Judean countryside, and there He spent time with them and was engaged in a baptizing ministry.
Meanwhile, John was also continuing his baptizing ministry at Aenon, which was near Salim, because water was plentiful there, and people were coming to him and being baptized—
for John had not yet been arrested and thrown into prison by Herod.
A dispute arose between some of John’s disciples and a Jewish individual concerning the subject of ceremonial purification.

They came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, the One who was with you on the far side of the Jordan, the One to whom you bore testimony—look, this man is baptizing, and all the people are flocking to Him!”
John answered them and said, “A man is able to receive not a single thing, no authority or ministry, unless it has been granted to him as a gift from heaven.
You yourselves are witnesses to me and can bear testimony that I stated clearly, ‘I am not the Christ, but I have been sent ahead of that One to prepare His way.’

The One who has the bride as His own is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom, who stands nearby and listens for him, rejoices greatly and is filled with joy on account of the bridegroom’s voice. So this joy that belongs to me has now reached its full measure.
He must increase in prominence and influence, while I must decrease in significance and visibility.”

verses.heading: The One Who Comes From Above / The One Who Comes From Above
verses.text: The One who comes from above, from heaven, is above all others in authority and dignity. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth in origin and speaks from an earthly perspective and understanding. The One who comes from heaven is above all others in every respect.
What He has personally seen and heard in heaven, this He bears witness to, yet no one receives His testimony as truth.
The one who does receive His testimony has confirmed that God is true and trustworthy.
For the One whom God has sent as His messenger speaks the very words of God with divine authority, for He gives the Spirit without any measure or limitation.
The Father loves the Son with infinite love and has placed all things into His hand and under His authority.

The one who believes in the Son and trusts in Him possesses eternal life at this present moment. But the one who does not obey the Son and refuses to submit to Him will not see life or experience it, but the wrath of God remains resting upon him continually.

verses.heading: Jesus and the Samaritan Woman / Jesus and the Samaritan Woman
verses.text: When Jesus became aware that the Pharisees had heard the report that Jesus was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John was gaining
(although, in actual fact, Jesus Himself was not personally baptizing anyone, but rather His disciples were performing the baptisms),
He departed from Judea and set out once more for the region of Galilee.
It was necessary for Him to pass through the territory of Samaria on His journey.

So He arrived at a city of Samaria called Sychar, located near the plot of ground that Jacob had given as an inheritance to his son Joseph centuries earlier. 6’ Jacob’s well was located there. Jesus, being weary from the journey He had made, sat down by the well in this manner. It was approximately the sixth hour, around noon.
A woman from Samaria came to the well to draw water for her daily needs. Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink of water.”
(For His disciples had gone away into the city to purchase food supplies.)

The Samaritan woman responded to Him, “How is it that You, being a Jew, are asking me, a Samaritan woman, to give You water to drink?” (For Jews maintained no social association or dealings with Samaritans due to ethnic and religious hostilities.)

Jesus answered and said to her, “If you had known and understood the gift of God, and who it is that is saying to you, ‘Give Me a drink,’ you would have asked Him for living water, and He would have given it to you.”
The woman said to Him, “Sir, You have no bucket or vessel to draw with, and the well is deep. From where then do You obtain that living water You speak of?
Surely You are not greater than our father Jacob, are You, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, along with his sons and his livestock?”
Jesus responded and said to her, “Everyone who drinks of this natural water will become thirsty again before long.

But whoever drinks of the water which I will give to him will never be thirsty for all eternity. Rather, the water which I will give to him will become within him a fountain of water springing up continuously to eternal life.”
The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water You speak of, so that I will not be thirsty any longer nor need to come here repeatedly to draw water.”
He said to her, “Go, call your husband and return here with him.”
The woman responded and said to Him, “I do not have a husband.” Jesus said to her, “You have spoken correctly and truthfully when you said, ‘I do not have a husband,’
for you have had five husbands in succession, and the man whom you have now is not your husband in a legitimate marriage. This you have spoken in complete truth.”
The woman said to Him, “Sir, I perceive that You are a prophet who speaks for God.
Our fathers, the Samaritans, worshiped on this mountain, Mount Gerizim, but You Jews assert that in Jerusalem is the place where it is necessary for people to worship.”
Jesus said to her, “Believe Me and trust what I say, woman, that an hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem exclusively.
You Samaritans worship what you do not know or fully understand. We Jews worship what we know, because salvation and deliverance originate from the Jews.
But the hour is coming, and has now arrived, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father is indeed seeking such people as these to worship Him.
God is spirit in His essential nature, and it is necessary for those who worship Him to worship in spirit and truth.”
The woman said to Him, “I know that Messiah is coming—the One who is called Christ, the Anointed One. When that One comes, He will declare and explain everything to us.”
Jesus said to her, “I am He, the very One speaking to you at this moment.”

At this precise point in the conversation, His disciples arrived back at the well and were amazed that He was engaged in conversation with a woman. However, no one dared to ask, “What are You seeking from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?”
Then the woman left her water jar behind at the well and went away into the city. She began saying to the people there,
“Come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done in my life! Could this possibly be the Christ, the Messiah we have been expecting?”
They departed from the city and were making their way toward Him to investigate her claim.
During this interval of time, the disciples were urging Him repeatedly, saying, “Rabbi, eat some food.”
But He said to them, “I have food to eat that you are not aware of and do not know about.”
So the disciples began to say to one another in confusion, “No one brought Him anything to eat, did they? Has someone else provided food?”
Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of the One who sent Me and to bring His work to full completion.

Do you not have a saying among yourselves, ‘There are still four months remaining, and then the harvest season comes’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields before you, for they are already white and ready for harvest at this very moment.

The one who reaps the harvest receives wages as compensation and gathers fruit that results in eternal life, so that the one who sows the seed and the one who reaps the harvest may rejoice together in celebration.
For in this situation, the proverbial saying is demonstrated to be true: ‘One person sows the seed, while another person reaps the harvest.’
I sent you out to reap what you have not worked for or labored over. Others have worked hard and labored, and you have entered into the benefit of their work.”
Many of the Samaritans from that city placed their faith and believed in Him because of the word and testimony of the woman who testified, “He told me everything which I have ever done.”
When, therefore, the Samaritans came out to meet Him, they began to urge Him insistently to stay with them in their town. And He stayed there for two full days.
Many more people believed in Him on account of His own word and teaching.

They were saying to the woman, “No longer is it because of what you told us that we believe, for we ourselves have heard Him speak, and we know with certainty that this man is truly the Savior of the world.”
After the two days had elapsed, He departed from that place and traveled into the region of Galilee.
(For Jesus Himself testified that a prophet has no honor or respect in his own native town.)

So when He arrived in Galilee, the Galileans received Him warmly, having witnessed everything He had done in Jerusalem at the feast. For they themselves had also traveled to the feast and observed His works.

verses.heading: Jesus Heals the Royal Officer’s Child / Jesus Heals the Royal Officer’s Child / Mt. 8:5-13; Lk. 7:1-10
verses.text: So Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, the place where He had transformed the water into wine. In Capernaum, there was a certain royal officer, a man in the service of King Herod, whose son was gravely ill.

Upon hearing the report that Jesus had traveled from Judea into Galilee, this man went to Him and began to plead earnestly that He come down from Cana to Capernaum and heal his son, for the child was about to die.
Jesus, therefore, said to him, “Unless you people see miraculous signs and wonders with your own eyes, you will never believe and place your trust in Me!”
The royal officer said to Him urgently, “Sir, come down quickly before my child dies!”
Jesus said to him, “Go your way. Your son will live and recover.” The man believed and trusted the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he took his leave and departed.
As he was traveling down the road toward home, his servants met him along the way, bringing him the news and saying with joy that his child was living and recovering.

Then he inquired from them the exact hour at which his son had gotten better and begun to recover. They said to him, “Yesterday, at the seventh hour of the day, around one o’clock in the afternoon, the fever departed from him.”

Then the father realized that it was at that same precise hour when Jesus had said to him, “Your son lives and will recover.” And he himself believed and placed his faith in Jesus, along with his entire household and family.
Now this was the second miraculous sign that Jesus performed following His arrival from Judea into the region of Galilee.

verses.heading: The Healing at the Pool of Bethesda / The Healing at the Pool of Bethesda
verses.text: After these events had taken place, there was a feast of the Jews being observed, and Jesus traveled up to the city of Jerusalem to participate in it.
There is located in Jerusalem, near the Sheep Gate, a pool called in the Hebrew language Bethesda, which is surrounded by five covered colonnades providing shelter.

In these colonnades were lying a great multitude of those who were invalid and infirm—people who were blind, lame, and paralyzed, waiting for healing.* Some ancient manuscripts add verse 4, which reads: “ For an angel went down at a certain time into the pool and stirred up the water. Then, he who stepped in first after the stirring of the water was made whole from whatever disease he had at that time .”
verses.html:
In these colonnades were lying a great multitude of those who were invalid and infirm—people who were blind, lame, and paralyzed, waiting for healing.*
Some ancient manuscripts add verse 4, which reads: “ For an angel went down at a certain time into the pool and stirred up the water. Then, he who stepped in first after the stirring of the water was made whole from whatever disease he had at that time .”

verses.text: A certain man was present there who had been in his invalid and disabled condition for thirty-eight years, suffering from chronic illness.
When Jesus observed this man lying there helpless and realized that he had been in that condition for a long period of time already, He said to him, “Do you desire to be made well?”

The sick man answered Him, “Sir, I have no one, no friend or helper, to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up and agitated. But while I am making my way toward it, another person steps down ahead of me and enters before I can reach it.”
Jesus said to him with authority, “Arise and stand up. Take up your mat, and walk.”
Immediately, at that very moment, the man was made completely well. He took up his mat and began to walk about. (Now it was the Sabbath day on that particular day.)
So the Jewish religious authorities were saying to the one who had been healed, “It is the Sabbath day, and it is not lawful or permissible for you to carry your mat on this day.”
But he answered them in his defense, “The One who made me whole and restored my health—that very One gave me this instruction and said to me, ‘Take up your mat and walk.’ ”
So they questioned him further, demanding to know, “Who is the man who said to you, ‘Take up your mat and walk,’ violating the Sabbath?”
But the one who had been healed did not know who Jesus was or His identity, for Jesus had quietly withdrawn while a crowd was gathered in that place.

After these events had occurred, Jesus found the healed man at the temple and said to him, “Look, you have been made completely well. Sin no more from this time forward, so that nothing worse than your previous condition happens to you.”
The man went away from the temple and reported to the Jewish authorities that it was Jesus who had made him well and healed him.
For this reason and on this account, the Jewish leaders were persecuting Jesus and seeking to harm Him, because He was doing these healing works on the Sabbath day.
But Jesus replied to them in His defense, “My Father has been working until the present moment, and I also am working in the same manner.”

verses.heading: The Co-equality of Jesus with God / The Co-equality of Jesus with God
verses.text: For this reason, on account of this statement, the Jewish leaders were seeking even more earnestly to kill Him, because not only was He breaking the Sabbath regulations in their view, but He was also calling God His own Father in a unique sense, thereby making Himself equal with God in nature and authority.

verses.heading: The Authority of the Son / The Authority of the Son
verses.text: So Jesus replied and said to them, “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: The Son is able to do nothing on His own initiative or authority, acting independently, except what He sees the Father doing. For whatever the Father does, these same things the Son also does in the same manner and with the same authority.
For the Father loves the Son with infinite love and shows Him everything that He Himself is doing. And greater works than these miracles He will show Him, so that you will marvel
For just as the Father raises the dead from their graves and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wills and chooses to give it.
For the Father judges no one directly, but has entrusted the entire work of judgment to the Son,
so that everyone may honor the Son in the same way and to the same degree as they honor the Father. The one who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him into the world.

I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: The one who hears My word and believes and trusts the One who sent Me has eternal life at this present moment, and does not come into judgment or condemnation, but has crossed over and passed from death into life.
I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: An hour is coming, and has now arrived, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God speaking to them, and those who hear and respond will live.
For just as the Father has life in Himself as an inherent possession, so also He has granted to the Son to have life in Himself as an inherent possession.
And He has granted Him authority to execute judgment over all humanity, because He is the Son of Man, sharing in human nature.
Do not marvel at this truth, because an hour is coming when all those who are in the tombs and graves will hear His voice calling them forth

and they will come out from their graves—those who have done good things and righteous deeds will come forth to the resurrection that leads to life, but those who have practiced evil things and wickedness will come forth to the resurrection that leads to judgment and condemnation.

I am able to do nothing on My own initiative or by My own independent authority. Just as I hear instruction from the Father, I judge accordingly, and My judgment is just and righteous, because I do not seek My own will or desire, but rather the will of the One who sent Me into the world.

verses.heading: Witnesses to Jesus / Witnesses to Jesus
verses.text: “If I testify about Myself alone, My testimony is not considered legally valid or true by your standards.
There is another witness who bears testimony about Me and My identity, and I know with certainty that the testimony which He testifies about Me is true and reliable.
You have sent messengers and a delegation to John the Baptist, and he has borne witness to the truth concerning Me.
I do not receive or depend upon testimony from any human source for validation, but I say these things so that you may be saved and come to eternal life.
That man John was the burning and shining lamp, illuminating truth, and you were willing to rejoice for a brief time in his light and teaching.

But I have a testimony that is greater and more authoritative than that of John. For the works which the Father has given Me to accomplish and bring to completion—the very works which I am doing at this moment—testify about Me, confirming that the Father has sent Me.
And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified about Me. You have neither heard His voice at any time in your lives nor seen His visible form.
You do not have His word dwelling in you permanently, because you do not believe and trust the One whom He has sent to you.
You search and examine the Scriptures diligently because you think that in them you possess eternal life, and it is these very Scriptures that testify about Me.
Yet you are not willing to come to Me so that you may have life and experience it.
I do not accept or receive glory and honor from human beings as My source of validation.
But I know you and understand your hearts, that you do not have the love of God dwelling in yourselves.
I have come in the name and authority of My Father, and you do not accept Me. If another comes in his own name and authority, promoting himself, him you will receive.
How are you able to believe and place your faith in Me since you accept glory and honor from one another, and do not seek the glory and honor which comes from the only God?
Do not think that I will bring charges against you before the Father. The one who brings charges against you is Moses, in whom you have placed your hope and confidence.
For if you truly believed Moses and trusted his writings, you would believe Me, for that one wrote about Me.
But if you do not believe the writings of that one, how will you believe My words and teaching?” Notes

verses.heading: The Feeding of the Five Thousand / The Feeding of the Five Thousand / Matt. 14:13-21; Mk. 6:30-44; Lk. 9:10-17
verses.text: After these events had transpired, Jesus traveled away to the opposite shore of the Sea of Galilee (which is also known as the Sea of Tiberias).

A vast multitude of people was following Him in pursuit, because they were observing and witnessing the miraculous signs which He was performing upon those who were afflicted with sickness and disease.
Then Jesus went up onto the mountainside, and there He sat down in the company of His disciples to rest.
(Now the Passover feast, the great feast of the Jewish people, was soon to take place.)

Then Jesus, lifting up His eyes and seeing that a vast crowd was making their way toward Him, said to Philip with a question, “Where are we to purchase bread, so that these people may have something to eat?”
But He was posing this question to test Philip’s faith and understanding, for Jesus already knew what He was about to do to meet the need.
Philip answered Him with a calculation, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be sufficient for them, in order that each person may receive even a small portion.’’
One of His disciples, Andrew, who was the brother of Simon Peter, spoke up and said to Him,
“Here is a young boy who has five barley loaves and two small fish in his possession, but what are these meager provisions for such a vast number of people?”

Jesus gave this instruction: “Have the people sit down in a relaxed posture on the ground.” (Now there was an abundance of grass in that location.) So the people sat down in a relaxed posture, numbering approximately five thousand men.

Then Jesus took the loaves of bread into His hands, and having given thanks to the Father, He began to distribute the food to those who were reclining in a relaxed posture. He did likewise also with the fish, providing as much as they desired to eat.
When they had eaten their fill, He said to His disciples, “Gather up what remains of the broken pieces, so that nothing is wasted or lost.”
So they gathered them up, and they filled twelve baskets to overflowing with broken pieces from the five barley loaves which were left over after those who had eaten were satisfied.
When the people saw the miraculous sign which He performed, they began to say with conviction, “This is truly the Prophet who is destined to come into the world, the One Moses promised.”
So Jesus, having perceived that they were about to come and seize Him by force in order to make Him their king, withdrew once more to the mountain by Himself alone, escaping their intentions.

verses.heading: Jesus Walks on the Water / Jesus Walks on the Water / Matt. 14:22-27; Mk. 6:45-52
verses.text: Now when evening had arrived, His disciples went down to the shore of the sea,
and after getting into a boat, they began to make their way across to the other side of the sea, heading toward Capernaum. Darkness had already fallen, and Jesus had not yet come to join them.
A strong wind was blowing across the water, and the sea began to be stirred up with increasingly rough waves.

Then, when they had rowed approximately twenty-five or thirty stadia, a distance of about three or four miles, they observed Jesus walking on the surface of the sea and drawing near the boat; and they were alarmed.
But He spoke to them reassuringly, “It is I, I am. Do not be afraid.”
Then they were willing to take Him into the boat with them, and at once, the boat arrived at the land to which they were headed, reaching their destination.

verses.heading: Jesus is the Bread of Life / Jesus is the Bread of Life
verses.text: The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea noticed that there had been no other boats present there except one, and that Jesus had not entered together with His disciples into the boat when they departed, but that His disciples had gone away alone without Him.
But other boats from Tiberias arrived near the location where they had eaten the bread, after the Lord had given thanks and blessed it.

So when the crowd came to understand that Jesus was not present there, nor were His disciples, they themselves got into the available boats and traveled to Capernaum, actively seeking Jesus and hoping to find Him.
When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they said to Him with curiosity, “Rabbi, at what time did You arrive here? When did You come to this place?”

Jesus answered them directly and said, “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: You are seeking Me, not because you saw miraculous signs that pointed to My identity, but because you ate of the loaves and were satisfied and had your physical hunger met.

Do not labor for the food that perishes, but rather work for the food that remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you as a gift. For on Him God the Father has set His seal of authentication.”
Then they said to Him, seeking instruction, “What shall we do, so that we may perform and accomplish the works that God requires?”
Jesus answered and said to them, “This is the work that God requires, that you believe in and place your trust in Him whom He has sent into the world.”

So they said to Him, demanding proof, “Then what miraculous sign do You perform, so that we may see it with our own eyes and believe in You? What supernatural work will You perform to validate Your claims?
Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness during their journey, just as it stands written in Scripture: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’ ”
Then Jesus said to them with emphasis, “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: It is not Moses who has given you the bread from heaven, but My Father is giving you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world and all its people.”
So they said to Him eagerly, “Sir, give us this bread at all times, continually and without ceasing.”

Jesus declared to them, “I am the bread of life, the source of spiritual nourishment. The one who comes to Me in faith will never be hungry or experience spiritual want, and the one who believes in Me and trusts in Me will never be thirsty again or lack spiritual satisfaction.
But I said to you previously that you have seen Me with your own eyes and witnessed My works, and still you do not believe or place your trust in Me.
All whom the Father gives to Me as a gift will come to Me in faith, and the one who comes to Me I will never cast out or reject, never turning anyone away.
I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will or pursue My own agenda, but rather to do the will of the One who sent Me into the world.

Now this is the will of the One who sent Me, that I shall lose nothing and no one of all whom He has given to Me as a trust, but that I should raise it up and restore it to life on the last day at the resurrection.
For this is the will of My Father, that everyone who looks upon the Son with faith and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.”
So the Jewish leaders began to grumble about Him because He made the declaration, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
They began to say among themselves, ““Is this not Jesus the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know personally? How does He now make the claim and say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?”
Jesus responded and said to them, “Do not murmur among yourselves about what I have said.
No one has the ability to come to Me in faith unless the Father who sent Me draws him to Myself. And I will raise him up on the last day.
It stands written in the Prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God directly.’ Everyone who has heard instruction and learned from the Father comes to Me in faith.
This does not mean that anyone has seen the Father directly with physical eyes, except the One who is from God and originates with God—He alone has seen the Father face to face.
I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: “The one who believes and places his trust in Me has eternal life, even at this present moment.
I am the bread of life, the source of spiritual sustenance.
Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness during their wanderings, yet they died physically despite this provision.
This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat from it and not die spiritually or eternally.

I am the living bread that came down from heaven to give life. If anyone eats from this bread, he will live forever in eternity. And the bread which I will give for the life of the world also is My flesh, which I will sacrifice.”
Then the Jewish leaders began to dispute among themselves, saying with confusion and hostility, “How can this man give us His flesh to eat? How is this possible?”

Then Jesus said to them with great solemnity, “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, appropriating His sacrifice, you have no life in yourselves, no spiritual vitality.
The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood, embracing My sacrificial death, has eternal life at this moment, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For My flesh constitutes true food, genuine nourishment, and My blood constitutes true drink, genuine satisfaction.
The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood, accepting My atoning sacrifice, remains in Me in intimate union, and I remain in him in abiding presence.

Just as the living Father sent Me into the world, and I live because of the Father and draw My life from Him, so the one who feeds on Me spiritually, that one also will live because of Me and draw spiritual life from Me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven, not like the bread your fathers ate and yet died. The one who eats this bread will live forever in eternity.”
He spoke these profound things while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum, proclaiming this message publicly.

verses.heading: The Words of Eternal Life / The Words of Eternal Life
verses.text: Therefore, many of His disciples, when they heard this teaching, said with difficulty, “This is a hard and difficult saying to accept. Who has the ability to understand it or embrace it?”

But Jesus, knowing within Himself that His disciples were secretly speaking and grumbling about this teaching, said to them, “Does this provoke a sense of offense in you? Does this cause you to stumble?
Then what if you see and witness the Son of Man ascending to where He was before, returning to heaven? Would that resolve your difficulty?

It is the Spirit who gives life and imparts spiritual vitality. The flesh, by itself, yields no benefit or profit whatsoever. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit in nature, and they are life-giving in power.

Yet there are some among you who do not believe or place their trust in Me.” For Jesus had known from the beginning, before they ever followed Him, who those were who did not truly believe, and who it was who would betray Him.
And He continued saying, “For this reason, I have told you that no one has the ability to come to Me in genuine faith unless it has been granted to him as a gift from the Father.”
From this time forward, many of His disciples drew back, and no longer walked with Him or followed Him as disciples.
So Jesus said to the Twelve with a question, “You do not want to go away and leave Me too, do you? Do you also wish to depart?”
Simon Peter responded to Him with conviction, “Lord, to whom shall we go? Where else would we turn? You alone have the words of eternal life.
And we have believed and placed our trust in You, and have come to know with certainty, that You are the Holy One of God, set apart and sent by Him.”
Jesus answered them soberly, “Did I not choose you, the Twelve, selecting you for this purpose? Yet one of you is a devil, an adversary aligned with Satan!”
Now He was speaking of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, as he—though he was one of the Twelve chosen disciples—was going to betray Him to His enemies.

verses.heading: The Unbelief of Jesus’ Brothers / The Unbelief of Jesus’ Brothers
verses.text: After these things had taken place, Jesus was walking in the region of Galilee, for He was not willing to walk and minister in Judea, because the Jewish leaders were actively seeking to kill Him.
Now the feast of the Jews, the Feast of Tabernacles, was approaching.
So His brothers, according to the flesh, said to Him, “Leave this place, and go into Judea, so that Your disciples there also may see and witness Your works which You are performing.
For no one does anything in obscurity while he himself seeks to be publicly acknowledged. If You are performing these miraculous things, disclose Yourself to the world.”
For not even His own brothers believed in Him or trusted in His claims at this time.
So Jesus said to them in response, “My time, My appointed hour for public manifestation, has not yet come, whereas your time is always ready and opportune, since you are of the world.
The world cannot hate you or bear hostility toward you, but it hates Me with intense animosity, because I testify about it, that its deeds are evil and wicked.
You go up to the feast and participate in it. I am not going up to this feast at this time, because My appointed time has not yet fully come.”
Having said these things to them, He stayed in Galilee for the time being.

verses.heading: Jesus at the Feast of Tabernacles / Jesus at the Feast of Tabernacles
verses.text: But when His brothers had gone up to the feast, then He also went up to Jerusalem, not publicly, but rather, as it were, in secret and privately.
So the Jewish leaders were searching for Him at the feast and kept asking, “Where is He?”

There was much grumbling about Him among the crowds gathered there. Some were saying, “He is a good man, a righteous teacher,” but others were saying with suspicion, “No, on the contrary, He is deceiving the crowd.”
However, no one was speaking publicly about Him for fear of the Jewish authorities.
But when it was now the middle of the feast, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach with authority.

Then the Jewish leaders were wondering, saying among themselves, “How does this man know the sacred writings and possess such learning, despite not having been formally taught or trained by the rabbis?”
So Jesus answered them and explained, “My teaching is not My own in origin, but comes from the One who sent Me into the world.
If anyone desires to do His will and obey Him, he will know and understand about My teaching, whether it originates from God, or whether I am speaking from Myself on My own authority.

The one who speaks from himself and his own wisdom seeks his own glory and honor. But the One who seeks the glory and honor of the One who sent Him—He is true and genuine—and there is no unrighteousness or falsehood in Him.
Has not Moses given you the Law as a divine gift? Yet none of you keeps or obeys the Law faithfully. Why are you seeking to kill Me?
The crowd responded with hostility, “You have a demon possessing You! Who is seeking to kill You? You are paranoid!”
Jesus answered and said to them, “I performed one miraculous work on the Sabbath, and you all marvel because of it.

For this reason and because of this principle, Moses gave you the practice of circumcision (not that circumcision originates from Moses, but rather from the fathers, from Abraham and the patriarchs), and you circumcise a male child on the Sabbath day.
If a male child receives circumcision on a Sabbath day, so that the Law of Moses may not be violated, are you angry with Me because I made an entire man completely well on the Sabbath?
Do not form conclusions according to outward appearance and superficial observation, but judge with the righteous judgment that examines true reality.”

verses.heading: Is it Possible that this is the Christ? / Is it Possible that this is the Christ?
verses.text: Then some of the residents of Jerusalem began to say among themselves, “Is this man not the very one whom the authorities are seeking to kill?
And look, see how He is speaking publicly, and they are saying nothing to Him in opposition. Is it possible that the rulers have truly come to know that this man is the Christ, the Messiah?
But we know where this man originates from and His hometown, but when the Christ comes in His manifestation, no one will know where He comes from or His origin.”

Then Jesus, as He was teaching in the temple courts, cried out with a loud voice, saying, “You know Me, and you know where I am from in one sense. Yet I have not come from Myself or on My own initiative, but the One who sent Me is true, whom you do not know or have relationship with.
I know Him intimately, because I am from Him in origin and existence, and He sent Me as His commissioned representative.”
So they were attempting to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His appointed hour had not yet come to fulfillment.

But from among the crowd, many believed in Him and placed their faith in Him, and they began to say, “When the Christ comes, He will not perform more miraculous signs than this man has accomplished, will He?”

verses.heading: Officers Sent to Arrest Jesus / Officers Sent to Arrest Jesus
verses.text: The Pharisees heard the crowd secretly speaking and murmuring these things about Him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent temple officers with orders to arrest Him and bring Him in.
Then Jesus declared, “Yet, for a little while longer, I am with you in your presence, and then I am going away to the One who sent Me, returning to the Father.
You will search for Me, but will not find Me, and where I am going, you cannot come or follow.”

So the Jewish leaders said to one another in confusion, “Where is this One about to go, that we will not find Him? He is not about to go to the Dispersion, to the Jews scattered among the Greeks in foreign lands, and teach the Greeks, is He?
What is the meaning of this saying that He declared, 'You will search for Me and will not find Me, and where I am, you cannot come’? What does He mean?”

verses.heading: The Promise of the Spirit / The Promise of the Spirit
verses.text: Now on the last day of the feast, the great and climactic day of the celebration, Jesus stood and cried out with a loud voice, saying, “If anyone thirsts spiritually and desires satisfaction, let him come to Me and drink from the living water I provide.
The one who believes in Me and places trust in Me, just as the Scripture says and declares, ‘Out of his innermost being will flow rivers of living water, streams of spiritual life.’ ”

But He spoke this statement with respect to the Holy Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were going to receive after His glorification. For the Spirit was not yet given in this fullness, because Jesus had not yet been glorified—through His death, resurrection, and ascension.

verses.heading: Division Among the People / Division Among the People
verses.text: Then, having heard these words, some from among the crowd were saying, “This man is truly the Prophet whom Moses promised would come.”
Others were saying with conviction, “This man is the Christ, the Messiah!” Yet others were saying with doubt, “No, surely not, for the Christ does not emerge from Galilee, does He?
Has not the Scripture stated clearly that the Christ emerges from the lineage of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David lived and was born?”
So there was a division in the crowd on account of Him and differing opinions about His identity.
Some of them were intent on and desired to arrest Him, but no one laid hands on Him to take Him.

verses.heading: The Unbelief of the Chief Priests and Pharisees / The Unbelief of the Chief Priests and Pharisees
verses.text: Then the temple officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees empty-handed. And the leaders said to them with displeasure, “Why did you not bring Him back with you?”
The officers answered and explained, “Never has a man spoken in this manner with such authority and power! No one has ever taught like this!”
Then the Pharisees responded to them with contempt, “You have not been deceived too, have you? Have you also fallen under His influence?
Not one of the rulers or members of the Sanhedrin or of the Pharisees has believed in Him and placed faith in Him, has he?
But this ignorant crowd who does not know the Law in detail is doomed to destruction and under God’s curse!”
Nicodemus, the one who had come to Jesus earlier by night—who was one of them, a member of the Sanhedrin—said to them,
“Our Law does not pass judgment on a man unless it first hears from him directly and ascertains what he is doing, does it? Is this not a violation of proper procedure?”

They answered and said to him with derision, “You are not also from Galilee, are you? You are not a Galilean sympathizer, are you? Search the Scriptures carefully and see that no prophet arises from Galilee, according to expectation.” [[

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And everyone departed and went to his own house for the night.* 7:53-8:11 John 7:53–8:11 is not found in the earliest textual witnesses. The passage is considered a later interpolation, with a small group of manuscripts placing it, either in entirety or in portions, in one of several alternative locations: after John 7:36, John 21:25, Luke 21:38, or Luke 24:53.

verses.heading: The Woman Caught in Adultery / The Woman Caught in Adultery
verses.text: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives to spend the night.
Now, early in the morning at dawn, He came again to the temple courts. All the people were coming to Him, and He sat down and began to teach them with authority.
Now the scribes and the Pharisees brought before Him a woman who had been caught in the act of adultery, and having placed her in the center of their gathering,
they said to Him as a test, “Teacher, this woman has been caught in the very act of engaging in adultery, taken in the midst of her sin.
Now in the Law, Moses commanded us to stone such individuals to death. So what do you say about this case?”

Now they were saying this to test Him and trap Him, so that they might have a basis to accuse Him of violating the Law. But Jesus, bending down toward the ground, began to write with His finger on the ground, ignoring their challenge.
When they continued asking Him, He straightened up and said to them, “The one who is sinless among you, let him be the first to throw the stone at her in execution.”
Bending down once more toward the ground, He continued to write on the ground with His finger.

Now when they heard this challenge and their consciences were convicted, they began to depart, one by one, beginning with the older ones who had more life experience. Jesus was left alone—and the woman remained standing in the center where they had placed her.
Jesus, straightening up and looking around, said to her, "Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?”
She said, “No one has condemned me, Lord." So Jesus said with compassion, "Neither do I condemn you to judgment. Go on your way, and from now on, sin no more.”]]

verses.heading: Jesus the Light of the World / Jesus the Light of the World
verses.text: Again Jesus spoke to them on another occasion, declaring, “I am the Light of the world. The one who follows Me as a disciple will never walk in the darkness of sin and ignorance, but will have the light of life.”
Then the Pharisees challenged Him and said to Him, “You are giving testimony regarding Yourself and Your own identity. Your testimony is not true or legally valid according to our standards.”

Jesus answered and responded to them, “Even if I give testimony about Myself and bear witness to My own identity, My testimony is true and reliable, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.
You judge according to fleshly criteria and human standards. I do not judge anyone at this present time with condemnation.
But even if I do judge, My judgment is true and reliable, because I am not alone in My assessment—but I judge together with the Father who sent Me.
Even in your own Law, it stands written that the testimony of two witnesses is true and legally valid for establishing truth.
I am the One who gives testimony about Myself and My identity, and the Father who sent Me into the world gives testimony about Me.”

So they were saying to Him, challenging His claim, “Where is Your Father? Where is this witness You speak of?” Jesus responded, “You know neither Me nor My Father. If you knew Me and understood who I am, you would know My Father also, for we are one.”
He spoke these words in the treasury area while teaching in the temple courts, and no one arrested Him, because His appointed hour had not yet come to fulfillment.

verses.heading: Where I Am Going You Are Not Able to Come / Where I Am Going You Are Not Able to Come
verses.text: Then Jesus said to them again on another occasion, “I am going away from this world, and you will seek Me in the future, and you will die in your sin without forgiveness. Where I am going, you are not able to come or follow.”
So the Jewish leaders were saying among themselves, “Will He kill Himself and commit suicide, since He is saying, ‘Where I am going, you are not able to come’? Is that what He means?”

He was saying to them in explanation, “You are from below, from this earthly realm. I am from above, from the heavenly realm. You are from this world, with its values and ways. I am not from this world or share in its fallen order.
Therefore, I said to you that you will die in your sins, unforgiven and condemned. For unless you believe that I am, that I am the divine One, you will die in your sins without hope.”

So they were saying to Him with frustration, “Who are You claiming to be? What is Your identity?” Jesus said to them, “I am precisely what I have been saying to you from the beginning of My ministry. I am who I claim to be.
I have much to say and to judge about you and your actions, but the One who sent Me is true and trustworthy, and what I have heard from Him, these things I declare to the world.”
(They did not understand that He was speaking to them about God the Father and their relationship.)

Then Jesus said to them prophetically, “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will understand and come to know that I am, the divine One, and that I do nothing from Myself or on My own initiative. Rather, I say these things just as the Father taught and instructed Me.
The One who sent Me is with Me continually. The Father has not left Me alone, because I always do the things that are acceptable and pleasing to Him.”
As He was making these declarations, many people believed in Him and placed their faith in His identity.

verses.heading: The Truth Will Set You Free / The Truth Will Set You Free
verses.text: So Jesus said to those Jews who had believed in Him and had acknowledged Him, “If you continue in My word, abiding in My teaching, you are truly My disciples.
Then you will know the truth, and the truth will liberate you from bondage.”

They responded to Him with indignation, “We are descendants of Abraham and have not been enslaved to anyone at any time in our history. How can You claim, ‘You will become free’? We are already free!”
Jesus answered them solemnly, “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: Everyone who practices sin is a slave of sin.
Now the slave does not remain in the house forever as a permanent member. The son remains in the house forever with full rights and inheritance.
So if the Son liberates you from sin’s bondage, you will be truly free.
I acknowledge and recognise that you are physical descendants of Abraham. Yet you are seeking to kill Me, because My word finds no place in your hearts.
I speak of what I have seen and witnessed with My Father in heaven. Therefore, you also practice what you have heard from your father, following his example.”

verses.heading: You Are of Your Father the Devil / You Are of Your Father the Devil
verses.text: They replied and said to Him defensively, “Abraham is our father.” Jesus said to them, “If you were truly children of Abraham in spirit, you would do the works of Abraham, imitating his faith.
But now, at this present time, you are seeking to kill Me, a man who has spoken to you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this kind of thing.
You are doing the works and following the pattern of your father.” They said to Him, offended, “We were not born through sexual immorality or illegitimacy. We have one father—God Himself.”

Jesus said to them directly, “If God were truly your Father in a spiritual sense, you would love Me with genuine affection, for I came forth from God, and am here now in your presence. For I have not come from Myself or on My own initiative, but He sent Me as His commissioned representative.
Why do you not understand My speech and what I am saying? It is because you are not able to hear and receive My message.

You are of your father the devil, and you are willing to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand firm in the truth or abide in it, because there is no truth in him whatsoever. Whenever he speaks falsehood, he speaks from his own inherent disposition, because he is a liar by nature and the father of lies, the originator of all deception.
But because I am speaking the truth to you, you do not believe Me or receive My words.
Who among you convicts Me of sin? If I am speaking the truth to you, why do you not believe Me and trust what I say?
The one who is from God and belongs to Him hears the words of God and receives them gladly. For this reason, you do not hear or receive them, because you are not from God.”

verses.heading: Before Abraham Existed, I Am / Before Abraham Existed, I Am
verses.text: The Jewish leaders answered and said to Him with hostility, “Do we not rightly say that You are a Samaritan, a heretic, and have a demon possessing You?”
Jesus responded calmly, “I do not have a demon or evil spirit, but rather I honor My Father and give Him glory, and you dishonor Me and treat Me with contempt.
But I am not seeking My own glory or pursuing My own honor. There is One, the Father, who seeks it, and He judges those who reject Me.
I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: If anyone keeps My word, he shall never see death for all eternity. He will never experience spiritual death.”

The Jewish leaders, therefore, said to Him, “Now we know with certainty that You have a demon! Abraham died, and the prophets died, but You say, ‘If anyone keeps My word, he will never taste death for all eternity.’
You are not greater than our father Abraham who died, are You? The prophets also died! Who do You claim Yourself to be?”
Jesus responded, “If I glorify Myself and promote My own honor, My glory is worthless. It is My Father who glorifies Me, the One about whom you say, ‘He is our God.’

Yet you have not known Him or have any relationship with Him, but I know Him intimately. If I were to say that I do not know Him, I would be a liar just like you. But I know Him with certainty and keep His word faithfully.
Abraham your father greatly rejoiced that he would see My day, My coming and ministry, and he saw it prophetically and was glad.”
So the Jewish leaders said to Him with scorn, “You are not yet fifty years old in age, and You claim to have seen Abraham?”
Jesus said to them with solemn authority, “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: Before Abraham came into being, I am!” declaring His eternal, divine existence.
Then they picked up stones to stone Him for blasphemy, but Jesus hid His presence, and went out of the temple courts, passing through their midst unharmed.

verses.heading: Jesus is the Light of the World / Jesus is the Light of the World
verses.text: As Jesus was walking along, He observed a man who had never been able to see from the moment of his birth.
His disciples posed a question to Him: “Rabbi, what caused this man to be born without sight? Did he commit some sin, or was it his parents who sinned?”

Jesus responded: “The reason for his blindness has nothing to do with sin—neither his own nor that of his parents. He was born blind so that God’s mighty works could be put on display through his life.
While daylight remains, we must accomplish the work that the One who sent Me requires of us. The time is coming when darkness will fall and no work can be done.
During the time I remain in the world, I serve as the Light that illuminates it.”
Having spoken these words, Jesus spat onto the ground and formed mud by mixing the saliva with dirt. He then applied this mud to the man’s eyes.
Jesus instructed him: “Go to the pool called Siloam”—a name meaning “Sent”—“and wash yourself there.” The man obeyed, went to wash, and returned with his sight fully restored.
The people who lived nearby and those who had previously observed him sitting and begging began asking: “Is this not the same person who used to sit in that spot and beg for money?”

Some were convinced: “Yes, this is definitely him.” Others disagreed: “No, it cannot be him—just someone who resembles him closely.” But the man himself kept insisting: “I am indeed that same person.”
So they pressed him: “Then explain to us—how did your eyes come to be opened?”
He explained: “The man named Jesus made mud, applied it to my eyes, and instructed me: ‘Go to Siloam and wash there.’ So I went, washed as He said, and my sight came to me.”
They asked him: “Where can we find this man?” He replied: “I have no idea where He is.”

verses.heading: The Pharisees Doubt the Healing of the Man Born Blind / The Pharisees Doubt the Healing of the Man Born Blind
verses.text: They brought the formerly blind man before the Pharisees for examination.
It happened that the day on which Jesus had made the mud and restored the man’s sight was a Sabbath day.
The Pharisees then questioned him again about how his sight had been restored. He told them: “He placed mud on my eyes, I washed it off, and now I have the ability to see.”

This prompted division among the Pharisees. Some declared: “This man cannot be from God, since He violates the Sabbath regulations.” But others countered: “How could a man who is a sinner accomplish such miraculous signs?” They were split in their opinions.
They turned back to the man who had been blind and asked: “What is your assessment of Him, considering He is the one who opened your eyes?” The man responded: “He must be a prophet.”
The Jewish leaders refused to accept that he had actually been blind and received his sight until they summoned his parents to testify.
They interrogated them: “Is this your son? Are you claiming he was born blind? Then how do you explain the fact that he now has sight?”
His parents answered carefully: “We can confirm that this is our son, and we know for certain he was born blind.
But as for how he now possesses sight, we cannot explain that, nor do we know who gave him the ability to see. You should ask him directly—he is an adult and can speak on his own behalf.”
His parents spoke with such caution because they feared the Jewish authorities, who had already announced that anyone who confessed Jesus to be the Messiah would be expelled from the synagogue.
This fear is precisely why his parents said: “He is old enough to answer for himself—question him.”
So they summoned the healed man a second time and said to him: “Give glory to God by telling the truth. We have determined that this man is a sinner.”
He answered them: “Whether He is a sinner or not is beyond my knowledge. But one fact I know with complete certainty: I was blind, and now I see!”
They questioned him further: “What exactly did He do to you? How did He accomplish the opening of your eyes?”
He answered: “I have already given you a full account, and you paid no attention. Why do you want to hear it again? Are you perhaps considering becoming His disciples as well?”
At this they hurled insults at him and declared: “You are His follower! We are followers of Moses!
We know with certainty that God spoke directly to Moses, but regarding this man, we do not even know His origins.”
The man responded to them: “Now this is truly astonishing! You claim not to know where He comes from, yet He opened my eyes!
We all understand that God does not respond to the prayers of sinners. But He does listen to anyone who worships Him reverently and carries out His will.
Never in all of history has anyone heard of someone opening the eyes of a person born blind.
If this man did not come from God, He would possess no power to do anything of this nature.”
They shot back at him: “You were born completely immersed in sin, and you presume to instruct us?” Then they threw him out of the synagogue.

verses.heading: Spiritual Blindness / Spiritual Blindness
verses.text: Jesus learned that they had expelled him, and when He located him, He asked: “Do you place your faith in the Son of Man?”
The man replied: “Tell me who He is, Sir, so that I may believe in Him.”
Jesus said to him: “You have already seen Him with your own eyes; in fact, He is the very one speaking with you right now.”
Then the man declared: “Lord, I believe,” and he bowed down in worship before Him.
Jesus then said: “I have entered this world to bring about a judgment, so that those who cannot see will gain sight, and those who claim they can see will become blind.”
Some Pharisees who were present heard this statement and challenged Him: “Surely You are not suggesting that we are blind as well?”
Jesus replied to them: “If you were actually blind, you would bear no guilt for sin; but because you keep insisting ‘We can see clearly,’ your guilt remains upon you.”

verses.heading: The Parable of the Good Shepherd and the Sheep / The Parable of the Good Shepherd and the Sheep
verses.text: “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: Anyone who refuses to enter the sheep enclosure by the proper door, but instead climbs up from another direction, is nothing but a thief and a robber.
But the person who enters by the door is the legitimate shepherd of the sheep.
The doorkeeper opens the door for him, and the sheep recognize his voice. He calls each of his own sheep by their individual names and leads them out to pasture.
After he has brought all his own sheep out, he walks ahead of them, and the sheep follow behind him because they recognize his voice.
They will absolutely refuse to follow a stranger; instead, they will run away from him because they do not recognize the voice of strangers.”
Jesus presented this illustration to them, but they failed to grasp the meaning of what He was communicating.

verses.heading: Jesus is the Good Shepherd / Jesus is the Good Shepherd
verses.text: So Jesus spoke to them again: “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: I Myself am the gate for the sheep.
Everyone who came before Me operated as thieves and robbers, but the sheep refused to listen to their voices.
I am the door. Anyone who enters through Me will experience salvation and will move in and out freely, finding nourishment for life.
The thief’s only purpose in coming is to steal, slaughter, and devastate. But I have come so that they may possess life—and not just life, but life overflowing with abundance.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd willingly gives up his own life for the sake of his sheep.

A hired worker, on the other hand—since he is not actually the shepherd and does not own the sheep himself—sees the wolf approaching and abandons the sheep to their fate and flees. Then the wolf attacks the flock and scatters them in all directions.
He runs away because he is merely a paid worker and has no genuine concern for the welfare of the sheep.
I am the good shepherd. I know My own sheep intimately, and My own sheep know Me intimately,
just as the Father knows Me intimately and I know the Father intimately—and I willingly lay down My life for the sheep.

I have other sheep as well that do not belong to this particular fold. It is necessary for Me to bring those sheep also, and they will hear and recognize My voice. Eventually there will be one unified flock with one shepherd.
This is the reason the Father loves Me: because I lay down My life, with the purpose of taking it up again.

No one is taking My life from Me against My will. Rather, I lay it down voluntarily of My own free choice. I possess the authority to lay it down, and I possess the authority to take it back again. I received this mandate directly from My Father.”
These statements caused another division among the Jewish people.
Many of them were saying: “He is possessed by a demon and speaks like a madman. Why would anyone listen to what He says?”
Others were saying: “These are not the words of someone possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of blind people?”
