verses.heading: The Deity of Jesus / The Deity of Jesus
verses.text: Then the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was wintertime,
and Jesus was walking through the temple courts in the area known as Solomon’s Colonnade.
The Jewish leaders surrounded Him and demanded: “How much longer will You keep us in suspense? If You are truly the Messiah, tell us plainly and directly.”
Jesus answered them: “I have already told you, but you refuse to believe. The works that I perform in My Father’s name—these very works serve as testimony about who I am.
But you do not believe because you do not belong to My sheep.
My sheep hear My voice and recognize it. I know them intimately, and they follow Me.
I give them eternal life, and they will absolutely never perish—not ever. And no one has the power to snatch them out of My hand.
My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than anyone. No one has the ability to snatch them away from My Father’s hand.
I and the Father are one in essence.”
Once again, the Jewish leaders picked up stones with the intention of stoning Him to death.
Jesus responded to them: “I have shown you many good and beautiful works that come from the Father. Which specific one of these works are you stoning Me for?”
The Jewish leaders replied: “We are not stoning You for any good work You have done, but for blasphemy—because You, being merely a human man, are making Yourself out to be God.”
Jesus answered them: “Is it not written in your own Law: ‘I have declared, you are gods’?
If God called them ‘gods’—those people to whom God's word came—and the Scripture cannot be broken or invalidated,
then why do you accuse Me of blasphemy—Me, whom the Father set apart and consecrated for His purpose and sent into the world—simply because I stated ‘I am the Son of God’?
If I am not performing the works that My Father does, then you should not believe Me.

But if I am indeed performing them, even if you refuse to believe Me personally, at least believe the evidence of the works themselves. Then you will come to know that the Father dwells in Me and I dwell in the Father.”
At this point they tried once more to arrest Him, but He slipped away from their grasp.
Jesus then went back across the Jordan River to the location where John had first been baptizing. He remained there,
and many people came out to Him. They were saying: “John never performed even a single miraculous sign, but everything John spoke about this man has proven to be true.”
And in that location, many placed their faith in Him.

verses.heading: The Death of Lazarus / The Death of Lazarus
verses.text: Now there was a man who was gravely ill, named Lazarus, who lived in Bethany—the village where Mary and her sister Martha resided.
This Mary was the same woman who would later anoint the Lord with fragrant oil and wipe His feet with her hair. It was her brother Lazarus who was sick.
So the sisters sent a messenger to Jesus with this urgent message: “Lord, the one You love dearly is seriously ill.”
When Jesus received this news, He said: “This sickness will not ultimately result in death. Rather, it exists for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through what happens.”
Now Jesus deeply loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
Yet when He heard that Lazarus was sick, He deliberately remained where He was for two more days.
Then, after this delay, He said to His disciples: “Let us return to Judea.”
The disciples protested: “Rabbi, just recently the Jewish leaders were trying to stone You to death, and You want to go back there again?”
Jesus responded: “Are there not twelve hours of daylight in each day? If someone walks during the daytime, he does not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.
But if someone walks during the nighttime, he stumbles around, because the light is not present in him.”
After saying this, He continued: “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to awaken him from his sleep.”
So the disciples said: “Lord, if he has simply fallen asleep, then he will recover.”
Jesus had been speaking about his death, but they thought He was referring to ordinary, natural sleep.
So Jesus then told them in plain, direct language: “Lazarus has died.
And for your sakes I am glad I was not present there, so that you may come to believe more deeply. But let us go to him now.”
Then Thomas, who was called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples: “Let us also go, so that we may die together with Him.”

verses.heading: Jesus is the Resurrection and the Life / Jesus is the Resurrection and the Life
verses.text: When Jesus arrived, He discovered that Lazarus had already been lying in the tomb for four days.
Now Bethany was located near Jerusalem, only about two miles away,
and many of the Jewish people had come out to Martha and Mary to offer them consolation regarding the loss of their brother.
So when Martha heard the report that Jesus was approaching, she went out to meet Him, but Mary remained sitting in the house.
Martha said to Jesus: “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.
But even now I know that whatever You ask from God, God will grant to You.”
Jesus said to her: “Your brother will rise again and live.”
Martha replied to Him: “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection that will occur on the last day.”
Jesus declared to her: “I Myself am the resurrection and the life. The person who believes in Me will live, even if he dies physically.
And everyone who lives and continues believing in Me will never truly die for all eternity. Do you believe this truth?”
She said to Him: “Yes, Lord, I have come to believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God—the One who was prophesied to come into the world.”

verses.heading: Jesus Weeps / Jesus Weeps
verses.text: After she had spoken these words, she went away and called her sister Mary privately, saying: “The Teacher has arrived and is asking to see you.”
When Mary heard this news, she got up quickly and began making her way to Him.
Jesus had not yet entered the village itself, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.
The Jewish people who were in the house with Mary, consoling her, observed that she stood up quickly and went out. They followed her, assuming she was heading to the tomb to weep there.
When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw Him, she fell down at His feet and said to Him: “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”
When Jesus saw her weeping, and saw the Jewish people who came with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in His spirit and profoundly troubled within Himself.
He asked: “Where have you laid him?” They said to Him: “Lord, come and see for Yourself.”
Jesus wept.
The Jewish people who observed this began saying: “Look at how deeply He loved him!”
But some of them said: “Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have done something to prevent this man from dying?”

verses.heading: Lazarus is Raised / Lazarus is Raised
verses.text: Jesus, again deeply moved within Himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, with a stone laid against the entrance.
Jesus said: “Remove the stone.” Martha, the sister of the deceased, said to Him: “Lord, by this time there will be a terrible odor, for he has been dead four days.”
Jesus said to her: “Did I not tell you that if you would believe, you would witness the glory of God?”
So they removed the stone from the entrance. Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said: “Father, I give You thanks that You have heard Me.
I knew that You always hear Me, but I said this aloud for the benefit of the crowd standing around, so that they may believe that You sent Me.”
After He had said these things, He called out in a loud, commanding voice: “Lazarus, come out of there!”
The man who had been dead came out, his feet and hands still wrapped with burial strips of linen, and his face covered with a burial cloth. Jesus said to them: “Unwrap him and release him to go.”

verses.heading: The Plot to Kill Jesus / The Plot to Kill Jesus / Matt. 26:1-5; Mk. 14:1-2; Lk. 22:1-2
verses.text: As a result, many of the Jewish people who had come with Mary and had witnessed what Jesus did placed their faith in Him.
But some of them went to the Pharisees and reported to them what Jesus had done.
So the chief priests and the Pharisees convened a meeting of the Sanhedrin and said: “What action are we taking in light of the fact that this man is performing numerous miraculous signs?
If we allow Him to continue in this way, everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and destroy both our temple and our nation.”
But one of them, a man named Caiaphas, who was serving as high priest that year, said to them: “You people understand nothing at all!
You fail to take into account that it is better for you that one man should die on behalf of the people, rather than having the entire nation destroyed.”
Now he did not speak this from his own understanding, but because he was high priest during that year, he unknowingly prophesied that Jesus was destined to die for the nation—
and not only for the Jewish nation, but also to gather together into one people the scattered children of God from all places.
So from that day forward they made plans together to put Him to death.
Therefore Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jewish people. Instead, He withdrew from there to a region near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and there He stayed with His disciples.
Now the Jewish Passover was approaching, and many people went up from the countryside to Jerusalem before the Passover in order to purify themselves ceremonially.
They were searching for Jesus, and as they stood in the temple courts they were saying to one another: “What do you think? Will He come to the feast or not?”
The chief priests and the Pharisees had issued orders that if anyone learned where Jesus was, they must report it immediately so they could arrest Him.

verses.heading: Jesus is Anointed by Mary at Bethany / Jesus is Anointed by Mary at Bethany / Matt. 26:6-13; Mk. 14:3-9
verses.text: Six days before the Passover celebration, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus lived—the man Jesus had raised from the dead.
So they prepared a dinner in His honor there. Martha was serving the meal, while Lazarus was one of those reclining at the table with Him.

Then Mary took about a pint of extremely expensive perfume made from pure nard, anointed Jesus’ feet with it, and wiped His feet with her hair. The entire house was filled with the fragrant aroma of the perfume.
But Judas Iscariot, one of His disciples—the one who was planning to betray Him—objected,
“Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and the proceeds given to the poor?”
He said this not because he had any genuine concern for the poor, but because he was a thief. Since he was in charge of the money bag, he regularly helped himself to what was deposited in it.
So Jesus said: “Leave her alone. She has kept this for the day when I will be buried.
The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.”

verses.heading: The Conspiracy to Kill Lazarus / The Conspiracy to Kill Lazarus
verses.text: Meanwhile, a large crowd of Jewish people learned that Jesus was there. They came not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,
because on account of him, many of the Jewish people were going away from their leaders and placing their faith in Jesus.

verses.heading: The Triumphal Entry / The Triumphal Entry / Matt. 21:1-11; Mk. 11:1-11; Lk. 19:28-40
verses.text: The next day, the large crowd that had come for the feast heard that Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem.
They took branches from palm trees and went out to meet Him, shouting: “Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the King of Israel!”*
Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, just as the Scripture says:
“Do not be afraid, Daughter of Zion; look, your King is coming, seated on a donkey’s colt!”*

His disciples did not understand the significance of these things at first. But after Jesus was glorified, they remembered that these prophecies had been written about Him and that these events had been fulfilled in Him.
Now the crowd that had been with Him when He called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead continued bearing witness to what they had seen.
This is why the crowd went out to meet Him—because they had heard that He had performed this miraculous sign.
So the Pharisees said among themselves: “You see that your efforts are accomplishing nothing! Look—the whole world has gone running after Him!”

verses.heading: Some Greeks Seek Jesus / Some Greeks Seek Jesus
verses.text: Now there were some Greeks among those who had come up to worship at the feast.
These men came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and made a request of him: “Sir, we would like to see Jesus.”
Philip went and told Andrew about it. Then Andrew and Philip went together and told Jesus.
Jesus responded to them by saying: “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: Unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains only a single grain by itself. But if it dies, it produces much fruit.
The person who loves his life in this world will lose it, but the person who hates his life in this world will preserve it for eternal life.
If anyone wishes to serve Me, he must follow Me. And where I am, there My servant will be also. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.

verses.heading: The Son of Man Must be Lifted Up / The Son of Man Must be Lifted Up
verses.text: Now My soul is deeply troubled and distressed. What should I say? ‘Father, save Me from this hour’? No—it was precisely for this hour that I came.
Father, glorify Your name!” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”
The crowd standing there heard it and began saying that it had thundered. Others were saying: “An angel has spoken to Him.”
Jesus responded and said: "This voice did not come for My benefit, but for yours.
Now is the time of judgment for this world. Now the ruler of this world will be cast out.
And when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to Myself.”
He said this to indicate what kind of death He was about to die.
The crowd responded to Him: “We have heard from the Law that the Christ remains forever. How then can You say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man You are talking about?”

Jesus then said to them: “The Light will be with you only a little while longer. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness does not overtake you. The person who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of Light.” After Jesus had said these things, He departed and hid Himself from them.

verses.heading: The Unbelief of the Jews / The Unbelief of the Jews
verses.text: Even though He had performed so many miraculous signs right in front of them, they still refused to believe in Him.
This happened to fulfill the word spoken by the prophet Isaiah: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”*
For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah also said in another place:
“He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, nor understand with their hearts, nor turn back to Me—and then I would heal them.”*
Isaiah said these things because he saw Christ’s glory and spoke concerning Him.
Yet even so, many among the rulers actually believed in Him. But because of the Pharisees, they would not confess their faith openly, for fear of being expelled from the synagogue.
For they loved receiving honor from human beings more than receiving honor from God.

verses.heading: The Word Brings Judgment / The Word Brings Judgment
verses.text: Then Jesus called out and declared: “The person who believes in Me is not merely believing in Me, but in the One who sent Me.
And the person who sees Me is actually seeing the One who sent Me.
I have come into the world as Light, so that everyone who believes in Me will not have to remain in darkness.
If anyone hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
The person who rejects Me and does not receive My words has something that judges him: the very word I have spoken will judge him on the last day.
For I have not spoken on My own authority. Rather, the Father Himself who sent Me has given Me a commandment about what I should say and what I should speak.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And I know that His commandment leads to eternal life. Therefore, whatever I speak, I speak exactly as the Father has instructed Me to speak.” 13 Alluded to Ps. 118:26a 15 Quoted from Zech. 9:9 38 Quoted from Is. 53:1 40 Quoted from Is. 6:10

verses.heading: Jesus Washes the Feet of His Disciples / Jesus Washes the Feet of His Disciples
verses.text: Now before the Feast of the Passover began, Jesus knew that His hour had come to depart from this world and return to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the very end.
During supper, the devil had already planted in the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, the intention to betray Jesus.
Jesus knew that the Father had placed all things under His authority, and that He had come from God and was returning to God.
So He rose from the meal, laid aside His outer garments, and wrapped a towel around His waist.
Then He poured water into a basin and began washing the feet of His disciples, drying them with the towel He had wrapped around Himself.
When He came to Simon Peter, Peter said to Him: “Lord, are You actually going to wash my feet?”
Jesus answered and said to him: “What I am doing, you do not understand right now, but afterward you will understand.”
Peter said to Him: “You will never wash my feet—not ever!” Jesus answered him: “If I do not wash you, you have no share or partnership with Me.”
Simon Peter said to Him: “Lord, then wash not only my feet, but also my hands and my head!”
Jesus said to him: “The person who has bathed completely needs only to wash his feet; the rest of his body is entirely clean. And you disciples are clean—though not every one of you.”
For He knew who was going to betray Him. This is why He said: “Not all of you are clean.”
When He had finished washing their feet, He put His outer garments back on and returned to His place at the table. Then He said to them: “Do you understand what I have just done for you?
You call Me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord,’ and you speak correctly, for that is exactly what I am.
Now if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.
For I have given you an example to follow, so that you should do just as I have done for you.
I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: A servant is not greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
Now that you understand these things, you will be blessed if you actually practice them.
I am not speaking about all of you. I know the ones I have chosen. But the Scripture must be fulfilled: ‘The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me.’*
I am telling you this now, before it takes place, so that when it does happen, you may believe that I am who I claim to be.
I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: The person who welcomes anyone I send welcomes Me; and the person who welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me.”

verses.heading: Jesus Predicts His Betrayal / Jesus Predicts His Betrayal / Matt. 26:20-25; Mk. 14:17-21; Lk. 22:21-23
verses.text: After saying these things, Jesus became troubled in His spirit. He testified solemnly and said: “I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: One of you is going to betray Me.”
The disciples began looking at one another, completely uncertain about which one of them He meant.
One of His disciples—the one Jesus loved—was reclining close beside Jesus at the table.
So Simon Peter motioned to him and said: “Ask Him which one He is talking about.”
Leaning back against Jesus’ chest, he asked Him: “Lord, who is it?”
Jesus answered: “It is the one to whom I will give this piece of bread after I have dipped it.” Then He dipped the piece of bread and gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.
As soon as Judas received the bread, Satan entered into him. Jesus then said to him: “What you are about to do, do quickly.”
None of those reclining at the table understood why Jesus said this to him.
Since Judas was in charge of the money bag, some thought Jesus was telling him to purchase what they needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
As soon as Judas had taken the bread, he went out immediately. And it was night.

verses.heading: The New Commandment / The New Commandment
verses.text: After he had gone out, Jesus said: “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in Him.
If God is glorified in Him, God will also glorify the Son in Himself, and He will glorify Him immediately.
Little children, I will be with you only a little while longer. You will search for Me, and just as I told the Jewish leaders, so I tell you now: Where I am going, you cannot come.
I am giving you a new commandment: Love one another. Just as I have loved you, so you also must love one another.
By this everyone will recognize that you are My disciples—if you demonstrate love for one another.”

verses.heading: Jesus Predicts Peter's Denial / Jesus Predicts Peter's Denial / Matt. 26:31-35; Mk. 14:27-31; Lk. 22:31-34
verses.text: Simon Peter asked Him: “Lord, where are You going?” Jesus answered him: “Where I am going, you cannot follow Me now, but you will follow Me later.”
Peter said to Him: “Lord, why can I not follow You right now? I will lay down my life for Your sake.”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Jesus responded: “Will you really lay down your life for Me? I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: Before the rooster crows to announce the dawn, you will have denied knowing Me three times!” 18 Quoted from Ps. 41:9

verses.heading: Jesus is the Way, and the Truth, and the Life / Jesus is the Way, and the Truth, and the Life
verses.text: “Do not let your hearts be troubled and distressed. Continue trusting in God; trust also in Me.
In My Father’s house there are many dwelling places. If that were not true, I would have told you plainly. I am going to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming back to receive you to Myself, so that where I am, you may be there also.
You already know the way to the place where I am going.”
Thomas said to Him: “Lord, we do not know where You are going, so how can we possibly know the way to get there?”
Jesus said to him: “I Myself am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except by going through Me.
If you had truly known Me, you would have known My Father as well. From this moment forward, you do know Him and have seen Him with your own eyes.”
Philip said to Him: “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be sufficient for us.”
Jesus said to him: “Have I been with you for such a long time, Philip, and you still have not come to know Me? The person who has seen Me has seen the Father! How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I speak to you I do not speak on My own authority. Rather, it is the Father, dwelling in Me, who accomplishes His works.
Believe Me when I tell you that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me. Or at the very least, believe on account of the works themselves.

I tell you with absolute certainty and truth: The person who believes in Me will also do the works that I am doing. In fact, he will do even greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.
And whatever you ask in My name, I will do it, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you ask Me for anything in My name, I will do it.

verses.heading: The Promise of the Spirit / The Promise of the Spirit
verses.text: If you love Me, you will obey My commandments.
And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Intercessor to be with you forever—
the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you know Him, because He lives with you and will be in you.
I will not leave you as orphans without care or protection. I am coming to you.
In just a little while, the world will no longer see Me, but you will see Me. Because I live, you also will live.
On that day you will come to know that I am in My Father, and you are in Me, and I am in you.
The person who has My commandments and obeys them—that is the one who loves Me. And the person who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.”
Judas—not Iscariot—said to Him: “Lord, what has happened that You are about to reveal Yourself to us but not to the world?”
Jesus answered and said to him: “If anyone loves Me, he will obey My word. My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.
The person who does not love Me does not obey My words. And the word you hear is not Mine alone, but belongs to the Father who sent Me.
I have spoken these things to you while remaining with you.
But the Intercessor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name—He will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have said to you.
Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
You heard Me say to you: ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would be rejoicing that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I am.
I have told you this now before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe.
I will not speak with you much longer, because the ruler of this world is coming. He has no power or claim over Me,
but the world must learn that I love the Father and that I do exactly as the Father has commanded Me. Get up now; let us leave this place.”

verses.heading: Jesus is the True Vine / Jesus is the True Vine
verses.text: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser who cultivates it.
Every branch in Me that does not produce fruit, He removes. And every branch that does produce fruit, He prunes and cleanses, so that it may produce even more fruit.
You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.
Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as a branch cannot produce fruit by itself unless it remains connected to the vine, so you cannot produce fruit unless you remain in Me.
I am the vine; you are the branches. The person who remains in Me, and I in him—that person produces much fruit. For apart from Me you can accomplish nothing of eternal value.
If anyone does not remain in Me, he is thrown away like a branch and withers. People gather such branches and throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
If you remain in Me, and My words remain in you, ask whatever you desire, and it will be accomplished for you.
By this My Father is glorified: that you produce much fruit and prove yourselves to be My disciples.
Just as the Father has loved Me, so I have loved you. Remain in My love.
If you obey My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have obeyed My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.
I have spoken these things to you so that My joy may be in you, and so that your joy may be completely full.
This is My commandment: Love one another just as I have loved you.
No one possesses greater love than this: that someone would lay down his life for his friends.
You are My friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing. Instead, I have called you friends, because everything I have heard from My Father I have made known to you.
You did not choose Me; rather, I chose you and appointed you to go out and produce fruit—fruit that will endure. Then the Father will give you whatever you ask Him in My name.
This is what I command you: Love one another.

verses.heading: The World’s Hatred Against Jesus and His Disciples / The World’s Hatred Against Jesus and His Disciples
verses.text: If the world hates you, understand and remember that it hated Me before it hated you.
If you belonged to the world, the world would love you as its own. But because you do not belong to the world—because I chose you out of the world—the world hates you.
Remember the word I spoke to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well. If they obeyed My word, they will obey yours also.
But they will do all these things to you on account of My name, because they do not know the One who sent Me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
The person who hates Me hates My Father as well.
If I had not done among them works that no one else has ever done, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have seen these works and yet have hated both Me and My Father.
But this has happened to fulfill the word written in their Law: ‘They hated Me without any cause or reason.’
When the Helper comes—the One I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—He will testify about Me.
And you also must testify about Me, because you have been with Me from the beginning.
I have communicated these matters to you so that you will not fall away or be led into sin.
They will remove you from the synagogues. Indeed, an hour is approaching when anyone who murders you will suppose he is presenting worship to God.
And they will perform these actions because they have gained no knowledge of the Father or of Me.

But I have communicated these matters to you so that when the hour arrives, you may recall that I informed you concerning them. I did not communicate these matters to you from the beginning, because I was remaining with you.

verses.heading: The Work of the Spirit / The Work of the Spirit
verses.text: But now I am proceeding to the One who sent Me, and none of you inquires of Me, ‘Where are You proceeding?’
But because I have communicated these matters to you, grief has filled your hearts.
Yet I communicate the truth to you: It is beneficial for you that I depart. For if I do not depart, the Intercessor will not come to you. But if I proceed, I will send Him to you.
And when He arrives, He will expose and convict the world concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment:
concerning sin, because they do not place their faith in Me;
concerning righteousness, because I am proceeding to the Father and you will no longer see Me;
and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world stands condemned.
I still have many matters to communicate to you, but you lack the capacity to receive them now.

But when He arrives—the Spirit of truth—He will lead you into the entirety of truth. For He will not communicate from His own initiative, but whatever He hears He will communicate, and He will announce to you the matters that are approaching.
He will bring glory to Me, because He will receive from what is Mine and will announce it to you.
All things that the Father possesses are Mine. For this reason I stated that He receives from what is Mine and will announce it to you.

verses.heading: Your Sadness Will Turn into Joy / Your Sadness Will Turn into Joy
verses.text: A brief time, and you will no longer see Me, and again a brief time, and you will see Me.”

Some of His disciples therefore declared to one another, “What is this that He communicates to us, ‘A brief time, and you will not see Me, and again a brief time, and you will see Me,’ and, ‘Because I am proceeding to the Father’?”
So they were saying, "What is this ‘brief time’ of which He speaks? We have no understanding of what He is communicating.”

Jesus recognized that they desired to question Him, so He declared to them, “Are you deliberating among yourselves concerning this, that I stated, ‘A brief time, and you will not see Me, and again a brief time, and you will see Me’?
Truly, truly, I declare to you: You will weep and lament, but the world will experience joy. You will experience grief, but your grief will be transformed into joy.

When a woman gives birth, she has anguish because her hour has arrived. But when the child is born, she no longer recalls the suffering, because of her joy that a human being has been brought into the world.
So you also have grief now. But I will see you again, and your hearts will experience joy, and no one will remove your joy from you.
And in that day you will pose no questions to Me. Truly, truly, I declare to you: Whatever you request of the Father in My name, He will provide to you.
Until now you have requested nothing in My name. Request, and you will receive, so that your joy may be brought to completion.

verses.heading: I Have Overcome the World / I Have Overcome the World
verses.text: I have communicated these matters to you in figures of speech. An hour is approaching when I will no longer communicate to you in figures of speech, but will announce to you plainly concerning the Father.
In that day you will make requests in My name, and I do not declare to you that I will make petition to the Father on your behalf,
for the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have placed your faith in the fact that I proceeded from God.
I proceeded from the Father and have come into the world. Again, I am departing from the world and proceeding to the Father.”
His disciples declared, “Behold, now You are communicating plainly and not employing any figure of speech!
Now we understand that You possess knowledge of all things and have no need for anyone to pose questions to You. By this we place our faith in the fact that You proceeded from God.”
Jesus responded to them, “Do you now place your faith in Me?
Behold, an hour is approaching—and has now arrived—when you will be dispersed, each one to his own home, and you will abandon Me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
I have communicated these matters to you so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But maintain courage: I have conquered the world.”

verses.heading: The High Priestly Prayer of Jesus / The High Priestly Prayer of Jesus
verses.text: Jesus spoke these things, and raising His eyes to heaven in prayer, He said, “Father, the hour has come at last. Glorify Your Son through what is about to unfold, so that the Son may glorify You in return.
You have given Him authority over all flesh, over all humanity, so that to all whom You have given Him as a trust, He may give eternal life to them as a gift.
Now this is eternal life in its essence, that they may know You intimately, the Only true God in existence, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent as the Messiah.
“I have glorified You on earth and brought You honor, having completed the work that You gave Me to do and accomplish.
Now, Father, You glorify Me at Your side with the glory that I had with You before the world existed.

I have manifested Your name and revealed Your character to the men whom You gave Me out of the world. Yours they were by Your choice, and You gave them to Me as disciples, and they have kept Your word.
Now they have come to understand that all the things that You have given Me—My words, My works, My authority—are from You as the source.

Because the words which You gave to Me I have given to them faithfully, and they received them. They understood truly that I came from You in origin, and they believed that You sent Me as Your representative.
I am praying on their behalf at this moment. I am not praying on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those whom You have given Me, because they are Yours by election.
All things that are Mine are Yours, and Yours are Mine in shared possession, and I have been glorified in them.

I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to You in heaven. Holy Father, keep them in Your name, in Your character, which You have given to Me, so that they may be one in unity, just as We are one.

While I was with them, I kept them in Your name, which You have given to Me, and I guarded them from evil. None of them has perished except the son of destruction, Judas, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled as prophesied.
Now I am coming to You, and these things I am saying in the world while still present, so that they may have My joy brought to its full measure in themselves.
I have given them Your word and Your truth, and the world has hated them because of it, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
I do not pray that You take them out of the world by removing them, but that You keep them from the evil one.
They are not of the world in their values and allegiance, just as I am not of the world in Mine.
Sanctify them by the truth—that is, set them apart and make them holy through the truth. Your word is truth and reality.
As You sent Me into the world on a mission, so also I have sent them into the world with the gospel message.
For their sake I sanctify Myself and set Myself apart for sacrifice, so that they themselves also may be sanctified by the truth—both made holy by it and set apart for Your service.
I am not praying on behalf of these disciples only, but also on behalf of those who believe in Me through their word and testimony, future generations of believers.

I pray that they all may be one in spiritual unity, just as You, Father, are in Me and I am in You in perfect union, that they also may be in Us in fellowship, in order that the world may believe that You sent Me when they see this unity.
The glory which You have given to Me, I have given to them to reflect Your character, that they may be one in unity, just as We are one in nature—

I in them, and You in Me in perfect union—so that they may be brought to perfection in unity and maturity, that the world may know with certainty that You sent Me, and You loved them with the same love, just as You loved Me eternally.

Father, I desire and will that they also, whom You have given to Me as a precious trust, may be with Me where I am in glory, in order that they may see My glory which You have given Me, because You loved Me before the foundation of the world was laid.
Righteous Father, although the world does not know You or recognize You, I have known You intimately, and these disciples have known that You sent Me as Your representative.

I have made known to them Your name and revealed Your character, and will continue to make it known in the future, so that the love with which You loved Me may be in them dwelling, and I may be in them by My presence.”

verses.heading: The Betrayal and Arrest of Jesus / The Betrayal and Arrest of Jesus / Matt. 26:47-56; Mk. 14:43-50; Lk. 22:47-53
verses.text: After Jesus had spoken these words of prayer, He went out with His disciples to the other side of the brook of the Kidron, a valley east of Jerusalem, where there was a garden which He and His disciples entered for prayer.
Now Judas, the one who was betraying Him, also knew the place, because Jesus often gathered in that place with His disciples for fellowship and prayer.
So Judas, procuring the cohort of Roman soldiers and temple officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, came there with lanterns and torches and weapons, prepared to arrest Jesus.
Then Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon Him and would transpire, came out voluntarily and said to them, “Whom are you seeking?”
They responded to Him, “Jesus the Nazarene.” He said to them, “I am He,” declaring His divine identity. And Judas, the one who was betraying Him, was also standing with them in the arresting party.
Now when He said to them, “I am He,” they drew back in fear and fell to the ground, overwhelmed by His divine presence and authority.
He then questioned them again, “Who are you seeking? Tell Me again.” And they said, “Jesus the Nazarene.”
Jesus answered with authority, “I have told you that I am He. Therefore, if you are seeking Me, let these disciples go free.”
This was to fulfill the word which He had spoken in prayer: “Of those whom You have given Me I have not lost any of them.”
Then Simon Peter, having a sword concealed on him, drew it impulsively and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear in defense. (The name of the servant was Malchus.)
Jesus then said to Peter with rebuke, “Put the sword into the sheath. The cup of suffering which the Father has given Me, shall I not drink it willingly? This is My Father’s will.”

verses.heading: Jesus Before Annas and Caiaphas / Jesus Before Annas and Caiaphas / Matt. 26:57-58; Mk. 14:53-54; Lk. 22:54
verses.text: Then the cohort of Roman soldiers, the commander, and the officers of the Jewish temple police arrested Jesus and bound Him with ropes,
and led Him away to Annas first, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was serving as high priest that year.
Now it was Caiaphas who had recommended to the Jewish council that it was advantageous and politically expedient for one man to die for the people rather than the whole nation perish.

verses.heading: Peter’s Denial of Christ / Peter’s Denial of Christ / Matt. 26:69-70; Mk. 14:66-68; Lk. 22:55-57
verses.text: So Simon Peter and another disciple, likely John, were following Jesus at a distance. Now that disciple was known to the high priest through some connection, and he entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest,
but Peter stood at the door outside, not gaining entrance. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the female doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.
Then the female servant, who was the doorkeeper, said to Peter suspiciously, “You are not also one of the disciples of this man, are you?” He said with denial, “I am not! I do not know Him.”

Now the servants and the temple officers were standing there around a fire, having made a charcoal fire, because it was cold in the night air, and they were warming themselves. Peter was also with them, standing and warming himself, trying to blend in.

verses.heading: The High Priest Questions Jesus / The High Priest Questions Jesus / Matt. 26:59-66; Mk. 14:55-64; Lk. 22:66-71
verses.text: The high priest then questioned Jesus about His disciples and their number, and about His teaching.

Jesus answered him directly, “I have spoken openly to the world without concealment. I always taught in the synagogue and in the temple courts where all the Jews come together for worship, and I have said nothing in secret.
Why are you questioning Me about My teaching? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them. Ask My audience. Behold, they know what I said.”
When He had said these things, one of the officers, who was standing nearby, gave Jesus a blow to the face with his hand, saying, “Is that the way You respond to the high priest?”
Jesus responded to him calmly, “If I have spoken wrongly or falsely, bear witness of the wrong and show the error. But if I have spoken rightly and truthfully, why do you strike Me without cause?”
Then Annas sent Him bound with ropes to Caiaphas the high priest for further interrogation.

verses.heading: Peter Denies Jesus Again / Peter Denies Jesus Again / Matt. 26:71-75; Mk. 14:69-72; Lk. 22:58-62
verses.text: Now Simon Peter was still standing by the fire and warming himself. So they said to him with suspicion, “You are not also one of His disciples, are you?” He denied it emphatically, and said, “I am not! I do not know the man.”
One of the servants of the high priest, who was related to the one whose ear Peter cut off with the sword, said, “Did I not see you in the garden with Him? I recognize you.”
So Peter denied it again, a third time, and at once a rooster crowed, fulfilling Jesus' prediction.

verses.heading: Jesus Before Pilate / Jesus Before Pilate / Matt. 27:1-2, 11-14; Mk. 15:1-5; Lk. 23:1-5
verses.text: Then they led Jesus from the house of Caiaphas to the Praetorium, the Roman governor’s palace. Now it was early in the morning at dawn, and they themselves did not enter the Praetorium, so that they would not be ceremonially defiled by entering a Gentile building, but might eat the Passover meal in ritual purity.
So Pilate came out to them in accommodation and said, “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”
They answered and said to him evasively, “If this man were not acting in the wrong way and were not a criminal, we would not have handed Him over to you for judgment.”

So Pilate said to them, “Take Him yourselves, and judge Him according to your Law and your religious regulations.” The Jewish leaders said to him, “It is not lawful for us to kill anyone or execute capital punishment.”
This was so that the word of Jesus would be fulfilled which He had spoken, indicating what kind of death He was about to die—crucifixion by the Romans, not stoning by the Jews.
Then Pilate entered again into the Praetorium, and summoned Jesus and said to Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?”
Jesus answered, “Do you say this from yourself and your own understanding, or did others say this to you about Me?”
Pilate replied defensively, “I am not a Jew, am I? Your nation and the chief priests handed You over to me. What have You done to deserve this?”

Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world. If My kingdom were of this world and earthly, My servants would have been fighting, so that I would not be handed over to the Jewish authorities. But now My kingdom is not from here or of earthly origin.”

Therefore, Pilate said to Him, “So then, You are a king? Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king, and you are correct. To this end, I have been born, and to this end, I have come into the world: to testify to the truth and bear witness. Everyone who is of the truth hears My voice and follows Me.”

verses.heading: Jesus Condemned to Die / Jesus Condemned to Die / Matt. 27:15-31; Mk. 15:6-20; Lk. 23:13-25
verses.text: Pilate said to Him philosophically, “What is truth? How can anyone know?” After saying this, he went out again to the Jewish leaders and said to them, “I find no grounds for an accusation against Him. He is innocent.
But you have a custom that I release for you one prisoner at the Passover as an act of clemency. So do you wish that I release for you the King of the Jews?”
Then they shouted again with hostility, saying, “Not this man! We do not want Him, but Barabbas.” Now Barabbas was a robber and an insurrectionist.
So then Pilate took Jesus and flogged Him severely, having Him scourged with a Roman whip in hopes of satisfying the crowd.
When the soldiers had twisted together a crown of thorns, they put it on His head mockingly, and threw a purple robe around Him in ridicule of His kingship.
Then they kept approaching Him repeatedly, saying with sarcasm, “Hail, King of the Jews!” while continuing to give Him slaps in the face with their hands.
Pilate went out again and said to them, “See, I am bringing Him out to you, so that you will know that I find no grounds for an accusation against Him. He has done nothing worthy of death.”
Then Jesus came out, wearing the thorny crown and the purple robe. Pilate said to them, “Behold the man! Look at Him—He is just a man, suffering.”

So when the chief priests and the temple officers saw Him, they shouted with hatred, saying, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!” Pilate said to them, “Take Him yourselves and crucify Him. For I find no grounds for an accusation against Him.”
The Jewish leaders responded to him, “We have a law from Moses, and according to that law He ought to die, because He made Himself the Son of God, claiming equality with God.”
Now when Pilate heard this statement, he became increasingly afraid.
He entered the Praetorium again and said to Jesus, “Where are You from?” But Jesus gave him no answer, remaining silent.
So Pilate said to Him with irritation, “Are You not speaking to me? Do You not realize that I have authority to release You, and I have authority to crucify You?”

Jesus answered him, “You would have no authority over Me whatsoever if it were not given to you from above by God's sovereignty. Therefore, the one who handed Me over to you has greater sin and responsibility.”

From that time forward, Pilate was seeking to release Him and find a way out, but the Jewish leaders shouted, saying, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar and commits treason.”
So Pilate, when he heard these words of political threat, brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called The Stone Pavement, and in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
Now it was the day of Preparation of the Passover, the day before the Sabbath. It was approximately the sixth hour, around noon. He said to the Jewish leaders, “See your King! Here He is.”
Then they shouted with vehemence, “Away with that One! Away with that One! Crucify Him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king except Caesar.”

verses.heading: The Crucifixion of Jesus / The Crucifixion of Jesus / Matt. 27:32-44; Mk. 15:21-32; Lk. 23:26-43
verses.text: So then Pilate handed Him over to them to be crucified, yielding to their demands. So they took Jesus into their custody,
and He went out, carrying His own cross beam, to the place called The Place of a Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha,
where they crucified Him between two criminals, and with Him two others, one on either side, and Jesus in between them.
Now Pilate also wrote a notice and put it on the cross above His head, and it was written: “Jesus the Nazarene, The King of the Jews.”
So many of the Jewish people read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. And it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek, so all could read.
So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write ‘The King of the Jews,’ but instead, ‘He said, I am King of the Jews.’ ”
Pilate responded firmly, “What I have written, I have written. It stands.”

Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took His outer garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier to claim—and the tunic. Now the tunic was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom without seams.

So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it and ruin it, but cast lots for it, to determine whose it shall be,” so that the Scripture would be fulfilled, which states, “They divided My garments among themselves, and for My clothing they cast a lot.”* Therefore the soldiers did these very things, fulfilling prophecy.
Now His mother Mary and His mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene, stood near the cross of Jesus, watching His suffering.
Therefore, when Jesus saw His mother and the disciple whom He loved, John, standing nearby, He said to His mother, “Woman, behold your son! He will care for you.”
Then He said to the disciple, “Behold, your mother! Care for her.” And from that hour, the disciple accepted her into his own home as his responsibility.

verses.heading: The Death of Jesus / The Death of Jesus / Matt. 27:45-56; Mk. 15:33-41; Lk. 23:44-49
verses.text: After this, Jesus, knowing that all things had now been accomplished, in order that the Scripture would be fulfilled completely, said, “I am thirsty.”
A jar full of sour wine was standing there nearby, so they put a sponge full of the sour wine on a stalk of hyssop and brought it to His mouth.
Then, when Jesus had received the sour wine, He said triumphantly, “It is finished! It is accomplished!” And after He bowed His head voluntarily, He gave up His spirit.

verses.heading: Jesus’ Side Pierced / Jesus’ Side Pierced
verses.text: Then the Jewish leaders, since it was the day of Preparation, so that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a high and holy day), asked Pilate that their legs might be broken to hasten death, and that they might be taken away.
So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first criminal, and of the other who had been crucified alongside Him, to speed their death.
But, upon coming to Jesus, when they saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs as they did the others.
But one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear to verify death, and immediately blood and water flowed out, demonstrating His death.
The one who has seen this has given testimony, and his testimony is true and reliable, and he knows that he is speaking the truth, so that you also may believe in Jesus.
For these things took place so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not a bone of His will be broken,”* preserving Him as the perfect Passover Lamb.
Furthermore, another Scripture says, “They will look on the One whom they have pierced,”* prophesying this very moment.

verses.heading: The Burial of Jesus / The Burial of Jesus / Matt. 27:57-61; Mk. 15:42-47; Lk. 23:50-56
verses.text: After these things, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (though secretly, for fear of the Jewish authorities), asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus, and Pilate granted his request. So he came and took away His body with care.
Nicodemus, the one who had come to Him previously at night seeking truth, also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes about a hundred pounds in weight for burial preparation.
So they took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen wrappings with the spices, as is the custom of the Jews to prepare for burial.
Now in the place where He was crucified, there was a garden, and in the garden, a new tomb, in which no one had ever been buried before.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Therefore, because it was the day of Preparation of the Jews, and since the tomb was nearby and convenient, they laid Jesus there in haste before the Sabbath began. 24 Quoted from Ps. 22:18 36 Quoted from Ps. 34:20 37 Quoted from Zech. 12:10

verses.heading: The Resurrection of Jesus / The Resurrection of Jesus / Matt. 28:1-10; Mk. 16:1-8; Lk. 24:1-12
verses.text: Now on the first day of the week, Sunday morning, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb early, while it was still dark before dawn, and saw the stone had been removed from the tomb, rolled away.

So she ran with urgency and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, John, and said to them, “They have removed the Lord from the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid Him. His body is gone!”
Then Peter and the other disciple went out, and they were going to the tomb to investigate.
The two were running together in haste, but the other disciple ran ahead, faster than Peter, and reached the tomb first.
When he had stooped down to look inside, he saw the linen wrappings lying there undisturbed, but he did not enter.
Then Simon Peter also came following him, and he entered the tomb boldly and saw the linen wrappings lying there,
and the face cloth that had been on His head. It was not lying with the linen wrappings, but folded up separately in one place, indicating an orderly departure.
So then, the other disciple who had arrived at the tomb first also entered, and he saw the evidence and believed that Jesus had risen.
(For they did not yet understand the Scripture that it was necessary for Him to rise from the dead, though it had been prophesied.)
Then the disciples went back again to their own homes, pondering these things.

verses.heading: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene / Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene / Mk. 16:9-11
verses.text: But Mary stood outside the tomb, weeping in grief. So, as she was weeping, she stooped down to look into the tomb,
and she saw two angels in white garments sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had been lying.
They said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have placed Him. I cannot find Him.”
After she had said these things, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but she did not realize that it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking?” Supposing that He was the gardener who tended the area, she said to Him, “Sir, if you have carried Him away, tell me where you have put Him, and I will take Him away.”
Jesus said to her personally, “Mary.” Hearing His voice, having turned, she said to Him in Hebrew, “Rabboni!” (which means “Teacher”).

Jesus said to her, “Do not cling to Me or hold on to Me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father in final ascension. But go to My brothers, My disciples, and say to them, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, and My God and your God.’ ”
Mary Magdalene came and reported to the disciples with joy, “I have seen the Lord!”—and that He had said these things to her.

verses.heading: Jesus Appears to the Disciples / Jesus Appears to the Disciples / Matt. 28:16-20; Mk. 16:14-18; Lk. 24:36-49
verses.text: Now when it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors had been shut where the disciples were gathered on account of fear of the Jewish authorities, Jesus came supernaturally and stood in their midst and said to them, “Peace to you. Do not be afraid.”
Having said this, He showed His hands with the nail prints and His side with the spear wound to them as proof. The disciples then rejoiced greatly when they saw the Lord alive.
So Jesus said to them again, “Peace to you and be at rest. As the Father has sent Me into the world, so also I send you into the world with the gospel.”
Having said this, He breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
If you forgive the sins of any, they have been forgiven by God. If you retain the sins of any, they have been retained.”

verses.heading: Jesus and Thomas / Jesus and Thomas
verses.text: Now Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called Didymus meaning “Twin,” was not with them when Jesus came that first evening.

So the other disciples began to say to him, “We have seen the Lord alive!” But he said to them with skepticism, “Unless I see in His hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the mark of the nails, and put my hand into His side, I will certainly not believe.”

After eight days had passed, His disciples were inside again, and Thomas with them this time. Although the doors were locked for security, Jesus came supernaturally and stood in their midst and said, “Peace to you.”

Then He said to Thomas directly, “Place your finger here and see My hands with the wounds. Reach out your hand and put it into My side. And do not be unbelieving any longer, but believing and trusting.”
Thomas replied and said to Him in worship, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen Me with your eyes, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen Me, yet have believed through testimony.”

verses.heading: The Purpose of Writing the Book / The Purpose of Writing the Book
verses.text: Now Jesus also performed many other miraculous signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book or recorded here.
But these signs have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name and through Him.

verses.heading: Jesus Appears to the Seven Disciples / Jesus Appears to the Seven Disciples
verses.text: After these resurrection appearances, Jesus manifested Himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias, the Sea of Galilee. Now He manifested Himself in this way:
Simon Peter, Thomas who was called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee (James and John), and two others of His disciples were together.

Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing to return to my former occupation.” They said to him, “We also are coming with you.” They went out and got into the boat, but during that entire night they caught nothing despite their efforts.
Now when the early morning had already come at dawn, Jesus stood on the beach. However, the disciples did not realise that it was Jesus from a distance.
So Jesus called to them, “Children, you do not have any fish to eat, do you?” They answered Him, “No, we have caught nothing.”

He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some fish.” So they cast it as instructed, but could no longer pull it in, because of the large number of fish filling it.

Then that disciple whom Jesus loved, John, said to Peter with recognition, “It is the Lord!” So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his outer garment around himself (for he was stripped for work and lightly clothed) and threw himself into the sea to swim to Jesus.
But the other disciples came in the boat, dragging the net teeming with fish, for they were not far from the land, but approximately two hundred cubits distant, about a hundred yards.
So when they got out on the land, they saw a fire of burning coals lying there, and a fish lying on it cooking, and bread. Jesus had prepared breakfast.
Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have recently caught to add to the meal.”
So Simon Peter went up and pulled the net to the shore, full of large fish—one hundred and fifty-three in number. And although there were so many, the net was not torn, demonstrating a miracle.
Jesus said to them, “Come, have breakfast with Me.” None of the disciples ventured to ask Him, “Who are You?” because they knew with certainty that it was the Lord.
Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and likewise the fish, serving them as He had done before.
This was now the third time Jesus was manifested to the disciples as a group after He had been raised from the dead.

verses.heading: Jesus and Peter / Jesus and Peter
verses.text: Now when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me with supreme devotion more than these?” He said to Him, “Yes, Lord, You know that I regard You with affection.” Jesus said to him, “Feed My lambs.”

He said to him again, for a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me with supreme devotion?” He said to Him, “Yes, Lord, You know that I regard You with affection.” Jesus said to him, “Shepherd My sheep.”

He said to him for the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you regard Me with affection?” Peter was distressed and grieved, because He said to him the third time, “Do you regard Me with affection?” He said to Him, “Lord, You know all things. You know everything about me. You know that I regard You with affection.” Jesus said to him, “Feed My sheep.

I tell you with absolute certainty and truth, when you were younger, you used to dress yourself and walk wherever you wanted in freedom. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and bring you where you do not want to go.”
Now He said this, indicating by what kind of death Peter would glorify God. Having said this, He said to him, “Follow Me as My disciple!”

verses.heading: Jesus and the Beloved Disciple / Jesus and the Beloved Disciple
verses.text: Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved, John, following them—he who also had leaned back on His chest at the supper and said, “Lord, who is it that is betraying You?”
So, having seen him, Peter said to Jesus with curiosity, “Lord, but what about this one?”
Jesus said to him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what concern is it of yours? You follow Me and focus on your own calling!”

So this saying spread among the brothers, the believers, that this disciple would not die before Jesus returned. But Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but rather, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”
This is the disciple who is giving testimony about these things, and the one who has written these things in this Gospel, and we know that his testimony is true and reliable.

Now there are also many other things that Jesus did during His ministry, which, if they were written down one after the other in detail, I think the world itself would not even have enough space for the books that would be written to contain them all.

verses.heading: The Promise of the Holy Spirit / The Promise of the Holy Spirit
verses.text: In my previous account, Theophilus, I documented the comprehensive record of everything that Jesus initiated in both action and teaching during His earthly ministry,
extending to the very day when He was received into heaven, having first delivered specific directives through the Holy Spirit to those apostles He had personally selected and commissioned,

to these same individuals He also demonstrated beyond any reasonable doubt that He was genuinely alive following His crucifixion and suffering, presenting Himself through numerous convincing proofs and making repeated appearances to them throughout a forty-day period and delivering teachings concerning the kingdom of God.

During one gathering when He had assembled them together, He issued a firm command that they were not to leave Jerusalem but rather to remain there and wait expectantly for the fulfillment of the Father’s promise, about which He reminded them, saying that they had heard this directly from His own lips previously,

for John had administered baptism using water as the physical element, but they would experience baptism with the Holy Spirit as the divine agent, and this momentous event would occur within just a few days from that present moment.

Therefore, when the disciples had gathered together on this occasion, they proceeded to question Him earnestly, inquiring, “Lord, does this present time mark the moment when You will restore and reestablish the kingdom to Israel?”

He responded to them, saying, “The precise times and specific seasons are matters that the Father has fixed by His own sovereign authority, and it is not within your jurisdiction or privilege to possess knowledge of these appointed moments.

However, you will most certainly receive supernatural power and dynamic ability when the Holy Spirit descends upon you, and you shall become My witnesses—those who testify concerning Me—beginning in Jerusalem, then expanding throughout all the region of Judea, extending into Samaria, and ultimately reaching to the most remote and distant corners of the entire earth.”

verses.heading: The Ascension of Jesus / The Ascension of Jesus
verses.text: After He had completed these instructions, while they stood watching with their own eyes, He began to be lifted upward, and a cloud enveloped Him and received Him, removing Him completely from their sight.
As they continued gazing intently and fixedly upward into the sky during the time He was departing, suddenly, two men dressed in white garments appeared and stood beside them,

and these messengers addressed them, saying, “Men of Galilee, why do you continue standing here looking upward into the sky in this manner? This same Jesus, who has been taken up and removed from your presence into heaven in the way you have just witnessed, will return in exactly the same manner as you observed Him ascending into heaven.”

verses.heading: The Divine Choice of Matthias / The Divine Choice of Matthias
verses.text: Following this extraordinary event, they returned to Jerusalem from the mount known as the Mount of Olives, which is situated in close proximity to Jerusalem, approximately the distance permitted for travel on the Sabbath day.

Upon their entry into the city, they proceeded upward to the upper room where they had been staying—this group consisted of Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas the son of James.

All these individuals were continuously devoting themselves with a unified purpose to prayer, joined together with the women and with Mary the mother of Jesus, and along with His brothers who were also present.

During those particular days, Peter rose to his feet and stood up in the midst of the gathered brothers—at this time there was an assembled crowd of approximately one hundred and twenty persons gathered together in the same location—and he addressed them,

“Brothers and fellow believers, it was absolutely necessary that the Scripture should reach its fulfillment, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand prophetically through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became the guide and leader for those individuals who arrested Jesus.
For this man Judas was originally numbered among our company and had obtained his designated share in this ministry and apostolic service.”

(Now this particular man acquired a piece of land with the compensation he received as payment for his unrighteous deed, and when he fell headfirst with great force, his body burst open violently in the middle section and all his internal organs and intestines spilled out.

This incident became widely known to all the residents who were dwelling in Jerusalem, with the result that this particular field came to be called in their native language Akeldama, which, when translated and interpreted, means Field of Blood.)
“For it stands written in the book of Psalms: ‘Let his dwelling place become desolate, and let there be absolutely no one to inhabit it’;* furthermore, ‘Let another individual take his position.’*
Therefore, it is necessary and required that one man from among those who have accompanied us during the entire period of time when the Lord Jesus moved about and conducted His ministry among us—

beginning from the baptism administered by John and extending all the way until the day on which He was taken up and removed from our presence—one man selected from among these must become and serve as a witness alongside us concerning His resurrection from the dead.”
So they put forward two men for consideration, Joseph who was called Barsabbas (and who also bore the surname Justus) and Matthias.
Then, having offered prayer, they said, “You, Lord, who possess complete knowledge of the hearts of all human beings, show clearly which one of these two men You have chosen
to take the position in this ministry and apostolic office from which Judas turned away in order to go to his own place.”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Then they cast lots for them to determine the divine choice, and the lot fell upon and indicated Matthias; and he was counted together with the eleven apostles. 20 Quoted from Ps. 69:25 20 Quoted from Ps. 109:8

verses.heading: The Day of Pentecost / The Day of Pentecost
verses.text: When the day of Pentecost had fully come, they were all gathered together in unity in the same location.
Suddenly, a sound came from heaven like a violent, rushing, mighty wind, and it filled the entire house where they were sitting and assembled.
Then there appeared to them what looked like tongues of fire, distributing themselves among the group, and one individual tongue came to rest upon each one of them.

Every person present was filled completely with the Holy Spirit, and they began to speak words in other tongues or languages, just as the Spirit was granting them the supernatural ability to speak forth.
Now at that time there were Jewish people residing in Jerusalem, pious men who had come from every nation that exists under heaven.
When this supernatural sound occurred, the crowd assembled, and they were thrown into confusion because each individual person was hearing them speaking in his own native language and dialect.
They were continuously amazed and filled with astonishment, saying, “Are not all these individuals who are speaking Galileans by origin?
How then do we hear them, each one of us, in our own particular language to which we were born and in which we were raised?
Parthians and Medes and Elamites and those residing in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the regions and districts of Libya toward Cyrene, and visitors and sojourners who have come from Rome,
including both ethnic Jews and proselytes who have converted to Judaism, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them declaring in our own native tongues or languages the magnificent works of God.”
All who witnessed this were astonished and thoroughly perplexed, saying to one another in their confusion, “What could this possibly mean?”
However, others who were present were saying with derision, “They have been filled with sweet new wine.”

verses.heading: The First Apostolic Preaching / The First Apostolic Preaching
verses.text: But Peter, standing up together with the eleven apostles, raised his voice and spoke out clearly and boldly to them: “Men of Judea, and all you who are residing in Jerusalem, let this matter be made known to you, and pay careful attention to my words.
For these men are certainly not drunk, just as you are supposing in your minds, for the hour is only the third hour of the day, which is nine o’clock in the morning.
Rather, this extraordinary event is precisely what was spoken about through the prophet Joel:

‘And it will come to pass in the last days,’ says God, ‘that I will pour out from My Spirit upon all humanity, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy and speak forth divine revelation, and your young men will see supernatural visions, and your old men will dream prophetic dreams.
Indeed, even upon My male servants and upon My female servants I will pour out from My Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy and declare My word.
I will display wonders in the heaven above and miraculous signs on the earth below, including blood and fire and a dense cloud of billowing smoke.
The sun will be changed to darkness and the moon will turn to blood, before the coming of the great and glorious day of the Lord.
And it will be that every person who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved and delivered.’*

“Men of Israel, listen carefully to these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a Man who was authenticated by God to you through miracles and wonders and signs, which God performed and accomplished through Him in your very midst, just as you yourselves have full knowledge—
this particular One, delivered over according to the predetermined plan and foreknowledge of God, you murdered by crucifying Him through the agency of lawless and wicked men,
but God raised Him up from death, having loosened the agonies of death, since it was not possible for Him to be held or detained by it.
For David speaks with reference to Him: ‘I kept the Lord continually in view before me, for He is at my right hand so that I may not be shaken;
Because of this reality, my heart was made glad and my tongue rejoiced greatly; and moreover also my flesh will dwell in hope and confident expectation.
For You will not abandon my soul in Hades, nor will You allow Your Holy One to experience decay.
You have made known to me the ways of life; You will fill me with joy in Your presence.’*

"Brothers and fellow men, it is entirely realistic and permissible to speak with confidence to you concerning the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his burial place is with us to this very day.
Therefore, being a prophet and having knowledge that God had sworn to him with a solemn oath to seat one of his descendants on his throne,

and having foreseen this in advance through prophetic vision, he spoke and prophesied concerning the resurrection of the Christ, declaring that He was neither abandoned in Hades, nor did His flesh experience decay.
This Jesus—God raised Him up from the dead, to which fact we all are witnesses.

Therefore, having been lifted up to the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, He has dispensed this gift which you are both seeing with your eyes and hearing with your ears at this very moment.
For David himself did not ascend or go up into heaven, but he himself declares: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand,
until I make and establish Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet.” ’*
Therefore, let all the house and nation of Israel know with absolute certainty that God has made and appointed Him both Lord and Christ—this same Jesus, whom you crucified.”

Now when they heard these words and this message, they were pierced to the heart with deep conviction, and they said to Peter and to the rest of the apostles, “Brothers and fellow men, how should we respond?”

Then Peter declared and proclaimed to them with authority, “Repent and turn from your sins, and be baptized, each and every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
For the promise is extended and belongs to you and to your children and to all those who are far off, as many as the Lord our God will summon to Himself.”
With many additional words he testified and was exhorting them earnestly, saying, “Be saved and delivered from this perverse and corrupt generation.”
So those who received his message were baptized, and on that particular day there were added to their number approximately three thousand souls.

verses.heading: The Fellowship of the Believers / The Fellowship of the Believers
verses.text: They were continuously devoting themselves to the teaching and instruction of the apostles and to fellowship with one another, to the breaking of bread and sharing of meals, and to prayers.
A sense of awe was coming upon every soul, and many wonders and miraculous signs were being performed by the apostles.
All those who believed were together in the same place, and were possessing everything in common or in shared ownership.
They were selling their possessions, and were distributing these things and resources to all, according to whatever need anyone had.

Every single day, steadfastly continuing with one mind or united purpose in the outer courts of the temple and breaking bread and sharing meals from house to house in various homes, they were sharing their food with joy and sincerity of heart,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: praising and worshipping God and having favor and goodwill with all the people. And the Lord was adding every day those who were being saved to their number and company. 17-21 Quoted from Joel 2:28-32 25-28 Quoted from Ps. 16:8-11 34-35 Quoted from Ps. 110:1

verses.heading: The Healing of a Lame Beggar / The Healing of a Lame Beggar
verses.text: Now Peter and John were going up to the outer courts of the temple at the designated hour of prayer, which was the ninth hour of the day, three o’clock in the afternoon.

A certain man who had been crippled from his mother’s womb since birth was being carried, whom people placed every day at the gate of the temple complex called Beautiful, so that he could ask for alms from those who were going into the temple courts,
and when this man saw Peter and John about to enter the temple area, he began to ask them for alms.
But Peter fixed his eyes upon him, together with John, and said, “Look at us and give us your attention!”
The man began to fix his attention on them, expecting to receive something of value from them.
But Peter said, “Silver and gold I do not possess, but what I do have, this I give you—in the name and by the authority of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!”
