Grasping him by the right hand, he raised him up, and instantly his feet and ankles were made strong.
Leaping up with a spring, he stood upright and was walking around; and he entered into the temple courts with them, walking and leaping and praising God with exuberant joy.
All the people saw him walking around and praising God,

and they recognized him, realizing that he was the very one who used to sit at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, asking and begging for alms. They were filled with astonishment at what had happened to him.

verses.heading: The Second Apostolic Preaching / The Second Apostolic Preaching
verses.text: While he held onto Peter and John, all the people ran together and rushed to them in the portico called Solomon’s, overwhelmed with astonishment.

When he saw this gathering and response, Peter addressed the people: “Men of Israel, why do you marvel at this event? Or why are you staring at us, as if by our own personal power or godliness we have made him walk?

The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers and ancestors, has glorified His Servant Jesus, whom you delivered over and disowned in the presence of Pilate, when he had decided to release Him.
But you disowned the Holy and Righteous One, and asked that a man—a murderer—be granted to you,
and you killed the Originator of life, whom God raised up from the dead, of which fact we are witnesses.

On the ground of faith in His name—His name itself and the power it represents—has strengthened this man, whom you see with your eyes and know, and the faith that comes through Him and operates through Him has given to him this complete health before all of you who are gathered here.
And now, brothers and fellow countrymen, I understand that you did these things in ignorance, just as your rulers and leaders also did in the same manner.
But what God announced beforehand through the mouth of all the prophets, that His Christ would suffer, He has thus brought to completion in this way.
Therefore, repent and turn from your sins and turn back to God, for the purpose of the blotting out of your sins and transgressions,
so that times of refreshing and spiritual revival may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send forth the One who has been appointed and designated for you—Christ Jesus,
whom heaven must retain until the times of the restoration and reestablishment of all things, which God spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from ancient times.
Moses declared, ‘The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You shall listen to Him in all matters that He says to you.
And it will come to pass that every soul who does not give heed to that prophet will be utterly destroyed from the people.’*
Indeed, all the prophets from Samuel and those who followed after him in succession, as many as have prophesied, also have announced these days and this time.

You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, ‘And in your offspring all the families and nations of the earth will experience divine favor.’*

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: To you first and foremost, having raised up and brought forth His Servant, God sent Him to bless you by turning each one of you away from your wickedness and evil practices.” 22-23 Quoted from Deut. 18:15-19 25 Quoted from Gen. 22:18

verses.heading: The Arrest of Peter and John / The Arrest of Peter and John
verses.text: Now while they were addressing the people, the priests and the captain and commander of the temple guard and the Sadducees came up to them,
being deeply annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
They seized them and put them in custody in a prison until the next day, for it was already evening.
But many of those who heard the message believed and put their faith in Christ, and the count of the men grew to nearly five thousand.
It occurred that on the next day, their rulers and elders and scribes were assembled in Jerusalem,
including Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and as many as were from the high-priestly family and lineage.
They made them stand in the midst of the assembly and began to question them, saying, “By what power or authority or by what name did you do this thing?”
Then Peter, filled with and empowered by the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers of the people and elders and leaders,
if we are being investigated this day with reference to a good work and act of kindness done to a disabled man, by what means and through what power this man has been healed,

let it be understood by all of you and by all the people of Israel, that by the name and authority of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised up from the dead—by Him and through His power this man is presented before you in complete health.
This Jesus is the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, which has been made the cornerstone of the building.*
And there is salvation and deliverance in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven which has been given among men by which we must be saved and delivered.”

Now when they observed the confidence of Peter and John, and understood that they were untrained men without formal rabbinical education, they were wondering. And they took note of them that they had spent time with Jesus.
But observing the man who had been healed standing together with them, they had nothing to reply in contradiction.
But when they had commanded them to go outside and depart from the Sanhedrin council, they began to converse with one another,
saying, “What shall we do to and with these men? For that an exceptional sign and miracle has been done through them is clear to all those who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
But so that it may not spread further among the people, let us threaten them to speak never again in this name to anyone at all.”
When they had called them back in, they commanded them not to speak or to teach at all in the name of Jesus or under His authority.
But Peter and John answered and said to them, “Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to and obey you rather than God, you must judge for yourselves,
for we cannot refrain from speaking and testifying about what we have seen with our eyes and heard with our ears.”

After they had further threatened them, they released them, finding no way or means to punish them because of the people and the public response, for all were glorifying and praising God for what had taken place.
For the man was more than forty years old upon whom this sign and miracle of healing had been performed.

verses.heading: Prayer for Boldness to Speak the Word of God / Prayer for Boldness to Speak the Word of God
verses.text: When they had been released, they left and came to their own fellows and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.

When they heard it and received this report, they lifted their voices together with one accord to God and said, “Lord and Master, You are the One who created the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything and all things in them,
the One who through the mouth of our father David, Your servant, said by the Holy Spirit, ‘Why did the nations become furious, and the peoples plot empty schemes?
The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered themselves together, against the Lord and against His Anointed One.’*

For certainly in this city there were gathered together against Your holy Servant Jesus, whom You anointed and consecrated, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, together with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel,
to do and accomplish all that Your hand and Your purpose and plan had predestined to be done.
And now, Lord, take notice of their threats, and grant Your servants the ability to speak Your word with all boldness,
while You extend Your hand to heal and restore, and signs and wonders are performed through the name of Your holy Servant Jesus.”

When they had made their petition, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken physically, and they were all filled afresh with the Holy Spirit and continued to proclaim the word of God with fearless confidence.

verses.heading: Unity Among the Believers / Unity Among the Believers
verses.text: Now the full number of those who believed were of one heart and soul and mind, and no one said or claimed that anything that belonged to him was his own private property, but everything was common property and shared among them.
With great power and supernatural ability the apostles were giving and bearing their witness to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace and divine favor was upon them all.
For there was not even anyone needy or lacking among them, because as many as were owners of plots of land or houses were selling them and bringing the proceeds of what was sold
and placing it at the feet of the apostles in submission. And it was being distributed and given out to each person, just as anyone had need or requirement.
Now Joseph, who was called and surnamed Barnabas by the apostles (which name is translated and interpreted as son of encouragement and consolation), a Levite by tribe, a Cypriot by nationality,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: sold a field that was owned by him and brought the money, and he placed it at the feet of the apostles in humble submission. 11 Refers to Ps. 118:22 25-26 Quoted from Ps. 2:1-2

verses.heading: The Divine Judgment of Ananias and Sapphira / The Divine Judgment of Ananias and Sapphira
verses.text: But a certain man, Ananias by name, together with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property,
and he withheld some of the price for himself, and his wife was secretly aware of this deception. Then bringing only a portion of it, he placed it at the feet of the apostles.
But Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart and mind to lie to and deceive the Holy Spirit and to withhold for yourself some of the price of the piece of land?

While it remained unsold and in your possession, did it not remain your own property? And when it was sold, was the money not under your control? Why is it that you have purposed and conceived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to and deceived men, but to God Himself.”
While Ananias heard these words, he fell down suddenly and breathed his last and died. And great fear came upon all those who heard about it and learned of this event.
Then the young men arose, covered him up with burial cloths, and when he was carried out, they buried him in a grave.
Now it occurred there was an interval of about three hours, and his wife came in, not knowing what had taken place.
Peter asked, “Tell me whether you sold the land for this specific amount.” And she said, “Yes, for that exact price.”

But Peter said to her, “Why is it that you have agreed together to test and challenge the Spirit of the Lord? See, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door even now, and they will carry you out also.”
Immediately, she fell down at his feet and died. Then when the young men entered, they found her dead, and after they carried her out, they buried her beside her husband.
Great fear came upon the whole church, and upon all who heard about and learned of these things.

verses.heading: The Expansion of the Jerusalem Church / The Expansion of the Jerusalem Church
verses.text: Now many signs and wonders and miraculous works were being done among the people by the hands and ministry of the apostles. And they were all together in unity in Solomon’s Portico.
None of the rest of the people dared to join them, and yet the people were holding them in high esteem.
More believers were being added to their number, multitudes both of men and women,
so that they even carried out the sick into the streets and placed them on cots and mats, so that when Peter came by and passed through, at least his shadow might fall upon some of them.
The people also were coming together from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits and demons—all of whom were being healed and completely restored.

verses.heading: The Persecution of the Apostles / The Persecution of the Apostles
verses.text: But the high priest rose up and took action, and all those who were with him and sided with him (that is, the party of the Sadducees), and were filled with jealousy and envy.
They laid hands upon the apostles and seized them and put them in the public jail.
But during the night, an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, and when he had brought them out, he commanded,
“Go and stand in the outer courts of the temple and speak to the people all the words and message of this life and salvation.”

When they heard this instruction, they entered the temple courts at dawn and began to teach and instruct the people. Now when the high priest arrived, and those who were with him, they convened the Sanhedrin council—even all the assembly of the elders of the sons of Israel—and sent officers to the prison to bring them.
But when the officers came, they did not find them in the prison, and they went back and reported,
saying, “We found the prison shut with all security and the guards positioned at the doors, but when we opened them, we found no one inside.”
Now when both the captain and commander of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were thoroughly perplexed, wondering as to what this could mean.
Then someone came and reported to them, “Look, the men whom you put in prison are standing in the temple courts, teaching and instructing the people!”
Then the captain and commander with the officers departed and brought them back, not with force or violence, for they were afraid of the people, lest they be pelted with stones.
When they had brought them in, they made them stand before the Sanhedrin council. And the high priest questioned them,

saying, “We strictly ordered you not to teach and instruct in this name, yet see, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you are determined to bring the blood and guilt of this man upon us.”
But in reply, Peter and the apostles said, “It is necessary to obey and submit to God rather than men.
The God of our fathers raised Jesus from death, whom you killed by hanging Him upon a tree.
This One—God lifted up to His right hand as Prince and Savior, to grant repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
And we are testifiers of these events, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to the ones who obey and submit to Him.”
When the members of the council heard this declaration, they were enraged and wanted to execute the apostles.
However, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a respected teacher of the Law who was highly esteemed by all the people, stood up in the council. He directed that the apostles be taken outside temporarily.
Then he addressed the council: “Fellow Israelites, consider carefully what you intend to do to these men.
Not long ago, a man named Theudas appeared, claiming to be someone important. About four hundred men rallied to his cause. He was killed, and all his followers were scattered and came to nothing.
After him, Judas the Galilean appeared during the time of the census and led a rebellion, drawing people after him. He also died, and all his followers were dispersed.
Therefore, I advise you to leave these men alone and let them go. If their purpose or activity is merely human in origin, it will fail and disappear.
But if it comes from God, you will not be able to stop these men. You might even find yourselves fighting against God Himself!” The council was persuaded by his reasoning.
They called the apostles back in and had them flogged. They commanded them never again to speak in the name of Jesus, and then released them.
The apostles left the council chamber rejoicing because they had been considered worthy to suffer disgrace for the sake of the Name.
Day after day, in the temple courts and in private homes, they never stopped teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.

verses.heading: The Choosing of the Seven Deacons / The Choosing of the Seven Deacons
verses.text: As the community of disciples grew larger during this period, a complaint arose from the Greek-speaking Jewish believers against those who spoke Hebrew, because the Greek-speaking widows were being passed over when food was distributed each day.

The twelve called together the full community of disciples and addressed them: “Abandoning our calling to proclaim God’s message in order to supervise food distribution would not be appropriate for us.
Brothers and sisters, identify seven men from your own group who have solid reputations and are fully characterized by the Spirit and sound judgment. We will assign this duty to them.
But we will devote ourselves fully and without distraction to prayer and to the ministry of the word.

Everyone in the assembly approved of this plan. They selected Stephen, a man fully marked by faith and the Holy Spirit’s presence and power, along with Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch who had converted to Judaism.
These seven were brought to stand before the apostles, who prayed and placed their hands on them in commissioning.
God’s message continued expanding its reach. In Jerusalem, the disciple community grew substantially in size, and a considerable number of priests yielded to the faith.

verses.heading: The Persecution of Stephen / The Persecution of Stephen
verses.text: Stephen, who was filled with divine grace and supernatural power, began doing extraordinary miracles and powerful signs before the people.

Opposition emerged, however, from people who belonged to the synagogue community known as the Freedmen—this included Jewish people from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and the province of Asia. They initiated arguments with Stephen.
Yet they found themselves unable to counter the wisdom and the Spirit that characterized his speech.
Then they covertly persuaded some men to make accusations: “We heard him utter blasphemous statements about Moses and about God.”
They agitated the common people, the council of elders, and the religious scholars. Then they seized Stephen forcibly and hauled him before the Sanhedrin.
They arranged for false witnesses who declared, “This individual never stops making statements against the holy temple and against the Law.
We have heard him assert that this Jesus from Nazareth will tear down the temple and change the traditions Moses gave us.”
Everyone seated in the Sanhedrin council focused their attention on Stephen, and they observed that his face had taken on the appearance of an angel’s face.

verses.heading: Stephen’s Apologia / Stephen’s Apologia
verses.text: The high priest posed the question: “Are these charges true?”

Stephen gave this response: “Brothers and fathers, give me your attention. The God who possesses all glory appeared before our ancestor Abraham while he still resided in Mesopotamia, before he had moved to Haran.
God instructed him: ‘Leave behind your homeland and your kinfolk, and journey to the territory I will reveal to you.’
So Abraham departed from Chaldean territory and established residence in Haran. After his father’s death, God brought him to resettle in this very land where you now live.

Yet God provided him with no property rights here—not even enough ground to place one foot. Still, God gave a promise that He would grant this land as a possession to Abraham and his offspring, even though Abraham was childless at that time.
God communicated this to him: ‘Your offspring will live as aliens in a foreign territory. The inhabitants will enslave them and treat them harshly for a period of four hundred years.
However, I will execute judgment against the nation that enslaves them,’ God announced, ‘and afterward they will leave that place and give Me worship in this location.’*

God then established the covenant marked by circumcision with Abraham. This led Abraham to father Isaac, whom he circumcised eight days after birth. Isaac in turn fathered Jacob, and Jacob became father to the twelve tribal ancestors.
The tribal ancestors became jealous of Joseph and sold him into slavery in Egypt. But God’s presence remained with him.

God delivered Joseph from every hardship he faced. God granted Joseph wisdom and brought him into Pharaoh’s favor—Pharaoh being Egypt’s king—so that Pharaoh appointed him as governor over Egypt and over his entire royal household.
Then severe famine struck throughout Egypt and Canaan, creating enormous suffering, and our ancestors could locate no food supplies.
When Jacob received word that grain supplies existed in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there for their initial trip.
On the second trip, Joseph made his identity known to his brothers, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph’s family background.
Joseph then sent word for his father Jacob to come, along with all his extended family—seventy-five people altogether.
So Jacob traveled down to Egypt. Both he and our ancestors eventually died there.
Their remains were transported back to Shechem, where they were laid to rest in the burial site that Abraham had purchased with silver payment from Hamor’s descendants in Shechem.
As the time approached for God to fulfill what He had promised Abraham, our people multiplied and became numerous in Egypt.
Eventually a different king rose to power in Egypt who had no connection to Joseph’s legacy.
This king dealt deceptively with our people and brutalized our ancestors, forcing them to expose their newborn babies so the infants would perish.
Moses was born during this period. He was extraordinarily beautiful in God’s eyes. For three months he received care in his father’s home.
When he was set outside, Pharaoh’s daughter rescued him and raised him as though he were her own child.
Moses received comprehensive education in Egyptian wisdom and developed great capability in both speaking and acting.
When Moses had reached forty years of age, it occurred to him to visit his relatives, the Israelite people.
When he witnessed one of them suffering abuse from an Egyptian, he intervened to protect him, avenging the mistreated man by killing the Egyptian.
Moses anticipated that his fellow Israelites would recognize that God was bringing them deliverance through him, but they failed to grasp this.
The next day Moses encountered two Israelites engaged in a fight. He attempted to bring them to peaceful resolution, saying, ‘Men, you share kinship; why are you inflicting harm on each other?’
But the one acting as the aggressor shoved Moses aside, demanding, ‘Who designated you as our authority and judge?
Are you planning to murder me just as you murdered the Egyptian yesterday?’
This confrontation caused Moses to flee. He became a refugee in Midian’s territory, where he fathered two sons.
Forty years later, in the wilderness region near Mount Sinai, an angel manifested to Moses within the flames of a bush that was burning.
Moses was astounded when he saw this. As he moved closer to examine it, the Lord’s voice came to him:
‘I am the God of your ancestors—Abraham’s God, Isaac’s God, and Jacob’s God.’ Moses began trembling and was too frightened to continue looking.
Then the Lord directed him: ‘Remove your sandals from your feet, because the ground where you are standing has been made holy.
I have definitely observed the suffering of My people in Egypt. I have heard the sounds of their anguish and have come down to liberate them. Now then, I am commissioning you to return to Egypt.’

This Moses—the very one they had rejected by challenging ‘Who made you our authority and judge?’—this man God sent as both leader and liberator through the angel who had manifested to him in the bush.
This man guided them out of Egypt while performing miraculous wonders and signs in Egyptian territory, at the Red Sea, and throughout the wilderness over a forty-year period.
This Moses is the one who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up a prophet for you from among your own people, someone like me.’

This is the man who stood with the assembled people in the wilderness, accompanied by the angel who addressed him on Mount Sinai and by our ancestors. He received living divine utterances to transmit to us.
Yet our ancestors refused to submit to his leadership. They rejected him and in their deepest desires turned back toward Egypt.
They told Aaron, ‘Fashion gods for us who will lead our way. This Moses who brought us out from Egypt—we have no idea what has become of him.’
During that time they constructed an idol shaped like a calf. They presented offerings to this idol and celebrated what their own hands had manufactured.

So God turned away from them and handed them over to worship the celestial bodies, exactly as the prophetic writings state: ‘Did you present sacrificial animals and offerings to Me during the forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
Instead you carried the shrine of Moloch and the star representing your god Rephan, the idols you fashioned for worship. Therefore I will deport you beyond Babylon’s borders.’*
Our ancestors possessed the tent of testimony while in the wilderness. It had been constructed according to the pattern God had shown Moses, exactly as God had directed him.

Our ancestors received this tent and brought it with them under Joshua’s leadership when they took possession of the territories of the nations God expelled ahead of them. It remained in use through David’s lifetime.
David found favor in God’s sight and requested permission to establish a permanent dwelling for Jacob’s God.
Solomon, however, was the one who actually constructed a house for Him.
Yet the Most High does not inhabit buildings constructed by human effort, just as the prophet declares:
‘Heaven functions as My throne, while the earth serves as My footstool. What sort of house could you possibly build for Me, the Lord asks, or what location could serve as My resting place?
Did My own hand not create all these things?’*
You obstinate people, with hearts and ears that remain uncircumcised! You continuously oppose the Holy Spirit, exactly as your ancestors did.
Name a single prophet your ancestors did not persecute. They murdered those who predicted the arrival of the Righteous One. Now you have become His betrayers and murderers—
you who received the Law transmitted through angelic mediation, yet you have not observed it.”
When the council members heard these words, they became furious deep within and gnashed their teeth at him in rage.
But Stephen, filled completely with the Holy Spirit, fixed his gaze upward toward heaven and saw God’s glory, with Jesus standing at God’s right hand.
He declared, “I am looking at the heavens opened up, and I see the Son of Man standing at God’s right hand.”
They let out loud shouts, pressed their hands over their ears, and charged at him as one group.
After dragging him outside the city limits, they began pelting him with stones. The witnesses who testified against him laid their outer garments at the feet of a young man called Saul.
As the stones struck Stephen, he called out in prayer, “Lord Jesus, accept my spirit into Your care.”

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Then he collapsed to his knees and shouted loudly, “Lord, do not charge them with this sin.” After speaking these words, he fell asleep. 6-7 Quoted from Gen. 15:13-14 42-43 Quoted from Amos 5:25-27 49-50 Quoted from Is. 66:1-2

verses.heading: The Persecution of the Jerusalem Church / The Persecution of the Jerusalem Church
verses.text: Saul gave his consent to Stephen’s execution. A massive persecution campaign against the Jerusalem church erupted on that very day. All the believers scattered throughout the Judean and Samaritan regions, though the apostles stayed in the city.
Pious men carried Stephen to his burial and expressed profound grief over him.
Saul, meanwhile, was systematically devastating the church. He invaded one household after another, hauling away both men and women believers and having them imprisoned.

verses.heading: Philip’s Evangelistic Preaching in Samaria / Philip’s Evangelistic Preaching in Samaria
verses.text: Those who had been forced to flee traveled from place to place announcing the message.
Philip traveled to a Samaritan city and began declaring the Messiah to the inhabitants.
The crowds paid unified attention to Philip’s teaching as they listened to his words and observed the miraculous signs he was demonstrating.
Unclean spirits shrieked loudly as they came out of many people who had been possessed. Numerous individuals who were paralyzed or unable to walk received complete healing.
This created enormous celebration throughout that city.
A man named Simon had been operating in the city previously, practicing sorcery and astonishing the Samaritan population. He portrayed himself as someone of great importance.
Everyone in the city, from the socially insignificant to the prominent, paid him close attention. They said, “This individual embodies what is called the Great Power of God.”
They followed him because his sorcery had amazed them over an extended time period.
But when they came to believe Philip’s proclamation of the good news regarding God’s kingdom and the authority of Jesus the Messiah, both men and women received baptism.

Simon himself also became a believer. After his baptism, he attached himself to Philip as a constant companion. When he witnessed the signs and extraordinary miracles occurring, he was utterly astonished.

verses.heading: The Apostolic Delegates to Samaria / The Apostolic Delegates to Samaria
verses.text: When the apostles in Jerusalem received reports that Samaria had embraced God’s message, they sent Peter and John to go there.
When these two arrived, they prayed that the new believers would receive the Holy Spirit.
The Spirit had not yet come upon any of them—they had simply undergone baptism into the Lord Jesus’ name.
So Peter and John began placing their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon observed that the Spirit was transmitted through the apostles placing their hands on people, he brought them money.
He said, “Transfer this capability to me as well, so that whoever I place my hands on receives the Holy Spirit.”
Peter responded to him, “May your money go to destruction right along with you, since you imagined you could purchase God’s gift with money!
You possess no share or stake in this work, because your heart lacks integrity before God.
Turn away in repentance from this wickedness, and plead with the Lord that perhaps this intention in your heart might be pardoned.
I perceive that you are trapped in bitter envy and imprisoned by wrongdoing.”
Simon responded, “Please make your own petition to the Lord on my behalf, so that nothing you have spoken about comes upon me.”
After giving their testimony and delivering the Lord’s message, Peter and John returned toward Jerusalem, proclaiming the good news in numerous Samaritan villages along their route.

verses.heading: Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch / Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch
verses.text: An angel of the Lord addressed Philip with these instructions: “Get yourself ready and travel southward on the road that descends from Jerusalem to Gaza”—this route passed through wilderness.

Philip prepared himself and went. He encountered an Ethiopian man, a eunuch who held a position of authority under Candace, Ethiopia’s queen—he supervised her entire treasury. This official had journeyed to Jerusalem for worship
and was now returning home. As he rode in his chariot, he was reading aloud from the prophet Isaiah.
The Spirit directed Philip: “Approach that chariot and stay close to it.”
Philip ran up alongside and heard the man reading from the prophet Isaiah. Philip asked, “Do you comprehend what you are reading?”
The official answered, “How could I possibly understand without someone to guide me through it?” He urged Philip to climb up and take a seat beside him.
The specific Scripture passage he was reading was this: “Like a sheep being led to slaughter, and like a lamb that makes no sound before those who shear it, He does not open His mouth.
In His degradation, justice was withheld from Him. Who can describe His descendants? Because His life is removed from the earth.”*
The eunuch asked Philip, “I want to know—who is the prophet describing here? Is he speaking about himself or about someone else?”
Philip seized this opening. Beginning with that exact Scripture text, he explained the good news about Jesus to him.
As they continued traveling along the road, they arrived at a place where water was present. The eunuch said, “Look—water is here! What would prevent me from being baptized?”*
He ordered the chariot stopped. Both Philip and the eunuch descended into the water, and Philip baptized him.
When they emerged from the water, the Lord’s Spirit suddenly transported Philip away. The eunuch never saw him again, but he continued his journey filled with joy.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Philip, however, appeared at Azotus. He traveled through that entire region, proclaiming the good news in every town, until he finally reached Caesarea. 32-33 Quoted from Is. 53:7-8 36 Textual criticism indicates that Acts 8:37, which reads: And Philip said, “ If you believe with all your heart, it is possible” is a later interpolation, as it is missing from the earliest Greek codices. The verse, containing a confessional dialogue between Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch, is therefore not considered part of the original text.
verses.html:
Philip, however, appeared at Azotus. He traveled through that entire region, proclaiming the good news in every town, until he finally reached Caesarea. 32-33 Quoted from Is. 53:7-8
36 Textual criticism indicates that Acts 8:37, which reads: And Philip said, “ If you believe with all your heart, it is possible” is a later interpolation, as it is missing from the earliest Greek codices. The verse, containing a confessional dialogue between Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch, is therefore not considered part of the original text.

verses.heading: The Dramatic Conversion of Paul / The Dramatic Conversion of Paul
verses.text: Meanwhile, Saul was still exhaling violent threats and deadly intentions toward the Lord’s disciples. He approached the high priest
and asked him to write authorization letters to the Damascus synagogues. This would permit him to find any adherents to the Way—both male and female—and transport them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
As he traveled and was nearing Damascus, a brilliant light from heaven suddenly blazed around him.
He collapsed to the ground and heard a voice addressing him: “Saul, Saul, why are you pursuing Me with persecution?”
He responded, “Who are You, Lord?” The voice said, “I am Jesus, the One you are persecuting.
But get up now and proceed into the city, where you will receive instructions about what you must do.”
The men traveling as his companions stood there unable to speak. They heard the sound of the voice but could see no one.
Saul lifted himself from the ground, but when he opened his eyes, he could perceive nothing. They had to take his hand and lead him into Damascus.
For three days he remained sightless, consuming neither food nor drink.
A disciple named Ananias lived in Damascus. The Lord spoke to him through a vision: “Ananias.”He answered, “I am here, Lord.”
The Lord gave him these instructions: “Get up and go to Straight Street. At Judas’ house, inquire for a man from Tarsus named Saul. At this very moment he is praying,
and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias entering and placing hands on him so his sight will be restored.”
Ananias objected: “Lord, I have heard numerous accounts about this individual—all the harm he has inflicted on Your holy people in Jerusalem.
And he has arrived here with authorization from the chief priests to arrest everyone who calls upon Your name.”
But the Lord told him, "Go, because I have selected this man as My instrument. He will carry My name before Gentile peoples, before kings, and before the people of Israel.
I will reveal to him how extensively he must suffer for My name’s sake.”

So Ananias went and entered the house. He placed his hands on Saul and said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus—the one who appeared to you on the road you were traveling—has sent me so that you may recover your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
Immediately, something resembling scales dropped away from his eyes, and his sight returned. He got up and was baptized.

verses.heading: The Beginning of Paul’s Preaching of Jesus / The Beginning of Paul’s Preaching of Jesus
verses.text: After eating some food, his physical strength came back. Saul remained with the Damascus disciples for several days.
Without delay, he began announcing in the synagogues that Jesus is God’s Son.

Everyone who heard him was shocked. They said, “Is not this the man who devastated the Jerusalem believers who call on this name? Has he not come here specifically to arrest them and bring them to the chief priests?”
Yet Saul’s strength kept increasing. He was confounding the Jews residing in Damascus by demonstrating proof that Jesus is the Christ.

verses.heading: The Miraculous Escape of Paul / The Miraculous Escape of Paul
verses.text: After a considerable period had elapsed, the Jews conspired together with plans to kill him.
However, Saul learned of their plot. They were monitoring the city gates continuously, day and night, intending to murder him.
But his disciples took action during the night. They lowered him down through an opening in the city wall, using a large basket.

verses.heading: Paul in Jerusalem / Paul in Jerusalem
verses.text: Upon arriving in Jerusalem, Saul made attempts to associate with the disciples. But they were all frightened of him, unable to believe he was genuinely a disciple.

Barnabas, however, took responsibility for him. He brought Saul to the apostles and gave them a full account of how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, how the Lord had communicated with him, and how boldly Saul had proclaimed in Damascus using Jesus’ name.
So Saul remained with them in Jerusalem, moving about freely and speaking with boldness in the Lord’s name.
He engaged in conversations and debates with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they made attempts to assassinate him.
When the believers discovered this, they escorted him down to Caesarea and sent him away to Tarsus.

The church throughout the entirety of Judea, Galilee, and Samaria then experienced a period of peace. It was being strengthened and expanded in numbers as the believers conducted themselves in reverence toward the Lord and received encouragement from the Holy Spirit.

verses.heading: The Healing of Aeneas / The Healing of Aeneas
verses.text: As Peter was making a circuit through all the regions, he came down to visit the believers living in Lydda.
There he discovered a man named Aeneas who had been confined to a sleeping mat for eight years due to paralysis.
Peter addressed him: “Aeneas, Jesus the Messiah is healing you. Stand up and arrange your own mat.” He immediately stood up.
All the inhabitants of Lydda and the Sharon plain saw him, and they turned to the Lord in faith.

verses.heading: Dorcas Restored to Life / Dorcas Restored to Life
verses.text: In Joppa there lived a female disciple named Tabitha—in Greek her name was Dorcas. She devoted herself constantly to good deeds and charitable acts.
During that time period, she fell ill and died. After washing her body, they placed her in an upstairs room.
Since Lydda was located near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was in the area. They sent two men to him with this urgent appeal: “Please come to us immediately without delay.”

Peter went with them. When he arrived, they brought him upstairs to the room. All the widows gathered around him, weeping and displaying the tunics and other garments that Dorcas had sewn while she was still with them.
Peter directed everyone to leave the room. Then he knelt down and prayed. Turning toward the body, he said, “Tabitha, stand up.” She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat upright.
He extended his hand to her and helped her to her feet. Then he summoned the believers and the widows and presented her to them alive.
Reports of this spread throughout all of Joppa, and many people placed their faith in the Lord.
Peter remained in Joppa for a substantial period, staying as a guest with a man named Simon who worked as a leather tanner.

verses.heading: The Man Cornelius / The Man Cornelius
verses.text: A man named Cornelius lived in Caesarea. He held the rank of centurion in what was designated the Italian Regiment.
He was devout and feared God along with everyone in his household. He contributed generously to help people in need and prayed to God consistently.
About the ninth hour or around three o’clock in the afternoon, he had a clear vision in which he saw an angel of God approaching him. The angel said, “Cornelius.”
Cornelius stared at the angel in fear and asked, “What is it, Lord?” The angel responded, “Your prayers and your charitable gifts have ascended as a memorial before God.
Now send men to Joppa and summon a man named Simon, who is also called Peter.
He is lodging with Simon the leather tanner, whose house is located beside the sea.”
After the angel who had been speaking to him departed, Cornelius summoned two of his household servants and a devout soldier from among those who served him regularly.
He explained the entire situation to them and sent them to Joppa.

verses.heading: Peter’s Trance / Peter’s Trance
verses.text: The next day, while they were traveling and approaching the city, Peter went up onto the roof to pray. This was around noon.
He became hungry and wanted to eat. While the meal was being prepared, he entered a trance state.
He observed heaven opened and something resembling a large sheet descending, being lowered to earth by its four corners.
Inside it were all varieties of four-footed animals, reptiles that crawl on the ground, and birds that fly in the sky.
A voice addressed him: “Get up, Peter. Slaughter these and eat.”
But Peter said, “Absolutely not, Lord! I have never consumed anything defiled or unclean.”
The voice addressed him a second time: “What God has declared clean, you must not call defiled.”
This occurred three times, and then the object was immediately taken back up into heaven.

While Peter was still puzzling over what the vision he had experienced might mean, the men Cornelius had sent arrived. After making inquiries, they located Simon’s house and were standing at the gateway.
They called out, asking whether Simon called Peter was staying there as a guest.
While Peter was still contemplating the vision, the Spirit told him, “Listen—three men are searching for you.
Get up, go downstairs, and accompany them without any hesitation, because I have sent them.”
Peter went down to the men and announced, “I am the person you are looking for. What is the purpose of your visit?”

They replied, “Cornelius, a centurion—a righteous man who fears God and has an excellent reputation throughout the Jewish nation—received instructions from a holy angel to send for you to come to his house. He wants to hear what you have to say.”
So Peter invited them inside to be his guests. The following day Peter set out with them, and some of the believers from Joppa accompanied him.
The day after that, they arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was anticipating their arrival and had assembled his relatives and close friends.
As Peter was entering, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet, and began worshipping him.
But Peter pulled him up, saying, “Stand up. I myself am merely a human being.”
While conversing with him, Peter went inside and found a large gathering of people assembled.

He addressed them: “You are well aware that it violates Jewish law for a Jewish person to associate with or visit someone from another nation. Yet God has shown me that I should not designate any person as defiled or unclean.
This is why I came without raising objections when I was summoned. So now I ask: For what reason did you send for me?”
Cornelius explained, "Four days ago, at this exact hour—three in the afternoon—I was praying in my house. Suddenly a man dressed in brilliant clothing stood in front of me.
He said, ‘Cornelius, God has heard your prayer and has taken notice of your charitable deeds.
Therefore, send someone to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter. He is staying as a guest in the house of Simon the leather tanner, beside the sea.’
So I sent for you right away, and you have been gracious in coming. Now all of us are assembled here in God’s presence to hear everything the Lord has instructed you to communicate to us.”

verses.heading: The Gospel Preached to the Gentiles / The Gospel Preached to the Gentiles
verses.text: Then Peter began speaking: “I now genuinely comprehend that God shows no favoritism based on nationality.
Rather, in every nation, anyone who fears Him and practices righteousness is acceptable to Him.
This is the message He sent to the people of Israel, announcing the good news of peace through Jesus the Messiah, who is Lord over all.
You are aware of the events that occurred throughout all of Judea, starting in Galilee after the baptism that John proclaimed—

how God anointed Jesus from Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power. He traveled throughout the region doing good and healing everyone who was under the devil’s oppression, because God's presence was with Him.
We serve as witnesses to everything He accomplished both in the Jewish countryside and in Jerusalem. They executed Him by hanging Him on a wooden cross,
but God raised Him to life on the third day and permitted Him to appear visibly—
not to all the people, but to witnesses God had selected in advance, specifically to us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
He commanded us to proclaim to the people and to give testimony that He is the one God has appointed to judge those who are living and those who have died.
All the prophets give testimony about Him, declaring that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”

verses.heading: The Outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Gentiles / The Outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Gentiles
verses.text: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came upon everyone who was listening to the message.
The Jewish believers who had accompanied Peter were astounded that the Holy Spirit’s gift had been poured out even on Gentiles.
For they heard them speaking in other languages and magnifying God. Then Peter declared,
“Can anyone possibly withhold water and prevent these people from being baptized? They have received the Holy Spirit exactly as we did.”
So he gave orders for them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Afterward they requested that Peter stay with them for several days.

verses.heading: Peter’s Explanation to the Jerusalem Church / Peter’s Explanation to the Jerusalem Church
verses.text: The apostles and the believers throughout Judea received word that Gentiles had also embraced God’s message.
So when Peter traveled up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers confronted him critically,
charging, “You entered the homes of uncircumcised men and ate meals with them.”
Peter began explaining the situation to them systematically:

“I was in the city of Joppa praying when I fell into a trance. I saw a vision—something resembling a large sheet descending, being lowered from heaven by its four corners. It came right down to where I was.
As I examined it closely, I observed four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the sky.
Then I heard a voice instructing me, ‘Get up, Peter. Slaughter and eat.’
I responded, ‘Absolutely not, Lord! Nothing defiled or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
But the voice from heaven responded a second time: ‘What God has declared clean, you must not call defiled.’
This happened three times, and then everything was pulled back up into heaven.
At that precise moment, three men arrived at the house where I was staying. They had been sent to me from Caesarea.
The Spirit instructed me to accompany them without making any distinction. These six brothers also traveled with me, and we entered the man’s house.
He related to us how he had seen an angel standing in his house who said, ‘Send messengers to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter.
He will deliver a message to you through which you and your entire household will be rescued.’
As I began speaking, the Holy Spirit came upon them exactly as He had come upon us at the beginning.
I remembered the Lord’s declaration: ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
So if God granted them the identical gift He gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus the Christ, who was I to think I could obstruct God?”
When they heard this explanation, they stopped their objections. They praised God, saying, “This means God has granted repentance leading to life even to the Gentiles.”

verses.heading: The Church in Antioch / The Church in Antioch
verses.text: Now those who had been scattered due to the persecution that developed over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They proclaimed the message exclusively to Jewish people.
However, some of them—men from Cyprus and Cyrene—arrived in Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, announcing the good news about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord’s power accompanied them, and a large number believed and turned to the Lord.
Reports about this reached the church in Jerusalem, so they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When he arrived and witnessed the evidence of God’s grace, he was filled with joy. He urged them all to remain committed to the Lord with wholehearted resolve,
because he was a good man, filled with the Holy Spirit and with faith. A substantial number of people were added to the Lord.
Then Barnabas traveled to Tarsus to search for Saul.

When he located him, he brought him to Antioch. For an entire year they gathered with the church and taught considerable numbers of people. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first designated as Christians.
During that time period, prophets traveled down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

One of them, named Agabus, stood up and indicated through the Spirit that a severe famine was going to spread across the entire inhabited world. This actually occurred during Claudius’ reign as emperor.
The disciples determined to send relief assistance to the believers living in Judea, with each person contributing according to his ability.
They carried this out, sending their contribution to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.

verses.heading: The Death of James and the Imprisonment of Peter / The Death of James and the Imprisonment of Peter
verses.text: Around that time, King Herod took aggressive action against some members of the church.
He had James, John’s brother, executed by sword.
When he observed that this pleased the Jewish leaders, he proceeded to arrest Peter as well. This occurred during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
After capturing him, Herod placed him in prison under the guard of four squads of four soldiers each. His intention was to bring him before the people for trial after Passover concluded.
So Peter was kept under guard in the prison, while the church was making fervent prayer to God on his behalf.

verses.heading: Peter’s Miraculous Escape / Peter’s Miraculous Escape
verses.text: On the night before Herod planned to bring him out for trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, secured with two chains. Guards were stationed at the entrance, keeping watch over the prison.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, and light flooded the cell. The angel prodded Peter in the side, waking him, and said, “Get up quickly!” The chains fell away from his wrists.
The angel instructed him, “Fasten your belt and put your sandals on.” Peter did so. Then the angel said, “Put your cloak around you and follow me.”
Peter went out following the angel. He did not realize that what was happening through the angel was actual reality—he assumed he was experiencing a vision.

They passed through the first guard post, then the second, and came to the iron gate that opened into the city. It swung open for them automatically. They went through it and proceeded down one street, and then abruptly the angel departed from him.

When Peter came to full awareness of his situation, he said, “Now I know for certain that the Lord sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”
After realizing this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark. Many people had assembled there and were praying.
When Peter knocked at the outer gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to respond.
When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed that instead of opening the gate, she ran back inside and announced that Peter was standing at the gate.
They told her, “You have lost your mind.” But she kept insisting it was true. Then they said, “It must be his angel.”
Meanwhile Peter continued knocking. When they finally opened the gate and saw him, they were utterly astonished.

Peter gestured with his hand for them to be quiet, then described how the Lord had led him out of the prison. He said, “Report this to James and to the other brothers and sisters.” Then he departed and went to a different location.
When morning arrived, there was considerable commotion among the soldiers regarding what had become of Peter.
Herod conducted a thorough search for him and, failing to find him, interrogated the guards and ordered their execution. Then Herod traveled from Judea down to Caesarea, where he remained.

verses.heading: The Judgment of Herod / The Judgment of Herod
verses.text: Herod had been harboring intense anger toward the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came to him in a unified delegation. After securing the support of Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they requested peace terms, because their territories depended on the king’s region for food supplies.
On an appointed day, Herod dressed himself in royal robes, took his seat on the throne, and delivered a formal address to them.
The assembled crowd began shouting, “This is a god’s voice, not a human being’s!”
Immediately, because Herod failed to give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down. He was consumed by worms and died.
But God’s message continued to expand and multiply.
Barnabas and Saul completed their mission and returned from Jerusalem, bringing John, who was called Mark, with them.

verses.heading: The Beginning of the Global Spread of the Gospel / The Beginning of the Global Spread of the Gospel
verses.text: In the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen who had been raised with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
While they were engaging in worship before the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart Barnabas and Saul for Me, for the work to which I have summoned them.”
After they had fasted and prayed, they placed their hands on them and released them for service.
So, sent out by the Holy Spirit, they traveled down to Seleucia and from there sailed to Cyprus.
Upon arriving in Salamis, they began proclaiming God’s message in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them serving as their assistant.
They traveled across the entire island until they reached Paphos. There they encountered a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,
who was associated with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear God’s message.
But Elymas the sorcerer—for that is the meaning of his name—opposed them, attempting to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
Then Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fixed his gaze directly on Elymas

and declared, “You are saturated with every form of deceit and villainy, you offspring of the devil, you enemy of all that is right! Will you never stop twisting the Lord's straight paths into crooked ones?

Look—the Lord’s hand is against you now. You will be blind, unable to see the sun for a period of time.” Immediately mist and darkness enveloped him, and he groped around, searching for someone to lead him by the hand.
When the proconsul witnessed what had occurred, he became a believer, deeply impressed by the teaching about the Lord.

verses.heading: Paul’s Preaching at Pisidian Antioch / Paul’s Preaching at Pisidian Antioch
verses.text: Paul and his companions set sail from Paphos and arrived at Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them there and returned to Jerusalem.
They continued on from Perga and reached Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath day they entered the synagogue and sat down.
After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent them a message: “Brothers, if you have any word of encouragement for the people, please speak.”
Paul stood up, gestured with his hand for attention, and said: “Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen to me.
The God of this people Israel chose our ancestors and caused the people to flourish during their residence in Egypt. With uplifted arm He brought them out from that land.
For approximately forty years He endured their conduct in the wilderness.
After destroying seven nations in the land of Canaan, He distributed their territory to His people as an inheritance.
All this took approximately four hundred and fifty years. Following these events, He provided judges until the era of Samuel the prophet.
Then they requested a king, and God gave them Saul, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled for forty years.
After removing Saul, God raised up David as their king. God gave testimony about him: 'I have discovered David, Jesse’s son, a man aligned with My own heart, who will accomplish everything I desire.’
From this man’s lineage, in accordance with His promise, God has brought to Israel a Savior—Jesus.
Before Jesus began His public ministry, John had proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
As John was completing his mission, he said, ‘Who do you imagine I am? I am not the one you are expecting. But listen—someone is coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.’
Brothers—children of Abraham’s line, and those among you who fear God—this message of salvation has been sent specifically to us.
For the residents of Jerusalem and their leaders failed to recognize Jesus or comprehend the prophetic messages read every Sabbath. By condemning Him, they actually fulfilled those very prophecies.
Though they discovered no legitimate grounds for a death sentence, they requested Pilate to have Him executed.
When they had accomplished everything written about Him in the Scriptures, they took Him down from the cross and laid Him in a tomb.
But God raised Him from the dead.
For many days He appeared to those who had traveled with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They now serve as His witnesses to the people.
We are announcing the good news to you: What God promised to our ancestors,
He has fulfilled for us, their descendants, by raising Jesus to life. As it is written in the second Psalm: ‘You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.’*
Regarding the fact that God raised Him from the dead, never to experience decay again, He has spoken in this way: ‘I will grant you the holy and reliable blessings promised to David.’*
This is why He also states in another place: ‘You will not permit Your Holy One to experience decay.’*
Now David, after serving God’s purpose in his own generation, died and was laid with his ancestors, and his body did experience decay.
But the One whom God raised did not experience decay.
Therefore, my brothers, I want you to understand this: through this man forgiveness of sins is being proclaimed to you.
Through Him, everyone who believes receives justification from everything from which you could not be justified through the Law of Moses.
Be careful, then, that what the prophets spoke does not happen to you:
‘Look, you mockers, be astounded and perish, because I am performing a work in your days, a work you would never believe even if someone described it to you in detail.’ ”*
As Paul and Barnabas were leaving, the people urged them to speak about these matters again on the following Sabbath.
After the synagogue gathering dispersed, many Jews and devout converts followed Paul and Barnabas, who engaged them in conversation and urged them to continue in God’s grace.
On the next Sabbath, nearly the entire city assembled to hear the Lord’s message.
But when the Jewish leaders saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy. They began contradicting what Paul was saying and hurling insults at him.

Paul and Barnabas responded boldly: “It was necessary for God's message to be spoken to you first. Since you are rejecting it and judging yourselves unworthy of eternal life, we are now turning to the Gentiles.
For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have appointed you as a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’ ”*
When the Gentiles heard this, they began rejoicing and glorifying the Lord’s message. All who had been appointed for eternal life became believers.
The Lord’s message spread throughout the entire region.
But the Jewish leaders incited the prominent God-fearing women and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their territory.
So they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and traveled to Iconium.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: The disciples, meanwhile, were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit. 33 Quoted from Ps. 2:8 34 Quoted from Is. 55:3 35 Quoted from Ps. 16:10 41 Quoted from Hab. 1:5 47 Quoted from Is. 49:6

verses.heading: In Iconium / In Iconium
verses.text: In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas followed their customary practice of entering the Jewish synagogue. They presented their message so compellingly that a substantial number of both Jews and Greeks became believers.
However, the Jews who refused to believe agitated the Gentile population, poisoning their attitudes toward the believers.

Despite this opposition, Paul and Barnabas remained there for an extended period, speaking with confidence about the Lord. The Lord validated their message about His grace by empowering them to perform miraculous signs and wonders.
The city’s population became divided: some aligned themselves with the Jewish opposition, while others sided with the apostles.
When a conspiracy developed among both Gentiles and Jews, along with their leaders, to abuse and stone Paul and Barnabas,
they learned of the plot and escaped to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe, as well as the surrounding countryside,
where they continued announcing the good news.

verses.heading: In Lystra and Derbe / In Lystra and Derbe
verses.text: In Lystra, there was a man sitting who had been unable to use his feet from birth—he had never walked.
This man listened as Paul spoke. Paul looked directly at him and perceived that he possessed faith to be healed.
Paul called out in a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” The man leaped up and began walking around.
When the crowds witnessed what Paul had done, they began shouting in the Lycaonian language, “The gods have descended to us in human form!”
They started calling Barnabas “Zeus” and Paul “Hermes,” since Paul was the primary speaker.
The priest of Zeus, whose temple stood just outside the city, brought oxen and garlands to the city gates. He and the crowds intended to offer sacrifices to them.
But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard what was happening, they tore their garments and rushed into the crowd, crying out:

“Men, why are you doing this? We are human beings with the same nature as you! We are bringing you good news, urging you to turn away from these empty things to the living God, who created the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them.
In past generations, He allowed all the nations to follow their own paths.
Yet He never left Himself without witness, for He showed kindness by providing you with rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, satisfying you with food and filling your hearts with gladness.”
Even with these words, they barely restrained the crowds from offering sacrifices to them.
Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and persuaded the crowds to turn against them. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, assuming he was dead.
But when the disciples gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The following day, he and Barnabas departed for Derbe.

verses.heading: The Return to Lystra, Iconium, and Derbe / The Return to Lystra, Iconium, and Derbe
verses.text: After proclaiming the good news in that city and making many disciples, they retraced their steps to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
strengthening the disciples’ resolve and encouraging them to remain faithful. They told them, “We must pass through many difficulties to enter God’s kingdom.”
After Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each congregation, they prayed with fasting and entrusted them to the Lord in whom they had placed their faith.
They traveled through Pisidia and arrived in Pamphylia.
After proclaiming the message in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
From there they sailed back to Antioch, where they had originally been commended to God’s grace for the work they had now finished.
Upon their arrival, they assembled the congregation and gave a full report of everything God had accomplished through them, and how He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
They remained there with the disciples for a considerable time.

verses.heading: The Jerusalem Council / The Jerusalem Council
verses.text: Some men came down from Judea to Antioch and began teaching the believers: “Unless you undergo circumcision according to Moses’ tradition, you cannot be saved.”

This created sharp conflict and intense debate between them and Paul and Barnabas. It was decided that Paul and Barnabas, along with certain other believers, should travel to Jerusalem to consult with the apostles and elders regarding this controversy.
The church provided for their journey. As they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, they described how the Gentiles had turned to God, bringing great joy to all the believers.
When they arrived in Jerusalem, they were received warmly by the church, the apostles, and the elders. They reported everything God had accomplished through them.
But some believers from the Pharisee party stood up and insisted, “It is necessary to circumcise them and command them to observe the Law of Moses.”
The apostles and elders convened to examine this matter.

After extensive discussion, Peter stood up and addressed them: “Brothers, you know that some time ago God made a choice among you that through my mouth the Gentiles would hear the gospel message and believe.
God, who knows the human heart, bore witness to them by giving them the Holy Spirit just as He did to us.
He made no distinction between us and them, purifying their hearts through faith.
Why, then, are you now testing God by placing on the disciples’ necks a burden that neither our ancestors nor we have been able to bear?
On the contrary, we believe we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in the same way they are.”
The entire assembly fell silent and listened as Barnabas and Paul described all the miraculous signs and wonders God had performed among the Gentiles through them.
After they finished speaking, James responded: “Brothers, hear me.
Simeon has explained how God first showed concern for taking from among the Gentiles a people for His name.
The prophets’ words agree with this, as it is written:
‘After these things I will return and rebuild David’s fallen dwelling. I will rebuild its ruins and restore it,
so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, including all the Gentiles who are called by My name, says the Lord, who makes these things
known from ancient times.’*
Therefore, my judgment is that we should not create difficulties for those Gentiles who are turning to God.
Instead, we should write to them to abstain from things contaminated by idols, from sexual immorality, from what has been strangled, and from blood.
For Moses has had those who proclaim him in every city from ancient generations, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”

Then the apostles and elders, together with the entire church, decided to select representatives from among themselves and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, leading men among the believers.
They sent this letter with them: The apostles and elders, your brothers, To the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
We have learned that certain individuals went out from us without our authorization and have disturbed you with their teaching, unsettling your minds.
Therefore, we have unanimously decided to select representatives and send them to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul—
men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
We are therefore sending Judas and Silas, who will convey the same message orally.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no greater burden on you than these essential requirements:
abstain from food offered to idols, from blood, from what has been strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these things, you will do well. Farewell.
So these men were sent off and traveled down to Antioch. They gathered the congregation and delivered the letter.
When the people read it, they rejoiced at the encouragement it brought.
Judas and Silas, being prophets themselves, spoke at length to encourage and strengthen the believers.
After spending some time there, they were sent back peacefully by the believers to those who had commissioned them.*
But Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming the Lord’s message along with many others.
After some time had passed, Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us return and visit the believers in every city where we proclaimed the Lord’s message, to see how they are doing.”
Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark, along with them.
But Paul did not think it wise to take him, since he had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not continued with them in the work.
Their disagreement became so sharp that they separated from each other. Barnabas took Mark and sailed away to Cyprus,
while Paul selected Silas and departed, having been commended by the believers to the Lord’s grace.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the congregations. 16-18 Quoted from Amos 9:11-12 34 Textual evidence indicates that verse 34 is a later interpolation,as it is not found in the earliest manuscripts. The verse reads, “ But it seemed expedient to Silas to remain there.”
verses.html:
He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the congregations. 16-18 Quoted from Amos 9:11-12
34 Textual evidence indicates that verse 34 is a later interpolation,as it is not found in the earliest manuscripts. The verse reads, “ But it seemed expedient to Silas to remain there.”

verses.text: Paul also traveled to Derbe and then to Lystra. A disciple named Timothy was there—his mother was a Jewish believer, but his father was Greek.
The believers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he circumcised him because of the Jews in those areas, since everyone knew his father was Greek.
As they journeyed through the cities, they delivered the decisions that had been reached by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the believers to observe.
So the churches were being strengthened in the faith and increasing in number daily.

verses.heading: The Macedonian Call / The Macedonian Call
verses.text: They traveled through the Phrygian and Galatian region, having been prevented by the Holy Spirit from speaking the message in the province of Asia.
When they approached Mysia, they attempted to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.
So they bypassed Mysia and went down to Troas.
During the night, Paul had a vision: a Macedonian man was standing and pleading with him, “Cross over to Macedonia and help us.”
After Paul had seen the vision, we immediately sought to depart for Macedonia, concluding that God had summoned us to proclaim the good news to them.

verses.heading: The Conversion of Lydia / The Conversion of Lydia
verses.text: Setting sail from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the following day to Neapolis.
From there we went to Philippi, which is a leading city of that district of Macedonia and a Roman colony. We remained in that city for several days.
On the Sabbath day we went outside the city gate to the riverside, where we expected to find a place of prayer. We sat down and began speaking to the women who had assembled.
A woman named Lydia was listening—she was from the city of Thyatira, a dealer in purple fabric, and a worshipper of God. The Lord opened her heart to pay attention to what Paul was saying.
After she and her household were baptized, she extended this invitation: “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” She persuaded us to accept.

verses.heading: The Imprisonment of Paul and Silas / The Imprisonment of Paul and Silas
verses.text: As we were going to the place of prayer one day, we encountered a slave girl who had a spirit of divination. She brought her owners substantial profit through fortune-telling.
She began following Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation.”

She continued doing this for many days. Finally, Paul became so irritated that he turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus the Messiah to come out of her!” It came out at that very moment.
When her owners realized that their hope of profit was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the authorities.
Bringing them before the magistrates, they said, “These men are Jews and are creating chaos in our city
by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to accept or practice.”
The crowd joined in the attack against them, and the magistrates ordered them stripped and beaten with rods.
After inflicting many blows on them, they threw them into prison and commanded the jailer to guard them securely.
Having received such orders, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.

verses.heading: The Conversion of the Jailer and His Entire Household / The Conversion of the Jailer and His Entire Household
verses.text: Around midnight, Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, while the other prisoners listened to them.
Suddenly there was such a violent earthquake that the prison's foundations were shaken. Immediately all the doors flew open, and everyone's chains came loose.
When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors standing open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, thinking the prisoners had escaped.
But Paul shouted loudly, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”
The jailer called for lights and rushed in. Trembling, he fell down before Paul and Silas.
He brought them outside and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved—you and your household.”
They spoke the Lord’s message to him and to everyone in his household.
At that hour of the night, he took them and washed their wounds. Then he and all his family were immediately baptized.
He brought them up into his house and set food before them. He rejoiced greatly, having come to believe in God along with his entire household.
When daylight came, the magistrates sent officers with the message: “Release those men.”
The jailer reported this to Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders for your release. You may now leave and go in peace.”

But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens, and they threw us into prison. Now they want to release us secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come personally and escort us out.”
The officers reported these words to the magistrates. When they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, they became alarmed.
They came and appealed to them, then escorted them out and requested that they leave the city.
After leaving the prison, Paul and Silas went to Lydia’s house. When they had seen the believers and encouraged them, they departed.

verses.heading: Paul in Thessalonica / Paul in Thessalonica
verses.text: After passing through Amphipolis and Apollonia, Paul and his companions arrived in Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
Following his usual practice, Paul went to them and for three Sabbaths engaged with them from the Scriptures,
explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. He declared, “This Jesus whom I am proclaiming to you is the Christ.”
Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few prominent women.

But the Jews became jealous. They recruited some worthless men from the marketplace, formed a mob, and created an uproar in the city. They stormed Jason’s house, searching for Paul and Silas to bring them out to the people.
When they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some other believers before the city authorities, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have come here too,
and Jason has welcomed them as guests! They are all acting contrary to Caesar’s decrees, claiming there is another king—Jesus.”
They stirred up the crowd and the city authorities who heard these things.
After receiving a bond payment from Jason and the others, they released them.

verses.heading: In Berea / In Berea
verses.text: As soon as it was night, the believers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. Upon arriving, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
Now the Berean Jews were more noble-minded than those in Thessalonica. They received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures daily to verify whether these things were true.
As a result, many of them believed, along with a considerable number of prominent Greek women and men.
But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was proclaiming God’s message in Berea as well, they came there too, agitating and stirring up the crowds.
The believers immediately sent Paul away toward the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.
Those escorting Paul brought him as far as Athens. After receiving instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as quickly as possible, they departed.

verses.heading: In Athens / In Athens
verses.text: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he observed that the city was full of idols.
So he began reasoning in the synagogue with the Jews and the God-fearing Greeks, as well as in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.
