For God has unveiled these truths to us through the working of the Holy Spirit. The Spirit searches and examines all things, even the profound depths of God’s own nature.

For who among human beings truly comprehends the inner thoughts and nature of another person except that person’s own spirit dwelling within? In the same way, no one can truly know the thoughts and nature of God except the Spirit of God Himself.

Now we have not received the spirit that characterizes this fallen world system, but rather we have received the Spirit who comes from God, enabling us to understand and appreciate the things that God has graciously given to us.
These are the very things we speak about, not using words taught by human wisdom and philosophy, but using words taught by the Spirit, as we explain spiritual realities through Spirit-given language.

But the person who remains in their natural, unregenerate state does not welcome or accept the things that belong to the Spirit of God, because such things appear as foolishness to them. They lack the capacity to understand these truths because spiritual realities require spiritual discernment.
By contrast, the person who is spiritual assesses all things correctly, yet that spiritual person is not subject to accurate judgment or evaluation by unspiritual or natural people.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: For Scripture asks, “Who has come to know the mind of the Lord? Who could presume to instruct Him?”* Yet we who believe possess the mind of Christ and share His perspective. 9 Quoted from Is. 64:4 16 Quoted from Is. 40:13

verses.heading: Fleshly Divisiveness / Fleshly Divisiveness
verses.text: And I, fellow believers, found myself unable to address you as spiritually mature people, but instead had to speak to you as people still dominated by fleshly desires, as spiritual infants in Christ.
I fed you with milk rather than solid food, because you were not yet capable of digesting mature teaching. In fact, you still are not ready even now.

This is evident because you continue to be controlled by fleshly impulses. For where jealousy and quarreling exist among you, does this not prove that you are still fleshly, and that you are conducting yourselves according to merely human standards?
For when one person claims, “I belong to Paul,” while another says, “I belong to Apollos,” are you not demonstrating that you are operating on a merely human level?
After all, what is Apollos? And what is Paul? We are merely servants through whose ministry you came to faith, and each of us served in the capacity that the Lord assigned.
I planted the initial seed, Apollos provided water and nourishment, but it was God who caused the growth to occur.
Therefore, neither the one who plants nor the one who waters has any intrinsic significance; what matters is God who causes the growth.
Now the one who plants and the one who waters share a common purpose, yet each will receive his own individual reward corresponding to his own labor and effort.
For we are co-laborers working together in God’s service; you are God’s field under cultivation, you are God’s building under construction.

According to the grace of God that was given to me, I laid a foundation like a skilled master builder, and now another person is constructing upon it. But each builder must exercise care regarding how they build upon that foundation.
For no one has the ability to lay any foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
Now if anyone constructs upon that foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,

each person’s work will become evident and exposed. For the day of judgment will reveal it, because it will be disclosed by fire, and the fire itself will test and prove what quality of work each person has produced.
If the work that anyone has built upon the foundation survives the test, that person will receive a reward.
If anyone’s work is burned up and destroyed, that person will suffer loss, though the person themselves will be saved, yet only as one barely escaping through flames.
Do you not understand that you collectively are God’s temple and that the Spirit of God lives within you?
If anyone destroys God’s temple through divisiveness and false teaching, God will destroy that person, for God’s temple is sacred and holy, and you are that temple.

Let no one deceive themselves with false confidence. If anyone among you considers themselves wise according to the standards of this present age, let that person become foolish in the world’s eyes so that they may become truly wise in God’s sight.
For the wisdom that this world values is foolishness in God’s estimation. Scripture confirms this: “He is the One who traps the wise in the schemes of their own cunning.”*
And again Scripture states, “The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are futile and empty.”*
Therefore, let no one boast about human leaders or take pride in allegiance to particular people. For all things ultimately belong to you:
whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas; whether the world or life itself or death; whether things in the present or things yet to come—all of these are yours.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: And you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God. 19 Quoted from Job 5:13 20 Quoted from Ps. 94:11

verses.heading: The Apostles and Their Calling / The Apostles and Their Calling
verses.text: Let a person regard us in the proper light: as servants of Christ and stewards entrusted with managing the mysteries of God.
Furthermore, in this role as stewards, it is essential that a person be found faithful and trustworthy.
But as far as I am concerned, it matters very little to me whether I am examined and evaluated by you or by any human court. Indeed, I do not even evaluate and judge myself.
For although I am not conscious of anything I have done wrong, this does not mean I am thereby vindicated. The One who examines and judges me is the Lord.

Therefore, do not pronounce judgment on anything prematurely, before the appointed time, until the Lord comes. He will bring to light the hidden things concealed in darkness and will expose the motivations and intentions of human hearts. At that time, each person will receive whatever commendation is due from God.

Now, fellow believers, I have applied these principles figuratively to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that through our example you may learn the principle of not going beyond what Scripture teaches, so that none of you will become arrogant and prideful, siding with one leader against another.

For who gives you any basis for thinking you are superior to another believer? And what do you possess that you did not receive as a gift? And if you indeed received it as a gift, why do you boast as though you did not receive it but earned it yourself?

Already you act as though you are completely satisfied. Already you behave as though you have become wealthy. Without our guidance you have begun to reign as kings. And I sincerely wish you truly were reigning, so that we apostles might also reign together with you!

For it seems to me that God has put us apostles on display as last in line, like prisoners condemned to death in the arena, because we have become a spectacle for the whole world to observe, both angels and human beings.

We are regarded as fools for the sake of Christ, but you consider yourselves wise in Christ. We are weak, but you see yourselves as strong. You are held in honor, but we are treated with contempt and dishonor!
Up to this very moment, we experience both hunger and thirst, we wear inadequate clothing, we are beaten and mistreated, and we have no permanent home.
We toil and labor, working with our own hands to support ourselves. When people insult and revile us, we respond with blessing. When we are persecuted, we endure it patiently.
When we are slandered, we respond with gentle encouragement. We have become like the scum and refuse of the world, the garbage that everyone despises, right up to this present moment.

verses.heading: Paul’s Admonition / Paul’s Admonition
verses.text: I am not writing these things to shame you, but rather to admonish you as my beloved children.
For even if you have ten thousand instructors or tutors in Christ, you do not have many spiritual fathers, because through the gospel I became your father in Christ Jesus.
Therefore, I urge you earnestly: Become imitators of me and follow my example.

For this very reason, I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my ways and manner of life in Christ Jesus, which are the same as I teach in every place and in every church.
But some among you have become arrogant, assuming that I am not coming to visit you.
But I will come to you soon, if the Lord permits, and then I will discover not merely the talk and boasting of those who have become arrogant, but what actual power they possess.
For the kingdom of God does not consist in eloquent talk and empty words, but in the demonstration of power.
What is your preference? Shall I come to you with stern discipline like a rod, or shall I come in love and with a spirit of gentleness?

verses.heading: On Incest and Other Vices in the Church / On Incest and Other Vices in the Church
verses.text: It is widely reported that sexual immorality exists among you, and it is immorality of such a kind that does not even occur among pagan Gentiles—namely, that someone is living in a sexual relationship with his father’s wife.
Yet you have become puffed up with arrogance instead of mourning in sorrow, so that the one who has committed this act might be removed from your fellowship.
For I, though physically absent but present with you in spirit, have already passed judgment on the one who has perpetrated this deed, as if I were physically present with you.
When you are assembled together in the name of our Lord Jesus, and my spirit is with you along with the power of our Lord Jesus,
you are to hand this person over to Satan for the destruction of his flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.
Your boasting is not appropriate. Do you not realize that a small amount of leaven works its way through the entire batch of dough?
Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a fresh batch of dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ our Passover lamb has been sacrificed.
Therefore, let us celebrate the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of purity and truth.
I wrote to you in my previous letter not to associate with sexually immoral people—
not meaning at all the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, since then you would need to leave the world entirely.

But now I am writing to you that you must not associate with anyone who claims to be a believer if he is sexually immoral or greedy or an idolater or a slanderer or a drunkard or a swindler. Do not even eat with such a person.
For what business is it of mine to judge those outside the church? Are you not responsible for judging those inside?
But those outside God will judge. Remove the wicked person from among yourselves.

verses.heading: On Lawsuits Among Believers / On Lawsuits Among Believers
verses.text: When one of you has a grievance against a fellow believer, how dare you seek legal judgment before unrighteous magistrates instead of before the saints?
Are you unaware that the saints will participate in judging the world? If you are destined to judge the entire world, are you truly incompetent to adjudicate trivial disputes?
Are you unaware that we will evaluate angels? How much more should we be capable of resolving everyday matters?
So if you have disputes regarding everyday affairs, why do you place those whom the church considers least significant in positions of judgment?
I mention this to bring shame upon you. Can it really be that not even one wise man exists among you who could arbitrate between his brothers?
Instead, one brother initiates legal proceedings against another brother—and does so before those who reject the faith!
The mere existence of lawsuits among you already represents total failure. Why not instead accept being wronged? Why not instead accept being cheated?
Yet you yourselves commit wrongs and and defraud—and you do these things to your brothers!

Are you unaware that those who practice unrighteousness will have no inheritance in God’s kingdom? Do not deceive yourselves: neither those who engage in sexual immorality, nor idol worshipers, nor those who commit adultery, nor men who submit to homosexual acts, nor men who engage in homosexual acts,
nor those who steal, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor those who slander others, nor swindlers will inherit God’s kingdom.

Some of you formerly lived in these ways. Yet you have been cleansed, you have been sanctified or set apart as holy, you have been justified or declared righteous through the authority of the Lord Jesus and through the Spirit of our God.

verses.heading: On Sexual Immorality / On Sexual Immorality
verses.text: “Everything is permissible for me”—yet not everything proves beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me”—yet I refuse to be dominated by anything.

“Food exists for the stomach’s benefit and the stomach for food’s benefit”—yet God will abolish both. However, the body does not exist for sexual immorality’s sake, but for the Lord’s purposes, and the Lord exists for the body’s sake.
God raised the Lord from death and will likewise raise us through His power.
Are you unaware that your physical bodies constitute parts of Christ? Should I then remove parts of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Absolutely not!
Or are you unaware that whoever unites himself with a prostitute forms one body with her? Scripture declares, “The two shall become one flesh.”
However, whoever unites himself with the Lord forms one spirit with Him.
Run away from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man commits occurs outside his body, but whoever engages in sexual immorality sins directly against his own body.
Or are you unaware that your body functions as a sanctuary of the Holy Spirit dwelling within you, whom you received from God, and that you do not possess ownership of yourselves?
You were purchased at tremendous cost. Therefore, bring glory to God through your body.

verses.heading: On Christian Marriage / On Christian Marriage
verses.text: Now addressing the matters you wrote about: “Avoiding sexual contact with a woman benefits a man.”
However, because sexual immorality occurs so frequently, each man should maintain his own wife, and each woman should maintain her own husband.
The husband should fulfill his marital obligations toward his wife, and likewise the wife should fulfill hers toward her husband.
The wife does not possess independent authority over her own body; rather, her husband does. Likewise, the husband does not possess independent authority over his own body; rather, his wife does.

Do not withhold yourselves from one another, except perhaps by mutual agreement for a limited period, enabling you to dedicate yourselves to prayer. Then resume normal relations, preventing Satan from exploiting your lack of self-restraint to tempt you.
I offer this as a permitted concession, not as a binding directive.
I wish all men were even as I am. However, each man has his own gift from God, one in this manner, another in that manner.
To those who are unmarried and to widows I say: Remaining as I am would benefit them.
However, if they cannot maintain self-control, they should marry. Marriage is preferable to burning with unfulfilled desire.
To those who are married I give this directive (originating not from me but from the Lord): A wife must not separate from her husband.
But if she does separate, she must either remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. Similarly, a husband must not divorce his wife.
To the rest I say (speaking from my own authority, not the Lord’s direct command): If any brother has an unbelieving wife who consents to live with him, he must not divorce her.
If any woman has an unbelieving husband who consents to live with her, she must not divorce him.

The unbelieving husband is set apart through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is set apart through her believing husband; otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are regarded as holy because of the believer’s faith.
However, if the unbelieving partner chooses to depart, allow the separation. The brother or the sister is not bound to the marriage in such circumstances, for God has called us to peaceful living.
How can you know, wife, whether you will bring salvation to your husband? How can you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
Nevertheless, as the Lord has assigned to each man, as God has called each man, so let him conduct his life. This is how I establish practice in all the churches.
Was anyone already circumcised when called? He should not attempt to reverse the circumcision. Was anyone uncircumcised when called? He should not undergo circumcision.
Circumcision means nothing and uncircumcision means nothing; what matters is obeying God’s commandments.
Each man should remain in the condition in which he was called.
Were you a slave when called? Do not let it trouble you. But if you can obtain freedom, seize the opportunity.
The man who was called in the Lord while a slave is the Lord’s freedman. Likewise, the man who was called while free is Christ’s slave.
You were purchased at a price; do not become slaves of men.
Each man should remain with God in the condition in which he was called, brothers.
Now concerning virgins: I have no commandment from the Lord, but I offer my judgment as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.
Therefore, I consider this to be beneficial because of the present distress or crisis. It is good for a man to remain in his current condition.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you unattached to a woman? Do not seek a wife.
But even if you do marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Nevertheless, such people will experience trouble in this earthly life, and I want to spare you that.
But this I say, brothers: The time has been shortened, so that from now on even those who have wives should live as though they had none;
and those who mourn, as though they were not mourning; and those who rejoice, as though they were not rejoicing; and those who make purchases, as though they did not possess anything;
and those who utilize the world, as though not making full use of it. For the present form of this world is passing away.
I want you to be free from anxieties. The unmarried man is concerned about the Lord’s affairs, how he may please the Lord.
But the married man is concerned about worldly affairs, how he may please his wife,

and his interests are divided. The unmarried woman or the virgin is concerned about the Lord’s affairs, so that she may be holy in both body and spirit. But the married woman is concerned about worldly affairs, how she may please her husband.
I say this for your own benefit, not to place restrictions on you, but to promote what is appropriate and to secure undistracted devotion to the Lord.
But if anyone believes he is treating his betrothed improperly, if she is past the bloom of youth and it seems necessary, let him do what he wishes. He commits no sin; let them marry.
But the man who stands firm in his heart, being under no compulsion and exercising control over his own will, and has decided not to marry his betrothed, will do well.
Therefore, the man who marries his betrothed does well, and the man who does not marry her will do even better.
A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry whomever she wishes, only in the Lord.
Yet she is more blessed if she remains as she is, in my judgment—and I believe I also have the Spirit of God.

verses.heading: On Food Sacrificed to Idols / On Food Sacrificed to Idols
verses.text: Now concerning food sacrificed to idols: We know that “we all possess knowledge.” Knowledge inflates with pride, but love builds up.
If anyone imagines he knows something, he does not yet know as he ought to know.
But if anyone loves God, he is known by Him.
Therefore, concerning the consumption of food sacrificed to idols: We know that “an idol is nothing in the world,” and that “there is no God but one.”
For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—as indeed there are many “gods” and many “lords”—
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom all things come and for whom we exist, and there is one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

However, not everyone has this knowledge. Some people, having long been habituated through prior participation in idol worship, still eat the food as something offered to idols, and their conscience, being weak, becomes defiled.
But food does not commend us to God. We are neither disadvantaged if we abstain, nor advantaged if we eat.
But be careful that this right of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to those who are weak.
For if someone sees you who have knowledge dining in an idol’s temple, will not his conscience, being weak, be emboldened to eat food sacrificed to idols?
So the weak man is destroyed by your knowledge—the brother for whom Christ died.
Thus, by sinning against your brothers and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I may not cause my brother to stumble.

verses.heading: Paul Gives Up Certain of His Rights / Paul Gives Up Certain of His Rights
verses.text: Am I not operating as a free person? Do I not function as an apostle? Have I not personally witnessed Jesus our Lord? Are you not the evidence of my apostolic work in the Lord?
Even if others do not recognize my apostolic authority, surely you must, for you serve as the validation of my apostleship in the Lord.
This is my response to those who question and scrutinize me:
Do we not have the right to receive food and drink?
Do we not have the right to be accompanied by a believing wife, just as the other apostles do, along with the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones expected to continue supporting ourselves through manual labor?

What soldier ever serves in the military at his own financial expense? What farmer plants a vineyard but does not consume its fruit? What shepherd tends a flock but does not drink from the flock’s milk?
I am not presenting these arguments from a merely human perspective. Does not the Law itself affirm these principles?
For in the Law of Moses it is written: “You shall not muzzle an ox while it is treading out grain.”* Is God primarily concerned about oxen?

Or is He undoubtedly speaking with us in mind? Indeed, this was written for our instruction, because the one who plows should plow with expectation, and the one who threshes grain should do so with hope of sharing in the harvest.
If we have planted spiritual realities in your lives, is it excessive for us to harvest material support from you?

If others exercise this right to receive support from you, do we not have an even greater claim? Nevertheless, we have not exercised this right, but instead endure all hardships patiently, to avoid placing any obstacle in the path of Christ’s gospel.
Do you not understand that those performing temple duties receive their sustenance from the temple, and those serving at the altar share in the altar’s offerings?
In the same way, the Lord has ordained that those who proclaim the gospel should derive their living from gospel ministry.

But I have not utilized any of these privileges. And I am not writing these things to secure such treatment for myself. It would be preferable for me to die rather than allow anyone to nullify my grounds for boasting.
For if I proclaim the gospel, this gives me no basis for boasting, because compulsion has been placed upon me. Indeed, disaster would befall me if I failed to proclaim the gospel.
For if I do this willingly, I receive a reward; but if unwillingly, I have simply been entrusted with a stewardship responsibility.
What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel, I may offer the gospel free of charge, so as not to exploit fully my rights in gospel ministry.

verses.heading: Paul’s Enslavement for Ministry’s Purpose / Paul’s Enslavement for Ministry’s Purpose
verses.text: For though I am free from obligation to anyone, I have made myself a servant to everyone, in order to gain as many as possible.

I have become like a Jewish person to Jewish people, in order to gain Jewish people. To those living under the Law, I became as one under the Law (though I myself am not under the Law’s jurisdiction), in order to gain those under the Law.
To those without the Law, I became as one without the law (though I am not lawless before God, but under Christ’s law), in order to gain those without the Law.
I became weak to the weak, in order to gain the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by all possible means I might save some.
I do all these things for the gospel’s sake, so that I may become a fellow participant in its benefits.

verses.heading: Paul’s Bodily Discipline / Paul’s Bodily Discipline
verses.text: Do you not know that all runners in a stadium compete, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.
Everyone who competes in athletic contests exercises strict self-discipline in every area. They do this to receive a perishable crown, but we compete for an imperishable one.
Therefore, I run with clear purpose and direction, not aimlessly. I box with precision, not as one merely striking the air.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: I subject my body to rigorous discipline and bring it under strict control, lest after preaching to others, I myself should be rejected as unqualified. 9 Quoted from Deut. 25:4

verses.heading: Examples of Divine Discipline From Israel’s History / Examples of Divine Discipline From Israel’s History
verses.text: For I do not want you to remain unaware, brothers and sisters, that our ancestors all experienced the cloud’s protection, and all passed through the sea,
and all were baptized into identification with Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
and all consumed the same supernatural food,
and all drank the same supernatural drink. For they were drinking from the supernatural Rock that accompanied them, and that Rock was Christ.
Yet God was not pleased with most of them, for their bodies were scattered across the wilderness.
Now these events occurred as examples for our instruction, so that we would not crave evil things as they craved them.
Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, just as Scripture records: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to engage in revelry.”*
Nor should we engage in sexual immorality, as some of them did, resulting in twenty-three thousand falling under judgment in a single day.
Nor should we test Christ, as some of them tested Him and were destroyed by serpents.
Nor should we complain, as some of them complained and were destroyed by the destroying angel.
Now these events happened to them as warnings, and they were recorded for our instruction, upon whom the culmination of the ages has come.
Therefore, let the person who thinks he stands firm take care lest he fall.

No temptation has seized you except what is common to humanity. But God is faithful, who will not permit you to be tempted beyond your capacity, but with the temptation will also provide the way of escape, enabling you to endure it.

verses.heading: Warnings Against Idolatry / Warnings Against Idolatry
verses.text: Therefore, my beloved ones, flee from idolatry.
I speak to you as to thoughtful people; judge for yourselves what I am saying.
The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a participation in Christ’s blood? The bread that we break, is it not a participation in Christ’s body?
Because there is one loaf, we who are many constitute one body, for we all partake of the one loaf.
Consider Israel according to physical descent: Are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?
What am I implying then? That food sacrificed to an idol has any significance, or that an idol is anything?
No, but I am saying that what pagans sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not want you to become participants with demons.
You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and also the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the Lord’s table and also the table of demons.
Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? We are not stronger than He is, are we?

verses.heading: The Extent of Christian Freedom / The Extent of Christian Freedom
verses.text: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything builds up the community.
Let no one pursue their own advantage, but rather let each one pursue the advantage of others.
Eat whatever is sold in the meat market, raising no questions on the basis of conscience.
For “The earth belongs to the Lord, and everything in it.”*
If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, raising no questions on the basis of conscience.
But if someone says to you, “This has been offered in sacrifice to an idol,” do not eat it, for the sake of the one who informed you and for the sake of conscience.
Now when I say “conscience,” I mean not your own conscience, but the conscience of the other person. For why should my freedom be subject to judgment by another person’s conscience?
If I partake with thankfulness, why am I defamed concerning something for which I give thanks?
Therefore, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything to bring glory to God.
Give no offense, whether to Jewish people or to Greek people, or to the church of God,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: just as I also please everyone in every way, not seeking my own benefit, but the benefit of many, so that they may be saved. 7 Quoted from Ex. 32:6 26 Quoted from Ps. 24:1
Become imitators of me, just as I myself am an imitator of Christ.

verses.heading: On Head Coverings in Public Worship / On Head Coverings in Public Worship
verses.text: Now I commend you because you remember me in all matters, and you hold fast to the traditions exactly as I transmitted them to you.
But I want you to understand that Christ is the head of every man, and the man is the head of the woman, and God is the head of Christ.
Every man who prays or prophesies while having something covering his head dishonors his head.
And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for she is exactly the same as a woman whose head has been shaved.
For if a woman does not cover her head, let her hair be cut off as well. But if it is disgraceful for a woman to have her hair cut off or her head shaved, let her cover her head.
For a man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.
For man did not come from woman, but woman came from man.
For indeed man was not created for the woman’s sake, but woman was created for the man’s sake.
As a result, the woman ought to have a symbol of authority on her head, because of the angels.
However, in the Lord, woman does not exist in isolation from man, nor does man exist in isolation from woman.
For just as woman came from man, so also man comes through woman. But all things originate from God.
Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him,
but if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her? For long hair has been given to her as a covering.
But if anyone is disposed to be contentious, we have no such practice, nor do the churches of God.

verses.heading: Divisions and the Lord’s Supper / Divisions and the Lord’s Supper
verses.text: Now, in giving these instructions, I do not commend you, because you gather together not for the better, but for the worse.
For in the first place, when you gather together as a church, I hear that divisions exist among you, and I partly believe it.
For factions must indeed exist among you, so that those who are approved may become evident among you.
Therefore, when you assemble in the same place, it is not to eat the Lord’s Supper.
For in eating, each one takes his own meal first; and one person remains hungry, while another becomes drunk.

What! Do you not have homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you show contempt for the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Should I commend you? In this matter, I do not commend you.
For I received from the Lord what I also transmitted to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was betrayed, took bread,
and after giving thanks, He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.”*
In the same manner, He also took the cup after the meal, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you are proclaiming the Lord’s death until He comes.
Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
But let a person examine himself, and in this manner let them eat from the bread and drink from the cup.
For the one who eats and drinks, eats and drinks judgment upon himself if he does not properly discern the body.
As a result, many among you are weak and sick, and a considerable number have died.
But if we were judging ourselves rightly, we would not come under judgment.
But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
Therefore, my brothers and sisters, when you assemble to eat, wait for one another.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you do not gather together for judgment. And I will arrange the remaining matters when I come. 24 See Lk. 22:19

verses.heading: On the Spiritual Gifts / On the Spiritual Gifts
verses.text: Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers and sisters, I do not want you to remain uninformed.
You know that when you were pagans, you were led astray to voiceless idols, however you were influenced.
Therefore, I make known to you that no one speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is cursed,” and no one can say “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
Now there are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit distributes them.
And there are different kinds of service, and the same Lord oversees them.
And there are different kinds of working, but the same God produces all of them in everyone.
Now to each individual is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.
For to one person is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit;
to another faith by the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit;

and to another the working of miracles, and to another prophecy, and to another the ability to distinguish between spirits, to another different kinds of tongues, and to another the interpretation of tongues.
But the one and the same Spirit produces all these things, distributing to each individual just as He determines.
For just as the body is one unit and has many parts, and all the parts of the body, though many, form one body, so also is Christ.
For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jewish or Greek, whether enslaved or free, and all were given one Spirit to drink.
For the body does not consist of one part, but of many parts.
If the foot says, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” it is not for this reason any less part of the body.
And if the ear says, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” it is not for this reason any less part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
But now God has arranged the parts, each one of them in the body, just as He desired.
And if all were one part, where would the body be?
But now there are many parts, yet one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, “I have no need of you.” Or again, the head cannot say to the feet, “I have no need of you.”
On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable;
and the parts of the body that we consider less honorable, these we treat with greater honor, and our less presentable parts receive greater modesty,
whereas our presentable parts have no need of this. Yet God has composed the body by giving greater honor to the part that lacked it,
so that there may be no division in the body, but that the parts may have the same concern for one another.
And if one part suffers, all the parts suffer with it. If one part is honored, all the parts rejoice with it.
Now you collectively are the body of Christ, and individually you are parts of it.
And God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, then gifts of healing, those who help, those who administer, various kinds of tongues.
Not all are apostles, are they? Not all are prophets, are they? Not all are teachers, are they? Not all work miracles, do they?
Not all have gifts of healing, do they? Not all speak in tongues, do they? Not all interpret, do they?
Now eagerly desire the greater gifts. And I will show you a supremely excellent way.

verses.heading: A More Excellent Way / A More Excellent Way
verses.text: If I speak in the tongues of humans and of angels, but do not have love, I have become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
And if I have the gift of prophecy and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have complete faith so as to move mountains, yet do not have love, I am nothing.
And if I give away all my possessions to feed the poor, and if I surrender my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, it profits me nothing.
Love is patient, love is kind, love does not envy; it does not boast, it is not puffed up with arrogance,
it does not behave improperly; it does not seek its own interests, it is not provoked, it does not keep a record of wrongs;
it does not rejoice over unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;
it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
Love never fails. But if there are prophecies, they will be brought to an end. If there are tongues, they will cease. If there is knowledge, it will be brought to an end.
For we know in part, and we prophesy in part,
but when the complete comes, the partial will be brought to an end.
When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became an adult, I put away childish things.
For now we see through a mirror obscurely, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, just as I also have been fully known.
And now these three remain: faith, hope, love. But the greatest of these is love.

verses.heading: Prophecy and Tongues / Prophecy and Tongues
verses.text: Pursue love, and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.
For the one who speaks in a tongue does not speak to people but to God; for no one understands, but he speaks mysteries by the Spirit.
But the one who prophesies speaks to people for edification and encouragement and consolation.
The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, whereas the one who prophesies edifies the church.

Now I want all of you to speak in tongues, but even more that you would prophesy. And the one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive edification.
But now, brothers and sisters, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophecy, or by teaching?
Even lifeless instruments that produce sound, whether flute or harp, if they do not produce distinct notes, how will anyone know what is being played on the flute or what is being played on the harp?
For indeed, if the trumpet produces an unclear sound, who will prepare themselves for battle?
So you also, unless you produce intelligible speech through your tongue, how will anyone understand what is being said? For you will be speaking into empty air.
There are, perhaps, so many kinds of languages in the world, yet none lacks meaning.
If then I do not understand the meaning of the language, I will be a foreigner to the one speaking, and the one speaking will be a foreigner to me.
So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual manifestations, seek to excel in them for the edification of the church.
Therefore, let the one who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays but my mind remains unfruitful.
What is the conclusion then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the mind. I will sing praise with the spirit, and I will also sing praise with the mind.
Otherwise, if you offer blessing with the spirit, how will the one who occupies the position of the uninstructed say the “Amen” at your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
For you are giving thanks well indeed, but the other person is not being edified.
I give thanks to God that I speak in tongues more than all of you,
yet, in the church I would rather speak five words with my mind in order to instruct others as well, rather than ten thousand words in a tongue.
Brothers and sisters, do not be children in your thinking, but in regard to evil, be infants. In your thinking, however, be mature adults.
In the Law, it is written: “By people speaking other tongues and by lips of foreigners I will speak to this people, and even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”*
Therefore, tongues serve as a sign, not for believers but for unbelievers, whereas prophecy serves not for unbelievers, but for believers.
If, therefore, the whole church assembles in the same place and everyone speaks in tongues, and uninstructed people or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or an uninstructed person enters, he is convicted by all; he is examined by all.
The secrets of his heart are revealed, and consequently, falling on his face, he will worship God, declaring that God is truly among you.

verses.heading: Decency and Order in Worship / Decency and Order in Worship
verses.text: What is the conclusion then, brothers and sisters? When you assemble, each one has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, let there be only two, or at most three, and each in turn, and let one person interpret.
But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the church, and let him speak to himself and to God.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others evaluate what is said.
And if a revelation is given to another who is seated, let the first one keep silent.
For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged;
and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
For He is not a God of disorder, but of peace. As in all the churches of the holy ones,
let the women remain silent in the churches. For they are not permitted to speak, but must be submissive, as the Law also says.
But if they want to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is improper for a woman to speak in the church.
Or did the word of God originate with you, or did it come to you exclusively?
If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing to you is the Lord’s command.
But if anyone is ignorant, let him remain ignorant.
Therefore, my brothers and sisters, eagerly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: But let all things be done properly and in an orderly manner. 21 Quoted from Is. 28:11-12

verses.heading: The Resurrection of Christ / The Resurrection of Christ
verses.text: Now I make known to you, brothers and sisters, the gospel that I proclaimed to you, which you also received, in which you also stand,
by which you are also being saved, if you hold firmly to the message I proclaimed to you, unless you believed in vain.
For I passed on to you as of foremost importance what I also received, that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
and that He was buried, and that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
and that He appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at one time, most of whom remain alive until now, though some have fallen asleep.
After that, He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
Then last of all, as to one abnormally born, He appeared also to me.
For I am the least of the apostles, not fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
But by God’s grace, I am what I am, and His grace toward me did not prove fruitless. Rather, I worked harder than all of them, yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.
Therefore, whether it was I or they, this is what we proclaim, and this is what you believed.

verses.heading: The Resurrection of the Dead / The Resurrection of the Dead
verses.text: Now if Christ is proclaimed as having been raised from the dead, how can some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then neither has Christ been raised.
And if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is futile, your faith also is futile.
Moreover, we are found to be false witnesses about God, because we testified concerning God that He raised Christ, whom He did not raise—if indeed the dead are not raised.
For if the dead are not raised, then neither has Christ been raised.
And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is worthless; you are still in your sins.
Then also, those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished completely.
If we have hoped in Christ only for this life, we are of all people most pitiable.
But now Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
For since death came through a human being, the resurrection of the dead also comes through a human being.
For just as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
But each in their own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward, those who belong to Christ at His coming,
then the end, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when He has abolished all rule and all authority and power.
For it is necessary for Him to reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.
The last enemy to be abolished is death.
For “He has put all things in subjection under His feet.” But when it says that “All things are put in subjection,” it is clear that the One who subjected all things to Him is excluded.
Moreover, when all things are subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will be subjected to the One who subjected all things to Him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what will those who are baptized for the dead accomplish? If the dead are not raised at all, why then are they baptized for them?
Why do we also face danger every hour?
I solemnly affirm, brothers and sisters, by my boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
If in merely human terms I fought with wild beasts in Ephesus, what advantage is it to me? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”*
Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”*
Come to your senses righteously and stop sinning, for some have no knowledge of God—I say this to your shame.

verses.heading: The Nature of the Believers’ Resurrection Body / The Nature of the Believers’ Resurrection Body
verses.text: Now someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? And with what kind of body do they come?”
You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
And what you sow is not the body that will be, but you sow a bare seed—perhaps of wheat or of some other grain.
And God gives it a body according to His design, and to each of the seeds its own body.
Not all flesh is the same, but there is one kind of flesh of humans, and another flesh of animals, and another flesh of birds, and another of fish.
Moreover, there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; but the glory of the heavenly bodies is of one kind, and the glory of the earthly bodies is of another kind.
There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and yet another glory of the stars; for star differs from star in glory.
So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in perishability, it is raised in imperishability.
It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power.
It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. If there exists a natural body, there exists also a spiritual body.
So also it is written: “The first man, Adam, became a living being.”* The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
But the spiritual is not first, but the natural; then the spiritual.
The first man was from the earth, composed of dust; the second man is from heaven.
As was the one composed of dust, so also are those composed of dust; and as is the heavenly one, so also are those who are heavenly.
And just as we have borne the image of the one composed of dust, we will also bear the image of the heavenly one.

verses.heading: The Mystery of Resurrection / The Mystery of Resurrection
verses.text: Now I declare this, brothers and sisters, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
Behold, I tell you a mystery: We will not all fall asleep, but we will all be transformed,
in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be transformed.
For it is necessary for this perishable body to put on imperishability, and for this mortal body to put on immortality.
But when this perishable body puts on imperishability, and this mortal body puts on immortality, then will come to pass the saying that is written: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”*
“Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?”*
Now the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the Law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Therefore, my beloved brothers and sisters, be steadfast, unmovable, always excelling in the work of the Lord, knowing that in the Lord your labor is not in vain. 32 Quoted from Is. 22:13 33 Possibly a quote from the Greek poet called Menander 45 Quoted from Gen. 2:7 54 See Is. 25:8 55 Quoted from Hos. 13:14

verses.heading: Collection for the Poor Jerusalem Saints / Collection for the Poor Jerusalem Saints
verses.text: Now concerning the collection for the holy ones: Just as I gave instructions to the churches of Galatia, so you also are to do.
On the first day of every week, let each one of you set aside some amount and store it up as he may prosper, so that no collections need be taken when I come.
And when I arrive, whomever you approve, I will send them with letters to carry your gift to Jerusalem;
and if it is considered appropriate for me to go also, they will travel with me.

verses.heading: Travel Plans of Paul and Others / Travel Plans of Paul and Others
verses.text: But I will come to you after I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia,
and perhaps I will stay with you, or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I go.
For I do not want to see you now just in passing; for I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,
for a wide and effective door has opened to me, but there are many opponents.
Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without any cause for fear, for he is carrying out the Lord’s work, as I also am.
Therefore, let no one treat him with contempt, but send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to me; for I am expecting him along with the brothers and sisters.
Now concerning our brother Apollos, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers. However, it was not at all his desire to come at this time, but he will come when he has the opportunity.

verses.heading: Final Encouragement / Final Encouragement
verses.text: Be alert, stand firm in the faith, act courageously, be strong.
Let everything you do be done in love.
Now I urge you, brothers and sisters—you know that the household of Stephanas is the firstfruits of Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the holy ones—
that you also submit to such people, and to everyone who cooperates in the work and labors.
And I rejoice over the arrival of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because they have supplied what was lacking from you,
for they have refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore, give recognition to such people.

verses.heading: Final Greetings and Benediction / Final Greetings and Benediction
verses.text: The churches of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, along with the church in their house.
All the brothers and sisters send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
The greeting is in my own hand—Paul’s.
If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be accursed. O Lord, come!
The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

verses.heading: Greetings / Greetings
verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through God’s sovereign will, along with Timothy our brother, To God’s church located in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout the entire region of Achaia:
May you experience grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.heading: Ascription of Blessedness to God / Ascription of Blessedness to God
verses.text: Praise belongs to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father characterized by mercies and the God who provides every comfort,
the One who consoles us in every affliction we experience, enabling us to console those facing any kind of trouble, using the same comfort God Himself provides to us.
Just as Christ’s sufferings abound in our lives, so through Christ our comfort also abounds.
When we endure hardship, it benefits your comfort and salvation; when we receive comfort, it benefits your comfort, which proves effective as you patiently endure the same sufferings we also face.
Our confident expectation for you remains firm, because we understand that just as you participate in our sufferings, so you also participate in our comfort.

verses.heading: Divine Rescue / Divine Rescue
verses.text: We do not want you uninformed, brothers and sisters, about the severe affliction that came upon us in Asia—we were crushed by burdens far exceeding our strength, so much so that we lost all hope of surviving.
In fact, we felt the sentence of death already passed within ourselves, so that we would rely not on our own resources, but on God, who raises the dead,
who rescued us from such deadly peril, and who continues rescuing us, in whom we have placed our confident hope that He will rescue us again,
as you also join in helping us through your prayers, so that many people may give thanks on our behalf for the gracious favor bestowed on us in answer to many prayers.

verses.heading: Integrity of Paul and Others / Integrity of Paul and Others
verses.text: This is our reason for confidence: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially toward you, with sincerity and purity from God—not with earthly wisdom but with God’s grace.
We write you nothing beyond what you can read and understand, and I hope you will understand completely,
just as you have already understood us in part—that we are your reason for pride, just as you are ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus.

verses.heading: Paul’s Change of Plans / Paul’s Change of Plans
verses.text: With this confidence, I originally planned to visit you, so that you might receive a second experience of blessing,
and to pass through your area on my way to Macedonia, then return from Macedonia to you, and have you send me on toward Judea.
When I made these plans, did I act with fickleness? Or do I make plans according to human standards, saying “Yes, yes” and “No, no” at the same time?
As surely as God is faithful, our message to you has not been “Yes” and “No.”
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we proclaimed among you—Silvanus, Timothy, and I—was not “Yes” and “No,” but in Him it has always been “Yes.”
For all of God's promises find their “Yes” in Him; therefore, through Him we also say “Amen” to the glory of God through us.
Now the One who firmly establishes us with you in Christ and who anointed us is God,
who also sealed us and placed the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.
I call upon God as my witness—it was to spare you that I did not return to Corinth.
Not that we lord it over your faith, but we work alongside you for your joy, for you stand firm in your faith.
Yet I resolved this matter within myself: for your benefit, I chose not to make another visit that would bring renewed sorrow.
For if I am the cause of your pain, who then would be the source of my encouragement, except those whom I have saddened?

That is why I wrote as I did, so that when I eventually came, I would not be distressed by those who should have been my joy. I had confidence in all of you that my joy is inseparably tied to the joy of you all.
For I wrote to you out of deep affliction and inner anguish, with many tears, not with the intention of causing you pain, but so that you might fully understand the depth of my love for you.

verses.heading: Reaffirming Love for the Offender / Reaffirming Love for the Offender
verses.text: Now if someone has caused sorrow, he has not brought sorrow upon me alone, but in part—and I say this gently—upon all of you.
The corrective discipline imposed by the majority is sufficient for such a person.
Therefore, instead of continuing in severity, you should forgive him and comfort him, so that he is not overwhelmed and crushed by excessive sorrow.
For this reason, I urge you to reaffirm your love toward him in a tangible way.
Indeed, this was one purpose of my earlier writing: to test the genuineness of your character and to see whether you would demonstrate obedience in all matters.
Now whoever you forgive, I also forgive. For whatever I have forgiven, if there was anything to forgive, I did so for your sake, standing before Christ.
This was so that Satan would not gain an advantage over us, for we are well aware of his schemes and intentions.
Now when I came to Troas for the proclamation of the gospel of Christ, even though an opportunity for ministry had been opened to me by the Lord,
my spirit found no rest because I did not find Titus, my brother. Therefore, I said farewell to them and went on into Macedonia.

verses.heading: Triumphal Procession in Christ and the New Covenant Ministers / Triumphal Procession in Christ and the New Covenant Ministers
verses.text: But thanks be to God, who continually leads us as captives in His victorious procession in Christ, and who makes known through us the aroma of the knowledge of Him everywhere.
For we are, to God, the pleasing aroma of Christ among both those who are being saved and those who are perishing.
To the one group, we are a scent that issues from death and leads to death; to the other, a scent that issues from life and leads to life. And who is adequate for such a calling?
For we are not like the many who treat the word of God as a commodity for profit. Rather, we speak with sincerity, as those sent from God, speaking before God in union with Christ.

verses.heading: The New Covenant Ministry of the Spirit/Righteousness / The New Covenant Ministry of the Spirit/Righteousness
verses.text: Are we once again trying to recommend ourselves to you? Or do we require, as some do, letters of endorsement addressed to you or written on our behalf by you?
You yourselves are our letter, engraved upon our hearts, publicly recognized and read by all people,

clearly demonstrating that you are a letter belonging to Christ, produced through our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets that are human hearts.
Such confidence we possess through Christ as we stand before God.
It is not that we are adequate in ourselves to claim anything as originating from our own ability, but our adequacy comes from God,
who has made us fully capable to serve as ministers of a new covenant, not characterized by written code but by the Spirit. For the written code brings death, but the Spirit imparts life.

Now if the ministry that brought death, carved in letters on stone, came with glory, so that the sons of Israel could not fix their eyes on the face of Moses because of the radiance of his face—a radiance that was fading away—
how much greater will the glory be of the ministry that belongs to the Spirit?
For if the ministry that resulted in condemnation possessed glory, far more does the ministry that brings righteousness overflow with glory.
Indeed, what once had glory has come to have no glory by comparison, because of the surpassing glory that now eclipses it.
For if what was temporary came with glory, how much more does what is permanent remain in glory?
Therefore, since we have such a hope, we speak with great boldness,
and not as Moses did, who placed a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel would not gaze intently at the outcome of what was passing away.
But their minds were hardened. For to this very day, the same veil remains unlifted when the old covenant is read, because it is only in Christ that it is removed.
Indeed, to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart;
but whenever a person turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is present, there is freedom.

And we all, with faces uncovered, reflecting the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are continually being transformed into the same image, moving from one degree of glory to another, just as this transformation comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
For this reason, since we have received this ministry by the mercy of God, we do not become discouraged.

Instead, we have rejected secret and shameful practices. We do not conduct ourselves with deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. Rather, by openly setting forth the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled only to those who are perishing.
In their case, the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so that they cannot see the light of the gospel that displays the glory of Christ, who is the visible image of God.
For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for the sake of Jesus.

For God, who said, “Light shall shine out of darkness,”* is the One who has shone in our hearts, granting us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God as it is revealed in the face of Jesus Christ.

verses.heading: Divine Treasure in Earthen Vessels / Divine Treasure in Earthen Vessels
verses.text: But we possess this priceless treasure in fragile, earthly containers, so that the extraordinary greatness of the power may be clearly seen as coming from God and not from us.
We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; confused, yet not driven to despair;
persecuted, yet not abandoned; struck down, yet not destroyed.
We continually carry in our bodies the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be displayed in our bodies.
For we who live are constantly being handed over to death for the sake of Jesus, so that His life may also be revealed in our mortal flesh.
So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.

verses.heading: The Spirit of Faith / The Spirit of Faith
verses.text: But having the same Spirit of faith, in accordance with what is written, “I believed, therefore I spoke,”* we also believe, and for that reason we also speak,
knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and will present us together with you.
For all these things are for your benefit, so that grace, spreading to an ever-increasing number of people, may cause thanksgiving to overflow to the glory of God.
Therefore, we do not lose heart. Even though our outer man is wasting away, yet our inner man is being renewed day by day.
For our present affliction is light and momentary, yet it is producing for us an eternal weight of glory that surpasses all comparison,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: while we fix our attention not on what can be seen, but on what cannot be seen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal. 6 Quoted from Gen. 1:3 13 Quoted from Ps. 116:10

verses.heading: Our Eternal Building From God / Our Eternal Building From God
verses.text: For we know with certainty that if our earthly dwelling, which is like a temporary tent, is torn down, we possess a permanent structure from God, a dwelling not made by human hands, eternal in the heavens.
For while we live in this present condition, we groan inwardly, earnestly longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,
since when we are so clothed, we will not be found exposed or without covering.

For while we remain in this earthly tent, we groan under its burden, not because we desire to be stripped of our present existence, but because we desire to be further clothed, so that what is mortal may be completely consumed by life.
Now God Himself is the One who has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge and guarantee of what is to come.
Therefore, we are always confident, knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord—
for we conduct our lives by faith, not by what is seen—
yet we are confident and would rather prefer to be away from the body and to be at home with the Lord.
For this reason, we make it our aim to please Him, whether we remain in the body or are away from it.
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what is appropriate for what has been practiced through the body, whether good or evil.

verses.heading: The Ministry of Reconciliation / The Ministry of Reconciliation
verses.text: Therefore, knowing what it means to fear the Lord, we seek to persuade men, but our lives are fully known to God, and I hope they are also known in your consciences.

We are not again promoting ourselves before you, but rather giving you an opportunity to take pride in us, so that you may have an answer for those who take pride in outward appearance rather than inward reality.
For if we appear to be beside ourselves, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for your benefit.
For the love of Christ governs and directs us, because we have reached this settled conclusion: that One died on behalf of all, therefore all died.
And He died for all so that those who live would no longer live for themselves, but for the One who died for them and was raised from the dead.
Therefore, from this point forward, we regard no one merely from a human standpoint. Even though we once regarded Christ in this way, we no longer do so.
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he belongs to a new creation. The former things have passed away; behold, new realities have come into being.
Now all these things originate from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and entrusted to us the ministry of reconciliation—
namely, that God was acting in Christ to reconcile the world to Himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and He has entrusted to us the message of reconciliation.
Therefore, we serve as representatives on behalf of Christ, as though God Himself were appealing through us. We plead with you on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.
He made the One who knew no sin to be treated as sin for our sake, so that in Him we might become the righteousness that comes from God.

verses.heading: Encouragement Not to Receive God’s Grace in Vain / Encouragement Not to Receive God’s Grace in Vain
verses.text: Now as those who labor together with God, we also urge you not to receive the grace of God in a fruitless way.
For He says, “In a favorable time I listened to you, and in a day of salvation I came to your aid.”* Look now, this is the favorable time; look now, this is the day of salvation.

verses.heading: The Experiences of the Apostles / The Experiences of the Apostles
verses.text: We give no reason for anyone to stumble in any respect, so that the ministry will not be brought into disrepute,
but in every circumstance we commend ourselves as servants of God: through great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in severe trials,
in beatings, imprisonments, public disturbances, exhausting labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;
in purity, knowledge, patience, kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in genuine love,
in the word of truth, in the power of God, using the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and the left;
through honour and dishonour, through slander and praise; regarded as deceivers, yet true,
as unknown, yet well known; as dying, yet see, we live; as punished, yet not put to death;
as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything.
We have spoken openly to you, Corinthians; our heart has been opened wide.
You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted in your own affections.
Now in a corresponding response, I speak as to children: open your hearts wide also.

verses.heading: Against Unequal Yoking with Unbelievers / Against Unequal Yoking with Unbelievers
verses.text: Do not be joined together in an unequal partnership with unbelievers. For what partnership exists between righteousness and lawlessness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
What harmony exists between Christ and Belial? Or what share does a believer have with an unbeliever?

And what agreement does the temple of God have with idols? For we are the temple of the living God, just as God has said, “I will dwell among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.*
Therefore, “Come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean, and I will welcome you,*

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: and I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”* 2 Quoted from Is. 49:8 16 Quoted from Lev. 26:12. See also Jer. 32:38; Ezek. 37:27 17 Quoted from Is. 52:11 18 Rephrased from 2 Sam. 7:14; Is. 43:6
Therefore, since these promises belong to us, beloved, let us purify ourselves from every form of defilement, both bodily and spiritual, bringing holiness to completion in reverent fear before God.

verses.heading: Paul’s Joy Over Genuine Repentance / Paul’s Joy Over Genuine Repentance
verses.text: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, corrupted no one, and taken advantage of no one.
I am not saying this to accuse you, for I have already said that you are so deeply in our hearts that we share life and death together.
Great is my confidence in speaking openly to you, and great is my pride in you. I am filled with encouragement; in the midst of all our affliction, my joy overflows beyond measure.
For even when we came into Macedonia, our bodies found no rest. Instead, we were afflicted on every side, with conflicts on the outside and fears within.
But God, who comforts the downcast, encouraged us by the arrival of Titus,
and not only by his arrival, but also by the encouragement he received from you. He reported to us your deep concern, your sorrow, and your zeal on my behalf, so that my joy increased all the more.
For even if my letter caused you sorrow, I do not regret it. Though I did regret it for a time, since I see that the letter caused you pain, even if only briefly,

I now rejoice, not because you were distressed, but because your distress led to repentance. You were grieved in a way that accorded with the purpose of God, so that you suffered no harm from us in any respect.
For sorrow that accords with the purpose of God produces repentance that leads to salvation and leaves no regret, but worldly sorrow produces death.

For consider what this very sorrow in accordance with God’s purpose has produced in you: such determination to clear yourselves, such righteous indignation, such reverent fear, such longing, such zeal, such readiness to see justice done. In every respect, you have shown yourselves to be innocent in this matter.

Therefore, even though I wrote to you, it was not primarily for the sake of the one who committed the wrong, nor for the one who suffered it, but so that your earnest devotion to us might be made evident to you in the sight of God.
For this reason, we have been encouraged. And beyond this encouragement, we rejoiced even more at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
For if I have spoken proudly to him about you, I was not put to shame. Just as everything we said to you was spoken truthfully, so our boasting to Titus about you proved to be true.
And his affection for you has grown even deeper as he remembers the obedience of you all, how you welcomed him with reverence and humility.
I rejoice because I have complete confidence in you.

verses.heading: The Grace of Generosity / The Grace of Generosity
verses.text: Now we want you to know, brothers and sisters, about the grace of God that has been given among the churches of Macedonia,
that in a severe trial of affliction, their abundant joy and their deep poverty overflowed into a wealth of generosity.
For I testify that according to their means, and even beyond their means, they gave voluntarily,
earnestly pleading with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.
And they did this not merely as we had expected, but they first gave themselves to the Lord, and then to us, in keeping with the will of God.
Accordingly, we urged Titus that just as he had begun this work earlier, so he would also bring this act of grace to completion among you.
But just as you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all diligence, and in the love awakened among you—see that you also excel in this act of grace.
I am not speaking this as a command, but as a means of testing the sincerity of your love through the earnestness of others.

For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: though He was rich, possessing all the glory and privileges of divinity, yet for your sake He became poor, willingly laying them aside to take on human flesh with its limitations and sufferings, so that through His poverty you might become rich—gaining the true riches of redemption and eternal life.
And in this matter I offer my judgment, for this is beneficial for you, since you were the first not only to act but also to desire to do so a year ago.
Now bring this work to completion as well, so that just as there was readiness to desire it, there may also be completion according to what you have.
For if the willingness is present, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
The goal is not that others should be relieved while you are burdened, but that there should be equality.
At the present time, your abundance is meant to supply their need, so that their abundance may also supply your need, resulting in equality.
As it is written, “The one who gathered much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too little.”*

verses.heading: Commendation of Titus / Commendation of Titus
verses.text: But thanks be to God, who has placed the same earnest concern for you in the heart of Titus.
For he not only welcomed our appeal, but being himself very eager, he went to you of his own accord.
We have also sent with him the brother whose commendation in the gospel is well known throughout all the churches.

Not only that, but he has also been appointed by the churches to travel with us in administering this gracious gift, which we are managing for the glory of the Lord Himself and as an expression of our readiness to serve.
We are taking precautions so that no one will criticize us regarding the administration of this generous gift.
For we aim to do what is right, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
Along with them, we have sent our brother whom we have often tested and found to be earnest in many matters, but now even more so because of his great confidence in you.
If there is any question about Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for your benefit. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches and a glory to Christ.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Therefore, in the presence of the churches, show them the proof of your love and the reason for our confidence in you. 15 Quoted from Ex. 16:18

verses.heading: The Service of Giving to the Poor Saints in Jerusalem / The Service of Giving to the Poor Saints in Jerusalem
verses.text: It is really unnecessary for me to write further to you about this service for the saints,
for I know your willingness, about which I boast of you to the Macedonians, saying that Achaia has been prepared since last year, and your zeal has stirred up most of them.
Yet I have sent the brothers so that our confidence in you will not prove empty in this matter, and so that you may indeed be prepared, just as I have been saying.
Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—not to mention you—would be put to shame in this confident expectation.

For this reason, I considered it necessary to urge the brothers to go ahead of us to you and make arrangements in advance for your previously promised generous gift, so that it would be ready as a gift freely given and not as something forced.
Now this is the principle: The one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows generously will also reap generously.
Each person must give as he has determined in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God delights in a giver who gives with joy.
And God is able to make all grace overflow to you, so that in every circumstance, having complete sufficiency at all times, you may abound in every good work.
Just as it is written: “He has scattered abroad, He has given to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”*
Now the One who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will also supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest that comes from your righteousness.
In this way, you will be enriched in every respect for all generosity, which through us results in thanksgiving to God.
