However, we do see Jesus, who was made below angels for a brief period, now wearing the crown of glory and honor because He suffered death. Through God’s gracious provision, He tasted death as the representative for every person.

verses.heading: Bringing Many Sons to Glory / Bringing Many Sons to Glory
verses.text: For it was completely appropriate that God—the One for whose sake everything exists and through whose agency everything came into being—should lead many sons into glory by bringing the Pioneer of their salvation to completion through sufferings.
For the One who makes people holy and those being made holy all originate from one source. This is why He feels no shame in addressing them as brothers and sisters,
stating, “I will make Your name known to My brothers and sisters; within the gathered assembly I will sing praise to You.”*
And in another passage, “I will rest My confidence in Him.”* And again, “Here I stand with the children God has entrusted to Me.”*

Since, therefore, the children participate fully in flesh and blood, He similarly partook of that same nature, so that through His death He might destroy the one holding death’s power, namely, the devil,
and so that He might liberate all those who through their entire lives remained enslaved because of their fear of death.
For clearly He does not reach out to help angels, but reaches out to help Abraham’s descendants.

For this reason, it was necessary for Him to become similar to His brothers and sisters in all respects, so that He might prove to be a compassionate and trustworthy High Priest in matters pertaining to God, to accomplish propitiation for the people’s sins.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: For because He Himself experienced suffering under temptation, He has the capacity to assist those undergoing temptation. 6-8 Quoted from Ps. 8:4-6 12 Quoted from Ps. 22:22 13 Quoted from Is. 8:17 13 Quoted from Is. 8:18

verses.heading: Jesus, Greater Than Moses / Jesus, Greater Than Moses
verses.text: Consequently, holy brothers and sisters who participate in a calling originating from heaven, direct your careful consideration toward Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest we openly acknowledge,
who proved trustworthy to the One appointing Him, just as Moses also proved trustworthy throughout all of God’s household.
For Jesus has been evaluated as deserving greater honor than Moses, in the same measure that a house’s builder deserves greater honor than the house he constructs.
For every house receives construction from someone, but God is the One who constructed everything.
Now Moses demonstrated trustworthiness throughout all of God's household in a servant’s capacity, providing testimony to things that would later be communicated.
But Christ demonstrates trustworthiness in a Son’s capacity over God’s household—and we constitute His household, provided we retain our bold confidence and our hope’s boast.

verses.heading: Warning Against an Evil Heart of Unbelief / Warning Against an Evil Heart of Unbelief
verses.text: Therefore, exactly as the Holy Spirit communicates, “Today, should you perceive His voice,
do not make your hearts rigid as during the rebellion, during that testing day in the wilderness,
where your ancestors put Me to the test and observed My works across forty years.
Therefore, I grew angry with that generation, and I declared, ‘Their hearts perpetually wander, and they have failed to comprehend My ways.’
Just as I swore in My anger, ‘They will absolutely not enter My rest.’ ”*
Take care, brothers and sisters, lest there develop in any among you a wicked heart characterized by unbelief, resulting in falling away from the living God.
Instead, provide mutual encouragement daily, while it continues to be designated “Today,” so that none among you becomes calloused through sin’s deception.
For we have become Christ’s partners, assuming we maintain our initial confidence securely to the end.
As the passage declares, “Today, should you perceive His voice, do not make your hearts rigid as during the rebellion.”*
For who were the ones perceiving yet rebelling? Was it not all those who departed Egypt under Moses’ guidance?
And with whom did He experience anger across forty years? Was it not with those committing sin, whose corpses dropped in the wilderness?
And to whom did He swear they would not enter His rest, except to those demonstrating disobedience?

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: So we see they could not enter due to unbelief. 7-11 Quoted from Ps. 95:7-11 15 Quoted from Ps. 95:7b-8

verses.heading: The Attainment of Believers to the Sabbath Rest of God / The Attainment of Believers to the Sabbath Rest of God
verses.text: Therefore, let us fear, lest—while the promise to enter His rest continues to stand—anyone among you should appear to have missed reaching it.
For we too have received the gospel just as they did; yet the message they heard brought them no advantage, because they were not united by faith with those who heard it.

For we who have exercised faith enter that rest, just as He has stated, “Just as I swore in My anger, ‘They will absolutely not enter My rest,’ ”* though His works reached completion from the world’s foundation.
For He has spoken somewhere regarding the seventh day in this manner: “And God rested on the seventh day from all His works.”*
And once more in this passage He states, “They will absolutely not enter My rest.”*
Since, therefore, it remains true that some will enter it, and those who previously received the gospel failed to enter through disobedience,
He once more establishes a specific day—”Today”—communicating through David after considerable time, just as previously stated, “Today, should you perceive His voice, do not make your hearts rigid.”*
For had Joshua provided them rest, God would not have subsequently spoken about another day.
Consequently, a Sabbath rest remains reserved for God’s people.
For whoever has entered His rest has also ceased from his works, just as God ceased from His own.
Let us therefore exert ourselves diligently to enter that rest, so that no one falls through following that same disobedience pattern.

For God’s word is alive and energetically active, more penetrating than any sword sharpened on both edges, piercing to the separation point of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and capable of evaluating the heart's thoughts and intentions.
And no creature remains concealed from His sight, but everything lies exposed and laid bare before the eyes of Him to whom we must render our account.

verses.heading: Jesus, the Great High Priest and the Son of God / Jesus, the Great High Priest and the Son of God
verses.text: Since, therefore, we possess a great High Priest who has traversed the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us maintain our confession firmly.
For we do not possess a High Priest incapable of sympathizing with our weaknesses, but One tested in all respects as we are, yet apart from sin.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Let us therefore approach God’s throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and discover grace for timely help. 3 Quoted from Ps. 95:11 4 Quoted from Gen. 2:2 5 Quoted from Ps. 95:11 7 Quoted from Ps. 95:7b-8

verses.heading: The Imperfect High Priest / The Imperfect High Priest
verses.text: For every high priest selected from men is appointed to act on people’s behalf in matters relating to God, to present both gifts and sacrifices addressing sins.
He can respond gently to the ignorant and those who wander off course, since he himself experiences weakness.
Due to this weakness, he must present sacrifices for sins, both for the people and for himself.
And no one claims this honor independently; rather, he receives it when called by God, exactly as Aaron was.

verses.heading: The Perfect High Priest / The Perfect High Priest
verses.text: Similarly, Christ did not glorify Himself to become High Priest, but received appointment from the One who declare to Him, “You are My Son; today I have fathered You”;*
just as He also states elsewhere, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”*

Throughout His days in the flesh, He presented both prayers and supplications with intense cries and tears to the One capable of rescuing Him from death, and received a hearing due to His reverent submission.
Though existing as the Son, He learned obedience through His suffering experiences.
And having reached completion through those sufferings, He became the Author of eternal salvation for all who obey Him,
having received God’s designation as High Priest according to the order of Melchizedek.

verses.heading: Spiritual Regression / Spiritual Regression
verses.text: Regarding this we have extensive explanation, yet it proves challenging to clarify, since you have become sluggish in comprehension.

For although by now you should function as teachers, you require someone to teach you again the foundational elements of God’s revelations, and you have reached a point requiring milk instead of solid nourishment.
For anyone who subsists on milk lacks experience in the word of righteousness, being still infantile.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: But solid nourishment belongs to the mature, to those who through persistent practice have exercised their faculties to differentiate between good and evil. 5 Quoted from Ps. 2:7 6 Quoted from Ps. 110:4

verses.heading: Warning Against Falling Away / Warning Against Falling Away
verses.text: Therefore, leaving behind the foundational elements of the teaching of Christ, let us advance toward maturity, not establishing again a foundation of repentance from lifeless works and faith directed toward God,
of teaching regarding washings and hand-laying, and regarding the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
And this we will do, if God grants permission.
For it proves impossible to restore to repentance those once enlightened, who tasted the heavenly gift, who became Holy Spirit participants,
who tasted the good word of God and the powers of the ages to come,
yet then fell away—impossible to renew them again to repentance, since they crucify the Son of God afresh for themselves and expose Him to public disgrace.
For land that absorbs frequently falling rain and produces vegetation beneficial for those who cultivate it receives God's blessing.
But land that responds by producing only thorns and weeds proves itself useless. It stands under the curse of God’s judgment, and its final outcome is destruction.
Yet, beloved ones, though speaking this way, we remain persuaded of superior things concerning you—things accompanying salvation.
For God is not unjust to overlook your work and the love you demonstrated toward His name by serving God’s people and continuing such service.
We desire each of you to display this same earnestness right through to the end, for the full realization of your hope,
so that you will not become lethargic, but will imitate those who through faith and endurance inherit the promises.

verses.heading: The Unchangeableness of God’s Promise / The Unchangeableness of God’s Promise
verses.text: For when God made His promise to Abraham, since He could swear by none greater, He swore by Himself,
declaring, “I will certainly bless you abundantly and multiply you greatly.”
And thus, after enduring patiently, Abraham obtained what had been promised.
For people swear by someone superior to themselves, and the oath provides confirmation ending all arguments.
Similarly, when God desired to demonstrate more fully to the heirs of the promise the unchangeable character of His purpose, He confirmed it with an oath,
so that through two unchangeable realities, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might possess powerful encouragement to grasp the hope lying before us.
We possess this hope as our soul’s anchor, both reliable and stable, entering into the inner area behind the curtain,
where Jesus entered as a forerunner for our benefit, having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.

verses.heading: Melchizedek, the Priest of the Most High God / Melchizedek, the Priest of the Most High God
verses.text: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, encountered Abraham returning from defeating the kings and pronounced blessing on him.
To him Abraham also apportioned a tenth of everything. His name, interpreted, signifies first king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, signifying king of peace.

He appears without a recorded father, without a recorded mother, and without genealogy, having neither a documented beginning of days nor an end of life. In this way he resembles the Son of God and continues as a priest forever.
Now observe this man’s greatness: even patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the choicest plunder.

Now those who are Levi’s descendants and receive the priestly office possess a commandment according to the Law to collect tithes from the people, meaning from their brothers, though these also descended from Abraham.
But this one whose ancestry is not traced from them collected tithes from Abraham and blessed the one possessing the promises.
And indisputably, the inferior receives blessing from the superior.
In one instance, mortal men receive tithes; in the other instance, one receives them of whom it is testified that he lives.
And, one might say, through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, has paid tithes,
for he still remained in his ancestor’s body when Melchizedek encountered him.

verses.heading: The Priesthood of Jesus According to the Order of Melchizedek / The Priesthood of Jesus According to the Order of Melchizedek
verses.text: Now if perfection had been achievable through the Levitical priesthood, for based on it the people received the Law, what further necessity existed for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek rather than being designated according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood undergoes change, necessarily a change of Law must also occur.
For the One about whom these statements are made belonged to a different tribe, from which nobody has attended the altar.
For it is obvious that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe regarding which Moses communicated nothing concerning priests.
This becomes even more apparent if another priest arises bearing the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become priest not based on a legal requirement concerning physical lineage, but based on the power of an indestructible life.
For testimony is given, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”*
On one hand, a setting aside of the previous commandment occurs due to its weakness and ineffectiveness,
for the Law brought nothing to perfection. On the other hand, an introduction of a superior hope occurs, through which we approach God.
And this occurred not without oath-taking. For those men became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord has sworn and will not reverse His decision: ‘You are a priest forever.’ ”*
By this much greater measure, Jesus has become the guarantor of a superior covenant.
Now the previous priests existed in greater numbers, because death prevented their continuing.
But because He continues forever, He possesses a priesthood that does not transfer.
Consequently, He is able to save to the uttermost and totally those who approach God through Him, since He lives forever to intercede for them.
For such a High Priest proved fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and elevated above the heavens.

He possesses no need, as those high priests do, to present sacrifices daily, first for His own sins and subsequently for the people’s, because He accomplished this once for all when He presented Himself.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: For the Law appoints men as high priests who possess weakness, but the word of the oath, coming after the Law, appoints a Son who has been perfected forever. 17 Quoted from Ps. 110:4 21 Quoted from Ps. 110:4

verses.heading: The Mediator of a Better Covenant and a More Excellent Ministry / The Mediator of a Better Covenant and a More Excellent Ministry
verses.text: Now the central point in what we are communicating is this: We possess such a High Priest, One who has seated Himself at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,
serving as minister in the sanctuary, meaning in the authentic tabernacle that the Lord established, not any human.
For every high priest receives appointment to present both gifts and sacrifices; therefore it was necessary that this One also possess something to present.
Now were He on earth, He would not qualify as priest, since priests already exist who present the gifts according to the Law.

These serve in what constitutes a copy and shadow of heavenly realities, just as Moses received divine instruction when about to complete the tabernacle. For God stated, “Observe that you construct everything according to the pattern displayed to you on the mountain.”*
But now Christ has obtained a ministry far more excellent, since He mediates a superior covenant, one enacted upon superior promises.

verses.heading: The New Covenant / The New Covenant
verses.text: For had that first covenant been faultless, no occasion would have been sought for a second.
But finding fault with them, God states, “Behold, days are approaching, the Lord declares, when I will bring about a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

not like the covenant I established with their ancestors on the day I grasped their hand to lead them from Egypt’s land, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, the Lord declares.

For this constitutes the covenant I will establish with the house of Israel after those days, the Lord declares: I will place My laws into their minds, and inscribe them upon their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.
And they will no longer teach each one his neighbor, and each one his brother, stating, ‘Know the Lord,’ because all will know Me, from their smallest to their greatest.
For I will show mercy regarding their unrighteousness, and their sins I will remember no longer.”*

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: In calling this “new,” He has rendered the first obsolete. And what is becoming obsolete and aging is on the verge of disappearance. 5 Quoted from Ex. 25:40 8-12 Quoted from Jer. 31:31-34

verses.heading: The Earthly Sanctuary / The Earthly Sanctuary
verses.text: Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first section, in which were the lampstand and the table and the bread of the Presence; this is called the Holy Place.
Behind the second curtain stood a tent called the Most Holy Place,
containing the golden incense altar and the covenant ark completely overlaid with gold. Inside this were the golden jar holding the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the covenant tablets.
Above it stood the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. But we cannot now discuss these items in detail.
With these arrangements thus prepared, the priests enter the first tent constantly, conducting their ministry.
But into the second tent only the high priest enters, once annually, never without blood, which he presents for himself and for the sins of the people committed in ignorance.
The Holy Spirit indicates through this that the way into the holy places has not yet been revealed while the first tent still stands.
This serves as an illustration for the present time, showing that the gifts and sacrifices being presented cannot perfect the conscience of the worshipper.
These consist only of food and drink and various washings, regulations for the body imposed until the time of reformation.

verses.heading: Eternal Redemption / Eternal Redemption
verses.text: But Christ appeared as High Priest of the good things that have come, passing through the greater and more complete tent not made with hands, meaning not of this creation.
He entered once for all into the holy places, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having secured eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on the defiled, sanctify for bodily purification,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit presented Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God.

For this very reason, Christ serves as the mediator of a new covenant: through His sacrificial death, which secures release from the transgressions committed under the former covenant, those whom God has called may now receive the promised eternal inheritance.
For where a testament exists, the death of the testator must be established.
For a testament takes effect only at death, since it has no force while the testator lives.
Consequently, not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.

For when Moses had proclaimed every commandment according to the Law to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the scroll itself and all the people,
stating, “This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you.”*
And similarly he sprinkled both the tent and all the ministry vessels with blood.
Indeed according to the Law, almost everything receives purification with blood, and without the shedding of blood forgiveness does not occur.
Therefore it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with superior sacrifices to these.
For Christ did not enter holy places made with hands, copies of the authentic ones, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf.
Nor did He enter to present Himself repeatedly, as the high priest enters the holy places annually with blood not his own.
Otherwise He would have needed to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But now, once at the consummation of the ages, He has been revealed to remove sin through His sacrifice.
And just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after this judgment,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: so Christ, having been presented once to bear the sins of many people, will appear a second time, apart from sin, to those eagerly awaiting Him for salvation. 20 Quoted from Ex. 24:8

verses.heading: Christ’s Once-for-all Sacrifice / Christ’s Once-for-all Sacrifice
verses.text: For the Law has a shadow of the coming good things, not the actual form of the realities. It can never, through the same sacrifices offered continually year after year, perfect those who approach.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased being presented, because the worshippers, once cleansed, would no longer have consciousness of sins?
But in these sacrifices there is an annual reminder of sins.
For the blood of bulls and goats cannot remove sins.
Therefore, entering the world, He states, “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me.
In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Behold, I have come— in the scroll of the book it is written about Me— to do Your will, O God.’ ”*
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire, nor did You take pleasure in them”*—which are presented according to the Law—
then He stated, “Behold, I have come to do Your will.”* He removes the first to establish the second.
By that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily ministering and offering repeatedly the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
thereafter waiting until His enemies are placed as a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after stating,
“This is the covenant I will establish with them after those days, the Lord declares: I will put My laws upon their hearts, and upon their minds I will inscribe them,”
then He adds, “Their sins and their lawless deeds I will remember no more.”*
Now where forgiveness of these exists, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.heading: Drawing Near to God’s Presence / Drawing Near to God’s Presence
verses.text: Therefore, brothers and sisters, since we have confidence to enter the holy places through the blood of Jesus,
by a new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain, meaning His flesh,
and since we have a great priest over the household of God,
let us approach with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled clean from a wicked conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us maintain the confession of our hope unwavering, for the One who promised is faithful.
And let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,
not abandoning our assembling together, as some practice habitually, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

verses.heading: Warning Against Deliberate Sinning / Warning Against Deliberate Sinning
verses.text: For if we sin deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains any longer.
Rather, a terrifying expectation of judgment and a fury of fire about to consume the adversaries.
Anyone who rejects the Law of Moses will be put to death based on the testimony of two or three witnesses, with no showing of mercy.

How much worse punishment do you think will be deserved by the one who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, and has regarded as common the covenant blood by which he was sanctified, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
For we know the One who stated, “Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay.”* And again, “The Lord will judge His people.”*
It is terrifying to fall into the hands of the living God.

verses.heading: The Reward of Faith and Endurance / The Reward of Faith and Endurance
verses.text: But remember the earlier days when, after being enlightened, you endured a great suffering struggle.
Sometimes being publicly exposed to insults and afflictions, and sometimes becoming partners with those experiencing this treatment.
For you sympathised with the prisoners and joyfully accepted the seizure of your possessions, knowing you possess a superior and enduring possession.
Therefore, do not discard your confidence, which carries great reward.
For you have need of endurance, so that after doing the will of God, you may receive what is promised.
“For yet a very little while, the Coming One will come and will not delay.
But My righteous one will live by faith; and if he shrinks back, My soul has no pleasure in him.”*

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: But we are not among those who shrink back to destruction, but among those who have faith resulting in the preservation of the soul. 5-7 Quoted from Ps. 40:6-8 8 Quoted from Ps. 40:6 9 Quoted from Ps. 40:8 16-17 Quoted from Jer. 31:33-34 30 Quoted from Deut. 32:35 30 Quoted from Deut. 32:36 37-38 Quoted from Hab. 2:3-4

verses.heading: The Witnesses of Faith / The Witnesses of Faith
verses.text: Now faith is the settled confidence in what God has promised but not yet seen, and the firm inner certainty concerning realities that remain invisible.
For by this faith the people of ancient times received the approval of God.
By faith we come to understand that the universe was prepared by the spoken word of God, so that what is visible did not originate from material things that could be seen.

By faith Abel presented to God a sacrifice that was superior to Cain’s, and through it he was attested to be righteous, with God Himself testifying to the worth of his offering. Through this act of faith, though he has died, he continues to speak.

By faith Enoch was taken from this life so that he did not experience death, and he could not be found because God removed him. Prior to being taken, he had received the testimony that his life pleased God.
And apart from faith it is impossible to please God, because the one who comes near to Him must believe that He truly exists and that He rewards those who diligently seek Him.

By faith Noah, having been warned by God about events that had not yet occurred, responded with reverent obedience and constructed an ark to save his household. By this faith he exposed the unbelief of the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to leave and go to a place that he would later receive as an inheritance. He went out in obedience, even though he did not know where he was going.
By faith he lived as a resident alien in the land of promise, dwelling in tents along with Isaac and Jacob, who shared in the same promise.
For he was looking ahead to the city with permanent foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
By faith Sarah herself was enabled to conceive, even beyond the normal age for childbearing, because she regarded the One who had promised as faithful.

Therefore, even from one man who was as good as dead, God brought forth a countless number of descendants—so many they can be compared to the stars in the sky or the grains of sand along the seashore.

All of these died while trusting God, without receiving the promised fulfillment, but they saw it from a distance, welcomed it, and openly confessed that they were strangers and temporary residents on the earth.
Those who speak in this way clearly show that they are seeking a homeland of their own.
If they had continued to think about the land they left behind, they would have had the opportunity to return.
Instead, they longed for a better country, that is, a heavenly one. For this reason, God is not ashamed to be called their God, because He has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham, when God tested him, offered up Isaac. The one who had received the promises was in the act of offering his only son,
concerning whom it had been said, “Through Isaac your offspring will be named.”*
He reasoned that God was able even to raise the dead, and in a figurative sense, he did receive Isaac back from death.
By faith Isaac spoke blessings over Jacob and Esau concerning future events.
By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and worshipped God while leaning upon the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, near the end of his life, spoke about the future departure of the sons of Israel and gave instructions concerning his bones.
By faith Moses was hidden for three months by his parents after his birth, because they saw that the child was special, and they did not fear the king’s command.
By faith Moses, when he had grown to maturity, refused to be identified as the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.
He chose instead to share in suffering with the people of God rather than to enjoy the temporary pleasures of sin.
He regarded the disgrace associated with Christ as greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, because he was fixing his attention on the reward that was yet to come.
By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king, for he endured as though seeing the One who is invisible.
By faith he observed the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not strike them.
By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as if on dry ground, but when the Egyptians attempted the same, they were engulfed.
By faith the walls of Jericho collapsed after they had been encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute was spared from destruction along with those who disobeyed, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
And what more should I say? Time would fail me to recount the accounts of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets,
who through faith conquered kingdoms, carried out justice, obtained what God had promised, shut the mouths of lions,
extinguished the force of fire, escaped the blade of the sword, gained strength from weakness, became powerful in battle, and routed foreign armies.
Women received their dead raised back to life. Others were tortured to death, refusing release, so that they might attain a better resurrection.
Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were put to death by the sword. They wandered about clothed in sheepskins and goatskins, lacking necessities, afflicted, and mistreated—
people of whom the world was not worthy—roaming in deserts and mountains and living in caves and holes in the ground.
And all of these, though they received the approval of God because of their faith, did not obtain the promised fulfillment,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: because God had planned something better for us, so that apart from us they would not be made perfect or experience the complete fulfillment of His promises. 18 Quoted from Gen. 21:12

verses.heading: Jesus, the Pioneer and Completer of Faith / Jesus, the Pioneer and Completer of Faith
verses.text: Therefore, since we are encircled by such a great multitude of witnesses who testify to a life of faith, let us strip away every hindrance and the sin that clings so tightly, and let us run with perseverance the course laid out before us.

Let us direct our full attention to Jesus, the Originator and Perfecter of our faith. For the joy that lay ahead of Him, He endured the cross, giving no regard to its disgrace, and He has taken His place at the right hand of the throne of God.

verses.heading: Exhortation Concerning the Lord’s Discipline / Exhortation Concerning the Lord’s Discipline
verses.text: Reflect carefully on the One who endured such intense hostility from sinners directed against Himself, so that you do not grow exhausted or collapse inwardly.
In your struggle against sin, you have not yet been pressed to the point of shedding your blood.
Yet you have neglected the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not treat the discipline of the Lord as insignificant, and do not lose courage when He corrects you;
for the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He flogs every son whom He accepts.”*
Endure hardship as divine discipline; God is dealing with you as sons. What son is there whom a father does not discipline?
But if you are left without such discipline—something all true sons experience—then you are illegitimate and not genuine children.
Furthermore, we respected our earthly fathers when they corrected us. Should we not all the more subject ourselves to the Father of spirits and truly live?
They disciplined us for a short time according to their limited judgment, but God disciplines us for our good, so that we may participate in His holiness.
All discipline is painful at the time rather than pleasant, yet afterward it yields a harvest of peace and righteousness for those shaped by it.
Therefore, strengthen drooping hands and steady weakened knees.
Mark out straight paths for your feet, so that what is impaired will not be put out of joint, but instead be restored.

verses.heading: The Call to Peace and Holiness / The Call to Peace and Holiness
verses.text: Actively pursue peace with everyone, and pursue holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
Watch carefully that no one falls short of the grace of God, that no bitter root grows up to cause trouble and corrupt many.
Ensure that no one among you is sexually immoral or godless like Esau, who traded his birthright for a single meal.
For you know that later, when he desired to receive the blessing, he was rejected; he found no opportunity to undo his choice, even though he sought it with tears.

verses.heading: The Greater Reality to Which We Have Come / The Greater Reality to Which We Have Come
verses.text: You have not approached something tangible—a blazing mountain surrounded by darkness, gloom, and storm,
nor the blast of a trumpet or a voice whose words caused those who heard it to beg that nothing further be spoken to them.
For the people could not endure the strict command given to them: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”*
The sight was so terrifying that Moses said, “I am filled with fear and trembling.”*
But you have come to Mount Zion—to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem—to countless angels gathered in joyful assembly,
to the congregation of the firstborn whose names are recorded in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of righteous people brought to perfection,
and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to blood that has been sprinkled, speaking a message superior to the blood of Abel.

verses.heading: Warning Against Rejecting God’s Voice / Warning Against Rejecting God’s Voice
verses.text: Be certain that you do not refuse the One who is speaking. For if those who rejected the earthly warning did not escape, how much less will we escape if we turn away from the One who speaks from heaven?
At that time His voice shook the earth, but now He has promised: “Once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens.”*
This phrase “once more” indicates the removal of what can be shaken—that is, created things—so that what cannot be shaken may remain.
Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us respond with gratitude, and by it offer worship that is pleasing to God, marked by reverence and deep awe,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: for our God is indeed a consuming fire. 5-6 Quoted from Prov. 3:11-12 20 Quoted from Ex. 19:12-13 21 Quoted from Deut. 9:19 26 Quoted from Haggai 2:6

verses.heading: Concluding Exhortations / Concluding Exhortations
verses.text: Continue to love one another sincerely, as members of the same family of faith.
Do not neglect showing hospitality; in doing so, some have unknowingly welcomed angels into their homes.
Remember those who are imprisoned as if you were in chains with them, and those who are mistreated as if you were experiencing it yourself.
Honor marriage, and keep the marriage bed pure, for God will judge those who are sexually immoral and adulterers.
Keep your life free from greed, and be satisfied with what you have, for God has promised, “I will never leave you, nor will I ever forsake you.”*
Therefore, we can confidently declare: “The Lord is my helper; I will not fear. What can anyone do to me?”*
Remember your leaders, who spoke to you God’s word. Reflect on how their lives turned out, and follow the example of their faith.
Jesus Christ remains unchanging—yesterday, today, and forever.
Do not be swayed by diverse and strange or novel teachings. It is better for the heart to be strengthened by God’s grace than by rituals or foods, which have not benefited those who focus on them.
We have a spiritual altar, from which those serving in the old tabernacle could not partake.
The blood of animals brought into the sanctuary as sin offerings was burned outside the camp.
In the same way, Jesus suffered outside the city gate, to make the people holy through His own blood.
Let us, then, go to Him outside the camp, bearing the shame He bore.
We do not have a permanent city here, but we are seeking the one to come.
Therefore, through Jesus, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that acknowledge His name.
Do not neglect doing good and sharing with others; such sacrifices please God.
Obey and submit to your leaders, for they watch over your souls. Let them do this willingly, not reluctantly, for that would be harmful to you.

verses.heading: Request for Prayer / Request for Prayer
verses.text: Pray for us, for we are confident that we live with a good conscience, desiring to act honorably in all things.
I urge you all the more to pray, so that I may be restored to you more quickly.

verses.heading: Prayer and Doxology / Prayer and Doxology
verses.text: Now may the God of peace, who raised from the dead the great Shepherd of the sheep, our Lord Jesus, equip you with everything good to accomplish His will, working in us what is pleasing in His sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

verses.heading: Final Greetings / Final Greetings
verses.text: I urge you, brothers, to accept this word of exhortation; indeed, I have written to you briefly.
Know that our brother Timothy has been released. If he comes soon, I will see you with him.
Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send their greetings.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: May grace be with all of you. 5 Quoted from Jos. 1:5 6 Quoted from Ps. 118:6

verses.heading: Greeting / Greeting
verses.text: James, a servant wholly devoted to God and to the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes living in dispersion among the nations: Greetings.

verses.heading: Trials of Faith / Trials of Faith
verses.text: Count it as complete joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you are confronted with trials of many kinds,
because you recognize that the testing of your faith brings about steadfast endurance.
Let endurance be allowed to reach its full effect, so that you may become mature and whole, lacking nothing required for spiritual completeness.
If any of you is lacking wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But he must ask in faith, without inner hesitation, for the one who wavers is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed about by the wind.
Such a person should not expect to receive anything from the Lord,
being divided in allegiance and unstable in all his ways.
Let the brother who is in humble circumstances rejoice in the dignity God has given him,
and let the wealthy rejoice in being brought low, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.
For the sun rises with scorching heat and dries up the grass; its flower falls, and its outward beauty is destroyed. In the same way, the wealthy person will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.
Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, because once he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which God has promised to those who love Him.

verses.heading: Temptations to Sin / Temptations to Sin
verses.text: Let no one who is being tempted say, “I am being tempted by God,” for God is untouched by evil, and He Himself tempts no one.
Rather, each person is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own desire.
Then desire, after it has conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it reaches full maturity, brings forth death.

verses.heading: Good Giving and Perfect Gift from God / Good Giving and Perfect Gift from God
verses.text: Do not be led astray, my beloved brothers and sisters.
Every good act of giving and every perfect gift comes down from above, descending from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.
In accordance with His own purpose, He brought us into life through the word of truth, so that we would be a kind of firstfruits among all He has created.

verses.heading: Hearing and Doing God’s Word / Hearing and Doing God’s Word
verses.text: Be sure of this, my beloved brothers and sisters: Let every person be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
for human anger does not bring about the righteousness God desires.
Therefore, put away all moral impurity and the excess of wickedness, and humbly receive the word that has been planted within you, which is able to save your souls.
But become people who put the word into practice, not merely those who listen and deceive themselves.
For if anyone hears the word but does not act on it, he is like a man who looks at his natural face in a mirror;
he looks at himself, goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of person he was.

But the one who carefully looks into the perfect law that brings freedom, and continues in it, not as a forgetful hearer but as one who acts on what he has learned, this one will be blessed in what he does.

verses.heading: Pure and Undefiled Religion / Pure and Undefiled Religion
verses.text: If anyone claims to practise religion but does not keep his tongue under control, he is only deceiving himself; such religion has no real substance.
Religion that God the Father recognizes as pure and uncorrupted is shown in practical compassion for orphans and widows in their suffering, together with a life that remains untainted by the world.

verses.heading: Favoritism in the Church / Favoritism in the Church
verses.text: My brothers and sisters, as those who hold faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, you must not practice partiality.
For imagine that a man enters your assembly wearing gold rings and elegant clothing, and at the same time a poor person enters wearing worn and tattered garments.
If you give preferential attention to the one dressed in fine clothes and say, “Sit here in a place of honor,” while you say to the poor person, “Stand over there,” or, “Sit down at my feet,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges whose reasoning is shaped by corrupt motives?
Listen carefully, my beloved brothers and sisters: Has not God chosen those who are poor by the standards of this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
Yet you have dishonored the poor. Are not the wealthy the very ones who exploit you and drag you before the courts?
Are they not the ones who speak with contempt against the honorable name by which you have been called?
If you are truly carrying out the royal law according to Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing what is right.
But if you show favoritism, you commit sin and are convicted by the Law as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole Law but stumbles at a single point has become accountable for all of it.
For the One who said, “You shall not commit adultery,” also said, “You shall not murder.” If you do not commit adultery but do commit murder, you have become a violator of the Law.
Speak and act as people who are to be judged by the law that brings freedom.
For judgment will be without mercy toward the one who has shown no mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment.

verses.heading: Faith Without Works Is Dead / Faith Without Works Is Dead
verses.text: What benefit is it, my brothers and sisters, if someone claims to have faith but does not demonstrate it through works? Can such faith save him?
If a brother or sister is without adequate clothing and lacks daily nourishment,
and one of you says to them, “Go in peace; stay warm and eat well,” but you do not give them what their bodies need, what benefit is that?
In the same way, faith by itself, if it does not express itself in action, is dead.
But someone may object, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith apart from works, and I will show you my faith by what I do.
You believe that God is one; you do well. Even the demons believe this, and they shudder.
Do you want to be shown, you foolish person, that faith without works is barren?
Was not Abraham our father justified or shown to be righteous by works when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
You see that his faith was working together with his actions, and by his actions faith was brought to its intended completion.
In this way the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.
You see that a person is justified or shown to be righteous by works and not by faith that remains alone.
In the same manner, was not Rahab the prostitute also justified or shown to be righteous by works when she received the messengers and sent them out by another way?
For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead.

verses.heading: Restraining the Tongue / Restraining the Tongue
verses.text: Not many of you should aspire to be teachers, my brothers and sisters, because you know that those who teach will be evaluated with greater strictness.
For all of us fail in many respects. If someone does not fail in speech, he is a fully mature man, able also to exercise control over his whole body.
When we place a bit into the mouth of a horse so that it will submit to us, we direct the movement of its entire body.
Consider ships as well: Although they are very large and driven by strong winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the helmsman intends.
In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, yet it boasts of great accomplishments. See how a tiny spark can set an enormous forest on fire.

The tongue is also a fire, a sphere of unrighteousness. The tongue is set among our bodily members as something that corrupts the whole person, ignites the entire course of life, and is itself set on fire by hell.
For every kind of animal, bird, reptile, and sea creature is being tamed and has been tamed by mankind,
but no human being can tame the tongue. It is restless and destructive, saturated with deadly poison.
With it we praise our Lord and Father, and with it we speak curses against men who have been made according to the likeness of God.
From the same mouth come both praise and cursing. My brothers and sisters, this ought not to be so.
Does a spring send out fresh water and bitter water from the same opening?
Can a fig tree, my brothers and sisters, produce olives, or a grapevine produce figs? Neither can salt water yield fresh water.

verses.heading: Two Kinds of Wisdom / Two Kinds of Wisdom
verses.text: Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show it by a life marked by good conduct, displaying deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.
But if you cherish bitter jealousy and self-centered ambition in your heart, do not boast and do not deny the truth.
This kind of wisdom does not come down from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, and demonic.
For where jealousy and self-seeking ambition are present, disorder and every kind of corrupt practice will follow.
But the wisdom that comes from above is first pure, then peace-loving, gentle, reasonable and teachable, full of mercy and good fruits, free from favoritism and hypocrisy.
And a harvest of righteousness is sown in peace by those who actively pursue peace.

verses.heading: Against Worldliness / Against Worldliness
verses.text: From where do quarrels arise, and from where do conflicts come among you? Do they not originate from your cravings that wage war within your inner being?

You desire intensely but remain empty-handed. You murder—whether through actual bloodshed or through the hatred in your hearts that God counts as murder—and you covet, burning with jealous longing for what belongs to others, yet you still cannot obtain these things. You quarrel and fight. You lack because you do not ask God.
When you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with corrupt motives, intending to spend it on self-indulgent pleasures.

You unfaithful people, do you not understand that friendship with the world means opposition toward God? Therefore, anyone who chooses to align himself with the world sets himself against God as an enemy.
Or do you think the Scripture speaks without meaning when it says that God yearns with jealous concern over the spirit He has caused to dwell within us?
But He provides an even greater measure of grace. For this reason Scripture says, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
Therefore, place yourselves under God’s authority. Take a firm stand against the devil, and he will flee from you.

verses.heading: A Call to Sinners to Humble Themselves Before God / A Call to Sinners to Humble Themselves Before God
verses.text: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you who are divided in loyalty.
Recognize your misery, grieve, and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow.
Lower yourselves before the Lord, and He will raise you up.

verses.heading: Not Speaking Against One Another / Not Speaking Against One Another
verses.text: Do not speak against one another, brothers and sisters. The one who speaks against a brother or passes judgment on his brother speaks against the law and judges the law. If you judge the law, you are not living under the law but setting yourself up as its judge.
There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and to destroy. Who are you to pass judgment on your neighbor?

verses.heading: Boasting About Tomorrow / Boasting About Tomorrow
verses.text: Now listen, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, conduct business, and make a profit.”
You do not know what your life will be like tomorrow. What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a short time and then disappears.
Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will live and carry out this or that plan.”
But as it is, you take pride in your self-confidence. All such boasting is evil.
Therefore, for the one who knows what is right to do and does not do it, for that person it is sin.

verses.heading: Judgment of Rich Oppressors / Judgment of Rich Oppressors
verses.text: Come now, you who are wealthy: Grieve aloud and lament because of the calamities that are coming upon you.
Your wealth has rotted away, and your fine garments have become food for moths.
Your gold and silver have become corroded, and their corrosion will stand as evidence against you and consume your flesh like fire. You have hoarded riches in what are the last days.
Look closely: The wages you unjustly withheld from the laborers who reaped your fields are crying out for justice, and the cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of armies.
You have lived on the earth in indulgence and luxury, gratifying yourselves without restraint. You have fattened your hearts in preparation for a day of judgment.
You have condemned and put to death the righteous one, and he does not resist you.

verses.heading: Patience in Suffering / Patience in Suffering
verses.text: Therefore, be patient, brothers and sisters, until the coming of the Lord. Consider how the farmer waits for the precious yield of the soil, patiently enduring until it receives both the early and the late rains.
You also must be patient. Strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord is near.
Brothers and sisters, do not grumble against one another, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing right at the door.
Brothers and sisters, take as your example of suffering and patience the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
Look, we regard as blessed those who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the outcome the Lord brought about, showing that the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

verses.heading: Against Swearing / Against Swearing
verses.text: Above all, my brothers and sisters, do not swear oaths, either by heaven or by earth or by any other oath. Instead, let your “yes” truly mean yes and your “no” truly mean no, so that you may not fall under judgment.

verses.heading: Prayer and Singing Praises to God / Prayer and Singing Praises to God
verses.text: Is anyone among you suffering hardship? He should pray. Is anyone experiencing joy? He should sing praises.
Is anyone among you sick? He should call for the elders of the church, and they should pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, they will be forgiven.

Therefore, confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The prayer offered by a righteous person, when it is working, is remarkably powerful and effective in accomplishing God’s purposes.
Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and no rain fell on the land for three years and six months.
Then he prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth produced its harvest.

verses.heading: On Straying from the Truth and Restoration / On Straying from the Truth and Restoration
verses.text: My brothers and sisters, if anyone among you strays from the truth and someone turns him back,
let him know that the one who brings a sinner back from the error of his way will save his soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.

verses.heading: Greeting / Greeting
verses.text: Peter, entrusted by Jesus Christ with apostolic authority, To the chosen ones who live as exiles scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through the sanctifying work of the Spirit, resulting in obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace be multiplied to you.

verses.heading: Ascription of Blessing to God / Ascription of Blessing to God
verses.text: Praised be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in His abundant mercy has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
into an inheritance that is imperishable, uncontaminated, and unfading, kept safe in heaven for you,
who are being protected by God’s power through faith for a salvation prepared to be disclosed in the final age.
In this reality you rejoice greatly, even though presently for a brief period, if it must be so, you have been distressed by various trials,
in order that the proven genuineness of your faith—far more precious than gold that perishes despite being refined by fire—may result in praise, glory, and honor when Jesus Christ is revealed.
Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not see Him now, you believe in Him and greatly rejoice with inexpressible and glorious joy,
as you receive the outcome of your faith—the salvation of your souls.
Regarding this salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace promised to you searched diligently and investigated carefully,

seeking to discover what person or what time the Spirit of Christ within them was pointing to when He testified in advance about the sufferings prepared for Christ and the glories that would follow them.

It was disclosed to them that they were serving not their own interests but yours, concerning the very matters that have now been proclaimed to you through those who announced the good news to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven—matters that angels desire to examine closely.

verses.heading: Called to Be Holy / Called to Be Holy
verses.text: Therefore, preparing your minds for action and exercising self-discipline, set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As children characterized by obedience, do not allow yourselves to be shaped by the desires that formerly controlled you in your ignorance.
Rather, just as the One who summoned you is holy, so you yourselves must become holy in your entire way of life,
because it stands written: “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”*

And since you address as Father the One who judges each person impartially based on that person's deeds, conduct yourselves with reverent fear throughout the period of your temporary residence on earth,
recognizing that you were ransomed from the empty way of life handed down from your ancestors, not with perishable commodities such as silver or gold,
but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without defect or blemish.
He was foreknown before the world’s foundation but was manifested in these final times for your sake—
you who through Him trust in God, who raised Him from the dead and granted Him glory, so that your faith and hope rest in God.

verses.heading: The Abiding Word / The Abiding Word
verses.text: Having purified your souls through obedience to the truth for genuine brotherly affection, love one another deeply from a pure heart,
for you have been born anew, not from perishable seed but from imperishable seed, through the living and enduring word of God.
For “all flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers and the flower drops off,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: but the Lord’s word endures forever.”* This is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news. 16 Quoted from Lev. 11:44 25 Quoted from Is. 40:6, 8
Therefore, strip away all malice, all deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and all slanderous speech.
Like newborn babies, crave the pure spiritual milk, so that through it you may grow up into the fullness of salvation—
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good.

verses.heading: The Living Stone and His Chosen People / The Living Stone and His Chosen People
verses.text: As you approach Him—a living stone rejected by human beings but chosen and valuable in God’s eyes—
you yourselves, like living stones, are being constructed into a spiritual house to serve as a holy priesthood, presenting spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For Scripture contains this statement: “Look, I am laying in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone, and whoever believes in Him will never be disappointed.”*
To you who believe, therefore, belongs the honor, but to those who refuse to believe, “The stone that the builders rejected— this very one has become the cornerstone,”*
and “A stone that causes stumbling and a rock that brings offense.”* They stumble because they disobey the message—which is also what they were appointed to do.

But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people belonging exclusively to God, so that you may declare the praises of the One who summoned you out of darkness into His amazing light.
Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

verses.heading: Christians’ Honorable Conduct and Just Suffering / Christians’ Honorable Conduct and Just Suffering
verses.text: Beloved, I appeal to you: Recognize yourselves as temporary residents and exiles in this world, and therefore resist the bodily appetites that battle against your soul.
Let your behavior among unbelievers be exemplary, so that when they slander you as evildoers, your manifest goodness will lead them to praise God when He arrives in judgment.
Accept the authority of human governing institutions out of loyalty to the Lord—whether the emperor or highest ruler,
or regional administrators whom he delegates to prosecute criminals and honor the law-abiding.
The intention of God is that your upright lives should silence the slander of those who speak against you in their ignorance.
Conduct yourselves as liberated people, yet never exploit that liberty as license for wickedness; rather, live as those bound in service to God.
Treat all people with dignity. Love your fellow believers. Revere God. Respect the ruling authority.
Those in household service: Accept the authority of your masters with profound deference—not merely when they treat you fairly and gently, but even when they are severe.
It is praiseworthy when someone bears suffering unjustly because their conscience is oriented toward God.
There is no virtue in accepting punishment you deserve for wrongdoing. But enduring hardship despite innocent conduct—this merits the approval of God.
This is precisely the vocation to which you were appointed, since Christ suffered on your behalf, providing a pattern for you to trace with your own lives—
He who was utterly sinless, whose speech contained no falsehood;
who, when reviled, returned no abuse; who, when tortured, uttered no threats, but continuously surrendered Himself to the righteous Judge;
who bore the weight of our transgressions in His own flesh on the tree, that we might become dead to sin and alive to righteousness; by His wounds your healing was accomplished.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: You once wandered astray like directionless sheep, but have now come home to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls. 6 Quoted from Is. 28:16 7 Quoted from Ps. 118:22 8 Quoted from Is. 8:14

verses.heading: Submission to Husbands / Submission to Husbands
verses.text: Similarly, wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, so that even if some refuse to obey the word, they may be won over without words through their wives’ conduct,
when they witness your respectful and pure behavior.
Your adornment should not be external—braiding hair, wearing gold jewelry, or putting on fine clothes—
but rather the inner person of the heart, with the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is of great worth in God’s sight.
For this is how the holy women of the past who placed their hope in God used to adorn themselves, by submitting to their own husbands,
just as Sarah obeyed Abraham, addressing him as master. You have become her daughters when you do what is right without giving way to fear.

verses.heading: Instruction for Husbands / Instruction for Husbands
verses.text: Husbands, likewise, live with your wives in an understanding way, showing honor to the woman as the weaker partner, since you are joint heirs of the gracious gift of life, so that nothing will obstruct your prayers.

verses.heading: Called to Inherit a Blessing / Called to Inherit a Blessing
verses.text: Finally, all of you should be united in spirit, sympathetic, showing brotherly love, compassionate, and humble.
Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but on the contrary, offer a blessing, because you were called to this so that you might inherit a blessing.
For, “Whoever desires to love life and see good days must restrain his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deception.
He must turn away from evil and practice good; he must pursue peace and chase after it.
For the Lord’s eyes rest on the righteous, and His ears are attentive to their prayer. But the Lord’s face is set against those who practice evil.”*

verses.heading: Suffering for Righteous Cause / Suffering for Righteous Cause
verses.text: Who will harm you if you become enthusiastic about doing good?
But even if you should suffer for the sake of righteousness, you are blessed. “Do not fear what they fear or be disturbed.”*
Rather, sanctify or set apart Christ as Lord in your hearts, always prepared to give a defense to anyone who asks you to account for the hope you possess—yet do so with gentleness and reverence,
maintaining a good conscience, so that those who speak maliciously against your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame regarding the matters in which they slander you.
For it is better to suffer for doing good, if that is God’s will, than for doing evil.

verses.heading: The Example and Purpose of the Suffering of Jesus / The Example and Purpose of the Suffering of Jesus
verses.text: For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous on behalf of the unrighteous, in order to bring you to God. He was put to death in the flesh but made alive in the Spirit,
in which He also went and made proclamation to the spirits in prison—
those who disobeyed long ago when God waited patiently in Noah’s day, while the ark was being constructed. In the ark a few people, specifically eight souls, were rescued through water.
This water symbolizes the baptism that now rescues you—not the removal of physical dirt, but the request to God for a clear conscience—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subjected to Him. 10-12 Quoted from Ps. 34:12-16 14 Quoted from Is. 8:12b

verses.heading: Living for God’s Will / Living for God’s Will
verses.text: Since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same mindset, because whoever has suffered in the flesh has finished with sin,
in order to live the remainder of your earthly life no longer for human passions but for God’s will.
For the time already passed is sufficient for having pursued what the Gentiles desire—living in debauchery, lusts, drunkenness, wild parties, carousing, and detestable idolatry.
They find it strange that you do not plunge with them into the same flood of reckless excess, and they heap abuse on you.
They will have to give account to the One who stands ready to judge the living and the dead.

For this purpose the gospel was proclaimed even to those who are now dead, so that although they were judged in the flesh according to human standards, they might live in the spirit according to God’s standards.

verses.heading: The End of All Things Has Drawn Near / The End of All Things Has Drawn Near
verses.text: The end of all things is near. Therefore, be of sound judgment and sober-minded for the purpose of prayer.
Above everything else, maintain intense love for one another, because love covers a multitude of sins.
Show hospitality to one another without complaining.
As each one has received a gift, use it to serve one another as faithful stewards of God’s varied grace.

If anyone speaks, let him speak as one conveying God’s own words; if anyone serves, let him serve with the strength God provides, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.

verses.heading: Sharing in the Sufferings of Christ / Sharing in the Sufferings of Christ
verses.text: Beloved, do not be surprised at the painful trial you are experiencing, as though something unusual were happening to you.
Rather, to the degree that you participate in Christ’s sufferings, rejoice, so that you may also rejoice and be overjoyed when His glory is revealed.
When you endure reproach on account of allegiance to Christ, you are blessed, for the Spirit of glory—indeed, the very Spirit of God—rests on you.
Ensure that none among you experiences punishment as one guilty of murder, theft, criminal conduct, or intrusion into matters beyond your concern.
Yet should someone undergo hardship for bearing the identity of a follower of Christ, let there be no shame in this; rather, let him honor God by carrying that designation.
The appointed moment has arrived for divine judgment to commence with the household of God, and if such reckoning starts with us, what end awaits those who defy the gospel of God?
And, “If the righteous person is barely saved, where will the ungodly and sinner appear?”*

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Therefore, let those who suffer according to God’s will entrust their souls to their faithful Creator while continuing to do good. 18 Quoted from Prov. 11:31

verses.heading: Shepherding the Flock of God / Shepherding the Flock of God
verses.text: I exhort the elders among you as one who is himself a fellow elder, who bore witness to the sufferings of Christ, and who anticipates participating in the glory soon to be revealed:

Shepherd the flock of God placed in your charge, exercising oversight—not from obligation, but from voluntary devotion, in accordance with the will of God; not motivated by sordid profit, but with genuine enthusiasm;
not wielding tyrannical control over those entrusted to your guardianship, but modeling exemplary conduct before the flock.
When the Supreme Shepherd is manifested, you will obtain the imperishable crown of honor.

verses.heading: Submission to the Elders / Submission to the Elders
verses.text: In the same way, the younger believers are to place themselves under the authority of the elders. In fact, every one of you must adopt a posture of humility toward others, because, “God arrays Himself against the arrogant, yet extends favor to those who abase themselves.”*
Therefore lower yourselves beneath the sovereign authority of God, that He may elevate you when the moment arrives.
Transfer the entirety of your burdens onto Him, for you occupy His concern.

verses.heading: Firmness in the Faith / Firmness in the Faith
verses.text: Maintain vigilance and sobriety of mind. Your adversary, the devil, circles about as a predatory lion seeking prey to consume.
Oppose him through unwavering adherence to the faith, recognizing that the brotherhood of believers dispersed across the earth endures identical tribulations.

Once you have endured affliction for a season, the God who dispenses every grace—He who summoned you into His everlasting glory through union with Christ—will personally perfect, stabilize, fortify, and ground you.
To Him belongs dominion through all ages. Amen.

verses.heading: Final Greetings / Final Greetings
verses.text: By means of Silvanus, whom I consider a trustworthy brother in the faith, I have composed this concise correspondence to exhort you and to affirm that this is the authentic grace of God. Remain steadfast within it.
She who is in Babylon, elected alongside you, extends salutations, as does Mark, whom I regard as my spiritual son.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: Exchange greetings with one another through the kiss of love. Peace to all who dwell in Christ. 5 Quoted from Prov. 3:34

verses.heading: Greeting / Greeting
verses.text: Simeon Peter, one who belongs entirely to Jesus Christ as His servant, and is sent with apostolic authority, To those who have received a faith equally precious as ours through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:
May grace and peace be abundantly increased to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has granted to us all things necessary for living and for godliness through the knowledge of the One who summoned us to His own glory and virtue,

through which He has bestowed on us His precious and magnificent promises, so that through these you might become sharers in God’s nature, having fled from the spiritual and moral decay that is in the world through sinful craving.

verses.heading: Spiritual Qualities in Increasing Measure / Spiritual Qualities in Increasing Measure
verses.text: For this precise reason, apply all diligence to add to your faith moral excellence, and to moral excellence add knowledge,
and to knowledge add self-discipline, and to self-discipline add patient endurance, and to patient endurance add godliness,
and to godliness add brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness add love.
For if these qualities belong to you and are increasing, they keep you from being useless or barren in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For whoever lacks these qualities is spiritually shortsighted to the point of blindness, having become forgetful of the cleansing he received from his former sins.
Therefore, brothers and sisters, be even more zealous to make certain your calling and election, for if you practice these things, you will absolutely never stumble.
For in this manner, entry into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be abundantly supplied to you.

verses.heading: Peter’s Imminent Death / Peter’s Imminent Death
verses.text: Therefore, I intend to keep reminding you concerning these matters, even though you already know them and stand firm in the truth that is present with you.
I regard it as right, as long as I remain in this bodily tent, to awaken you by means of reminder,
knowing that the putting off of my bodily tent is coming soon, just as our Lord Jesus Christ revealed to me.
And I will endeavor to ensure that after my departure you will always have the ability to remember these things.

verses.heading: Christ’s Honor and Glory, and the Prophetic Word / Christ’s Honor and Glory, and the Prophetic Word
verses.text: For we did not follow artfully fabricated myths when we made known to you the power and appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we had become eyewitnesses of His magnificence.
For He received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice came to Him from the magnificent glory, declaring, “This is My Son, My Beloved One, in whom My delight rests”*—
and we ourselves heard this voice borne from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.

And we possess the prophetic word made more reliable, to which you do well to pay careful attention, as to a lamp giving light in a murky place, until the day breaks and the morning star arises in your hearts.
Understanding this first of all, that no prophecy of Scripture originates from one’s private interpretation.

verses.heading: Notes / Notes
verses.text: For prophecy never came by human initiative, but people spoke from God as they were borne along by the Holy Spirit. 17 See Matt. 17:5; Mk. 9:7; Lk. 9:35

verses.heading: The Condemnation of the False Prophets and False Teachers / The Condemnation of the False Prophets and False Teachers
verses.text: But false prophets also appeared among the people, just as there will also be false teachers among you, who will surreptitiously introduce destructive heresies, even repudiating the Master who bought them, bringing upon themselves swift destruction.
And many will follow their licentious practices, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed.
And driven by greed, they will exploit you with fabricated arguments. The judgment pronounced against them long ago has not been suspended, and their destruction is not delayed.
For God did not withhold judgment from angels who rebelled. Instead, He cast them down into Tartarus, consigning them to utter darkness where they are kept under restraint, awaiting final judgment.
Nor did He hold back judgment from the ancient world. When He brought the flood upon a society that had rejected Him, He preserved Noah—a preacher of righteousness—together with seven others.
Likewise, He condemned Sodom and Gomorrah, reducing those cities to ruin and turning them into a lasting warning of what awaits those who persist in godlessness.
Yet at the same time, He rescued righteous Lot, who was deeply distressed by the unrestrained and immoral behavior of lawless people around him.
Living among them day after day, that righteous man was inwardly tormented as he witnessed and heard their continual acts of defiance against God.
From all this we learn that the Lord knows how to deliver the godly from trial, while at the same time keeping the unrighteous under punishment until the day when judgment is finally executed.

This judgment falls especially on those who surrender themselves to corrupt bodily desires and who treat all authority with contempt. They are reckless, arrogant, and self-assertive, and they show no fear when they speak abusively against the glorious ones.
Even angels—who surpass them in strength and power—do not bring slanderous accusations against them in the presence of the Lord.

Yet these individuals resemble irrational beasts—creatures governed solely by instinct, bred for capture and slaughter. They pronounce judgment upon matters of which they possess no understanding, and in the very destruction that befalls such animals, they too shall perish.

Their suffering will be the fitting return for the harm they cause. They take pleasure in shameless self-indulgence even in public. They are moral stains within the community, openly delighting in their deceptive excesses while sharing meals among you.

Their gaze is saturated with lust for an adultress, and they are incapable of breaking free from sin. They prey on those whose faith is unstable. Their hearts have been disciplined—not in godliness, but in greed. Accursed children!
By leaving the straight path, they have gone astray, choosing to follow the example of Balaam son of Beor, who was drawn by the reward of unrighteous gain.
